validity_flags: Small WinoGrande difference has no statistical support; mechanism attribution remains speculative.
Random baseline column is ambiguously mapped to tasks.

ideas.title: Reported language-model quality remains behind the Transformer
ideas.statement: FDM validation PPL64.9 exceeds the Transformer’s36.3. The limitations paragraph attributes this to training scale121M tokens versus billions used by competitive SSMs.
ideas.conditions: The same paper says its FDM and Transformer baseline were both trained on WikiText-103, so comparison to external SSM data scales does not establish why the within-paper Transformer gap occurs.
validity_flags: Causal attribution of the quality gap to data scale is not isolated by experiments.

ideas.title: Llama2Vec embedding-based token prediction
ideas.statement: Llama2Vec uses Embedding-Based Auto-Encoding to predict original-sequence tokens and Embedding-Based Auto-Regression to predict continued-sequence tokens. The present authors characterize these as token-level bag-of-tokens objectives.
validity_flags: The bag-of-tokens limitation is the present paper’s interpretation of prior methods.

ideas.title: Compression as sequence-level representation pretraining
ideas.statement: Train an LLM encoder to produce compact memory-token embeddings that replace the original context for a frozen decoder’s downstream sequence prediction, then use those memory embeddings for text representation.

ideas.title: Trainable compressor feeding a frozen language model
ideas.statement: Figure 1 contrasts MNTP, Llama2Vec token-logit prediction and LLM2Comp. LLM2Comp appends k memory tokens to the input, adapts the encoder, and passes memory representations to a frozen LLM to predict a sequence.

ideas.title: Dimensional collapse of embeddings
ideas.statement: Dimensional collapse means embedding vectors occupy a low-dimensional subspace instead of using the full embedding space.

ideas.title: Training-free LLM pooling and prompting
ideas.statement: Last-token pooling uses the final layer’s last-token state; weighted mean pooling aggregates sequence-token states; PromptEOL and MetaEOL prompt the last token; Echo Embedding duplicates input so later copies access full context. Echo and MetaEOL increase effective context length and embedding cost.

ideas.title: Adaptation strategies related to compression pretraining
ideas.statement: The paper situates compression pretraining among supervised contrastive learning, instruction tuning, in-context learning, synthetic-data training, joint generation/representation objectives, modified losses and pretext-task adaptation.

ideas.title: Bidirectional encoder with frozen causal decoder
ideas.statement: The target encoder f_theta is adapted from original LLM g_phi with bidirectional attention; LoRA trains the encoder while the original LLM stays frozen. Final hidden states of appended special memory tokens are the compressed context.

ideas.title: Reconstruction compression objective
ideas.statement: For context n_1,...,n_a and appended memory tokens, mtilde_i=f_theta(n_1,...,n_a,m_1,...,m_i)[-1]. The frozen decoder predicts n_hat_l=g_phi(mtilde_1,...,mtilde_k,n_1,...,n_{l-1}); training minimizes NLL of the original context.
ideas.conditions: Encoder adapted with LoRA; decoder frozen. Notation uses sequential memory prefixes despite describing the encoder as bidirectional.
validity_flags: Memory-prefix notation and full bidirectional computation are not fully reconciled in the prose.

ideas.title: Two compression-collapse diagnostics
ideas.statement: The study distinguishes low rank of pooled embeddings from high similarity between unpooled memory tokens.

ideas.title: Prompt-free cold-start token probability probe
ideas.statement: Cold start means computing individual and cumulative probabilities of programming-related tokens with no explicit prompt. It probes pretrained model distributions beyond shared tokenizer vocabularies.
ideas.conditions: The paper does not specify BOS/empty-input implementation or a uniform sampling temperature here.
validity_flags: No held-out coding benchmark validation of this proposed proxy is supplied.

ideas.title: Stated cold-start scope differs from later tables
ideas.statement: Section 2.5 says cold-start metrics could be computed only for R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B/7B/14B/32B, R1-Distill-Llama 8B/70B, and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct; later tables additionally report a larger Qwen family and quantized coder models while omitting a Llama-70B row.
validity_flags: Reporting-scope inconsistency; distinguish named evaluation list from tabulated observations.

ideas.title: Programming Keywords Probability (PKP)
ideas.statement: PKP is cumulative cold-start probability assigned to programming keywords such as def, import and class.
ideas.conditions: Chosen keyword vocabulary; sums are over programming-keyword tokens.

ideas.title: Special Tokens Probability (STP)
ideas.statement: STP is cumulative cold-start probability assigned to programming-related structural tokens, including parentheses, brackets and indentation markers.
validity_flags: Special tokens here means programming-symbol/formatting tokens, not exclusively model-control tokens.
Structural probability mass is not direct evidence of syntactic competence or generation noise.

ideas.title: Natural Language Probability control
ideas.statement: NLP measures probability of common natural-language tokens and is used as a comparison baseline for programming-related probability mass.
validity_flags: The paper does not enumerate the natural-language control token set in its text.

ideas.title: Distilled models emphasize structural-token mass
ideas.statement: Section 2.5.2 reports STP 0.1006–0.7246 and distilled-family PKP 0.0011–0.0062. It compares these to an asserted Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct PKP of 0.0902 and reports NLP 0.00013–0.0017.
validity_flags: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct PKP 0.0902 conflicts with Table 6 unquantized instruct row 0.2572; 0.0902 instead appears in Q2_K row.
NLP range is not evidence of statistical stability.
Structural bias and coding-quality explanations are unvalidated interpretations.

ideas.title: SVD improves over random initialization
ideas.statement: On Qwen3-4B, random Gaussian versus SVD initialization yields LoCoMo 24.26/12.15 versus 25.72/15.40 F1/EM and LongMemEval-S 38.54/22.33 versus 41.24/25.54. EM gains are 3.25 and 3.21 points.
ideas.conditions: One-factor ablation with other TMEM defaults fixed.
validity_flags: Does not empirically verify the theorem alignment assumption or isolate finite-step optimization speed.

ideas.title: Generator and compressor share frozen Gemma-2b weights
ideas.statement: Experiments use Gemma-2b for the generator and compressor and share backbone weights across modules for resource efficiency.
ideas.conditions: Compression-specific LoRA and embeddings train; backbone remains frozen.

ideas.title: Larger distilled models need not have greater mean keyword probability
ideas.statement: The text reports R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B KAP 1.53e-5 versus R1-Distill-Qwen-7B 2.78e-7 and interprets this as nonmonotonic dependence on size.
validity_flags: The 7B KAP value in Table 4 is inconsistent with PKP 0.0017 and a common 276-keyword average; retain reported value.

ideas.title: SlideVQA answer metrics
ideas.statement: The paper evaluates exact string match (EM), token-overlap F1, and Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity (ANLS), an edit-based metric more tolerant of minor surface variation.
validity_flags: Prose describes ANLS via normalized edit distance but does not specify its similarity conversion or threshold.

ideas.title: BBH uses three-shot CoT prompts
ideas.statement: The reported BBH evaluation uses6500 problems across23 subsets and adopts the3-shot CoT original prompts following Suzgun et al. (2022).

ideas.title: Task-aware compression families
ideas.statement: LongLLMLingua uses question-aware coarse-to-fine entropy estimation; RL compressors use task rewards, soft-prompt methods tune for tasks, and RECOMP trains question-conditioned summarization.

ideas.title: LLMLingua-2 distillation-to-classification pipeline
ideas.statement: GPT-4 compresses source text; automatic annotation maps compressed words to preserve/discard labels; quality filters remove noisy examples; a token classifier learns labels; preserve probabilities produce prompts for an LLM.

ideas.title: Three objectives for distilled compressed text
ideas.statement: Distillation targets token reduction, informativeness through retained essential information, and faithfulness through avoiding hallucinated content.

ideas.title: GPT-4 may modify source expressions or hallucinate
ideas.statement: Preliminary experiments found GPT-4 sometimes modifies original expressions and generates hallucinated content despite compression instructions, motivating constrained prompting, annotation and filtering.

ideas.title: Hidden-state and KV-cache compression requires internal access
ideas.statement: Context-hidden-state or KV-cache compression is described as orthogonal to textual prompt compression and difficult to apply to black-box LLMs.

ideas.title: Deletion-only reconstructable compression instruction
ideas.statement: The GPT-4 instruction requests short expressions reconstructable close to the original, permitting removal of unimportant words only; it forbids reordering, changing words, abbreviations/emojis, and added words/symbols.
ideas.conditions: Instruction used for synthetic targets; compliance is imperfect.

ideas.title: Data distillation permits variable compression ratios
ideas.statement: Because information density varies by genre and speaker and GPT-4 may ignore numeric limits, the instruction omits a fixed ratio and asks for the shortest text retaining as much information as possible.

ideas.title: GPT-4 assigns heterogeneous sentence compression
ideas.statement: The MeetingBank chunk-wise sentence compression distribution peaks near 2x, varies widely, and includes a visible >=20x bin; the prose says some sentences are discarded entirely.
validity_flags: Plot values approximate; distribution specific to distilled MeetingBank

ideas.title: Top tokens vary among distilled models
ideas.statement: The paper identifies frequent import/def/void programming keywords and describes preferred structural tokens as newline for R1-Qwen-1.5B, XML-style for 7B, C format specifier for 14B, parenthesis for 32B and hash for R1-Llama-8B; it interprets these as different syntax, markup or language biases.
validity_flags: Interpretations of training exposure and code understanding are speculative.
Some Table 4 special tokens are escaped tokenizer-byte strings rather than directly readable characters.
Table 4 literal 7B byte strings do not transparently substantiate the prose label XML-style; the 1.5B entry is not a bare newline.

ideas.title: Spaces are more probable than tabs under cold start
ideas.statement: Across the five tabulated distilled models, two/four-space tokens have greater cold-start probability than tab tokens. R1-Qwen-1.5B has a particularly large newline probability of 6.70e-2; R1-Llama-8B four-space probability is 8.71e-5 against tab 1.43e-6, about 60.9 times larger.
ideas.conditions: Single next-token probabilities, not measured multi-line formatting consistency.
validity_flags: The claim that larger models particularly favor four spaces is not universal: 7B and 32B have greater two-space than four-space mass.

ideas.title: Within-Qwen compression comparison
ideas.statement: To reduce cross-family differences, the study focuses on Qwen2.5 and compares quantization, parameter scale (1.5B, 7B, 14B, 32B) and base/instruct/coder variants.
validity_flags: Observational comparison of released model variants; training and deployment settings are not fully controlled in the paper.

ideas.title: Moderate quantization redistributes keyword and structural mass
ideas.statement: For Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Q2_K has PKP 0.0902 and STP 0.4248, whereas Q4_K_S has PKP 0.1231 and STP 0.2804. Q8_0 is described as close to the original. The authors regard the Q4_K_S balance as more favorable.
ideas.conditions: Prompt-free token probabilities; quantization variants in Table 6.
validity_flags: A favorable keyword/special-token ratio is an unvalidated proxy for generated-code quality.

ideas.title: Quantized coder variants preserve leading keyword identities
ideas.statement: Across quantization levels the leading programming keywords remain import/package/def/from, which the paper interprets as preserved coding semantics.
validity_flags: Top-token identity stability does not prove code semantic correctness.

ideas.title: High structural-token mass as a proposed noise warning
ideas.statement: The authors associate high special-token mass with repeated spaces, brackets and hashes that could lead to degenerate loops, and suggest lower structural mass might improve generation quality.
validity_flags: No generated-output loop-rate or correctness measurement is supplied.
The sentence attributing reduced STP to more aggressive quantization conflicts with the preceding Q2_K versus Q4_K_S example.

ideas.title: Qwen base cold-start probabilities vary little with scale
ideas.statement: Reported base Qwen PKP values are 0.143 at 1.5B, 0.113 at 7B, 0.123 at 14B and 0.142 at 32B, while STP is approximately 0.12–0.15.
validity_flags: 32B values are stated in prose but no corresponding row is present in Table 6.
The adjective healthier is an author interpretation, not a measured quality criterion.

ideas.title: Instruction tuning changes cold-start probabilities unevenly
ideas.statement: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct reaches STP about 0.449. Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct has PKP 0.0003 versus coder base about 0.121 and different top keywords, prompting the authors to question the smaller model’s behavior.
validity_flags: The claim that instruction tuning increases special-token probability across all sizes is contradicted by multiple Table 6 pairs.
At 1.5B coder STP also drops sharply (0.3104 to 0.0262), not just PKP.
No downstream coding degradation is directly established.

ideas.title: Arxiv example preserves the broad topic but corrupts scientific names
ideas.statement: Figure10 under a200-token constraint preserves discussion of redshift drift, cancellation of components and an optical-drift estimate up to10%, but the compressed-prompt summary calls GADGET-2 GGET2 and replaces Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker metric with Lemaître-Lemaître metric. It omits the full-prompt summary’s discussion of peculiar acceleration. Selective-Context’s output emphasizes different details.
ideas.conditions: Selected summarization case compared with full-prompt generation, not a validation of the underlying cosmological claims.
validity_flags: Topic-level similarity coexists with terminology corruption and omission; caption uses200-token constraint rather than Table1 budgets350/175.

ideas.title: Bilingual instruction data compresses reasoning and answer together
ideas.statement: Instruction tuning uses nearly 10M public samples covering Chinese and English. Responses prepend a chain of thought enclosed by think tags, and visual compression does not distinguish that reasoning from the final answer.

ideas.title: Instruction tuning loss applies only to response tokens
ideas.statement: The supervised loss is −sum_i sum_j log P_theta(u_j^i | {V_hat_k}_{k<i},u_<j^i,V(x)), where V(x) is the independently compressed input query. Cross-entropy comes solely from optical language modeling of the response.

ideas.title: Story example repeatedly replaces generated prefixes with image chunks
ideas.statement: Figure 6 uses a short Chinese request for a meaningful story, left as text. It shows an initial reasoning-and-outline response, then continuation with one completed prefix rendered as an image, then continuation after two compressed prefix images. The story centers on a robotic observer and cyclic awakening; the figure illustrates response-side compression while retaining a text tail.
validity_flags: Qualitative example; narrative and model-generated reasoning are untrusted example content, not evidence of factual correctness or controlled fidelity.

ideas.title: Whether larger data closes the downstream gap remains untested
ideas.statement: The author expects additional training data to close FDM’s LAMBADA and HellaSwag gaps relative to the Transformer.
ideas.conditions: No data-scaling experiment in the paper tests this expectation.
validity_flags: Forward-looking hypothesis, not a demonstrated scaling result.

ideas.title: Sparse attention reduces token interactions
ideas.statement: The paper characterizes sparse-attention methods as removing detected marginal-information tokens to reduce attention computation.

ideas.title: Interleaved chunk memory and sparse causal attention
ideas.statement: VIST2 inputs [c_hat_1,v_hat_1,c_hat_2,v_hat_2,...,v_hat_(n−1),c_hat_n]. Earlier chunks are represented for later text through visual contextual memory; within the current chunk, text is causal. The displayed mask gives 1 for k in {c_i,v_tilde_<i} when q in v_tilde_i, and Causal otherwise.
validity_flags: Printed piecewise mask (Causal otherwise) does not fully specify the earlier-text exclusions visible in Figure 2; notation mixes hat and tilde. Statement preserves both intended visual-memory policy and printed condition.

ideas.title: Rendered-text spatial redundancy supports dense encoding
ideas.statement: VIST2 relies on spatial redundancy in rendered text to compress linguistic information into dense visual latent representations.

ideas.title: Question-aware coarse-to-fine pipeline
ideas.statement: The small model first performs question-aware document selection with optional reordering, then iterative question-aware token compression with dynamic document budgets. A black-box target LLM consumes the compressed prompt, followed by subsequence recovery of the response.

ideas.title: Score the question conditioned on each document
ideas.statement: Coarse compression uses likelihood of the question given a document, rather than document likelihood given the question, because document-level scores can be diluted by irrelevant content.

ideas.title: Restrictive question suffix
ideas.statement: Append “We can get the answer to this question in the given documents” after the question when scoring document relevance. The authors interpret this restriction as regularization against hallucinations.
validity_flags: hallucination mitigation is an author interpretation, not directly measured here

ideas.title: Question-conditioned document ranking score
ideas.statement: Equation (2) defines r_k = -(1/N_c) sum_i log p(x_i^(que, restrict)|x_k^doc), averaging negative log-likelihood of question-plus-restriction tokens for each document. Retain documents ranked as relevant.
validity_flags: source ranking-direction inconsistency: higher negative log-likelihood ordinarily means lower likelihood; preserve printed formula and prose without resolving

ideas.title: Contrastive question-aware token scoring
ideas.statement: For retained documents, score how much a question changes each token’s information value rather than using conditional perplexity alone. Simply prepending the question lowers relevant-token perplexity and can erase its distinction from irrelevant tokens. Instruction and question compression retain ordinary token perplexity and the inherited iterative mechanism.

ideas.title: Contrastive perplexity score
ideas.statement: Equation (3) defines s_i = perplexity(x_i|x_<i) - perplexity(x_i|x^que, x_<i). Tokens with larger question-induced reduction are treated as more relevant; Appendix A implements this via log probabilities.
validity_flags: perplexity terminology differs from conventional exponentiated cross-entropy; Appendix A uses log-space information

ideas.title: Move more relevant documents toward the beginning
ideas.statement: After coarse selection, reorder retained documents according to their question-relevance scores, exploiting stronger access to beginning-of-prompt information to reduce lost-in-the-middle effects.
ideas.conditions: NaturalQuestions provides the main position-controlled experiment; Appendix B.2 says other benchmarks preserve order, but Appendix C explicitly includes non-NaturalQuestions reordering ablations.

ideas.title: Question-aware ranker recall
ideas.statement: On the NaturalQuestions multi-document QA comparison, the proposed document ranker has the strongest reported recall curve across retained-document counts among traditional similarity, embedding, and reranking baselines.
validity_flags: figure-based qualitative comparison; curves merge near full retention; no error bars

ideas.title: Contrastive scores localize answer-bearing context
ideas.statement: Unlike comparatively flat ordinary perplexity, average contrastive perplexity has a clear peak at the fifth document when that document contains the answer, illustrating question-sensitive localization.
validity_flags: illustrative distribution rather than a calibrated relevance probability

ideas.title: Linear rank-based document retention budgets
ideas.statement: For token x_i in document k, tau_i=tau_k^doc. The retained-token budget is tau_k^doc=max(min((1-2I(r_k)/Kprime)delta_tau+tau^doc,1),0). Rank index I starts at zero for highest relevance; tau^doc comes from the inherited budget controller and delta_tau controls spread.
validity_flags: clipping and rank-based allocation are heuristic; no exact total-budget conservation proof given

ideas.title: Token deletion can corrupt copied entities
ideas.statement: When an LLM copies entities from a compressed prompt, token deletion may produce incomplete names, places, or organizations despite preserving enough semantics for comprehension.
validity_flags: semantic-preservation wording is an author claim, not guaranteed for all entities

ideas.title: Recover output spans from original prompt
ideas.statement: Traverse generated tokens; find the longest response substring appearing in the compressed prompt, map it to the corresponding shortest original span containing that subsequence, replace it with the original span, and advance past the matched response substring. Unmatched tokens are copied unchanged. Prefix trees or sequence automata can accelerate matching.
validity_flags: source phrase maximum common shortest subsequence is ambiguous; tie-breaking and replacement safety not formalized

ideas.title: Target model setup
ideas.statement: Experiments use GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613 and LongChat-13B-16k. GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k-0613 is used for original prompts exceeding 4,000 tokens.
ideas.conditions: Model versions and API behavior are those used in the paper.

ideas.title: Compression implementation and decoding
ideas.statement: The compressor is LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, already aligned with supervised fine-tuning and RLHF. Experiments use greedy decoding at temperature zero, PyTorch 1.13.1, HuggingFace Transformers, and 200-token iterative compression segments.

ideas.title: Retrieval baselines preserve source order
ideas.statement: BM25, Gzip, SentenceBERT, OpenAI Embedding, and the LongLLMLingua document ranker remove low-relevance sentences or paragraphs to meet a token constraint while preserving original document order, except explicitly reported reordering variants.

ideas.title: Matched small model and coarse-to-fine controls
ideas.statement: Selective Context and LLMLingua baselines both use LLaMA-2-7B-Chat. LLMLingua and LongLLMLingua first reduce the prompt at coarse level to k times the final constraint, then perform token-level compression to reach the final budget.

ideas.title: Higher compression can hurt retrieval-only baselines
ideas.statement: Across the reported 2x to 4x and 3,000 to 2,000 token constraints, retrieval-only baselines generally lose performance as retention decreases, whereas the question-aware ranker and full system are more robust. Reduced recall is offered as an explanation, not established causally.
validity_flags: author hypothesis for mechanism; not every row/task follows identical trend

ideas.title: NaturalQuestions at about 2x compression
ideas.statement: For GPT-3.5-Turbo, LongLLMLingua achieves accuracies [77.2,72.9,70.8,70.5,70.6] at answer-document positions [1,5,10,15,20] without reordering; reordered accuracy is 76.2. Original accuracies are [75.7,57.3,54.1,55.4,63.1]. Prompts average 1,429 versus 2,946 tokens.
ideas.conditions: NaturalQuestions 20-document setting; greedy GPT-3.5-Turbo.

ideas.title: NaturalQuestions at about 4x compression
ideas.statement: For GPT-3.5-Turbo at the 4x constraint, no-reorder accuracies are [75.0,71.8,71.2,71.2,74.7], reordered accuracy is 75.5, and mean length is 748 tokens (3.9x reduction). The 75.5 reordered score versus 54.1 original score at position 10 differs by 21.4 percentage points; the same-position no-reorder improvement is 17.1 points.
validity_flags: paper headline uses percent for a percentage-point comparison and combines reordered score with original answer position; 4x first-position score is slightly below original

ideas.title: LongChat results across answer positions
ideas.statement: LongChat-13B achieves no-reorder accuracy [68.7,59.4,57.3,55.9,58.4] at 2x and [68.7,60.5,59.3,58.3,61.3] at 4x, with reordered scores 66.1 and 66.7. Original scores are [68.6,57.4,55.3,52.5,55.0], supporting transfer of the compression approach to this open model.
ideas.conditions: NaturalQuestions 20 documents; comparison limited to tested model and data.

ideas.title: Question-unaware compression underperforms on NaturalQuestions
ideas.statement: At 4x, LLMLingua scores 23.5 at position 10 and Selective Context 24.7 for GPT-3.5-Turbo, below zero-shot 56.1 and original 54.1. Full LongLLMLingua reaches 71.2 at the same position; question-aware ranker alone reaches 69.3.
validity_flags: case-specific comparison; noise-retention explanation is not independently isolated here

ideas.title: NaturalQuestions end-to-end latency
ideas.statement: The table reports 4.1 latency units for original prompts, 2.9 (1.4x speedup) for LongLLMLingua at 2x, and 2.1 (2.0x) at 4x. The same table shows Selective Context slowing to 7.4/6.8 and OpenAI-embedding retrieval to 4.9/4.3.
ideas.conditions: V100-32GB end-to-end compression plus LLM request timing; table does not label time unit.
validity_flags: wall-clock API measurements are environment-dependent; variability not reported

ideas.title: Controlled component ablations
ideas.statement: Ablations replace question-aware coarse ranking with entropy-only or SBERT ranking, reverse the conditional likelihood, remove the restrictive suffix, remove question-aware token scoring, impose uniform document budgets, remove/add subsequence recovery, or replace the compressor with GPT2-small.
ideas.conditions: NaturalQuestions and appendix long-context ablations; model details later identify GPT2-dolly.

ideas.title: LongBench at the 3,000-token constraint
ideas.statement: LongLLMLingua scores [40.7,46.2,27.2,70.6,53.0,55.2] for single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code, respectively; average 48.8 versus original 44.0. Mean length is 3,283 versus 10,295 tokens, latency 10.0 versus 15.6, and speedup 1.6x.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo, six LongBench category averages; reordering scope is inconsistent between Appendix B.2 and Appendix C.
validity_flags: nominal token constraint differs from realized mean length
page 6 prose says +1.2 points and BM25 AVG48.9, whereas Table2 gives +0.5 points over 2,000 tokens and BM25 AVG40.6; 48.9 is BM25 Code score

ideas.title: LongBench at the 2,000-token constraint
ideas.statement: LongLLMLingua scores [39.9,43.2,27.4,69.8,53.0,56.7] by the six LongBench categories, average 48.3, using 1,822 tokens and 6.1 latency units (2.6x speedup). Original average is 44.0; ranker-only average 46.3, LLMLingua 34.6, Selective Context 24.8, OpenAI 29.8, SBERT 25.8, and BM25 23.6. LLMLingua slightly exceeds full-system code score: 56.8 versus 56.7.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo; categories are heterogeneous metrics, average is reported benchmark aggregate.
validity_flags: not uniformly best on every task/category; no uncertainty intervals

ideas.title: Question-aware coarse scoring dominates NaturalQuestions ablation
ideas.statement: At 2x with answer document tenth, full LongLLMLingua scores 70.8; removing question awareness yields 39.7, SBERT coarse ranking 65.7, reversing conditional direction 53.4, and removing restriction 70.3. Across all five positions entropy-only ranking incurs the largest losses among these coarse variants.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo, NaturalQuestions 2x.
validity_flags: restriction effect alone is small; hallucination itself is not measured

ideas.title: Fine scoring, adaptive budget, and recovery ablations
ideas.statement: At tenth answer position under 2x, removing fine question awareness drops accuracy from 70.8 to 68.9, removing dynamic budgets to 68.7, and removing recovery to 69.4. Recovery added to LLMLingua raises its tenth-position score from 40.4 to 43.5 but leaves it far below the full system.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo, NaturalQuestions 2x.
validity_flags: no confidence intervals or significance tests

ideas.title: Smaller compressor and reordering ablations
ideas.statement: GPT2-small compressor produces accuracies [74.6,71.7,70.1,69.8,68.5] versus full [77.2,72.9,70.8,70.5,70.6]. Reordering gives 76.2 regardless of original answer position, improving middle positions but slightly lowering the original first-position result 77.2.
ideas.conditions: NaturalQuestions 2x; GPT2-small uses GPT2-dolly per Appendix B.2.
validity_flags: paper claim every component removal hurts at every position overstates reordering behavior

ideas.title: Latency includes compression overhead
ideas.statement: End-to-end timing includes prompt compression and target LLM request time, using V100-32GB, repeated measurements averaged across NaturalQuestions, LongBench and ZeroSCROLLS. Authors attribute slower OpenAI embedding to repeated API calls and slower Selective Context to sequential semantic-unit entropy evaluation.
validity_flags: number of repetitions, dispersion and network variability not supplied

ideas.title: Context-window extension alternatives
ideas.statement: Related work extends windows through staged pretraining, modified or interpolated position embeddings, linear or sparse attention, or external memory. The paper distinguishes these architecture/training approaches from inference-time prompt compression.

ideas.title: Prompt-compression taxonomy and black-box access
ideas.statement: The paper distinguishes token pruning/merging requiring model access, soft compression via GIST/AutoCompressor/ICAE requiring parameter fine-tuning, and small-model entropy/perplexity pruning via Selective Context or LLMLingua. The first two groups are contrasted with direct black-box applicability.
validity_flags: taxonomy is the authors framing of cited methods, not an independently verified exhaustive classification

ideas.title: Question dependence prevents shared context caching
ideas.statement: Different questions require recompressing the same context; LongLLMLingua therefore prevents straightforward compressed-context reuse. The paper also describes approximately twice the compression computation of LLMLingua, adding deployment overhead.
validity_flags: twice-as-much wording is approximate and not accompanied by a separate complexity analysis

ideas.title: Task-aware reuse as future direction
ideas.statement: Extending question-aware compression to task-aware compression is proposed as a way to reuse compressed contexts and permit caching across questions.
validity_flags: suggested extension, not evaluated in this paper

ideas.title: Complex or subtle dependencies can weaken coarse ranking
ideas.statement: Coarse question-aware document scoring may lose effectiveness when the relation between context and prompt is complex or subtle, despite successful multi-hop QA evaluation.

ideas.title: Log-probability form of contrastive score
ideas.statement: Appendix A equation (6) writes the contrastive score as q(x_i)[log p(x_i|question, prefix)-log p(x_i|prefix)] = q(x_i) log[p(x_i|question, prefix)/p(x_i|prefix)], where q is the ground-truth token distribution. The authors state that log-space computation avoids overflow.
validity_flags: identity requires treating perplexity as log-space information, not conventional exponentiated perplexity

ideas.title: Conditional pointwise mutual information interpretation
ideas.statement: The paper interprets contrastive token scoring as conditional pointwise mutual information between token and question given the prefix. Its appendix applies Bayes and asserts that the score represents likelihood of the question conditioned on token and prefix.
validity_flags: Bayes expression ordinarily requires p(question|prefix), not unconditional p(question)
log likelihood ratio is not linearly proportional to a probability as printed in equation (8); at fixed positive constants it gives a monotonic log relation
claimed equivalence is presented with these algebraic qualifications; no performance theorem

ideas.title: Bidirectional encoder and linear softmax head
ideas.statement: For original words x={x_i}_{i=1}^N, h=f_theta(x), p(x_i,Theta)=softmax(W h_i+b), with two labels preserve/discard and trainable Theta={theta,W,b}.

ideas.title: Estimate question sensitivity from token scores
ideas.statement: The appendix proposes using contrastive token likelihoods to represent question-sensitive information across a prompt, avoiding independent generation of a question for each token; it describes obtaining this sensitivity in a single inference.
ideas.conditions: Requires baseline and question-conditioned likelihoods in equation (3).
validity_flags: single-inference wording is not a full accounting of both likelihood computations; limitations state roughly doubled compressor work

ideas.title: NaturalQuestions evaluation design
ideas.statement: The experiment uses the Liu et al. NaturalQuestions multi-document QA construction: 2,655 questions, 20 Contriever-retrieved documents per question, one answer-bearing document, and five controlled answer positions (1st,5th,10th,15th,20th). Mean prompt length is 2,946 tokens; questions originate in Google queries with Wikipedia answers.
ideas.conditions: Dataset inherited from Liu et al. 2024, based on Kwiatkowski et al. 2019.

ideas.title: LongBench evaluation design
ideas.statement: The English LongBench evaluation contains 3,750 problems, 16 tasks in six categories: single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. The paper uses the published evaluation scripts and gives mean length 10,289 in dataset prose.
validity_flags: Tables 2/5 report 10,295 original tokens rather than 10,289

ideas.title: ZeroSCROLLS evaluation design
ideas.statement: The paper describes 4,378 ZeroSCROLLS problems, ten tasks across summarization, QA, aggregate sentiment classification, and information reordering, with mean prompt length 9,788; it uses the validation set and published scripts.

ideas.title: MuSiQue evaluation design
ideas.statement: MuSiQue is described as 39,876 training, 4,834 validation, and 4,918 test problems requiring inference across several documents. The experiment uses the validation set and published scripts; dataset prose gives mean length 2,477 tokens.
validity_flags: Table7 reports 2,427 original tokens, differing from dataset prose 2,477

ideas.title: Budgets and compressor hyperparameters
ideas.statement: Experiments use a Tesla V100 32GB, tiktoken GPT-3.5-Turbo token counts, coarse granular coefficient k=2, instruction budget tau_ins=0.85, question budget tau_que=0.9, segment length 200, and dynamic-budget delta_tau=0.3.
validity_flags: Appendix B.2 calls restriction sentence part of equation (3), although document scoring is equation (2)

ideas.title: Reordering scope is inconsistently described
ideas.statement: Appendix B.2 states reordering is only used in NaturalQuestions for fair comparison, but Appendix C includes LongBench and MuSiQue no-reordering ablations and LooGLE results with and without reordering. The paper does not reconcile this implementation-scope discrepancy.

ideas.title: Average per-word cross-entropy objective
ideas.statement: LLMLingua-2 minimizes L(Theta)=(1/N) sum_i CrossEntropy(y_i,p(x_i,Theta)) using preserve/discard labels distilled from GPT-4.

ideas.title: Contrastive localization survives answer relocation
ideas.statement: Figure 5 repeats the score comparison with answer-bearing documents at positions 1,10,15. Contrastive average perplexity peaks at the answer position while ordinary perplexity varies relatively weakly, extending the fifth-position example.
validity_flags: illustrative plots; no uncertainty intervals or calibrated relevance values

ideas.title: LongBench coarse-question scoring ablations
ideas.statement: At the 2,000-token constraint, full-system average is 48.3; entropy-only coarse ranking gives 37.4, SBERT 36.4, reversed conditioning 30.6, and no restriction 46.1. Removing question awareness lowers synthetic-task score from 53.0 to 18.0 (35.0 points in Table 4).
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo, LongBench six categories.
validity_flags: Appendix C.2 prose says maximum35.8 points whereas table full-vs-no-awareness synthetic difference is35.0

ideas.title: LongBench token scoring and budget ablations
ideas.statement: Removing question-aware fine compression reduces LongBench average from 48.3 to 44.2; removing dynamic budgets gives 45.7. Corresponding synthetic scores are 44.5 and 48.0 versus full 53.0, and single-document QA 35.7 and 36.1 versus 39.9.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo, 2,000-token constraint.
validity_flags: no significance tests or dispersion supplied

ideas.title: Recovery and reordering have small average LongBench effects
ideas.statement: LongBench average falls from 48.3 to 47.8 without recovery and 48.0 without reordering. Both removals improve Synthetic from 53.0 to 53.8; summarization is 27.3 without recovery and unchanged 27.4 without reordering. Thus improvements are not uniform across categories.
validity_flags: contradicts broad prose that document reordering is effective for all types of tasks

ideas.title: GPT2 compressor trades average quality for a smaller model
ideas.statement: The GPT2-small ablation averages 43.0 on LongBench, below full-system 48.3 and original 44.0, with category scores [35.9,39.4,25.0,60.6,42.0,55.4] at 1,892 tokens.
validity_flags: some categories exceed original while aggregate does not; no latency number supplied for this ablation

ideas.title: LongBench gains transfer to LongChat
ideas.statement: At 2,000-token constraint, LongChat-13b gets category scores [31.3,34.6,24.6,46.1,27.8,48.8], average 35.5, versus original [27.4,30.3,20.3,49.9,12.5,42.5], average 30.5. Mean length falls from 10,295 to 1,822. Few-shot score declines by 3.8; synthetic rises15.3 and code 6.3.
validity_flags: page14 prose says maximum synthetic improvement15.5 and other improvements3–5, but table gives15.3 synthetic and6.3 code

ideas.title: LongChat benefits exceed comparator averages
ideas.statement: On LongBench with LongChat, full LongLLMLingua averages35.5, ranker-only 32.3, LLMLingua 22.7, Selective Context20.2, SBERT 16.7 and BM25 12.5. Original is 30.5, so only the question-aware variants exceed the original aggregate among these compressed comparators.
ideas.conditions: 2,000-token constraint, heterogeneous category metrics.

ideas.title: HotpotQA selector-swap result
ideas.statement: Under the same SEER answerer, HotpotQA scores 62.78 with BM25-selected pages and 60.22 with learned visual selection (-2.56 points).
ideas.conditions: Matched completed tasks and page budget; official task scorer.

ideas.title: ZeroSCROLLS at 3,000 tokens
ideas.statement: LongLLMLingua obtains AVG 33.0 versus original 32.5, mean 3,431 versus9,788 tokens, latency 8.2 versus12.2 and 1.5x speedup. Task vector [GvRp, SSFD, QMsm, SQAL, QALT, Nrtv, Qspr, MuSQ, SpDg, BkSS] is [22.1,12.8,15.9,17.1,67.0,27.8,31.3,23.9,65.8,46.5].
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo validation set; not every task exceeds original.

ideas.title: ZeroSCROLLS at 2,000 tokens
ideas.statement: At the tighter budget, LongLLMLingua scores AVG 32.7 with1,826 tokens and 5.2 latency units (2.3x speedup). Task vector is [20.1,12.4,14.9,16.5,65.1,27.7,30.7,23.6,68.5,47.2] versus original [21.8,12.1,17.9,17.4,66.7,25.3,29.8,20.0,69.7,44.1]. It retains aggregate performance but loses some summarization and QALT performance while improving MuSQ and BkSS.
validity_flags: Appendix prose mixes dataset descriptions and rounded changes; table reports MuSQ+3.6 and BkSS+3.1 at this budget
LLMLingua row shows4.8 latency with0.3x speedup, inconsistent with original12.2; preserve source error rather than adopting it

ideas.title: ZeroSCROLLS baseline sensitivity to budget
ideas.statement: Question-aware full compression remains33.0/32.7 at 3,000/2,000-token budgets, whereas ranker-only drops29.3 to 24.9 and LLMLingua 30.7 to 27.2. Other2,000-budget averages are BM25 20.1, SBERT 20.5, OpenAI20.6 and Selective Context19.4.
validity_flags: author notes validation set is relatively small; no intervals reported

ideas.title: MuSiQue multi-hop gains
ideas.statement: Under nominal2x compression with GPT-3.5-Turbo, LongLLMLingua raises MuSiQue F1 from 45.8 to 51.2 (+5.4), reducing tokens from 2,427 to 1,077 (reported2.3x). Comparator F1 values are BM25 28.5, SBERT 36.2, ranker46.3, Selective Context19.6 and LLMLingua 40.1.
ideas.conditions: Validation-set multi-hop QA; table title spells MuSicQue.

ideas.title: MuSiQue needs question-aware coarse selection
ideas.statement: MuSiQue F1 falls from 51.2 to 43.2 with entropy-only coarse ranking,47.3 with SBERT,44.0 with reversed conditional likelihood, and 49.2 without restriction.
validity_flags: restriction ablation alone does not measure hallucination; author explanation is interpretive

ideas.title: MuSiQue fine scoring, budget, recovery, and reordering effects
ideas.statement: MuSiQue F1 is 48.4 without question-aware fine compression,48.2 without dynamic budgets,50.7 without recovery,49.2 without reordering, and 48.4 with GPT2-small, compared with full 51.2. GPT2-small remains2.6 points above original 45.8.
validity_flags: source prose lists drop range0.5–2.8 although dynamic budget removal drops3.0
GPT2 acceleration claimed without a corresponding latency value in table

ideas.title: LooGLE long-dependency QA at about 10x
ideas.statement: LongLLMLingua obtains retrieval40.0, timeline reorder35.0, computation19.7, reasoning33.6 and average 32.1, compared with original 24.1/20.9/13.5/32.1 and average 22.6. Mean length falls from 30,546 to 3,121 tokens (reported10x). Retrieval improves15.9 points; gains differ substantially by task.
ideas.conditions: LooGLE long-dependency QA subset.
validity_flags: no uncertainty intervals; category metric aggregate reported by paper

ideas.title: Document reordering helps LooGLE including timeline tasks
ideas.statement: Removing reordering reduces LooGLE average from 32.1 to 30.9 and task scores from 40.0/35.0/19.7/33.6 to 39.3/33.8/18.7/31.6. The timeline-reordering task itself improves from 33.8 without document reordering to 35.0 with it.
validity_flags: observed task result does not guarantee arbitrary timeline-preserving behavior

ideas.title: LooGLE comparator performance
ideas.statement: LooGLE averages are19.2 BM25,22.0 SBERT,28.3 ranker-only,10.4 Selective Context,17.3 LLMLingua,32.1 full LongLLMLingua,22.6 original and 7.7 zero-shot. The question-aware full pipeline outperforms both retrieval-only and question-unaware compression baselines on all four reported task columns.
validity_flags: compression ratios differ slightly across baselines:8x–10x

ideas.title: Estimated API costs per 1,000 examples
ideas.statement: Using the paper’s GPT-3.5-Turbo pricing assumptions for input and generated output, estimated original→compressed dollar costs per 1,000 examples are4.6→1.3 for multi-document QA (71.7% saved),31.5→3.0 LongBench (90.5%),30.6→3.2 ZeroSCROLLS (89.5%),3.8→1.8 MuSiQue (52.6%), and 93.6→5.6 LooGLE (94.0%).
ideas.conditions: Historical paper estimates, not current pricing; total model API input/output cost per 1,000 samples.
validity_flags: compressor hardware/energy and operational cost are not separately included
rounded dollar amounts and percentages as printed

ideas.title: Thirtyfold compression example retains an answer only with token question awareness
ideas.statement: In Figure6’s NaturalQuestions Nobel-prize example at 30x, removing token-level question awareness produces “No answer found in the given search results.” With question-aware token compression the LLM returns “Wilhelmrad”; subsequence recovery restores “Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen”, matching the reference.
validity_flags: single illustrative case; not an estimate of success probability at30x

ideas.title: Subsequence recovery restores a deleted year digit
ideas.statement: In the NaturalQuestions Dancing on Ice example under4x compression, the original year2019 becomes209 in the compressed prompt and raw LLM response. Recovery returns2019, equal to the reference answer.
validity_flags: single case; demonstrates numeric corruption and repair but does not establish general repair reliability

ideas.title: Compressed code case predicts the call but misses reference structure
ideas.statement: In the LongBench lcc example at 2,000-token constraint, compressed-context GPT-3.5-Turbo returns contact.setLastMessageTransmitted(query.getEnd());, while the reference is an if statement testing that call. The zero-shot response instead calls contact.removeQuery(query). Compression retains useful context but the shown prediction is not exact.
validity_flags: illustrative near-match rather than exact correctness; no executable-code test reported

ideas.title: Compressed demonstrations preserve a classification answer
ideas.statement: Figure9 shows heavily compressed TREC few-shot demonstrations and the query “What is a fuel cell?”. GPT-3.5-Turbo answers “Definition of something”, unchanged by subsequence recovery and matching ground truth at the2,000-token constraint.

ideas.title: 512-token chunks mitigate overcompression of long text
ideas.statement: Original contexts are divided into chunks of at most 512 tokens ending with a period; GPT-4 compresses each separately. The authors observed higher compression ratios for long contexts and attribute resulting loss partly to limited long-context handling.
ideas.conditions: Figure 4 uses GPT-4-32k and output limit 4096.
validity_flags: Causal explanation is conjectural; plot is observational

ideas.title: Ambiguity, variation, and reordering obstruct label alignment
ideas.statement: A compressed word may match repeated occurrences, change morphology, or change position; these three GPT-4 behaviors complicate extracting binary preservation labels.

ideas.title: Sliding bidirectional fuzzy alignment assigns labels
ideas.statement: Algorithm 1 initializes original-word labels false and prev=0; for each compressed word it searches distance i=1..s/2, testing right=min(|S_ori|,prev+i) then left=max(0,prev-i), sets a fuzzy-matched original word true, advances prev only on right matches, and stops at the first match.
validity_flags: Literal pseudocode uses boundary min(|S_ori|,...) without an explicit indexing convention; do not infer implementation details.

ideas.title: Variation rate detects words absent from source
ideas.statement: For word sets S_comp and S_ori, VR=(1/|S_comp|) sum over w in S_comp of I(w not in S_ori). The highest 5% variation-rate examples are excluded to reduce potentially hallucinated material.
validity_flags: Word absence is a hallucination proxy, not semantic verification

ideas.title: Matching rate measures assigned preservation labels
ideas.statement: MR=(1/|S_ori|) sum over w in S_ori of I(l(w)=True), measuring annotated preserved original words relative to original size.

ideas.title: Hitting rate uses original-size normalization
ideas.statement: The printed definition is HR=(1/|S_ori|) sum over w in S_comp of I(w in S_ori), intended to regularize ambiguous many-to-one alignment.
validity_flags: Prose calls this a proportion of compressed words, but equation normalizes by original size; preserve the printed definition.
Set notation and occurrence-sensitive word lists are not fully reconciled.

ideas.title: Alignment-gap quality filtering
ideas.statement: AG=HR−MR; ideal alignment is said to have gap zero, and the highest 10% gap examples are discarded. A large positive gap suggests many source-present compressed words were not labeled as matches.
validity_flags: Quality proxy; no formal proof of semantic correctness

ideas.title: Preserve/discard classification constrains output to source words
ideas.statement: LLMLingua-2 uses binary token classification with a bidirectional Transformer encoder trained on distilled MeetingBank data; preserve probability determines deletion. Source-only selection prevents newly generated words.
validity_flags: Paper claims guaranteed faithfulness; extraction guarantees source-word selection, not preservation of all meaning or truth.

ideas.title: Ratio-controlled top-probability word extraction
ideas.statement: With retained fraction tau=compressed word count/original word count and compression ratio 1/tau, select N_tilde=tau*N highest-preserve-probability words and retain their original order.
ideas.conditions: Word-based ratio; integer rounding is not specified here.

ideas.title: Average subword probabilities preserves whole words
ideas.statement: To accommodate tokenization differences across small and target models, each multi-token word remains intact and its score is the mean predicted preserve probability of its subword tokens.

ideas.title: LLMLingua budget controller can wrap the classifier
ideas.statement: Replacing LLMLingua perplexity-based iterative token compression with LLMLingua-2 while keeping its budget controller allows coarse-to-fine compression for multiple demonstrations or documents, targeting roughly 15x ratios.
ideas.conditions: Depends on LLMLingua coarse selection; separate from standalone task-agnostic token selection.

ideas.title: Encoder variants and main training configuration
ideas.statement: LLMLingua-2 uses XLM-RoBERTa-large and LLMLingua-2-small uses multilingual BERT. Both are fine-tuned for 10 epochs with Adam, learning rate 1e-5, batch size 10, using Transformers/PyTorch 2.0.1/CUDA 11.7.

ideas.title: Default downstream target is deterministic GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613
ideas.statement: Unless otherwise stated, reported downstream results use GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613 with greedy decoding and temperature zero.

ideas.title: MeetingBank preserves QA at about threefold compression
ideas.statement: Table 1 reports LLMLingua-2 QA EM 86.92 at 970 tokens/3.1x, small 85.82 at 984/3.0x, versus original 87.75 at 3003, Selective-Context 66.28 at 1222/2.5x and LLMLingua 67.52 at 1176/2.5x.
ideas.conditions: MeetingBank test, GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613; synthetic QA references.
validity_flags: No uncertainty intervals shown; realized lengths differ

ideas.title: MeetingBank summary metrics differ from QA preservation
ideas.statement: At Table 1 settings, LLMLingua-2 summary BLEU/Rouge1/Rouge2/RougeL/BERTScore are 17.37/48.64/22.96/34.24/88.27; small gives 17.41/48.33/23.07/34.36/88.77, versus original 22.34/47.28/26.66/35.15/88.96.
ideas.conditions: MeetingBank summarization, GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613.

ideas.title: Five benchmark groups test in- and out-of-domain compression
ideas.statement: MeetingBank test supplies in-domain summary and QA evaluation (QA exact match); LongBench and ZeroSCROLLS cover long contexts; GSM8K and BBH cover reasoning/in-context learning with metrics inherited from LLMLingua/LongLLMLingua.

ideas.title: Primary comparison uses LLaMA-2-7B compressors
ideas.statement: Selective-Context and LLMLingua both use LLaMA-2-7B as primary task-agnostic baselines; task-aware comparisons include retrieval methods and LongLLMLingua. Dagger-marked table values are reported from Jiang et al. 2023b.

ideas.title: LongBench under 2000-token constraint
ideas.statement: LongBench average score: LLMLingua-2 39.1 at 1954 tokens; small 38.2 at 1891; LLMLingua 34.6 at 1950; Selective-Context 24.8 at 1925; question-aware LongLLMLingua 48.0 at 1809; original 44.0 at 10295.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613; constraints are nominal and realized token counts differ; prior-baseline values from Jiang et al. 2023b.
validity_flags: LongLLMLingua has question information unavailable to task-agnostic compressors

ideas.title: LongBench under 3000-token constraint
ideas.statement: LongBench average score: LLMLingua-2 42.4 at 3392 tokens; small 41.9 at 3278; LLMLingua 37.4 at 3421; Selective-Context 32.0 at 3328; question-aware LongLLMLingua 48.8 at 3283; original 44.0 at 10295.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613; constraints are nominal and realized token counts differ; prior-baseline values from Jiang et al. 2023b.
validity_flags: LongLLMLingua has question information unavailable to task-agnostic compressors

ideas.title: LongBench averages hide task-specific strengths and weaknesses
ideas.statement: At 2000-token constraint, LLMLingua-2 scores SingleDoc/MultiDoc/Summary/FewShot/Synthetic/Code=29.8/33.1/25.3/66.4/21.3/58.9; at 3000=35.5/38.7/26.3/69.6/21.4/62.8. Original=39.7/38.7/26.5/67.0/37.8/54.2. Code and sometimes few-shot improve while SingleDoc and synthetic decline.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613; same 6 task categories in displayed order.
validity_flags: Do not interpret average improvement as winning every task

ideas.title: ZeroSCROLLS average nearly preserved at reduced length
ideas.statement: At 2000-token constraint, LLMLingua-2/small/LLMLingua/Selective-Context/LongLLMLingua score 33.4/33.3/27.2/19.4/32.5; at 3000 they score 33.5/33.4/30.7/20.7/32.8. Original scores 34.7 at 9788 tokens; LLMLingua-2 uses 1898 and 3206 tokens.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613; dagger values drawn from Jiang et al. 2023b.

ideas.title: GSM8K demonstrations compress to 5x–14x with similar EM
ideas.statement: LLMLingua-2 gives GSM8K EM79.08 at 457 tokens/5x one-shot constraint and 77.79 at 178/14x half-shot. Small gives 78.92/77.48; LLMLingua79.08/77.41; Selective-Context53.98/52.99. Full-shot78.85 uses2366 tokens; zero-shot48.75 uses11.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613, compressed in-context reasoning examples.
validity_flags: Small decimal differences lack uncertainty estimates

ideas.title: BBH supports moderate compression but half-shot hurts EM
ideas.statement: LLMLingua-2 BBH EM70.02 at269 tokens/3x one-shot and61.94 at176/5x half-shot; small69.54/60.35; LLMLingua70.11/61.60; Selective-Context54.27/54.02. Full-shot70.07 uses774 tokens; zero-shot32.32 uses16.
ideas.conditions: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0613.
validity_flags: Results show a quality/compression tradeoff; no uncertainty intervals

ideas.title: Compressed MeetingBank prompts outperform originals for Mistral-7B
ideas.statement: Mistral-7B-v0.1 Table 4 MeetingBank QA/Rouge1: LLMLingua-2 76.22/30.18 (970 tokens), small75.97/29.93 (984), Selective-Context58.13/26.84 (1222), LLMLingua50.45/23.63 (1176), original66.95/26.26 (3003).
validity_flags: Long-context limitations may confound comparison; restricted subset later in Table 13

ideas.title: Mistral-7B SingleDoc QA improves with LLMLingua-2 compression
ideas.statement: For Mistral-7B, LLMLingua-2 LongBench SingleDoc score is26.8 at1967 tokens/7.4x and27.3 at2853/5.1x; small25.3 at1949 and27.9 at2888; original24.5 at14511. Selective-Context22.0/26.0 and LLMLingua19.5/20.8 are lower at these budgets.
validity_flags: Inputs can exceed target model training context length; Table 13 controls to <=8K

ideas.title: Task-agnostic LLMLingua-2 trails LongLLMLingua on LongBench
ideas.statement: The paper acknowledges weaker LongBench performance than question-aware LongLLMLingua and attributes the gap to question information, while emphasizing reuse and generalization.
validity_flags: Prose citation year-letter differs from bibliography mapping; LongLLMLingua is Jiang2023b
Attribution of gap is not isolated by a controlled causal test

ideas.title: LLMLingua-2 lowers measured compressor latency
ideas.statement: On MeetingBank with a V100-32G GPU at2x/3x/5x ratios, LLMLingua-2 compressor latency is0.5/0.4/0.4 seconds, LLMLingua2.9/2.1/1.5, and Selective-Context15.9/15.6/15.5.
ideas.conditions: Paper hardware and workload; does not establish hardware-independent speedups.

ideas.title: End-to-end compression speedups are workload-dependent
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports uncompressed end-to-end latency14.9s and LLMLingua-2 end-to-end9.4/7.5/5.2s at2x/3x/5x, labeled1.6x/2.1x/2.9x speedups.
ideas.conditions: MeetingBank; V100-32G GPU; default target conditions unless specified.
validity_flags: Printed 2.1x at3x is not exactly 14.9/7.5 (~1.99); rounding or measurement basis unexplained

ideas.title: GPT-4 reconstruction examples are qualitative information-preservation evidence
ideas.statement: The authors prompt GPT-4 to reconstruct source from compressed prompts and claim close reconstructions suggest no essential information loss; Figures7–8 provide two examples.
validity_flags: Selected qualitative reconstructions do not prove lossless compression or exclude LLM prior-based reconstruction

ideas.title: Instruction plus chunking improves QA while reducing variation
ideas.statement: Table7 LongBench SingleDoc QA shows full LLMLingua-2 instruction/chunking ratio2.6x,VR2.2,QAF1 36.7; without chunking21x,6.0,27.9. Four prior instructions yield (ratio,VR,F1): (123x,13.7,19.1),(27x,7.8,26.1),(78x,9.6,23.7),(49x,9.4,24.9).
validity_flags: Ratios differ substantially, so this is not equal-budget isolation of instruction quality

ideas.title: MeetingBank-only training limits generalization evidence
ideas.statement: The main compression training dataset contains only MeetingBank transcripts; out-of-domain tests provide evidence for transfer but do not establish universal domain generalization.

ideas.title: Adding 50K TriviaQA examples yields modest benchmark gains
ideas.statement: After adding50K TriviaQA-wiki examples, the 2000-token LLMLingua-2 LongBench average rises39.1→39.5 and ZeroSCROLLS stays33.4. LongBench categories change29.8/33.1/25.3/66.4/21.3/58.9→30.7/33.9/25.4/66.6/22.6/58.1; code decreases.
validity_flags: No uncertainty intervals; realized budgets vary

ideas.title: Shared redundancy patterns may explain cross-domain transfer
ideas.statement: The authors conjecture that redundancy patterns are similar across semantically different domains and can transfer from in-domain training; testing this mechanism remains future work.
validity_flags: Explicit conjecture, not a demonstrated mechanism

ideas.title: GPT-4-32k distillation settings
ideas.statement: Appendix A uses GPT-4-32k, temperature0.3, top_p1.0 and maximum4096 generated tokens; complete-sentence chunks do not exceed512 tokens. It also states transcripts exceeding28K tokens are truncated to reserve4K output tokens.
validity_flags: Order/interaction of 28K transcript truncation and512-token chunking is not fully specified

ideas.title: MeetingBank compression dataset statistics
ideas.statement: Table8 contains5169 original/compressed example pairs and41746 chunks. Mean sentence count falls232→132, mean tokens3635→1415, for reported2.57x compression.
ideas.conditions: Statistics as reported; filtering stage relative to this table is not specified.

ideas.title: Lemmatization and local windows handle GPT-4 word changes
ideas.statement: Before sliding-window matching, spaCy lemmatization reduces tense/voice/number variants to base forms. A local bidirectional window addresses reordered words, repeated occurrences, and limits mismatching newly introduced words.
validity_flags: No numeric window-size value specified in the paper

ideas.title: Qualitative ratio examples preserve selected salient words
ideas.statement: Figure6 colors words retained at2x,3x,5x on two meeting examples. At higher ratios, retained material emphasizes program names, Alex Mitchell, project quantities/money, and project/timeline/extend content while many fillers disappear.
validity_flags: Two selected qualitative examples; no independent context-awareness metric or ablation

ideas.title: Reconstruction prompts GPT-4 with compressed transcript
ideas.statement: For Figures7–8, GPT-4 is told the transcript was compressed by dropping words and asked to reconstruct the original based on the compressed transcript.

ideas.title: Synthetic MeetingBank QA evaluation references
ideas.statement: The evaluation uses862 MeetingBank test transcripts. GPT-4-32K generates10 short question-answer pairs per transcript; answers over50 tokens are discarded and remaining pairs examined for source-present answers, retaining3 pairs per transcript.
validity_flags: Synthetic QA; checking process and annotator agreement not reported

ideas.title: GPT-4 summaries serve as evaluation ground truth
ideas.statement: MeetingBank summary evaluation compares against GPT-4-32K generated summaries, which the paper calls ground truth.
validity_flags: LLM-generated reference summaries; not independently established truth

ideas.title: Two MeetingBank reconstruction examples retain broad content
ideas.statement: Figure7 shows original200 tokens→compressed98→reconstructed198; Figure8 shows160→83→123. Both are labeled2x compression and retain much of the meeting subject matter.
validity_flags: Qualitative author-selected examples; no quantitative fidelity metric

ideas.title: Displayed reconstruction can change specific factual relations
ideas.statement: Inspection of Figure7 shows reconstructed wording adds a CNN representative, changes program duration into the speaker’s tenure, and interprets fragmented20/28-county text as20 out of28 counties. These changes qualify the paper’s claim of reconstruction without essential information loss.
validity_flags: Extractor-observed evidence limitation; no external factual verification
Transcript disfluency makes intended original semantics partly ambiguous

ideas.title: Distillation system prompt frames expert deletion-based compression
ideas.statement: Figure9 adds a system prompt casting GPT-4 as a linguist good at shortening passages by removing unimportant words while retaining information, followed by the five-condition user instruction.

ideas.title: Four prior GPT-4 compression prompts tested in ablation
ideas.statement: Figure10 attributes four instructions to LLMLingua: rephrase to5% tokens; summarize reasoning in a few sentences; remove redundancy while retaining key information/reasoning; or first remove low-information sentences then stopwords/punctuation/redundant expressions step by step.

ideas.title: Reported encoder sizes and training time
ideas.statement: Appendix H reports XLM-RoBERTa-large355M parameters and about23h training for LLMLingua-2; multilingual BERT110M and about16h for LLMLingua-2-small.
validity_flags: Parameter counts and time are source-reported; no external model-metadata verification
Training hardware is not specified in Appendix H

ideas.title: Measured peak memory is lower with the small classifier
ideas.statement: Appendix I reports MeetingBank peak GPU memory2.1GB for LLMLingua-2,16.6GB for LLMLingua and26.5GB for Selective-Context, the latter two using LLaMA-2-7B.
ideas.conditions: Source workload; batching and peak-measurement details not specified in this paragraph.

ideas.title: Multilingual pretraining is proposed to explain Chinese transfer
ideas.statement: English-only MeetingBank training is evaluated on1000 Chinese LongBench samples across5 tasks; the authors attribute transfer gains to encoder multilingual capabilities acquired in pretraining.
validity_flags: Mechanistic attribution is not established by an ablation

ideas.title: Question-aware coarse budgets augment LLMLingua-2
ideas.statement: LLMLingua-2+ uses LongLLMLingua coarse-grained compression to allocate document-specific ratios according to question perplexity conditioned on each document, giving more tokens to more relevant documents.
ideas.conditions: RAG or multidocument QA; this extension is question-aware.

ideas.title: Corpus-wide threshold creates sample-specific compression rates
ideas.statement: Rather than a fixed rate for every sample, LLMLingua-2 can score all corpus tokens, set one preservation-probability threshold satisfying the overall compression constraint, and retain above-threshold tokens in each sample.
ideas.conditions: Requires access to scores across the corpus; different samples receive different rates.

ideas.title: BBH example retains words but corrupts an arithmetic expression
ideas.statement: Figure11 compares original139 tokens, LLMLingua57, and LLMLingua-2 54 for counting six fruits. LLMLingua-2 keeps fruit names and the final answer6 with fewer malformed words than LLMLingua, yet displays1+1=6 after deletion.
validity_flags: Source-only deletion can corrupt equations or remove question content; not a semantic-faithfulness guarantee

ideas.title: Dataset-level learning may smooth individual teacher errors
ideas.statement: The authors conjecture LLMLingua-2 outperforms individual GPT-4 compressions because learning across the dataset mitigates teacher noise and information loss.
validity_flags: Author conjecture; no direct denoising mechanism test

ideas.title: GSM8K example preserves legible arithmetic but inherits source error
ideas.statement: Figure12 compares a249-token highlighter-pen example with LLMLingua144 and LLMLingua-2 138 tokens. LLMLingua-2 retains more legible equations and the displayed answer115, unlike many fragmented baseline words.
validity_flags: Displayed source reasoning incorrectly treats five30-pen boxes as30 pens; preserving source reasoning does not establish mathematical correctness

ideas.title: Learned classifier outperforms direct GPT-4 compression on MeetingBank QA
ideas.statement: Table9 direct GPT-4 compression achieves84.86 EM at1221 tokens/2.5x; LLMLingua-2-small85.82 at984/3.0x; LLMLingua-2 86.92 at970/3.1x; original87.75 at3003. GPT-4 uses the same teacher instruction and512-token chunking.
ideas.conditions: MeetingBank QA with default GPT-3.5 downstream target.
validity_flags: Different realized lengths; no uncertainty intervals

ideas.title: Evaluate shorter original prompts to control Mistral context length
ideas.statement: Because the Mistral target was trained with an8K context length, Appendix P restricts an additional evaluation to original prompts shorter than8K tokens to check whether benefits persist.
validity_flags: Prose says shorter than8K; Table13 says discards more than8K; boundary treatment is not fully specified

ideas.title: SentComp example drops answer-bearing province details
ideas.statement: Figure13 colors the retained generic Chinese museum opening statement blue but the answer-bearing province/region list red; the retained compressed text cannot answer the displayed question about museums above county level.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative source example, not an aggregate SentComp evaluation.

ideas.title: DebateSum example drops answer-bearing industry details
ideas.statement: Figure14 shows extractive summary text about uncertainty and trade while red omitted text lists clothing except fur, textile/leather machinery, and textile yarn/thread needed for the displayed textile-industry question.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative source example, not an aggregate DebateSum evaluation.

ideas.title: Global-then-local timestamped compressed sequence
ideas.statement: For frame i, Hframe^(i)=[Te^(i),Hevent^(i)] contains one timestamp plus E event tokens. The final representation Hfinal=[Hscene,Hframe^(1),…,Hframe^(N)] has S+N(1+E) tokens and dimension B×(S+N(1+E))×D.
ideas.conditions: Maintains explicit scene/event hierarchy and temporal markers; this is a task-oriented lossy representation.

ideas.title: English-trained compressor transfers to Chinese LongBench
ideas.statement: Table10 at about5x: LLMLingua-2 average38.1 at3023 tokens versus LLMLingua28.6 at3060 and original42.5 at14940. LLMLingua-2 SingleDoc/MultiDoc/Summary/FewShot/Synthetic scores46.7/23.0/15.3/32.8/72.6 versus baseline35.2/20.4/11.8/24.3/51.4; original61.2/28.7/16.0/29.2/77.5.
ideas.conditions: 1000 Chinese samples across5 tasks; compressor trained on English MeetingBank.
validity_flags: No uncertainty intervals; improves all categories versus LLMLingua but only FewShot versus original

ideas.title: MeetingBank QA degrades more slowly across ratios
ideas.statement: Figure15a on100 MeetingBank examples shows LLMLingua-2 above Selective-Context and LLMLingua for tested ratios2x–10x. At10x its EM is about40 versus about17 and11 respectively; all start near86 at1x.
ideas.conditions: 100-sample subset; approximate visual values only.
validity_flags: No error bars; subset selection unspecified

ideas.title: Summary quality is more robust under LLMLingua-2 compression
ideas.statement: Figure15b on100 MeetingBank samples shows LLMLingua-2 Rouge1 stays about41.5 at10x versus Selective-Context34 and LLMLingua28.2; its curve briefly exceeds its1x score at2x–4x.
ideas.conditions: Approximate plot readout on100-sample MeetingBank subset.
validity_flags: No error bars; visual trend does not prove beneficial compression generally

ideas.title: LongLLMLingua budgets improve LLMLingua-2 across answer positions
ideas.statement: Table11 NaturalQuestions20-document4x target: LLMLingua-2 scores48.6/44.5/43.6/40.9/39.9 for answer positions1st/5th/10th/15th/20th and46.2 after reorder; LLMLingua-2+ scores74.0/70.4/67.0/66.9/65.3 and71.9, using739 versus748 tokens. The mean gain is about25.3 score points.
ideas.conditions: LLMLingua-2+ adds question-aware document budgets; nominal4x and realized3.9x.
validity_flags: Prose percent wording is ambiguous; values imply absolute-score-point improvement

ideas.title: Question-aware LongLLMLingua remains strongest in Table11
ideas.statement: At NaturalQuestions20-doc4x settings, LongLLMLingua scores75.0/71.8/71.2/71.2/74.7/reorder75.5, above LLMLingua-2+ in all six columns. Original answer-position scores75.7/57.3/54.1/55.4/63.1 use2946 tokens; zero-shot scores56.1 using15.
ideas.conditions: Prior dagger-marked baseline values reported from Jiang2023b.
validity_flags: Question-aware and task-agnostic methods have different inputs

ideas.title: Dynamic sample rates outperform fixed rates under corpus constraints
ideas.statement: Table12 LongBench SingleDoc: at nominal7x, fixed25.1 at2131 tokens/6.8x versus dynamic29.5 at2125/6.8x; at nominal5x, fixed27.4 at3185/4.5x versus dynamic32.2 at3164/4.5x. Absolute gains are4.4 and4.8 points.
validity_flags: Prose reports4.5% for second setting, conflicting with displayed32.2−27.4=4.8 points; retain table values.

ideas.title: Per-sample token targets differ from corpus rate constraints
ideas.statement: Table12 token-target LLMLingua-2 scores29.8 at1954 tokens/7.4x for2000 target and35.5 at3392/4.3x for3000 target; these are different budgeting conditions from fixed/dynamic corpus-rate variants and original39.7 at14511.
validity_flags: Budgeting regimes should not be conflated; realized targets differ

ideas.title: GPT-4 compressed text increases noun, adjective and numeral shares
ideas.statement: Figure16 shows higher relative frequencies after compression for NN,NNP,NNS,JJ andCD, and lower shares for determiners, pronouns, prepositions and several function-word categories. The authors infer priority for nouns, adjectives and numerals.
ideas.conditions: Word-category distribution of original and GPT-4-compressed prompts; visual values approximate.
validity_flags: Relative category composition is not directly a per-token preservation probability or causal measure of importance

ideas.title: A 53x example illustrates late-text corruption
ideas.statement: Figure 4(e) presents a 1701-token source compressed into 32 latent tokens (labelled 53x), with a reconstruction that begins similarly but shows substantial corrupted text later.
ideas.conditions: One red-bordered failure case, outside the 600-1300-token quantitative test range; no 53x aggregate precision is reported.

ideas.title: LongMemEval multi-event earnings illustration
ideas.statement: Figures 11–12 present twenty QA pairs, including three relevant sale amounts: $225 jam, $150 potted herbs and $120 fresh herbs. The model reports $225+$150+$120=$495, matching the labeled amount. Other displayed memories concern dates, gift baskets, pricing, market trends, promotions, products and herb handling, illustrating substantial distractor material.
ideas.conditions: Single illustrative LongMemEval case, not standalone factual advice or broad performance evidence.
validity_flags: Arithmetic answer is semantically correct but differs from bare labeled amount under literal normalized EM.

ideas.title: Causal next-token training is a mismatch for holistic embeddings
ideas.statement: The paper motivates adaptation by arguing that causal attention and next-token prediction do not directly optimize holistic sequence representations.
validity_flags: Motivating argument, not a universal impossibility result.

ideas.title: LLM2Vec bidirectional MNTP adaptation
ideas.statement: LLM2Vec converts causal attention to bidirectional attention and uses masked next-token prediction, predicting masked tokens from contextual preceding-token representations.

ideas.title: CCL-Bench geographic coverage and urban concentration
ideas.statement: CCL-Bench reports 30 of 34 provincial-level regions (88.24%), 93.75% mainland coverage, 35.84% city-level coverage, and about 34.00% of images from first-tier/new first-tier cities.
ideas.conditions: Descriptive statistics for the 300-image China benchmark.
validity_flags: City-level coverage denominator and geographic representativeness assessment are not specified; regional coverage does not by itself establish global generalization.

ideas.title: Manual locatable-clue and difficulty annotations
ideas.statement: CCL-Bench manually annotates natural environment, infrastructure, transportation, and cultural/symbolic clues; clue density and distinctiveness determine Easy, Medium, or Hard difficulty strata.

ideas.title: Four scene classes span scale and clue density
ideas.statement: CCL-Bench defines rural scenes with sparse natural and human traces; information-dense urban scenes; aerial/distant views emphasizing layouts, skylines and landmarks; and close-up shots of buildings, textures or decorative details.
ideas.conditions: China-focused, user-captured internet imagery.

ideas.title: Reconstruction findings do not establish downstream ultra-long-context performance
ideas.statement: The work explicitly limits its current investigation to text reconstruction, so proposed long-context QA, summarization and analysis applications remain untested within this paper.
ideas.conditions: Quantitative evidence is Fox English documents of 600-1300 source tokens; qualitative evidence includes English/Chinese examples and one 1701-token failure.

ideas.title: Use the C3 autoencoder for latent-space language generation
ideas.statement: The authors propose using C3 to encode variable-length text into fixed-length latent tokens and decode it, as an autoencoder component for diffusion language models and latent autoregressive models.
ideas.conditions: Proposed reuse; neither generative framework is implemented or evaluated here.

ideas.title: Cascade a lightweight VLM with an LLM for multimodal compression
ideas.statement: A proposed extension replaces or expands the text compressor with a lightweight VLM coupled to an LLM for visually rich documents, multiple images and videos.
ideas.conditions: Future direction aimed at lower long-context costs; no multimodal cascade experiment in this report.

ideas.title: Prometheus detector simulation chain
ideas.statement: Prometheus [21] uses LeptonInjector [22] with deep-inelastic cross-section tables [23] to generate interactions around an IceCube-like detector. PROPOSAL [17] models charged-lepton energy loss, an internal module computes hadronic-cascade light yield, and Photon Propagation Code transports photons to sensors, yielding arrival-time series.
ideas.conditions: Only charged-current interactions are encoded in this work; neutral-current extension is proposed, not demonstrated.

ideas.title: Reduce sensor photon series to count and mean arrival time
ideas.statement: Because sensors near the detector can receive many photons, the simulation output used for encoding summarizes each sensor by {x,y,z,q_tot,t̄}, retaining total photon count and mean arrival time instead of the full time series.
ideas.conditions: The main encoding converts positions to spherical coordinates about the charge-weighted event center; temporal distribution details are omitted by this summary.

ideas.title: Deterministic ordering of context observables
ideas.statement: For even n, each base context has 2^(n−1)+1 observables, ordered with Z^{⊗n} first and then alphabetically ordered X/Y products of the chosen X-count parity; index i ranges from 0 through 2^(n−1).
ideas.conditions: Even n; context order is preserved under later rotations.

ideas.title: Generator identifies distinct rotated contexts for even n at least four
ideas.statement: For n≥4 in the even-n construction, each rotated even context has a unique generator C^even_β(0): it shares no same-position Pauli factor with any other observable in the context, and its identity fixes β. The same applies to odd contexts, yielding distinct even/odd context families.
ideas.conditions: Uniqueness statement cites Ref. [14]. No overlap refers to distinct context sets, not disjoint observable membership.

ideas.title: Prompted autoregressive reconstruction from compressed context
ideas.statement: The decoder receives latent context concatenated with the task prompt "repeat the text: " and is trained to autoregressively reproduce the original ground-truth token sequence.
ideas.conditions: Only text reconstruction is investigated, as a benchmark for preservation across compression and decompression.

ideas.title: Python loop limits current throughput and kernel improvements remain prospective
ideas.statement: The author attributes approximately22tokens/s decode throughput to a Python-level loop and proposes a fused kernel to close the gap to Transformer peak speed.
ideas.conditions: No fused-kernel implementation or performance measurement is provided, so closing the gap remains an expectation.
validity_flags: Causal bottleneck diagnosis and speed parity prediction are not supported by profiling or fused-kernel tests.

ideas.title: S=8 reduction does not match the stated formula
ideas.statement: Table 4 reports 93.38% reduction for S=8,E=32, but Eq.13 with N=1.836,Dv=384 gives about 90.53%. The paper does not explain this discrepancy; the reported S=8 performance should not be paired with 93.38% as a verified reduction.
ideas.conditions: Recalculation of printed formula; not a corrected experimental measurement.

ideas.title: Public-dataset annotation statistics
