ideas.statement: Table 5 lists (#videos,chapters/video,answer chars/video,answer chars/s): YouCook2 (2K,7.7,67.7 en,0.21); ActivityNet (20K,3.7,47.6 en,0.40); Charades-STA (10K,1.8,11.0 en,0.36); ViTT (8K,5.0,110.5 en,0.44); VideoStory (20K,6.1,unreported,unreported); Video Storytelling (105,13.5,162.6 en,0.22); E-SyncVidStory (6K,6.9,194.1 zh,5.21). None has Think statistics in this table.
ideas.conditions: These are the paper’s reported dataset statistics, not independently reconciled dataset facts. Different languages and protocols limit direct length comparison.

ideas.title: Main and supplementary token accounting differ
ideas.statement: Main Eq.12 gives S+N(1+E) tokens for a global scene prefix over frames, whereas supplement Eq.13 assigns S+N·E visual tokens to every ASR segment. The supplement also names Dv a token dimensionality while using it as a token-count denominator; timestamps and other inputs are omitted. Thus 82.59% should be retained as the authors’ conditional visual-token calculation, not a verified total-context or compute reduction.
ideas.conditions: Internal source-accounting discrepancy; actual implementation and tokenizer outputs have not been inspected.

ideas.title: Small encoder and larger decoder connected by latent context
ideas.statement: C3 cascades two differently sized LLMs: a small encoder converts variable-length text into a fixed set of latent tokens, and a larger decoder consumes those tokens to perform a downstream task.
ideas.conditions: This paper evaluates reconstruction of the original input, using latent lengths such as 32, 64, and 100.

ideas.title: Clifford conjugation cycles Pauli operators
ideas.statement: Conjugating by Γ1 maps X→Y→Z→X; Γ2=Γ1† gives the reverse cycle X→Z→Y→X. Tensor-product Γβ, whose index has n base-3 digits, defines C^s_β=Γβ C^s_0 Γβ† without changing observable order.

ideas.title: Advanced RL for varied forms of context condensation
ideas.statement: The conclusion identifies complex knowledge graphs and the range of ways to condense contexts as motivations to investigate more advanced reinforcement-learning models and integration methods.
ideas.conditions: Author-stated future work; no advanced model or condensation strategy is evaluated.

ideas.title: Bellman optimality target for graph-integration Q values
ideas.statement: Equation (1) states Q*(s,a) = E[R_(t+1) + γ max_(a′) Q*(S_(t+1),a′) | S_t=s, A_t=a]. R_(t+1) is the immediate reward, γ discounts future rewards, and the maximum selects the highest-valued next-state action.
ideas.conditions: Presented as standard Q-learning background; no theorem establishes convergence or optimality for the proposed compressed-state KG setting.

ideas.title: Condensed contexts requiring knowledge graph integration
ideas.statement: Contexts are brief or condensed representations of information that require expansion, inclusion, or linkage within an existing knowledge graph. Their condensation may introduce ambiguity and information loss.
ideas.conditions: This paper uses context compression as a KG integration problem; it does not define a prompt-token budget or provide an explicit compression algorithm.
validity_flags: Condensation is described conceptually without an operational definition or measured compression ratio.

ideas.title: Neural approximation of the action-value function
ideas.statement: The DQN represents Q(s,a;θ) using input, hidden, and output layers and learns network parameters θ to approximate the optimal action-value function Q*(s,a).
ideas.conditions: Only generic layer types are given; sizes, activations, inputs to each layer, and architecture tuning are absent.
validity_flags: Standard DQN description; the paper does not substantiate a distinct network architecture.

ideas.title: DQN framework for context integration into knowledge graphs
ideas.statement: The proposed framework casts a knowledge graph as the environment, context-integration operations as actions, and post-integration graph-quality improvements as rewards; a DQN agent learns integration strategies with the aim of reducing manual intervention.
ideas.conditions: A conceptual RL formulation for integrating summarized contexts; the source supplies general Q-learning equations but no fully specified implementation.
validity_flags: Claims of a customized implemented DQN are not accompanied by architecture sizes, state embeddings, action-generation details, or exact reward definition.

ideas.title: Squared temporal-difference loss with target network
ideas.statement: Equation (3) trains the DQN by minimizing L(θ) = [r + γ max_(a′) Q(s′,a′;θ⁻) − Q(s,a;θ)]² for a transition. The text states that each training iteration adjusts θ using descent to reduce this loss.
ideas.conditions: A per-transition squared target error is displayed. Batch sampling, replay buffer, optimizer, terminal-state treatment, and training budget are not specified.

ideas.title: RL background for dynamic graph enrichment
ideas.statement: The prior-work discussion frames RL integration as sequential decisions about where and how to add data to improve graph quality and coherence; it mentions entity resolution, relationship prediction, and automated KG construction and expansion as applications.
validity_flags: Broad survey claim with citation [6]; no specific prior implementation or transferred component is identified.

ideas.title: Unspecified framework and preliminary DQN tuning
ideas.statement: The paper says the DQN was implemented in a known learning framework and its design and parameters adjusted after initial testing to support reliability across graph datasets.
ideas.conditions: The framework, selected hyperparameters, search ranges, preliminary-test protocol, and reliability evidence are not identified.
validity_flags: Underspecified experimental configuration; reliability is an author claim without validation details.

ideas.title: Reported FB15k integration accuracy
ideas.statement: Table I reports FB15k integration accuracy of 80% for the rule-based baseline, 85% for supervised learning, and 95% for DQN. Its improvement columns say 15% and 10%; the displayed accuracies imply absolute gains of 15 and 10 percentage points, respectively.
ideas.conditions: Simulated condensed-context integration on FB15k; no operational accuracy definition or error bars.
validity_flags: Author-reported result; unnamed baselines, undefined accuracy/quality measures, missing splits and run counts, and no statistical uncertainty prevent independent validation.
Percent versus percentage-point terminology is ambiguous in source; the extraction distinguishes arithmetic implications from the printed labels.

ideas.title: FB15k benchmark source and role
ideas.statement: The paper selects FB15k, derived from Freebase with diverse entities and relationships, as one benchmark for simulated context integration; it describes link prediction and entity resolution as common uses of this dataset.
ideas.conditions: Dataset description is background; use in this paper is the context-integration evaluation.

ideas.title: Reported FB15k graph-quality index and conflicting prose
ideas.statement: Table III reports FB15k KG Quality Index values of 0.70 for rules, 0.75 for supervised ML, and 0.90 for DQN; reported relative gains are 28.6% over rules and 20% over supervised ML. Figure 2 visually reproduces these values. The prose instead claims a 25% quality improvement without naming a comparator, inconsistent with either table gain.
ideas.conditions: KG Quality Index is named but neither defined nor given a justified numerical range.
validity_flags: Author-reported result; unnamed baselines, undefined accuracy/quality measures, missing splits and run counts, and no statistical uncertainty prevent independent validation.
Unresolved internal numerical contradiction: narrative 25% versus table gains 28.6% and 20%.

ideas.title: Reported FB15k context-integration time
ideas.statement: Table II reports FB15k integration times of 60 seconds for rules, 50 seconds for supervised ML, and 40 seconds for DQN, with respective efficiency gains of 33.3% and 20%. The narrative states a 20% reduction relative to an unnamed method, consistent with the table only when the comparator is supervised ML.
ideas.conditions: No hardware, workload size, training cost, timing boundaries, or run count is specified.
validity_flags: Author-reported result; unnamed baselines, undefined accuracy/quality measures, missing splits and run counts, and no statistical uncertainty prevent independent validation.
Prose comparator is unspecified; 20% is not the reduction relative to the rule-based time.

ideas.title: Policy seeks accumulated integration rewards
ideas.statement: The integration policy π(a|s) chooses an action according to the current graph state, with the objective of maximizing rewards over time.
ideas.conditions: The exploration strategy, horizon, episode boundaries, and policy extraction from Q are not specified.

ideas.title: Entity, relationship, and data-modification actions
ideas.statement: An action a in A is an operation incorporating condensed context into the graph, including introducing entities, introducing relationships, or modifying existing data.
ideas.conditions: The source does not enumerate or parameterize the action space or define validity constraints.
validity_flags: Action selection and construction are underspecified for reproduction.

ideas.title: Fixed-size embedding of knowledge graph state
ideas.statement: A state s in S represents the current graph elements, connections, and contextual details, compressed by embedding methods into a fixed-size vector.
ideas.conditions: The embedding method, vector dimension, graph-size handling, and information-retention behavior are unspecified.
validity_flags: Representation is conceptual; no demonstration that the vector preserves sufficient information or has the Markov property.

ideas.title: Knowledge graph structure and applications
ideas.statement: The paper describes knowledge graphs as structures containing entities, concepts, and their interconnections, supporting semantic search, recommendation, question answering, and natural language understanding.

ideas.title: Temporal-difference update of action values
ideas.statement: Equation (2) updates Q(s,a) ← Q(s,a) + α[r + γ max_(a′) Q(s′,a′) − Q(s,a)], where α is the learning rate, r the reward, and s′ the next state.
ideas.conditions: No values or schedules for α or γ are provided. The prose writes an experience tuple (s,a,r,s) without a prime, whereas the displayed update uses s′.
validity_flags: Next-state notation is inconsistent between displayed equation and surrounding prose; transcription follows the rendered equation.

ideas.title: Qualitative quality distribution in performance-variance figure
ideas.statement: Figure 1 shows KG Quality Index boxplots for Rule Based, Supervised ML, and DQN Based, with approximate medians of 0.69, 0.75, and 0.89. DQN has the highest displayed median and at least one high plotted outlier above 1.0; the figure includes whiskers and low outliers but does not identify the underlying dataset, sample count, or trial construction.
ideas.conditions: Approximate visual reading only; exact quartiles, variance estimates, significance, and provenance cannot be recovered from this plot alone. The source does not define a [0,1] bound for its quality index.
validity_flags: Unexplained empirical distribution and quality-index scale; plotted values above 1 are preserved without assuming they violate an unstated bound.

ideas.title: Reward based on graph-quality improvement
ideas.statement: R(s,a) measures the improvement in knowledge graph quality caused by an integration action. The method cites precision and thoroughness as reward measures; the experiment narrative additionally names accuracy, comprehensiveness, and consistency.
ideas.conditions: No mathematical reward formula, metric weights, ground-truth procedure, or quality-index definition is provided.
validity_flags: Reward and reported quality metric are not operationally defined.

ideas.title: Reinforcement learning through environment interaction
ideas.statement: The source describes reinforcement learning as an agent learning decisions by interacting with an environment; unscripted action selection and flexibility under changing environments motivate its application to knowledge graph context integration.
validity_flags: High-level motivation, not a guarantee of adaptation or optimality.

ideas.title: Rule-based integration and manual curation
ideas.statement: Prior work is characterized as schema-respecting rule-based integration and manual curation. Rules can be precise but lack flexibility; manual curation can preserve quality and relevance but is difficult to scale to large daily data volumes.
validity_flags: Qualitative characterization, without named algorithms or evidence quantified in the prior-work discussion.

ideas.title: CCL-Bench scene mix
ideas.statement: Figure 3(c) shows Rural 29.66%, Urban 32.67%, Aerial/Distant 19.67%, and Close-up 18.00%; the paper describes urban/rural and wide/close views as roughly balanced.

ideas.title: Separate Mapper transforms the goal
ideas.statement: A separate Mapper role applies the generated mapping rule to goal text instead of making the Attacker both propose and apply the rule; the paper reports that the combined Attacker approach was suboptimal.

ideas.title: Simulated condensed-context integration protocol
ideas.statement: The experiments prepare datasets to simulate condensed contexts needing KG updates, run a DQN in a virtual graph environment with merging actions, and evaluate integration accuracy, elapsed time, and resulting graph quality.
ideas.conditions: Reported on FB15k and WN18. No algorithm or compression ratio for creating contexts, data split, sample count, random seed, number of runs, evaluation metric definition, or hardware configuration is given.
validity_flags: Insufficient implementation and experimental reporting to independently reproduce the reported results.

ideas.title: Supervised prediction for knowledge graph enrichment
ideas.statement: The paper describes supervised enrichment models that predict entity connections or classify and connect new data using graph structure, text descriptions, and external references. A stated limitation is the need for substantial labeled training data as knowledge evolves.

ideas.title: Periodically copied target-network parameters
ideas.statement: The source describes a target network whose parameters are periodically copied from the DQN and held fixed over several updates to improve learning stability.
ideas.conditions: Equation (3) labels target-network parameters θ⁻, while the prose repeatedly calls both target and online parameters θ; copy frequency is not reported.
validity_flags: The source notation does not distinguish online and target parameters consistently; the method statement follows the stated copying behavior.

ideas.title: Traditional integration requires rules or labeled data
ideas.statement: The introduction argues that traditional context-integration methods can be rigid under changing data, require human rule definition or labeled-data preparation, and limit time efficiency and scalability.
validity_flags: The introduction incorrectly conflates rule-based approaches with supervised learning models; extraction preserves their shared claimed limitations without treating these classes as identical.

ideas.title: Unspecified rule-based and supervised comparators
ideas.statement: The experiments compare the DQN integration strategy with a rule-based method and an existing supervised learning model, but identify them only by broad method class.
ideas.conditions: The paper does not name baseline implementations, detail their training/tuning, or demonstrate matched compute and data.
validity_flags: Baseline underspecification prevents a reproducible fairness assessment.

ideas.title: Reported WN18 integration accuracy
ideas.statement: Table I reports WN18 integration accuracy of 78% for the rule-based baseline, 82% for supervised learning, and 90% for DQN. Its improvement columns say 12% and 8%; the displayed accuracies imply absolute gains of 12 and 8 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Simulated condensed-context integration on WN18; no operational accuracy definition or error bars.
validity_flags: Author-reported result; unnamed baselines, undefined accuracy/quality measures, missing splits and run counts, and no statistical uncertainty prevent independent validation.
Source labels absolute accuracy differences as percentage improvements.

ideas.title: Use document-specialized visual encoders
ideas.statement: The general-purpose visual encoder is not optimized for dense document text; future work could use document-centric CLIP-style encoders trained on academic/structured text to increase compression without losing fine detail.

ideas.title: WN18 benchmark source and role
ideas.statement: The paper selects WN18, derived from WordNet and focused on semantic connections among concepts, to test whether the integration method adapts across different knowledge graph structures.
ideas.conditions: Dataset description is background; no domain-transfer training/test protocol is specified.

ideas.title: Reported WN18 graph-quality index and conflicting prose
ideas.statement: Table III reports WN18 KG Quality Index values of 0.68 for rules, 0.73 for supervised ML, and 0.88 for DQN; reported relative gains are 29.4% over rules and 20.5% over supervised ML. Figure 2 visually reproduces these values. The prose instead claims 22% quality improvement without naming a comparator, inconsistent with either table gain.
ideas.conditions: KG Quality Index is named but neither defined nor given a justified numerical range.
validity_flags: Author-reported result; unnamed baselines, undefined accuracy/quality measures, missing splits and run counts, and no statistical uncertainty prevent independent validation.
Unresolved internal numerical contradiction: narrative 22% versus table gains 29.4% and 20.5%.

ideas.title: Reported WN18 context-integration time and conflicting prose
ideas.statement: Table II reports WN18 integration times of 65 seconds for rules, 55 seconds for supervised ML, and 43 seconds for DQN, with efficiency gains of 33.8% and 21.8%. The main-result prose instead reports an 18% time reduction against an unspecified method, which does not match either table comparison.
ideas.conditions: No hardware, workload size, training cost, timing boundaries, or run count is specified.
validity_flags: Author-reported result; unnamed baselines, undefined accuracy/quality measures, missing splits and run counts, and no statistical uncertainty prevent independent validation.
Unresolved internal numerical contradiction: narrative 18% versus table gains 33.8% and 21.8%.

ideas.title: Distinct event and chapter timelines
ideas.statement: The worked jacket-video annotation illustrates event intervals that are finer than chapter intervals; chapter captions and titles share boundaries, and several event observations can be composed into one chapter.

ideas.title: Annotation filtering and manual benchmark checks
ideas.statement: Training examples with excessively short or long chapter durations are filtered by rules; E-HVC-Bench receives manual checks of temporal segmentation and chapter boundaries.

ideas.title: HiVid-Narrator architecture and input routing
ideas.statement: Figure 3 routes system prompt tokens directly to the LLM, while vision, ASR and encoded timestamps feed the compression path; the LLM receives scene context followed by timestamped event context.
ideas.conditions: Figure and equations clarify routing; Figure 3 caption loosely says four inputs are compressed, so it should not be read as compressing the system prompt.

ideas.title: Domain-aware ASR filtering and correction
ideas.statement: Whisper-V3-Large transcribes audio; Qwen3-32B scores e-commerce relevance/quality from 0 to 5 with threshold 4, using few-shot prompts; Qwen-Plus corrects the initial transcript using JSON video metadata and structured product attributes.
ideas.conditions: Addresses noisy music, accents, rapid speech, brand/model names and domain language; threshold inequality is not explicitly specified.

ideas.title: FDM separates recurrent compression from selective token retrieval
ideas.statement: The Fan Duality Model combines a wave component that compresses long-range patterns in a fixed-size complex hidden state using phase-preserving Givens rotations with a particle component using learned associative addressing in a local-global cache.
ideas.conditions: The design fixes local window W=256 and global capacity K=16 independently of sequence length N.

ideas.title: Wave-particle deadlock proposition attributed to Fan 2026
ideas.statement: The paper restates the proposition that no linear operator A on C^(D×D) can both preserve the norm of every h and strongly decrease the norm of some h*. It uses this incompatibility to motivate separate propagation and retrieval components.
ideas.conditions: The proposition concerns one fixed linear operator; it does not establish an impossibility theorem for nonlinear, gated, or time-varying sequence systems. Primary metadata verifies the Fan2026 bibliography title as arXiv2604.07716v1, the earlier version of this same paper; no external predecessor nomination is made.
validity_flags: The incompatible norm conditions are definitional; no general lower bound on recurrent-model recall is proven.

ideas.title: Transformer memory bottleneck as motivating comparison
ideas.statement: The introduction motivates FDM with quadratic Transformer attention and claims 4,247 MB for KV cache alone at N=8,192 for a 137M-parameter model.
ideas.conditions: This introductory description differs from the experimental setup, which calls the Transformer 122M parameters and labels the same 4,247 MB figure decode memory.
validity_flags: Internal parameter-count and memory-scope inconsistency: introductory 137M/KV-cache-only versus experimental 122M/decode memory.

ideas.title: Joint optimization is hypothesized to starve the cache of gradient
ideas.statement: The author proposes that joint optimization creates a gradient sink in scan parameters, undertraining the cache, and that freezing the wave parameters redirects learning through the cache circuit.
ideas.conditions: The paper infers this mechanism from improved perplexity; it supplies no direct gradient-flow measurement or induction-head causal test.
validity_flags: Proposed optimization mechanism, not directly established by the presented measurements.

ideas.title: Linear sequence models compress history into recurrent state
ideas.statement: The paper groups S4, Mamba, Mamba-2, RWKV, and RetNet as sequence models with O(1) inference memory through recurrent state compression, and positions FDM as an extension with explicit wave-particle separation and Freeze-Scan.
ideas.conditions: O(1) is with respect to sequence length for a fixed model/state size; these systems are discussed as related work rather than experimentally benchmarked.

ideas.title: Associative recall and induction heads motivate the cache
ideas.statement: The paper cites Based for the MQAR benchmark and difficulty of in-context recall in linear models, and cites Transformer induction heads as an analogue for the associations it seeks to learn in FDM.
ideas.conditions: The statement that Based introduces MQAR is the source author’s attribution; the extraction does not independently establish benchmark priority.
validity_flags: Benchmark-priority attribution is not independently established; induction-head analogy is conceptual.

ideas.title: Efficiency as minimizing target queries
ideas.statement: Efficiency is motivated by computational and financial costs of LLM queries, and the proposed optimization tries to improve the prompt before querying the target.

ideas.title: Learned cache selection is contrasted with post-hoc KV compression
ideas.statement: The author contrasts FDM’s end-to-end learned s_eff token selection with H2O and StreamingLLM, which the paper characterizes as post-hoc KV cache compression.
ideas.conditions: These are contextual comparisons; no H2O or StreamingLLM empirical baseline is reported.

ideas.title: Local-global cache borrows a local-window and global-token pattern
ideas.statement: The paper cites Longformer and BigBird for combining local windows and global tokens in full attention, and states that FDM implements this pattern in a linear RNN using O(W+K) memory.
ideas.conditions: This is an explicit design relationship; it is not a claim of algorithmic equivalence to either prior model.

ideas.title: Fan recurrent operator combines rotation, retention, and complex injection
ideas.statement: The recurrence is h_t=(1−p_t)⊙R(θ_t)h_(t−1)+p_t⊙(W_r x_t+iW_i x_t), with h_t∈C^D. R comprises n_G norm-preserving Givens rotations.
ideas.conditions: Norm preservation applies to R alone; the complete gated recurrence includes attenuation and input injection.
validity_flags: The number n_G of rotations and detailed parameterization are not specified in the six-page paper.

ideas.title: Measurement probability uses learned logarithmic and sinusoidal positional terms
ideas.statement: The score is s_eff(t)=β_t log(t+2)+W_pos[sin(πt/T),cos(πt/T)]^T, and p_t=0.5σ(s_eff(t)+μ)+ε. The author interprets the logarithmic term as renormalization-group running, intended to preserve early wave coherence and allow later information injection; smooth scaling replaces hard clipping to retain gradients.
ideas.conditions: The text claims p_t∈(0,0.5], although positive ε would instead shift the logistic range upward. β_t, μ, ε, and T are not fully specified, and the learned positional terms do not alone guarantee a monotonic measurement rate.
validity_flags: Potential inconsistency between stated probability interval and additive ε.
Renormalization-group interpretation and temporal monotonicity are asserted without a formal derivation.

ideas.title: Shared-weight two-pass scan applies a gated perturbative correction
ideas.statement: First compute h_t^(1)=Fan(p_t,θ_t,W_r x_t,W_i x_t), then δ_t=GivensH(h_t^(1),x_t)−h_t^(1) with g=σ(Δ_gate), and compute h_t^(2)=Fan(p_t,θ_t,W_r x_t+gδ_t,W_i x_t). Both passes share all weights.
ideas.conditions: The author calls this a Born approximation analogy; the GivensH transformation and how its complex correction enters the real-input argument are not elaborated.
validity_flags: Perturbative/Born terminology is an analogy; no approximation-error bound is supplied.
GivensH implementation details are not specified in the paper.

ideas.title: Attention-based video token pruning
ideas.statement: FastV is described as removing 50% of tokens after shallow layers, and VisionZip as retaining high-attention tokens before clustering.

ideas.title: Evaluator objective with universal-rule constraint
ideas.statement: Equation (2) maximizes E(x_i,T(x_i^p)) over x_i^p=F_i(x_i), subject to S(x_j,T(F_i(x_j)))=10 for all x_j with j≠i. It formalizes the intended universal rule objective.

ideas.title: Cache retrieves a union of recent tokens and learned global top-K tokens
ideas.statement: The mask is local(i,j)∨global(i,j), where local(i,j)=1[max(0,i−W)≤j<i], W=256, and global(i,j)=1[j∈TopK({s_eff(k):k<i},K)], K=16. Global selection uses learned measurement scores from prior positions.
ideas.conditions: The equations use only earlier tokens. TopK is understood to return indices associated with scores; the text does not give tie handling, cache update implementation, or details of differentiating selection.

ideas.title: Fixed cache capacity gives constant decode memory with respect to context length
ideas.statement: With fixed W=256 and K=16, the paper reserves W+K=272 cache slots and claims O(W+K)=O(1) decode memory with respect to sequence length N, alongside a fixed-size recurrent state.
ideas.conditions: This is a fixed-model decode-state claim, not a constant prefill-memory or unlimited exact-recall guarantee. The union mask may reference fewer than 272 distinct tokens because windows can overlap and short prompts have fewer tokens.
validity_flags: Exactly 272 describes provisioned capacity, not necessarily 272 unique past tokens selected by the union mask.
No formal implementation-level memory audit or unbounded-context recall guarantee is given.

ideas.title: Freeze-Scan separates full-model convergence from cache specialization
ideas.statement: Phase 1 trains all parameters. Phase 2 freezes Φ_wave={W_θ,W_r,W_i,W_β,Givens,Δ_gate,CausalConv}, totaling 14.9M parameters, and optimizes all remaining Φ_cache parameters (122.1M) at learning rate 10^−4. The paper describes the trainable route as embed→cache→lm_head.
ideas.conditions: The timing of the phase transition and detailed phase-one schedule are not specified. Induction-head formation is an interpretation, not a measured circuit result.
validity_flags: Training-phase boundary and phase-one duration are underspecified.
A positive cache learning effect does not alone establish an induction-head mechanism.

ideas.title: Complex state is interpreted as a holographic plate read using current input
ideas.statement: The author interprets the fixed-dimensional complex h_t as history encoded by phase interference and x_t as a reference beam that selectively reconstructs relevant information through modulation. Direct projection by lm_head is compared to incoherent illumination.
ideas.conditions: This is a physical analogy motivating an input-conditioned decoder; the paper provides no theorem that the entire history is losslessly recoverable and does not directly measure holographic information.
validity_flags: A finite state is not shown to preserve all historical information exactly; nonzero baseline performance also does not support a literal only-noise reading.

ideas.title: Hierarchical Video Narrative Generation
ideas.statement: The task first produces temporally grounded, fine-grained event descriptions called Temporal Chain-of-Thought, then contiguous chapters, each with a title and concise summary.

ideas.title: LCC selector-swap result
ideas.statement: Under the same SEER answerer, LCC scores 25.71 with BM25-selected pages and 48.31 with learned visual selection (+22.60 points).
ideas.conditions: Matched completed tasks and page budget; official task scorer.

ideas.title: Prompt-level and token-level attack taxonomy
ideas.statement: The paper distinguishes prompt-level role-playing, which constructs scenarios, from prompt-level wordplay, which transforms text, and from token-level optimization. It attributes rule reuse to wordplay while noting manual static-rule construction as a limitation.

ideas.title: AutoBreach multi-role black-box framework
ideas.statement: AutoBreach uses multiple LLM roles to propose, assess, apply, and judge wordplay mapping rules for black-box target LLMs. Its proposed design combines wordplay sampling, sentence compression, chain-of-thought examples, and two-stage refinement.

ideas.title: Zero-initialized reference modulation preserves the starting model
ideas.statement: Single-head decoding sets h_decoded=h_t⊙(1+tanh(W_ref x_t)). Zero-initializing W_ref makes h_decoded=h_t at initialization, preserving the base model output.
ideas.conditions: The source calls this phase modulation. The equation is an elementwise multiplicative gate, and the complex/real type of W_ref is not specified.

ideas.title: Multi-head reference gates are averaged and regularized for orthogonality
ideas.statement: The H-head decoder sets h_decoded=h_t⊙(1/H)Σ_i=1^H(1+tanh(W_ref,i x_t)). It adds L_orth=λΣ_(i≠j)||W_ref,i W_ref,j^T||_F² to encourage distinct head directions.
ideas.conditions: The paper interprets the heads as reading distinct semantic directions or wavelengths; λ and the optimization details are not supplied, and no semantic independence guarantee is proved.
validity_flags: Orthogonality regularization encourages matrix decorrelation but does not prove distinct semantic information.

ideas.title: Sequential reference-beam training probes layer-wise improvements
ideas.statement: Train one reference beam per layer in order starting from layer 0, freezing each after convergence to reduce gradient interference. The measured perplexity changes are used to infer the layer distribution of recoverable information.
ideas.conditions: This is an order-dependent sequential training probe; perplexity contributions are not direct information-content measurements.
validity_flags: Order-dependent probe confounds independent layer contributions and does not quantify mutual information.

ideas.title: WikiText-103 setup compares unequal-size FDM and Transformer models
ideas.statement: The reported common setup uses a 137M FDM with d=576, 12 layers, K=16, W=256 and a 122M Transformer, trained on WikiText-103 (121M tokens) using AdamW, sequence length 1024, and batch size 8.
ideas.conditions: The six-page source does not give hardware, seeds, variability, tokenizer, full architecture/schedule details, or complete MQAR training/evaluation configuration. The dataset token count is not the cumulative number of tokens processed across all optimization steps.
validity_flags: Reproducibility details and uncertainty estimates are incomplete.
Model parameter counts differ: FDM 137M versus Transformer 122M.

ideas.title: ASR-guided scene-aware video token compression
ideas.statement: SPA-Compressor is introduced as a plug-and-play compressor that aligns visual tokens with ASR segmentation to form compact scene-aware representations while aiming to retain details.
ideas.conditions: The introductory scene-boundary wording is operationalized later as sentence-aligned frame segments; the preservation claim is empirical, not a lossless guarantee.

ideas.title: English and classical Chinese reconstruction examples
ideas.statement: Figure 4 demonstrates visually near-verbatim reconstruction of an English prose example of 902 tokens (32 latents, labelled 28x) and a classical Chinese example of 743 tokens (32 latents, labelled 23x).
ideas.conditions: Two selected qualitative examples; no aggregate Chinese benchmark is supplied.

ideas.title: Text-to-latent token compression ratio
ideas.statement: C3 measures compression as the number of original text tokens divided by the number of latent context tokens.
ideas.conditions: Token-count compression; not a byte-rate or information-theoretic coding measure.

ideas.title: Reconstruction of random-character and disordered-text examples
ideas.statement: Figure 4 shows an English example with non-semantic random characters (209 source tokens, 32 latents, labelled 6x) and structurally disordered Chinese (185 source tokens, 32 latents, labelled 5x); the authors report verbatim reconstruction including the disorder.
ideas.conditions: Selected examples at considerably lower compression than the 28x/23x coherent cases; they do not establish semantic-independence over arbitrary inputs.

ideas.title: Attention architecture changes reduce long-context cost
ideas.statement: The related-work survey describes sparse attention (Longformer and BigBird), linear attention and state-space models (Mamba) as approaches that reduce attention cost, often requiring architecture changes and possibly trading off task performance.
ideas.conditions: Background survey; token count itself is not reduced by the attention change.

ideas.title: 100-latent-token reconstruction comparison
ideas.conditions: Fox English reconstruction, 100 latent/vision tokens; exact table values take precedence over rounded prose claims such as over 99.5%.

ideas.title: 32-latent-token reconstruction at up to 39.4x compression
ideas.conditions: Fox English reconstruction with 32 latent tokens; 31.0x is the printed table value for 1000-1100 and conflicts with Figure 1 (33.0x), so it is not silently corrected.

ideas.title: 64-latent-token reconstruction comparison
ideas.conditions: Fox English reconstruction, 64 latent/vision tokens. C3 receives text while baseline receives images; table values preserved exactly despite small chart disagreements.

ideas.title: English Fox reconstruction test with controlled text lengths
ideas.statement: Following the DeepSeek-OCR experimental protocol, C3 evaluates English documents from Fox, tokenizes ground-truth text using the official Qwen tokenizer, selects 600-1300-token documents and tests 64, 100 and 32 latent tokens using the repeat-text prompt.
ideas.conditions: The paper assumes differences between Qwen and baseline tokenizers have negligible effect. No test-set size, precision formula or error bars are supplied.

ideas.title: Reported 20x and 40x reconstruction performance
ideas.statement: The abstract reports about 98% decoding accuracy at 20x compression versus about 60% for DeepSeek-OCR, and about 93% at 40x.
ideas.conditions: Fox English-document text reconstruction; approximate abstract summary, with exact bins and precision values retained in detailed table ideas.

ideas.title: Connector and modified attention complicate joint optimization
ideas.statement: A randomly initialized connector between pretrained LLM and VE creates asynchronous parameter optimization; modified attention adds difficulty beyond ordinary LLM fine-tuning, motivating staged training.

ideas.title: Training stages freeze distinct modules
ideas.statement: Table 7 reports caption training on COCO/SA1B with VE and LLM frozen, connector trained, 690M images; MT-OCR on WuDao with LLM frozen and VE/connector trained, 1B tokens; OLM on Arxiv/Gutenberg/WuDao with VE/connector frozen and LLM trained, 1B tokens; instruction tuning with VE/connector frozen and LLM trained, 10M instructions. Arxiv/Gutenberg/NarrativeXL/WuDao are labeled long-text-understanding data, DeepSeek-R1-Distill long-text-generation data.

ideas.title: Generate multilevel document questions and long reasoning answers
ideas.statement: From Arxiv, Gutenberg and WuDao documents longer than 512 tokens, Qwen3 generates questions at difficulty levels 1–5 and chain-of-thought answers. Responses over 2048 tokens are retained; training randomly samples 10M resulting entries.

ideas.title: Effective-token pooling improves the NLL example
ideas.statement: For the NLL model trained on 128k samples, removing redundant tokens raises average performance from 48.38 to 51.09.
ideas.conditions: A selected NLL case; random representative selection, with no uncertainty bars reported for this filtering analysis.

ideas.title: Shared optimizer and stage-specific training settings
ideas.statement: Training uses PyTorch 2.6.0 and Hugging Face Transformers. All stages use AdamW, weight decay 1e−4, warmup ratio .01, cosine LR schedule and one epoch. PT1/PT2/PT3 learning rates are 5e−4 and SFT 1e−5; maximum lengths 1024/4096/8192/8192. Batch sizes by stage are 96/64/64/64 for 0.6B, 64/32/16/16 for 4B, and 48/24/8/8 for 8B, with PT3/SFT batch sizes achieved via gradient accumulation.

ideas.title: Visual encoder patch-token count
ideas.statement: The ViT-L/16 encoder produces m=floor(H/16)×floor(W/16) visual tokens: v_tilde_i=E(V_hat_i) in R^(m×d_v).

ideas.title: Optimize Espresso beta during iteration
ideas.statement: The paper proposes optimizing beta on the fly at every iteration, following reference 32, as future work that may improve convergence.
ideas.conditions: Original proposed extension, not implemented or evaluated here.

ideas.title: Allocate visual tokens according to local content
ideas.statement: Fixed-size chunks and static compression may waste capacity across regions with different information density. Future adaptive compression could allocate visual tokens using local informativeness or structural complexity, balancing efficiency and reconstruction fidelity.

ideas.title: Printed text-to-text probability objective
ideas.statement: For X of length L and Y of length M, Eq. 1 depicts P(Y|X) → sum_i^M P_theta(y_i|X,y_<i), representing next-token modeling in the prose.
validity_flags: As printed, Eq. 1 is not the standard probability factorization; preserved rather than silently corrected.

ideas.title: Caption pretraining yields strong ROUGE and comparable CLIPScore
ideas.statement: On the COCO test set, VIST2 0.6B/4B/8B obtain (R-1,R-2,R-L,CS)=(.462,.318,.451,.4901)/(.489,.342,.473,.4881)/(.518,.369,.501,.4867). Listed VLM comparators have lower ROUGE but CS ranges .3916–.4923; MiMo-VL has CS .4923.
validity_flags: Caption prose points to Table 2 although caption results are Table 1. No uncertainty intervals or repeated-seed statistics reported.

ideas.title: Caption warm-up data and stopping rule
ideas.statement: Caption pretraining uses a reported 690 million SA1B-Dense-Caption and COCO-CN samples and stops near loss 0.9; Table 7 repeats 690M images.

ideas.title: Caption warm-up freezes both pretrained backbones
ideas.statement: The first pretraining stage trains the modal aligner on image captioning while keeping visual encoder and LLM frozen.

ideas.title: Positions advance by preceding visual-token counts
ideas.statement: VIST2 sets a token position to the summed numbers of preceding chunks’ visual tokens plus its within-chunk offset j, giving visual and text tokens a shared compressed positional space.
validity_flags: Summation bounds/index notation are abbreviated in the source.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-OCR uses DeepEncoder and MoE decoding
ideas.statement: DeepSeek-OCR is characterized as context optical compression using multi-stage DeepEncoder and a mixture-of-experts decoder to represent document pages in compact visual tokens.

ideas.title: DotsOCR jointly predicts document layout and content
ideas.statement: DotsOCR is described as jointly learning layout detection, content recognition and relational understanding in one pass, evaluated on XDocParse.
validity_flags: Appendix describes 1.7B parameters; Table 2 labels DotsOCR as 3B.

ideas.title: LongBench compares text, retrieval, and compression methods
ideas.statement: LongBench baselines include naive and fine-tuned Qwen3 4B/8B; BM25, SBERT and OpenAI retrieval; and LongLLMLingua, SnapKV, Beacon, and AdmTree-7B compression methods. Metrics are grouped as single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot, and code.

ideas.title: Use C3 as a front-end for million-token downstream contexts
ideas.statement: The authors propose compressing contexts beyond an LLM native window, potentially millions of tokens, into manageable latents for books, legal documents and codebases, enabling question answering, summarization and analysis with reduced costs.
ideas.conditions: Future application. The present study tests short document reconstruction and does not demonstrate million-token encoding, downstream QA or measured cost reductions.

ideas.title: Headline accuracy and token claim
ideas.statement: The abstract reports over 15% accuracy improvement over naive RAG while using one-eighth as many input tokens on five QA benchmarks with MedOmniKB.
ideas.conditions: Aggregate abstract claim; later tables and retrieval-depth settings supply the specific comparisons.
validity_flags: The abstract does not specify relative percent versus percentage-point gain or the aggregation for this headline.

ideas.title: Reranking may discard supporting evidence
ideas.statement: The authors motivate retaining every retrieved passage optically because relevance-based reranking filters noise but can drop supporting evidence in knowledge-intensive questions.
validity_flags: Qualitative motivation illustrated by a medical question; not a quantified theorem.

ideas.title: FaviComp familiarity-aware compression
ideas.statement: FaviComp generates abstractive compressions by ensemble decoding to lower evidence perplexity under the target model without training.

ideas.title: Soft context compression
ideas.statement: Soft compression maps retrieved documents to compact continuous representations consumed by the generator.
validity_flags: Contrary to the abstract generalization, the same section identifies query-dependent online OSCAR.

ideas.title: xRAG modality bridge
ideas.statement: xRAG projects dense retrieval embeddings into the LLM representation space through a lightweight modality bridge for extreme compression.

ideas.title: PISCO distilled document vectors
ideas.statement: PISCO distills document knowledge into fixed-length embedding vectors by sequence-level knowledge distillation.

ideas.title: OSCAR online query-dependent soft compression
ideas.statement: OSCAR performs query-dependent soft compression at inference time, bridging online hard and offline soft approaches.

ideas.title: Optical text compression
ideas.statement: Optical text compression renders textual contexts in two dimensions and processes them through a vision encoder to obtain fewer tokens; the proposed rationale is that visual tokens encode typography, spatial layout and semantics.
validity_flags: Higher density does not establish lossless compression for arbitrary text or resolutions.

ideas.title: Causal Visual Flow
ideas.statement: DeepSeek-OCR 2 is cited as introducing Causal Visual Flow to improve reading-order recognition for complex visual layouts.

ideas.title: Glyph rendering-parameter search
ideas.statement: Glyph renders long text to images for vision-language understanding and uses an LLM-driven genetic search over font size, layout and resolution to trade compression against downstream accuracy.

ideas.title: MiniCPM-V4.5 baseline targets compact deployment
ideas.statement: MiniCPM-V4.5 is characterized as an end-side multimodal model with OCR and multimodal understanding at compact parameter size.

ideas.title: Dependence on a paid proprietary helper model
ideas.statement: The authors identify GPT-4 Turbo for every role as preferable for optimal results and acknowledge that its paid API can raise economic cost. Vicuna-based AutoBreach results are substantially lower.

ideas.title: LITA relative time and SlowFast tokens
ideas.statement: LITA is described as using time tokens relative to video duration and a SlowFast token architecture for temporal localization.

ideas.title: Mixed dense-captioning corpus split across stages
ideas.statement: Training combines ActivityNet Captions, COIN, ViTT, VTG-IT and E-HVC-146K. Whisper-V3-Large generates sentence ASR with time spans for every dataset; only E-HVC uses the new annotation pipeline. The mixed corpus is split equally between two stages, preserving E-HVC product-category distribution.

ideas.title: Momentor continuous time tokens
ideas.statement: Momentor is described as using continuous time tokens and segment-level modeling for fine-grained temporal reasoning.

ideas.title: Prior narration dataset progression
ideas.statement: The paper contrasts temporal event-description datasets YouCook2, ActivityNet Captions and Charades-STA with sequential Video Storytelling and e-commerce E-SyncVidStory; it argues that they do not explicitly capture the visual-grounding-to-summary hierarchy.

ideas.title: Keye-VL initialized SigLIP/Qwen backbone
ideas.statement: HiVid-Narrator initializes the projector and LLM from Keye-VL pretrained weights, uses SigLIP-400M-384-14 as the vision encoder and Qwen3-8B as the language model.
ideas.conditions: Explicit pretrained dependency [26]; encoder/model references [33] and [30].

ideas.title: SPA-Compressor results on YouCook2 and ActivityNet
ideas.statement: With SPA versus without, YouCook2 (SODA_c,CIDEr,F1) improves from (2.1,6.7,25.1) to (2.4,8.4,30.5); TRACE reports (2.2,8.1,22.4). ActivityNet (SODA_c,CIDEr,METEOR) improves from (6.0,24.4,6.7) to (6.9,26.6,7.8); TRACE is (6.0,25.9,6.4), while VTimeLLM has higher CIDEr 27.6.
ideas.conditions: YouCook2 zero-shot; ActivityNet supervised. Best scores are metric-specific; no uncertainty intervals, repeated-seed results or significance tests are reported.

ideas.title: Learnable scene queries distill global multimodal context
ideas.statement: Scene memory is Ms=[Afused,Vf] with La+N·Lv tokens. S randomly initialized learned scene queries are normalized then updated for Ls layers by residual cross-attention to Ms and residual feed-forward transformations, yielding Hscene∈R^(B×S×D).
ideas.conditions: Scene queries attend jointly to ASR and vision across all timestamps, forming a global information bottleneck.

ideas.title: Latent representations may explain optical compression gains
ideas.statement: The authors hypothesize that compression gains in optical systems arise primarily because latent tokens represent information more efficiently than discrete text tokens, rather than from converting text into an image.
ideas.conditions: Motivation for direct text compression; no controlled causal ablation or formal rate bound is supplied.

ideas.title: Non-interpretable latent context instead of a generated summary
ideas.statement: C3 trains an encoder to distill input text into a fixed-length set of non-interpretable latent tokens rather than generating a human-readable summary.
ideas.conditions: The claim that this potentially preserves richer semantic information than summarization is motivational; no direct summarization comparison is reported.

ideas.title: Trainable fixed-length context query tensor
ideas.statement: C3 introduces a trainable context query Q of shape N by D, where N is the desired fixed latent-token count and D is the Qwen2.5 1.5B embedding hidden dimension.
ideas.conditions: N is fixed for an encoder output configuration although source text length varies; the paper does not state the numeric value of D.

ideas.title: Analogy between C3 late-position loss and memory decay
ideas.statement: Figure 5 illustrates C3 as progressively fading at the end of a sequence, optical compression as uniformly blurred, and human memory as fading sequentially, proposing a qualitative analogy.
ideas.conditions: Schematic illustration rather than experimental evidence about human memory or a measured mechanistic equivalence.

ideas.title: Summary and memory-token context compression
ideas.statement: The related-work discussion places C3 alongside methods that generate summaries or memory tokens for long contexts, citing Bulatov et al. (2022) for representing historical information.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison; C3 instead produces non-interpretable learned latent vectors.

ideas.title: Limits of raw and prompt-space agent memory
ideas.statement: The authors motivate memory compression by long-context attention cost and irrelevant or redundant histories; summaries can omit fine-grained evidence, while retrieval depends on embeddings, query formulation, and index maintenance. Frozen-parameter agents require evidence to be reintroduced as prompt tokens.
validity_flags: Motivating characterization, not a universal impossibility result.

ideas.title: TMEM intra-episode parametric memory
ideas.statement: TMEM writes distilled experience into fast LoRA weights during a single rollout, while base parameters stay fixed within the rollout and are optimized across rollouts. Adapted weights affect later decisions without requiring repeated insertion of the same evidence into the prompt.

ideas.title: Hardware and runtime environment
ideas.statement: Experiments use NVIDIA H800 GPUs, Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64 and 666 GB system memory. Pretext and UCL stages use one H800; SCL uses eight H800 GPUs.

ideas.title: Summary-based agent memory
ideas.statement: The paper characterizes MemAgent as chunk-wise memory overwriting for long conversational contexts without tools and MEM1 as a corresponding search-agent method with external tool calls; it situates them among recurrent, forgetting-inspired, learned, and adaptive context compression methods.

ideas.title: Retrieval-based external memory
ideas.statement: RAG, Generative Agents, MemGPT, GraphRAG, Mem0, Memory-R1, and A-MEM retain external records for selective retrieval. The authors contrast these systems with fast-weight memory and note retrieval misses and store-construction overhead.

ideas.title: Test-time training as related work
ideas.statement: Test-time training adapts parameters during inference. Prior long-context or language TTT includes end-to-end TTT, LaCT, TLM, TT-SI, and hypernetwork-based Doc-to-LoRA; the paper distinguishes its selective, distilled agent memory updates from whole-context/document training.

ideas.title: Nonparametric and outer-loop self-evolving agents
ideas.statement: Reflexion, SPRING, Voyager, ExpeL, SPIN, UI-Voyager, and LSE are discussed as prior approaches to verbal critique, strategy or skill reuse, self-generated training, and context refinement. TMEM emphasizes adaptation within an episode rather than mainly between episodes or tasks.

ideas.title: Augmented state and adaptive action policy
ideas.statement: An episode draws task q from D and has at most T generation events. State s_t=(q,h_t,m_t,Δ_t) combines working context, explicit textual memory and fast LoRA parameters; a_t~π_(θ₀+Δ_t)(·|c_t), where c_t is (q,h_t,m_t) for ordinary task/tool/final actions or (q,h_t,m_t,d) for memory-writing actions. Setting Δ_t≡0 recovers explicit-memory agents.

ideas.title: Adaptive grounded QA supervision
ideas.statement: The memory-writing prompt asks for an adaptive number of concise instruction/output QA pairs, including factual and experiential preferences, plans, events and temporal details. Every question must be answerable from explicit session evidence; answers must be directly supported, near-duplicates avoided, and no usable evidence yields an empty JSON array.
validity_flags: Prompt requirements are intended safeguards; paper does not establish that every generated pair satisfies them.

ideas.title: Context-triggered fast-weight rollout
ideas.statement: Memory triggers occur before final output where ℓ(h_t)+ℓ(m_t)>L_max. Between boundaries, ordinary action a_t is sampled from the adapted policy, observation o_t from P_env, h_(t+1)=(h_t,a_t,o_t), while m and Δ remain unchanged. At a trigger the same policy receives memory prompt d and samples extraction action a_ti.
ideas.conditions: Boundaries t₀=0 and t_(N+1)=T; empty event ranges ignored.
validity_flags: Figure 2 uses ≥L schematically while formal trigger text uses >L_max.

ideas.title: TMEM and summary-only boundary updates
ideas.statement: At a trigger, TMEM sets (m_(t+1),Δ_(t+1),h_(t+1))=(∅,𝒯(Δ_t,a_t),∅): QA supervision is absorbed by online SFT/LoRA and no textual memory carries forward. Summary-only instead sets (a_t,Δ_t,∅), retaining the summary and leaving weights unchanged. Final action receives reward and has no subsequent environment transition.

ideas.title: Standard random LoRA initialization
ideas.statement: The comparison initializes Δ₀=BA with B=0 and randomly drawn A. This preserves the base model initially but uses an arbitrary low-rank adaptation subspace; the authors argue few-step online updates may be spent discovering useful directions.
validity_flags: The inefficiency explanation is motivation; numerical and theoretical comparisons are separately conditioned.

ideas.title: Fixed SVD subspace for online LoRA
ideas.statement: For selected FFN weight W=UΣVᵀ, initialize B₀=0 and A₀=Σ_r V_rᵀ using top-r right singular vectors and values. Freeze A=A₀ and update only B online; Δ₀=B₀A₀=0 preserves the original policy while adaptation is restricted to a pretrained high-energy row space.

ideas.title: Conditional SVD approximation advantage
ideas.statement: Under Appendix A assumptions, the best approximation error attainable with the SVD-initialized row space is no greater than expected error with an isotropic random Gaussian row space; inequality is strict when target-update energy concentration ρ_r(Δ*,W)>r/d_in. Appendix A gives gap E[E(A_rand)]−E(A_SVD)=(ρ_r−r/d_in)||Δ*||²_F and equality if and only if ρ_r=r/d_in.
ideas.conditions: Best fixed-subspace approximation of a target update, not an unconditional guarantee of online convergence or downstream performance.
validity_flags: Requires target/pretrained-subspace alignment assumption; full assumptions and proof extracted from Appendix A.

ideas.title: Outcome reward over fast-weight rollouts
ideas.statement: The base model optimizes J(θ₀)=E_(τ~p_(θ₀,𝒯,P_env))[R(τ)] across rollouts. Each τ includes ordinary actions, observations, extraction actions, explicit-memory transitions and fast-weight updates; θ₀ is fixed during each rollout while Δ evolves.

ideas.title: Stop-gradient policy optimization
ideas.statement: Treat 𝒯 as rollout transition dynamics and stop gradients through online updates generating Δ_t. Estimate the base-parameter policy gradient by outcome reward times the sum of ∇θ₀ log π_(θ₀+sg(Δ_t)) for all ordinary actions plus extraction/final boundary actions. This assigns policy credit to generated supervision as well as task behavior without differentiating through the LoRA optimizer.
validity_flags: Approximate gradient of the coupled process under stop-gradient treatment; not full meta-gradient through adaptation.

ideas.title: Shared-backbone three-run evaluation
ideas.statement: Four memory strategies are compared using Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B across LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, multi-objective search and CL-Bench. Strategies share backbone within each benchmark; reported main scores average three runs under fixed settings.
validity_flags: Results are reported by the paper and not independently replicated.

ideas.title: Task-specific MemAgent and MEM1 baselines
ideas.statement: No memory keeps only the current working context. Conversational/context-learning summary memory follows MemAgent chunk-wise overwriting; multi-objective search follows MEM1 running compressed memory with external search. The retrieval baseline follows A-MEM, and these baselines keep parameters frozen per evaluation episode.

ideas.title: Scene and event representation semantics
ideas.statement: In this model, scene tokens summarize global/video-segment semantics such as product introduction, whereas event tokens represent frame-specific gestures or visual attributes.

ideas.title: Normalized F1 and EM scoring
ideas.statement: Conversational QA uses per-instance token F1 and Exact Match after lowercasing, punctuation removal and whitespace normalization, then averages over instances. Search parses an ordered list, matches each position to its subgoal and averages position-level F1/EM per episode before aggregation. Tables report mean and standard deviation across three independent runs unless otherwise stated.

ideas.title: Packed independent QA search subgoals
ideas.statement: Following MEM1, each multi-objective search episode packs 4 or 8 independent QA subgoals. The agent searches unresolved questions across steps and outputs answers in original order using a fixed list; these are independent questions rather than optimization objectives.

ideas.title: Capability-filtered CL-Bench evaluation
ideas.statement: To avoid near-floor 4B/8B scores, the authors run Qwen3-30A3B on the full CL-Bench and retain instances answered at least partially correctly under the rubric, yielding 289 across Domain Knowledge, Empirical Discovery, Procedural Task and Rule System. Qwen3-Max judges rubric correctness; total accuracy is instance-level over all retained examples, categories are subset accuracies. Selection did not use any 4B/8B method performance.
validity_flags: Model-selected answerable subset and LLM judge limit generalization to full CL-Bench.

Source bibliography cites CL-Bench as Luo et al. (2025), arXiv:2504.18978, but primary arXiv metadata for that identifier is an unrelated robotics paper. CL-Bench reference identity remains unresolved; reported results are preserved as source claims.

ideas.title: Rank-six FFN adapters in the final four layers
ideas.statement: All tasks use rank r=6 LoRA only on gate_proj, up_proj and down_proj FFN matrices in the final four Transformer layers, leaving attention projections unchanged. SVD factor A is frozen and B updates cumulatively across triggers without resetting.

ideas.title: Online SGD and benchmark trigger budgets
ideas.statement: At each memory trigger parse extracted JSON into instruction-answer pairs and run online SFT with SGD, learning rate 5×10⁻⁴, five epochs and batch size 16. Trigger budgets are 4096 for LoCoMo, 12288 for LongMemEval-S, 8192 for search and 4096 for CL-Bench; the counter sums working context and explicit memory, then clears the context.

ideas.title: Memory-agent data and GRPO training configuration
ideas.statement: Conversational RL reuses MemAgent long-context QA data and search RL reuses MEM1 multi-objective data/protocols. Memory methods share data, format, train/evaluation separation, rollout budget and update schedule. Training uses GRPO for 200 updates, batch 64, minibatch 16, learning rate 10⁻⁶, response cap 1024 tokens and eight rollouts per prompt; search allows ten turns per episode.

ideas.title: Pre-RL LoCoMo results
ideas.statement: On LoCoMo, TMEM has the highest reported F1/EM within each model size: No Memory 4B F1 23.33±0.41, EM 8.30±0.22, 8B F1 18.48±0.39, EM 3.12±0.18; MemAgent 4B F1 20.74±0.36, EM 11.48±0.29, 8B F1 24.26±0.35, EM 15.90±0.31; A-MEM 4B F1 25.66±0.34, EM 11.33±0.28, 8B F1 20.92±0.33, EM 8.64±0.26; TMEM 4B F1 25.72±0.32, EM 15.40±0.27, 8B F1 26.75±0.31, EM 20.24±0.29. Its 4B F1 gain over A-MEM is only 0.06, whereas the 4B EM improvement over the strongest explicit baseline is 3.92 points.
ideas.conditions: Three-run means±SD, percentage scores, before RL; same backbone per comparison.
validity_flags: Small 4B F1 gap relative to reported run variation; no significance test reported.

ideas.title: Pre-RL LongMemEval-S results
ideas.statement: On full-haystack LongMemEval-S, reported results are No Memory 4B F1 5.30±0.19, EM 0.00±0.00, 8B F1 3.50±0.16, EM 0.00±0.00; MemAgent 4B F1 36.45±0.44, EM 23.20±0.38, 8B F1 31.66±0.42, EM 17.40±0.35; A-MEM 4B F1 29.22±0.41, EM 17.76±0.36, 8B F1 28.99±0.40, EM 18.40±0.34; TMEM 4B F1 41.24±0.45, EM 25.54±0.39, 8B F1 41.87±0.43, EM 25.42±0.37. TMEM improves over the strongest explicit baseline by 4.79 F1/2.34 EM points at 4B and 10.21 F1/7.02 EM at 8B.
ideas.conditions: Three-run means±SD, percentage scores, before RL.

ideas.title: Pre-RL 4-objective search results
ideas.conditions: Three-run means±SD, percentage scores, before RL; ordered answer-list evaluation.
validity_flags: The paper treats the 8B 4-objective gain (+1.00 F1/+0.23 EM) as directional rather than decisive.

ideas.title: Pre-RL 8-objective search results
ideas.conditions: Three-run means±SD, percentage scores, before RL; ordered answer-list evaluation.

ideas.title: Filtered CL-Bench 4B results
ideas.conditions: 289-instance model-filtered set; mean±SD across three runs; category and instance-level total denominators differ.
validity_flags: For 4B, prose calls +2.42 the gain over best explicit memory, but Table 3 gives 32.87−26.99=5.88; +2.42 is versus no memory (30.45).

Source bibliography cites CL-Bench as Luo et al. (2025), arXiv:2504.18978, but primary arXiv metadata for that identifier is an unrelated robotics paper. CL-Bench reference identity remains unresolved; reported results are preserved as source claims.

ideas.title: Filtered CL-Bench 8B results
ideas.conditions: 289-instance model-filtered set; mean±SD across three runs; category and instance-level total denominators differ.
validity_flags: Filtered answerable-set result, not full-distribution performance.

Source bibliography cites CL-Bench as Luo et al. (2025), arXiv:2504.18978, but primary arXiv metadata for that identifier is an unrelated robotics paper. CL-Bench reference identity remains unresolved; reported results are preserved as source claims.

ideas.title: RL increases conversational memory scores
ideas.statement: On the plotted conversational results, TMEM gains +5.12 F1/+5.02 EM on LoCoMo (25.72/15.40 to 30.84/20.42) versus MemAgent +2.62/+2.46 and A-MEM +2.79/+3.54. On LongMemEval-S, TMEM gains +4.92/+4.84 (41.24/25.54 to 46.16/30.38), versus MemAgent +3.26/+3.23 and A-MEM +3.34/+2.66.
ideas.conditions: Gains from three-run average scores; post-RL totals above are arithmetic from base plus textual gain.
validity_flags: Figure 3 and adjacent prose omit an explicit backbone label; plotted base values correspond to Qwen3-4B.
Larger uplift supports the proposed mechanism but does not isolate causal contributions of extraction versus ordinary-action learning.

ideas.title: RL improves packed search memory
ideas.statement: TMEM reaches 31.52 F1/21.17 EM after RL on 4-objective search and 29.43/19.95 on 8-objective search, gains of +4.78/+4.91 and +4.92/+4.92. These exceed the strongest post-RL explicit baseline by +4.34/+3.29 and +4.36/+2.63, respectively.
ideas.conditions: Three-run averaged results; Figure 4 base scores match Qwen3-4B Table 2 values.
validity_flags: Figure does not explicitly label the backbone.

ideas.title: Intermediate context budgets maximize measured accuracy
ideas.conditions: Rank, learning rate, TTT epochs and extraction policy fixed.
validity_flags: Observed optimum among tested budgets; no universal optimum established.

ideas.title: Extraction frequency versus evidence quality
ideas.statement: The authors interpret low-budget degradation as over-frequent extraction and aggressive compression discarding fine detail before absorption; large budgets create noisy long contexts that make grounding and QA extraction harder. Trigger budget controls update frequency/cost and the update operator controls how strongly distilled information enters fast weights.
validity_flags: Mechanistic explanation is an author interpretation of ablation patterns.

ideas.title: QA supervision outperforms raw text and free summaries
ideas.statement: For Qwen3-4B, raw next-token training, free-form summary training and QA-pair training yield LoCoMo F1/EM 21.19/10.74,24.86/14.28,25.72/15.40 and LongMemEval-S 10.37/7.62,35.44/20.18,41.24/25.54. QA pairs improve over summary supervision by 5.80 F1/5.36 EM on LongMemEval-S.
ideas.conditions: One-factor ablation, Qwen3-4B; free-form summary here trains fast weights and differs from summary-only prompt memory.
validity_flags: The claim that QA alignment causes the gains is an interpretation rather than a direct causal decomposition.

ideas.title: Freezing A preserves most measured adaptation benefit
ideas.statement: Training only B gives LoCoMo 25.72/15.40 and LongMemEval-S 41.24/25.54 F1/EM; training A+B gives 25.89/15.58 and 41.51/25.66. The extra gains are +0.17/+0.18 and +0.27/+0.12, so the authors choose frozen A to reduce online-updated factors.
ideas.conditions: Qwen3-4B and SVD initialization; other factors fixed.
validity_flags: No uncertainty is shown in this ablation table.

ideas.title: Per-episode efficiency accounting
ideas.statement: Efficiency uses Qwen3-4B, batch size one and the same local evaluation pipeline. Wall-clock time includes memory operations, retrieval/index access, summary rewriting or online LoRA updates as appropriate, plus SVD initialization on the first episode; GPU memory is peak allocation.
validity_flags: Hardware details and amortization of first-episode SVD cost are not specified in the efficiency description.

ideas.title: TMEM runtime and GPU-memory trade-off
ideas.statement: Table 7 reports LoCoMo seconds/episode and GB: no memory 1.69/46.3, A-MEM 2.03/13.4, MemAgent 0.94/11.2, TMEM 1.53/21.3; LongMemEval-S: 8.73/78.5,15.33/13.2,5.12/12.7,6.55/22.9, respectively. TMEM is faster than retrieval and slower than summary, consumes more GPU memory than both explicit memory methods, and less than no memory.
ideas.conditions: Qwen3-4B, batch size one; local pipeline; per-episode time and peak allocated GPU memory.
validity_flags: Prose says TMEM lies between retrieval and summary in both time and GPU cost, but table shows TMEM GPU memory exceeds both.
No-memory is defined as current working context but efficiency prose says raw context grows throughout the episode; exact truncation behavior is not fully specified.

ideas.title: Target-update spectral alignment coefficient
ideas.statement: For W∈R^(d_out×d_in) with top-r right singular vectors V_r and nonzero target perturbation Δ*, define ρ_r(Δ*,W)=||Δ*V_r||²_F/||Δ*||²_F∈[0,1], the fraction of target energy in W’s leading right-singular subspace. Best fixed-A LoRA approximation is E(A)=min_B ||Δ*−BA||²_F.
ideas.conditions: A∈R^(r×d_in) has rank r; B∈R^(d_out×r); Δ*≠0 and r≤rank(W).

ideas.title: SVD theorem requires at least random-level alignment
ideas.statement: Assumption 1 requires ρ_r(Δ*,W)≥r/d_in, so the leading pretrained row space captures at least the target energy expected in a uniformly random r-dimensional subspace. The setup also requires Δ*≠0, full-row-rank A and r≤rank(W), making the selected singular values positive. The authors motivate alignment using decaying pretrained spectra and a citation to Aghajanyan et al. (2021).
validity_flags: Spectral decay of W alone does not imply target-update alignment.
Paper does not measure ρ_r for the evaluated online updates; practical alignment statement remains an assumption/motivating claim.

ideas.title: Fixed LoRA approximation reduces to row-space projection
ideas.statement: For fixed full-row-rank A, B*=Δ*Aᵀ(AAᵀ)⁻¹ and P_row(A)=Aᵀ(AAᵀ)⁻¹A. Thus E(A)=||Δ*P_perp||²_F=||Δ*||²_F−||Δ*P_row(A)||²_F, depending only on row space, not its basis or singular-value scaling.
ideas.conditions: Unconstrained minimization over B, fixed full-row-rank A.

ideas.title: Closed-form SVD-subspace residual
ideas.statement: For A_SVD=Σ_rV_rᵀ with positive selected singular values, P_row(A_SVD)=V_rV_rᵀ and E(A_SVD)=(1−ρ_r)||Δ*||²_F.
ideas.conditions: Appendix A setup; result itself does not require ρ_r≥r/d_in.

ideas.title: Gaussian random subspace expected residual
ideas.statement: For independent Gaussian rows A_rand~N(0,σ²I) and nondegenerate variance, the thin QR factorization A_randᵀ=QR gives P_row=QQᵀ. Rotational invariance makes the subspace Haar-distributed on Gr(r,d_in), hence E[QQᵀ]=(r/d_in)I and E[E(A_rand)]=(1−r/d_in)||Δ*||²_F.
ideas.conditions: r≤d_in; random Gaussian initialization independent of fixed target Δ*.

ideas.title: SVD factor scaling induces a directional preconditioner
ideas.statement: For gradient G_k=∇_Δℓ_k and fixed A, an SGD step on B induces Δ_(k+1)−Δ_k=−ηG_kAᵀA. For SVD A, AᵀA=V_rΣ_r²V_rᵀ, so directions receive effective scaling ησ_j(W)². The authors interpret this as adaptive preconditioning and claim it accelerates few-step convergence.
validity_flags: Directional scaling identity is distinct from a convergence-rate proof; no stability assumptions or rate bound are given.

Remark’s Gaussian comparison states nonzero eigenvalues near σ²r. For r×d_in entries with variance σ², expected trace is r*d_in*σ², so the average nonzero-eigenvalue scale is d_in*σ²; the quoted concentration/equal-weight claim is not established by the proof.

ideas.title: Segmented likelihood-ratio derivation
ideas.statement: Under the stop-gradient convention, hold the fast-weight distribution produced by 𝒯 fixed when differentiating θ₀. Up to θ₀-independent factors, trajectory likelihood is a product of ordinary-action policy likelihoods and one boundary-action likelihood per segment. Applying ∇J=E[R∇log p(τ|θ₀)] and dropping differentiation through 𝒯 and its fast-weight outputs gives equation (14), equivalent to the main estimator.
ideas.conditions: Rollout randomness includes actions, environment observations and randomness in the online update operator.
validity_flags: Approximation excludes adaptation-path derivatives; not a claim that the full transition distribution is independent of θ₀.

ideas.title: Unfiltered CL-Bench 4B accuracy
ideas.statement: Qwen3-4B accuracy percentages on the full CL-Bench: No Memory: DK 6.49, ED 1.51, PT 3.82, RS 4.24, total 4.63; MemAgent: DK 4.83, ED 1.51, PT 4.46, RS 3.89, total 4.11; A-MEM: DK 5.28, ED 1.51, PT 3.82, RS 3.89, total 4.11; TMEM: DK 6.49, ED 2.51, PT 5.10, RS 4.06, total 5.00. TMEM has the highest total, but absolute performance remains near the floor.
ideas.conditions: Unfiltered split: DK 663, ED 199, PT 471, RS 566; total 1899. Only accuracy rates, without deviations, are reported.
validity_flags: Full-set results are far lower than the filtered 289-instance results; avoid extrapolating filtered scores.

Source bibliography cites CL-Bench as Luo et al. (2025), arXiv:2504.18978, but primary arXiv metadata for that identifier is an unrelated robotics paper. CL-Bench reference identity remains unresolved; reported results are preserved as source claims.

ideas.title: Unfiltered CL-Bench 8B accuracy
ideas.statement: Qwen3-8B accuracy percentages on the full CL-Bench: No Memory: DK 6.49, ED 1.01, PT 5.31, RS 4.06, total 4.90; MemAgent: DK 6.18, ED 1.01, PT 5.73, RS 4.06, total 4.90; A-MEM: DK 5.88, ED 1.51, PT 4.46, RS 3.53, total 4.37; TMEM: DK 6.33, ED 1.51, PT 6.37, RS 4.06, total 5.16. TMEM has the highest total, but absolute performance remains near the floor.
ideas.conditions: Unfiltered split: DK 663, ED 199, PT 471, RS 566; total 1899. Only accuracy rates, without deviations, are reported.
validity_flags: Full-set results are far lower than the filtered 289-instance results; avoid extrapolating filtered scores.

Source bibliography cites CL-Bench as Luo et al. (2025), arXiv:2504.18978, but primary arXiv metadata for that identifier is an unrelated robotics paper. CL-Bench reference identity remains unresolved; reported results are preserved as source claims.

ideas.title: Conversational extraction prompt inputs
ideas.statement: Appendix D’s LoCoMo/LongMemEval system template provides the question, previous extracted QA history and a session, wrapped in question, qa_history and session tags, and asks for SFT QA grounded only in that session.
validity_flags: Previous QA history in this template is not reconciled with main TMEM transition m=∅ and no carried textual memory; implementation detail is ambiguous.

ideas.title: Single-subquestion search and ordered final-answer template
ideas.statement: Appendix D’s search prompt alternates one keyword/short-phrase search query for a single unresolved question with a final concise semicolon-separated answer list in original order. The context includes question, history, search and information fields; output must be either search tags or answer tags.

ideas.title: LoCoMo charity-race factual memory illustration
ideas.statement: Figure 8 shows seven QA memories covering mental-health interests, running, the charity race, self-care and refreshing activities. The final question about the charity race’s cause receives “Mental health,” matching the labeled answer after normalization.
ideas.conditions: Single illustrative case, not an independent quantitative evaluation.
validity_flags: Caption calls these retrieved memory QA pairs; it does not show an online LoRA trace or independently isolate parametric recall.

ideas.title: LoCoMo adoption-plan illustration
ideas.statement: Figure 9’s seven QA pairs cover adoption application/interview timing, goals, inclusive agency choice and single-parent challenges. The model answers the summer-plans question with researching adoption through an LGBTQ+-supportive agency, while the label is researching adoption agencies; the caption claims semantic alignment.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative example only.
validity_flags: Semantic alignment is not normalized exact match; displayed memories do not explicitly tie the plan to summer.

ideas.title: LoCoMo family-outdoor preference illustration
ideas.statement: Figure 10 shows six memories about family importance, camping traditions and past outdoor activities. The model infers national park rather than theme park, matching the labeled preference “National park; she likes the outdoors.”
ideas.conditions: Qualitative illustration of inference from memories, not direct accuracy or mechanistic evidence.
validity_flags: Short model response and explanatory label differ under exact-string evaluation.

ideas.title: Extracting reusable numerical-memory lessons
ideas.statement: Figure 13 illustrates four procedural QA memories: identify all revenue events before computing, verify each amount is a distinct sale, select the three relevant amounts, and exclude unrelated product/marketing/pricing/loyalty details. It demonstrates that the supervision representation can include lessons about memory use as well as facts.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative distilled procedure; no separate experiment attributes improvement to these four lessons.

ideas.title: Packed search case preserves answers and disambiguating constraints
ideas.statement: Figure 14 illustrates a four-question search with answers orange, Tromeo and Juliet, John John Florence, and British, semantically matching the labeled ordered list. Eleven QA entries include answers, supporting facts, query construction, and disambiguation between Romeo + Juliet and Tromeo and Juliet using the James Gunn/loose-adaptation constraints.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative case; factual example contents are benchmark evidence rather than independently verified world knowledge.
validity_flags: First answer adds wording beyond the label, so semantic agreement differs from exact match.
Displayed original JSON has a trailing comma before the closing array; parser robustness is not explained.

ideas.title: Distilled search-memory operating lessons
ideas.statement: Figure 15 illustrates four procedural memories: search one question at a time to tie evidence to an answer; store concise directly supported QA after useful retrieval; use near-duplicates as confirmation without duplicate memories unless a new constraint is added; return concise semicolon-separated answers in original order.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative experience extraction; no separate causal validation of these lessons.

ideas.title: KV-cache memory and throughput bottleneck
ideas.statement: The KV cache stores token-level attention representations, grows linearly with sequence length, and can exceed model-parameter memory; reduced sequence concurrency lowers inference throughput.
ideas.conditions: Transformer long-context autoregressive inference.

ideas.title: Recoverable KV offloading
ideas.statement: KV offloading moves entries to slower, cheaper system memory and selectively reloads them, preserving access over time unlike permanent cache eviction.
ideas.conditions: Selection must still retrieve necessary entries; theoretical accessibility does not ensure practical accuracy.

ideas.title: Context intensity counts required retrieved information
ideas.statement: Context-intensive tasks require looking up and cross-referencing many pieces of prompt information, even when the transformation itself is simple. The paper classifies high intensity as at least 10 needles on average, medium as 3–10, and low as fewer than 3.
ideas.conditions: The source definitions overlap at exactly 10 needles; intensity is distinct from context length and reasoning difficulty.

ideas.title: Low-intensity evaluation can hide offloading failures
ideas.statement: The surveyed post-training KV offloading literature evaluates almost exclusively on low-context-intensity tasks. Harder distractors in NIAH do not necessarily increase the amount retrieved; context-intensive LongBench subtasks are underrepresented or excluded.
ideas.conditions: Survey of cited methods and benchmarks in Table 1, not a universal claim about all future literature.

ideas.title: MultiNeedle 128K context-intensive retrieval
