ideas.statement: MultiNeedle from NeedleBench v2 contains synthetic retrieval over many independent needles or connected dependencies such as family trees, increasing context intensity relative to ordinary NIAH.
ideas.conditions: Artificial simple tasks; chosen benchmark subset.

ideas.title: LongProc HTML-to-TSV transformation
ideas.statement: The chosen HTML-to-TSV 8K subset has 120 synthetic conversion tasks generated from Arborist websites; a rules-based HTML parser could largely solve them.
ideas.conditions: Only one of LongProc’s 17 tasks averages inputs above 16K; the selected transformation probes information retrieval rather than difficult semantics.

ideas.title: Loong provides realistic but confounded verification
ideas.statement: Loong uses multi-document QA where every document contributes relevant information, but scientific/financial knowledge, English–Chinese multilinguality, reasoning and costly LLM judging confound isolated assessment of KV offloading.
ideas.conditions: Used for verification after cleaner synthetic and Text2JSON analyses.

ideas.title: Text2JSON structured extraction benchmark
ideas.statement: Text2JSON has 500 samples in four categories: products, medical professionals, organizations and movies. LLM-generated facts mimic real data with privacy moderation; prompts range 10.0K–63.5K GPT-2 tokens (mean 20.1K), and ground-truth outputs contain 3–20 multi-field entries.
ideas.conditions: Designed to separate context intensity from extreme context length and specialized reasoning.

ideas.title: Main-text exact-item IoU description
ideas.statement: Section 3.1 describes comparing each item by exact match and reporting intersection over union, avoiding an LLM judge. Figure 1 illustrates intersection 1 over union 3. Appendix B instead specifies partial attribute credit after exact name alignment; these descriptions are not equivalent.
ideas.conditions: Preserve the internal metric-description discrepancy; Appendix B provides the more detailed operational account.

ideas.title: InfiniGen low-rank predictive retrieval
ideas.statement: InfiniGen approximates keys by SVD to identify important entries, loading them from system memory concurrently with the previous layer’s computation.
ideas.conditions: Cited prior offloading baseline, retaining original keys in host memory.

ideas.title: ShadowKV and ArkVale group landmarks
ideas.statement: ShadowKV uses layer-wide truncated SVD (recommended rank 160) and groups of eight consecutive tokens represented by mean keys; ArkVale uses cuboid digests, with group sizes across these methods of 8–32 tokens. GPU-resident summaries select groups to load.
ideas.conditions: Prior offloading designs that performed adequately on low-intensity tasks.

ideas.title: YAKV simplified offloading algorithm
ideas.statement: YAKV starts from ShadowKV but replaces key SVD with 4-bit HIGGS (d=2,n=256), selects individual keys using 1–2-bit GPU approximations, removes grouping and ShadowKV outliers, and offloads both keys and values without prefetching.
ideas.conditions: A deliberately minimal baseline; later sections specify adaptive budget and residual-selection refinements.

ideas.title: Selection approximations drive context-intensive failures
ideas.statement: The paper attributes observed context-intensive degradation to suboptimal key compression, inaccurate selection criteria and grouping; these approximations can miss necessary keys or load false positives even when NIAH remains accurate.
ideas.conditions: Empirical attribution examined by ablations; does not prove all offloading accuracy loss has these causes.

ideas.title: KV compression alternatives and effective precision
ideas.statement: The ablation compares rank-160/256/512 truncated SVD, uncompressed keys, FP8 E4M3, NVFP4 with microscaling (4.5 bits/value), and HIGGS vector quantization plus randomized Hadamard transform (d=2,n=256; 4.02 bits/value).
ideas.conditions: Official ShadowKV code; Llama-3.1-8B on MultiNeedle and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on Text2JSON; additional models in Appendix C.

ideas.title: Aggressive SVD loses context-intensive accuracy
ideas.statement: Default rank-160 SVD fails to match full-attention accuracy even after loading approximately ten times as many tokens. Increasing rank improves accuracy, but rank 512 for 8×128-dimensional keys with two projection matrices compresses worse than FP8; HIGGS provides a better observed memory–accuracy tradeoff.
ideas.conditions: Section 4.1 ablation settings; not a fundamental impossibility result for all SVD designs. Budget counts sparse, outlier and local tokens.

ideas.title: True-dot-product selection oracle
ideas.statement: The selection oracle ranks individual keys by their true query dot products and serves only as an accuracy upper bound for selection.
ideas.conditions: It is not an efficient practical offloading algorithm; storing all full-precision keys on GPU or loading all from CPU is impractical for the target setting.

ideas.title: Grouping requires substantially larger retrieval budgets
ideas.statement: Removing SVD allows near-lossless accuracy but grouped selection needs roughly 5–10% of tokens versus ShadowKV’s default 1.56%; average-key landmarks and cuboid digests remain less accurate than the true-score oracle even with groups reduced to 2–4 tokens.
ideas.conditions: Llama-3.1-8B/MultiNeedle and Qwen3-4B/Text2JSON, Section 4.2; SVD disabled.

ideas.title: Outlier and recent-token buffers
ideas.statement: ShadowKV stores tokens poorly represented by their groups as outliers (including attention sinks), while a local buffer preserves recent tokens.
ideas.conditions: Separate GPU-resident token budgets in grouped offloading.

ideas.title: Larger outlier or local buffers do not fix grouping
ideas.statement: Doubling ShadowKV’s default outlier or local-token buffer leaves substantial accuracy gaps; group-selection error is not easily repaired this way.
ideas.conditions: SVD disabled; MultiNeedle-128K for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-4B. Outliers swept 192–768 (default 384); local tokens 16–64 (default 32); other parameters default. Appendix D repeats on Text2JSON with outliers32–128(default64) and local16–64(default32), again without closing the gap.

ideas.title: Extreme quantization for individual-key selection
ideas.statement: GPU-resident HIGGS proxies can select individual keys at 1.02 bits/value (d=8,n=256) or 2.02 bits/value (d=4,n=256), avoiding grouped landmarks. BF16/chunk8, 4-bit/chunk2 and 2-bit/chunk1 each average about 2 bits per key component for comparison.
ideas.conditions: Host-resident full keys remain available; proxies are used for selection rather than final attention. Scale overhead makes precise bit rates slightly greater than integers.

ideas.title: Individual quantized selection outperforms grouping and low rank
ideas.statement: Across Figures 5–6, 2-bit individual HIGGS proxies generally outperform ShadowKV group-8 landmarks at equal GPU proxy memory and LRQK rank 32 at greater memory. Four-bit HIGGS approaches the full-precision individual-key selection upper bound.
ideas.conditions: SVD compression disabled; MultiNeedle on Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen3-4B and Text2JSON on Qwen3-4B/30B-A3B. Curves are empirical and not pointwise monotonic.

ideas.title: Residual landmark quantization extension
ideas.statement: A proposed extension stores one 4-bit group landmark per eight keys plus a 1-bit residual correction for each key, yielding roughly 1.5 bits/value for selection.
ideas.conditions: Not included in the paper’s stated base YAKV; detailed algorithm and ablation in Appendix E.

ideas.title: Adaptive budget allocation extension
ideas.statement: A proposed Top-P extension partitions the KV retrieval budget between heads to increase covered attention, inspired by AdaKV.
ideas.conditions: Optional extension excluded from final YAKV; Appendix F distinguishes ordinary Top-P from the improving fixed-budget Top-KP variant.

ideas.title: Matched host-to-device transfer evaluation
ideas.statement: The combined comparison uses equal total PCIe transfer per decoding token, taking recommended ShadowKV parameters as reference and tuning YAKV, LRQK and InfiniGen to match. InfiniGen is modified to aggregate scores within GQA query groups and is not evaluated on Qwen3.
ideas.conditions: Four context-intensive benchmarks and four Llama/Qwen models; equal transfer is not equal GPU-memory use or latency.

ideas.title: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 matched-transfer results
ideas.statement: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 accuracy percentages in [Text2JSON, MultiNeedle, LongProc, Loong, mean] order: Original=[91.25, 98.91, 50.5, 46.81, 71.87]; ShadowKV=[69.38, 92.64, 15.75, 44.56, 55.58]; ArkVale=[22.1, 96.64, 3.37, None, None]; LRQK=[87.99, 98.64, 8.75, 44.7, 60.02]; YAKV=[90.83, 98.45, 33.37, 47.34, 67.5]. Missing values were not reported. Original GiB: 2.74,18.00,5.22,11.53; offloaded methods: 0.02,0.14,0.04,0.09 (average 0.07).
ideas.conditions: Section 4.4 configurations; transfer numbers rounded, original full-attention values describe full cache; no uncertainty intervals reported.

ideas.title: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 matched-transfer results
ideas.statement: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 accuracy percentages in [Text2JSON, MultiNeedle, LongProc, Loong, mean] order: Original=[97.88, 100, 59.7, 56.29, 78.47]; ShadowKV=[80.39, 98.82, 27, 51.53, 64.44]; ArkVale=[46.05, 99.91, 14.06, None, None]; LRQK=[95.66, 99.82, 31.75, 55.5, 70.68]; YAKV=[96.74, 99.82, 38, 57.58, 73.04]. Missing values were not reported. Original GiB: 1.84,12.00,3.48,7.69; offloaded: 0.014,0.09,0.03,0.06 (average 0.05).
ideas.conditions: Section 4.4 configurations; transfer numbers rounded, original full-attention values describe full cache; no uncertainty intervals reported.

ideas.title: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct matched-transfer results
ideas.statement: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct accuracy percentages in [Text2JSON, MultiNeedle, LongProc, Loong, mean] order: Original=[46.75, 94.55, 22.71, 37.28, 50.32]; ShadowKV=[10.46, 85.73, 4.59, 31.25, 33.01]; InfiniGen=[2.64, 84.91, 0, None, None]; ArkVale=[1.19, 90.09, 0.06, None, None]; LRQK=[3.3, 93.18, 0.85, 30.49, 31.96]; YAKV=[30.6, 93.36, 14.02, 33.53, 42.88]. Missing values were not reported. Original GiB: 2.44,16.00,4.64,9.64; offloaded: 0.02,0.12,0.04,0.08 (average 0.06).
ideas.conditions: Section 4.4 configurations; transfer numbers rounded, original full-attention values describe full cache; no uncertainty intervals reported.

ideas.title: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct matched-transfer results
ideas.statement: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct accuracy percentages in [Text2JSON, MultiNeedle, LongProc, Loong, mean] order: Original=[27.69, 85.45, 0.99, 20.77, 33.73]; ShadowKV=[9.46, 72.91, 0.15, 19.74, 25.57]; InfiniGen=[5.47, 84.73, 0.01, None, None]; ArkVale=[0.45, 78.82, 0.01, None, None]; LRQK=[2.05, 84.64, 0.01, 18.31, 26.25]; YAKV=[25.7, 80.82, 0.24, 19.84, 31.65]. Missing values were not reported. Original GiB: 2.14,14.00,4.06,8.44; offloaded: 0.02,0.11,0.03,0.07 (average 0.06).
ideas.conditions: Section 4.4 configurations; transfer numbers rounded, original full-attention values describe full cache; no uncertainty intervals reported.

ideas.title: Near-lossless claim is task dependent
ideas.statement: Although YAKV has the strongest reported average among offloading methods, Table 2 retains LongProc gaps of 17.13 points for Qwen3-4B and 21.70 points for Qwen3-30B-A3B against full attention; it is not uniformly near-lossless across context-intensive tasks.
ideas.conditions: Differences computed from displayed Table 2 values. Llama structured-output failures further limit accuracy.

ideas.title: Weak-model structured-output failure mode
ideas.statement: The authors attribute poor Llama 3 performance on Text2JSON and LongProc to models getting stuck and producing invalid output structures.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative inspection of generated responses; even full-attention Llama baselines perform poorly.

ideas.title: Continuous-batching throughput protocol
ideas.statement: YAKV is implemented on mini-SGLang with modified HIGGS kernels and evaluated on synthetic 65K prompts with forced decoding and shuffled Text2JSON+MultiNeedle real inputs; new requests continuously fill the batch. Reported throughput and TPOT include prefill, and dense Qwen3-32B uses YaRN beyond its native 32768 context.
ideas.conditions: Single H200; batch size chosen to fit memory; base full-attention comparison at batch 1.

ideas.title: Synthetic throughput improves through larger batches
ideas.statement: On 65K forced-decoding prompts, Qwen3-30B-A3B rises from 18.5 tok/s (batch1,54 ms TPOT) to 42.1 tok/s (YAKV batch16,380 ms), a 2.28× throughput speedup; Qwen3-32B YaRN rises from 27.0 (batch1,37 ms) to 43.2 tok/s (batch16,370 ms), 1.60×.
ideas.conditions: Single H200; throughput gains coexist with higher individual-token latency.

ideas.title: Real-data throughput gains differ by decoding workload
ideas.statement: Qwen3-30B-A3B Instruct real-data throughput rises from 26.32 tok/s at batch1 to 76.2 at YAKV batch32 (2.89×), with TPOT 38→420 ms. Thinking rises from 25.64 to 127.0 tok/s (4.95×), with TPOT 39→252 ms.
ideas.conditions: Single H200; continuous batching includes prefill. Thinking emits more tokens and is decoding-heavy; Instruct is relatively prefill-heavy.

ideas.title: Minimal implementation and architecture scope
ideas.statement: YAKV is intended as an analysis-driven baseline rather than the fastest system; the main description omits prefetching, adaptive budgets and improved quantization. Main ablations focus on full-attention-trained models.
ideas.conditions: Appendices E/F study optional refinements, and Appendix K later examines hybrid-model accuracy separately.

ideas.title: ShadowKV reproduction versus context-intensive tasks
ideas.statement: The authors report reproducing near-lossless Llama-3.1-8B ShadowKV results on RULER and selected LongBench subtasks, then finding drops on Loong and MultiNeedle using the same official code.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative preliminary reproduction report; numerical RULER/LongBench results are not supplied here.

ideas.title: ShadowKV loses Loong score at all four levels
ideas.statement: For Llama-3.1-8B, full-attention versus ShadowKV [score,perfect] pairs are: spotlight locating [63.24,.53] vs [46.15,.37]; comparison [37.20,.19] vs [25.81,.12]; clustering [25.63,.01] vs [15.70,.01]; chain-of-reasoning [37.27,.18] vs [24.75,.06].
ideas.conditions: Official Loong code, GPT-4-turbo judge, default ShadowKV parameters; judge-dependent metric.

ideas.title: Fixed MultiNeedle evaluation sample
ideas.statement: Experiments use needlebench_v2_multi_retrieval_128k from NeedleBench v2 through OpenCompass commit 1246210, hiding 11 synthetic needles in 128K tokens and scoring exact retrieval over the same 100 English examples for all sweeps.
ideas.conditions: Fixed samples avoid drawing different needles for each experiment; Appendix G additionally records OpenCompass version 0.5.1.post1.

ideas.title: Text2JSON mixture and output schemas
ideas.statement: GPT-5.2 generates all category records. Each instance samples 3–20 records per category plus 3–10 FineWeb-Edu passages, is manually moderated, and concatenates segments with double newlines. Target records have name plus specialization/city (doctors), country/year (movies), address/site (organizations), or material/color (products).
ideas.conditions: The source claims no personal data. Generation prompts can include extra product attributes, but extraction targets only the stated three fields; outputs may be in arbitrary order.

ideas.title: LSHT selector-swap result
ideas.statement: Under the same SEER answerer, LSHT scores 40.25 with BM25-selected pages and 41.00 with learned visual selection (+0.75 points).
ideas.conditions: Matched completed tasks and page budget; official task scorer.

ideas.title: Name-anchored soft entity IoU
ideas.statement: Appendix B aligns gold and predicted entities by exact unique-name match. Unmatched predicted/gold names are false positives/negatives. A matched entity scores 1 when required fields and values are correct and reduced credit otherwise; summed entity scores are divided by matched count plus false positives plus false negatives.
ideas.conditions: Deterministic partial-credit attribute metric; exact decrement rule and malformed-JSON handling are not specified in the PDF. Conflicts with Section 3.1’s exact-item wording.

ideas.title: Compression ablations extend across model-task pairs
ideas.statement: Additional Figure 7 experiments show rank-160 SVD underperforming alternatives on Qwen3-4B MultiNeedle and Qwen3-30B Text2JSON; on Llama3.1-8B Text2JSON, all curves benefit from much larger budgets and NVFP4 is especially poor.
ideas.conditions: Figure 7 covers total sparse+outlier+local budgets up to about 15% for Qwen panels and 30% for Llama; visual trends rather than fabricated exact chart values.

ideas.title: Residual proxies permit decomposed dot products
ideas.statement: For approximate keys K_hat=repeat(L)+R, query scoring is Q K_hat=repeat(QL)+QR: score quantized group-average landmarks, repeat their scores across group entries, then add query–residual scores without reconstructing full keys.
ideas.conditions: L denotes chunk-average landmarks and R low-bit residuals; HIGGS inference kernels can implement this linear decomposition. Source notation omits conventional key transpose.

ideas.title: Residual 1.5-bit proxies approximate 2-bit accuracy
ideas.statement: Combining 4-bit group-of-eight landmarks with 1-bit per-key residuals achieves performance close to 2-bit individual HIGGS proxies at nominally 25% lower proxy memory, outperforming ordinary 1-bit proxies.
ideas.conditions: Figure9: Llama3.1-8B MultiNeedle and Qwen3-4B/30B Text2JSON; scale overhead excluded from nominal bit arithmetic; curves are not exact equality.

ideas.title: Approximate two-stage top-k search
ideas.statement: A faster proposed selector first chooses high-dot-product group landmarks, then computes residual contributions only for keys in those groups, borrowing residual-quantization nearest-neighbor search ideas.
ideas.conditions: Approximate proposal; no standalone speed measurement supplied. Related earlier group-testing work is acknowledged.

ideas.title: Two GQA score aggregation rules for Top-P
ideas.statement: GQA mean averages scores within a query-head group then applies Top-P; GQA any runs Top-P separately for each query head and retrieves the union of selected tokens.
ideas.conditions: A KV head is shared by multiple query heads, so aggregation changes selected count and attention coverage.

ideas.title: Ordinary Top-P gives little improvement
ideas.statement: Under the paper’s protocol, replacing fixed Top-K with Top-P provides little or no improvement in generation quality versus transferred-token count; GQA mean and GQA any behave differently.
ideas.conditions: Figure10 Llama3.1-8B MultiNeedle and Qwen3-4B Text2JSON, skip-first-layers=0; does not refute Top-P results under other protocols.

ideas.title: Shared per-layer token budgets
ideas.statement: AdaKV, CAKE and LAVA reallocate a fixed total budget K across heads rather than assigning K/kv_heads uniformly, aiming to cover more attention mass; pruning typically sets this once at prefill using accurate scores.
ideas.conditions: Cited predecessor approach from permanent pruning; offloading can in principle reconsider per decoding step.

ideas.title: Top-KP dynamically allocates across heads
ideas.statement: Top-KP computes attention scores from queries and 2-bit HIGGS proxies, then selects the K highest-scoring token/head entries across the layer, varying per-head counts while holding the total retrieval budget fixed.
ideas.conditions: Intended to use comparable attention scores rather than raw unnormalized query–landmark logits. Excluded from final YAKV because variable-count per-head attention lacked a low-level implementation.

ideas.title: Offloading lacks ground-truth decoding scores
ideas.statement: Dynamic per-step budget allocation is difficult because offloading cannot access true attention scores without retrieving keys, while raw query–landmark logits are unnormalized across heads and grouped proxies can select irrelevant tokens.
ideas.conditions: Motivates improved quantized proxies and comparable attention-score allocation; no independent proof of novelty.

ideas.title: Top-KP improves quality at fixed budget
ideas.statement: Figure11 reports consistently better generation quality for Top-KP than ordinary Top-K at equal retrieval budget on Llama3.1-8B MultiNeedle and Qwen3-4B Text2JSON.
ideas.conditions: Optional refinement; no end-to-end runtime implementation or speed result reported.

ideas.title: Exact matched-transfer configurations
ideas.statement: ShadowKV: rank160,384 outliers,32 local,group8,1.5625% sparse values. InfiniGen: alpha99,capacity1,partial-weight-ratio.3,0.78125% KVs. ArkVale:page16,sinks32,window64,unlimited-layers0,0.78125% pages rounded up. LRQK:rank32,recent64,0.78125% KVs. YAKV:4.02-bit KVs,2.02-bit proxies,recent64,3.125% sparse KVs.
ideas.conditions: Appendix G settings for Section4.4; budgets match host transfer by accounting for compressed size and whether both keys and values are transferred.

ideas.title: InfiniGen evaluation adaptations favor accuracy
ideas.statement: InfiniGen is modified for GQA; alpha99 forces maximum allowed retrieval rather than optional smaller threshold-selected sets. It retrieves half as many entries as ShadowKV because both16-bit keys and values cross PCIe. Selection is used only during decoding because original full-score materialization is unsuitable for long prefill.
ideas.conditions: Provides an accuracy-favoring upper-bound configuration for this implementation, not its unmodified native setup.

ideas.title: Four-bit HIGGS compresses transferred KVs without major accuracy loss
ideas.statement: Quantizing both keys and values to4-bit HIGGS reduces nominal CPU transfer bytes by four versus16-bit KVs while matching BF16 accuracy closely; quantizing keys to NVFP4 may degrade accuracy more than quantizing values.
ideas.conditions: Figure12 Llama3.1-8B MultiNeedle and Qwen3-4B/30B Text2JSON across sparse budgets; nominal4× does not include quantization-scale overhead.

ideas.title: CPU cache and shared contiguous GPU workspace
ideas.statement: The Mini-SGLang implementation keeps the complete KV cache in CPU memory and uses an intermediate contiguous GPU buffer for selected entries, allocated once and shared across layers. HIGGS quantization is per head and per token because heads retrieve different token sets.
ideas.conditions: Workspace paging is omitted because the intermediate buffer does not benefit from it.

ideas.title: Per-token scale-memory overhead
ideas.statement: The implementation reports quantization-scale memory equal to 2/head_dim of the memory needed by a full-precision16-bit KV cache. Concatenating K and V into one vector or sharing scales across consecutive tokens could reduce the overhead.
ideas.conditions: These scale-sharing optimizations are proposed but not implemented.

ideas.title: GPU-driven mapped-memory retrieval kernels
ideas.statement: Custom CUDA kernels implement HIGGS quantization, scoring and CPU-to-GPU copying, while Triton handles Top-K. Landmark dequantization and scoring are fused. Mapping the CPU KV tensor into GPU address space turns GPU reads/writes into PCIe transactions and avoids explicit cudaMemcpy and per-layer CPU–GPU synchronization.
ideas.conditions: Selected indices originate on GPU; performance evaluated within the described Mini-SGLang prototype.

ideas.title: Further kernel and serving-feature integration
ideas.statement: Future implementation work includes further kernel optimization, chunked prefill and a paged layout for the full cache.
ideas.conditions: Features absent from measured prototype; the authors assert this does not compromise their benchmarks, but portability to other production workloads remains untested here.

ideas.title: Real-data serving workload and timing definitions
ideas.statement: Runtime inputs combine Text2JSON and MultiNeedle with mean≈38K and maximum≈126K tokens. BF16 Qwen3-30B-A3B full attention fits only batch1; continuous load keeps batches full. RPS means responses/second, TTFT request-to-first-token time, and TPOT time/output-token.
ideas.conditions: Instruct is prefill-heavy and Thinking decode-heavy; memory-limited comparison depends on hardware and model precision.

ideas.title: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 latency and throughput sweep
ideas.conditions: SingleH200 with continuous real-data batching; larger batches improve aggregate throughput while increasing TTFT and TPOT. No confidence intervals reported.

ideas.title: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 latency and throughput sweep
ideas.conditions: SingleH200 with continuous real-data batching; larger batches improve aggregate throughput while increasing TTFT and TPOT. No confidence intervals reported.

ideas.title: Qwen3-32B latency and throughput sweep
ideas.statement: Rows [batch,RPS,TTFT_ms,TPOT_ms,mean_output_tokens,throughput_tok/s]: [[1, 0.02, 9049, 30, 1416, 33.3], [4, 0.024, 9088, 97, 1656, 41.2], [8, 0.033, 9725, 157, 1539, 51.0], [16, 0.045, 14341, 214, 1671, 74.8]]. Batch1 is full-attention baseline; other rows are YAKV.
ideas.conditions: SingleH200 with continuous real-data batching; larger batches improve aggregate throughput while increasing TTFT and TPOT. No confidence intervals reported.

ideas.title: Hardware requirements and experimental costs
ideas.statement: Accuracy experiments Sections4.1–4.4 can run on one A100-80G,512GiB RAM and16 average CPU cores. Runtime experiments require H200 with PCIe5x16 and similar host resources. Authors estimate≈8500 A100-hours plus<24 B200-hours total; individual Qwen3-4B benchmark results take0.5–2 GPU-hours on24–48GiB GPUs. Loong judging costs$10–30 per canonical evaluation and≤$1200 total.
ideas.conditions: Author-reported replication guidance and total development/rerun costs; optimal batches/runtime may change on other GPUs.

ideas.title: Some linear and hybrid models fail intensive extraction
ideas.statement: Table8 MultiNeedle/Text2JSON scores: Jamba-2-3B57.45/13.34; LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct0.00/3.68; Olmo-Hybrid-Instruct-SFT-7B0.18/0.00. Qualitative inspection attributes most failures to repetition loops or invalid output formats.
ideas.conditions: Different models/sizes/training are compared; results do not isolate architectural causality.

ideas.title: Qwen3.5 hybrids remain competitive on intensive tasks
ideas.conditions: Scores are for models, not YAKV-offloaded hybrids; cross-model training and size confounds remain. Reference113 is titled Qwen3 technical report despite the Qwen3.5 claim.

ideas.title: Few attention layers may suffice for context-intensive tasks
ideas.statement: The authors hypothesize from hybrid-model results that a relatively small number of self-attention layers may preserve context-intensive reasoning while other layers use more efficient subquadratic modules.
ideas.conditions: Suggestion from observational cross-model comparison, not a controlled ablation or theoretical guarantee. Fixed-size hidden states may restrict long-context retention.

ideas.title: Pre-RoPE and post-RoPE YAKV variants
ideas.statement: The stated main implementation quantizes keys after RoPE to avoid rotating past keys at every step. An alternative quantizes before RoPE and applies rotation after retrieval; selection proxies remain post-RoPE in both variants.
ideas.conditions: AppendixL comparison uses Section4.4 default hyperparameters; main-table values numerically coincide with the pre-RoPE rows for the two reported cases despite the stated main post-RoPE setup.

ideas.title: Image Matching Module checks visual consistency
ideas.statement: The Image Matching Module retrieves visual matches from a nationwide geographic database, checks clue consistency, and supplies candidate locations when reasoning remains ambiguous.
validity_flags: Nationwide database coverage, construction, retrieval settings, and update policy are not specified in the paper.

ideas.title: Dataset length statistics count characters
ideas.statement: Supplementary dataset comparisons define Chapters/Video as average temporal clips/chapters, Think Length as the temporal trace, and Answer Length as the descriptive text (E-HVC chapter summaries). Text lengths count characters, not model tokens, and language is indicated where known.
ideas.conditions: Cross-language character lengths should not be interpreted as directly comparable token budgets.

ideas.title: Reported 82.59% visual-token reduction calculation
ideas.statement: Substituting S=64,E=32,N=1.836,Dv=384 gives 122.752/704.832≈0.1741 retained fraction, or approximately 82.59% reduction. This arithmetic agrees with the main default table entry under the supplement’s stated accounting assumptions.
ideas.conditions: Conditional visual-token calculation; does not reconcile main/supplement scope or verify Dv as token count.

ideas.title: Grounding before summarization for e-commerce
ideas.statement: The authors argue that fast-paced product videos require temporal grounding before thematic synthesis because single-step narration may hallucinate product attributes or omit features.

ideas.title: E-HVC dual-granularity annotation density
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports E-HVC-146K: 146K videos, 4.1 chapters/video, 693.0 think characters/video (17.0/s), 290.0 answer characters/video (6.94/s, zh). E-HVC-Bench: 1.8K rounded videos, 4.2 chapters/video, 706.8 think characters/video (17.4/s), 309.1 answer characters/video (7.42/s, zh). The exact benchmark count elsewhere is 1,852.
ideas.conditions: Character lengths, not token counts; source reports answer language zh. Think-language is not explicitly labeled in table.

ideas.title: In-domain E-HVC results and compressor trade-off
ideas.statement: On E-HVC-Bench, SPA yields SODA_c/CIDEr/METEOR/BERTScore 14.48/1.45/32.01/74.25 versus uncompressed 13.94/1.46/31.32/68.34 and Keye-VL 12.83/1.34/28.29/69.23. SPA improves three metrics over the uncompressed model but slightly lowers CIDEr.
ideas.conditions: Supplement clarifies InternVL3 and Qwen rows are fine-tuned despite missing daggers in main table. S=64,E=32. Relative SODA_c improvement over Keye-VL is reported as 12.9%.

ideas.title: Zero-shot E-HVC-Bench performance
ideas.conditions: Task-difficulty comparison; these models are not fine-tuned on E-HVC.

ideas.title: Increasing scene capacity at fixed event capacity
ideas.statement: At E=32, increasing S=8,16,32,64 gives SODA_c 12.99,13.16,13.57,14.48; CIDEr 0.92,1.11,1.32,1.45; METEOR 30.99,31.43,31.31,32.01; BERTScore 65.26,69.11,71.90,74.25. The paper chooses S=64 as a better quality/capacity balance.
ideas.conditions: E-HVC-Bench. Reported 93.38% for S=8 is inconsistent with the supplement formula; preserve as reported, not a verified calculation.

ideas.title: Limits of demonstrated factuality and efficiency
ideas.statement: The reported evaluation covers automatic caption/localization/title metrics, annotation-quality ablations and token-count ratios; it does not separately quantify factual product-attribute errors or present a controlled inference latency, memory or end-to-end FLOP benchmark. Broad factuality and deployment-efficiency claims therefore exceed the directly reported measurements.
ideas.conditions: Based on full 12-page audit. No dedicated limitations or future-work section; absence of additional experiments is not a proof of poor performance.

ideas.title: Benchmark-specific dense-captioning and title evaluation
ideas.statement: YouCook2 uses zero-shot SODA_c, CIDEr and temporal-localization F1; ActivityNet uses supervised SODA_c, CIDEr and METEOR. E-HVC-Bench uses those caption metrics plus BERTScore specifically for chapter-title semantic similarity. All use sentence-timed Whisper ASR.
ideas.conditions: Scores across zero-shot and supervised/fine-tuned settings are not a controlled model-only comparison.

ideas.title: Frame-specific event conditioning is underspecified
ideas.statement: The presented event equations replicate learned queries over frames and use shared ASR/scene memory, while timestamps are explicitly introduced in the later assembly equations; the text does not specify how distinct frame conditioning enters the event decoder beyond its prose claim of temporal anchoring.
ideas.conditions: Extraction-level observation about the written mathematical specification, not proof that the implementation lacks frame conditioning.

ideas.title: Scene-primed event query decoding
ideas.statement: E learned event queries per frame are replicated across N frames, normalized, then passed through Le residual self-attention, cross-attention and feed-forward decoder layers. Their cross-attention memory Me=[Afused,Hscene] uses speech plus global scene context; output Hevent has shape (B·N)×E×D.
ideas.conditions: Self-attention allows event-query specialization; vision enters event decoding through fused ASR and scene memory, not as a separately listed direct event-memory term.

ideas.title: Event-token gains saturate near the chosen capacity
ideas.statement: At S=64, E=8,16,32,64 gives SODA_c 13.21,13.18,14.48,14.52; CIDEr 1.08,1.26,1.45,1.43; METEOR 31.11,31.45,32.01,32.11; BERTScore 66.24,73.21,74.25,73.29. Increasing E from 32 to 64 gives little SODA/METEOR gain, worsens CIDEr/BERTScore, and lowers reported reduction from 82.59% to 74.26%.
ideas.conditions: E-HVC-Bench; authors select S=64,E=32 as default, not a universally optimal setting.

ideas.title: One-frame-per-second visual grounding for annotation
ideas.statement: The annotation pipeline samples one frame per second with timestamps and asks Qwen-VL-Max for physical product attributes, spatial arrangements, text and usage demonstrations.

ideas.title: Vist slow-fast optical context
ideas.statement: Vist uses a fast path that renders distant low-salience context through a frozen lightweight visual encoder and a slow path that supplies proximal text tokens directly for fine-grained reasoning.

ideas.title: Supplementary per-ASR-segment compression ratio
ideas.statement: For an ASR sentence with average N frames, the supplement allocates S scene plus N·E event tokens and defines r=(S+N·E)/(N·Dv)=(S/N+E)/Dv; token reduction is (1−r)·100%. It reports N≈1.836 and Dv=384.
ideas.conditions: This is a reported visual-token accounting formula excluding timestamp/system-prompt/ASR-token costs and compressor FLOPs. N here differs from main-text total sampled frames N=144.

ideas.title: Sentence-level temporal interleaving
ideas.statement: Before compression, X=[T0,V0,T1,V1,S1,…,T(N−1),V(N−1),SM]; each frame timestamp precedes its Lv visual tokens and ASR sentence tokens follow their corresponding frames. Ti∈R^d, Vi∈R^(Lv×d), Sj∈R^(Ls×d).
ideas.conditions: N frames and M ASR sentences. A semantic event may span multiple sentences; no explicit event-boundary detector is required.

ideas.title: Refined temporal traces improve training-data ablation
ideas.statement: For fixed SPA configuration S=64,E=32, no TCoT, rough TCoT and refined TCoT yield respectively SODA_c 13.16/13.64/14.48, CIDEr 1.33/1.36/1.45, METEOR 31.21/31.82/32.01 and title BERTScore 68.43/72.25/74.25.
ideas.conditions: E-HVC-Bench; refinement combines frame descriptions and high-quality ASR, so the ablation does not isolate either source alone.

ideas.title: Four-source temporal annotation refinement
ideas.statement: Qwen-Plus refines the temporal trace from frame descriptions, high-quality ASR, video metadata and the ARC-Hunyuan initial trace; outputs chronological key observations and audio-visual correspondences.

ideas.title: TimeChat temporal representation
ideas.statement: TimeChat is described as using dual Q-Formers for timestamp embedding and sliding-window long-video processing.

ideas.title: TRACE event-structured output
ideas.statement: TRACE is described as representing each event with timestamps, salient scores, and captions and using task-interleaved decoding.

ideas.title: Training schedule and default compressor size
ideas.statement: Training uses AdamW, total batch 64 across 16 NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Stage 1 performs one epoch of full fine-tuning at 1e−4 taking 23 hours; Stage 2 performs one epoch at 5e−5, freezes other components to train compression/time encoding, and takes 14 hours. Default S=64,E=32,Ls=Le=2,N=144 frames.
ideas.conditions: Reported stage times have different trainable components; they are not a controlled inference-speed benchmark.

ideas.title: Task adaptation followed by compression-aware training
ideas.statement: Stage 1 trains the uncompressed baseline for localization/captioning; Stage 2 introduces SPA-Compressor and a GRU-based Time Encoder so the model can retain performance with fewer tokens while learning timestamp embeddings.

ideas.title: In-place TTT combines sparse fast updates with sequential outer checkpoints
ideas.statement: Domain TTT trains on cumulative prompt text, passes each HF checkpoint into the next phase, and uses 50 outer steps per phase, batch 64/microbatch 1, length 16,384, AdamW LR 5e−6 with cosine decay (warmup .02, decay .90), weight decay .1 and norm 1.0. Fast-weight layers are [0,6,12,18,24,30,36], LR 3, chunk 4096, hidden_states target, with FSDP2, mixed precision, checkpointing, flash_attention_2 and ttt_mode/ttt_proj enabled.
validity_flags: This accumulating outer-loop training qualifies the main-text description of TTT solely as reset-per-input locality; layer indices are transcribed as reported, not validated against the actual backbone implementation.

ideas.title: Append query embeddings and use unchanged causal self-attention
ideas.statement: The encoder input concatenates the source text tokens followed by learned context-query embeddings; it processes both uniformly with native causal self-attention, adding no cross-attention layers or other architectural modification.
ideas.conditions: Query positions occur after the text and therefore can attend to the preceding source under causal attention.

ideas.title: Direct text input avoids visual conversion artifacts
ideas.statement: C3 omits text rendering and visual encoding, so layout, color, image blurring and visual-encoder information loss are absent from its text compression pipeline.
ideas.conditions: Requires access to input text; this does not establish better OCR on images or robustness to layout-dependent meaning.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-OCR optical context compression
ideas.statement: The cited DeepSeek-OCR approach renders text into an image, encodes it into visual latent tokens, and uses OCR as the reconstruction bridge; the paper attributes roughly 10x token compression at 97% decoding accuracy to it.
ideas.conditions: Background account of Wei et al. (2025), not a new C3 result.

ideas.title: Domain accuracy jointly measures task correctness and format fidelity
ideas.statement: Wrong-format answers score zero. ToolUse regex-extracts Action and Action Input lines, parses JSON, and requires matching action-name multisets and merged input dictionaries. SciKE-Bio requires an exact single-letter <answer>X</answer> tag matching gold.

ideas.title: Rendering-based visual text compression family
ideas.statement: The related-work survey identifies DeepSeek-OCR and Glyph as representative methods that render long text into images and compress it with visual encoders.
ideas.conditions: Background survey. The subsequent singular-model 10x statement is ambiguous after naming both works, so it is not attributed to Glyph here.

ideas.title: Gold-token density
ideas.statement: Gold-token density is the fraction of packed context tokens drawn from gold documents.
ideas.conditions: A document-origin statistic, not an answer-span or reasoning-sufficiency statistic.

ideas.title: External modules can shorten the main LLM input
ideas.statement: The paper cites Ge et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2024) as prior external-module approaches that reduce the main LLM input token length, analogous to a Q-Former.
ideas.conditions: Authors characterize prior compression as severely limited but provide no direct comparison to these methods.

ideas.title: Pretraining supplies the encoder information-extraction capacity
ideas.statement: The encoder design assumes a pretrained LLM already has useful extraction, semantic-understanding and summarization capacity, motivating adaptation of Qwen2.5 rather than construction of a new compressor.
ideas.conditions: Architectural rationale; the paper does not isolate pretraining effects experimentally.

ideas.title: Read out final-layer query hidden states as latent context
ideas.statement: After the encoder forward pass, the final-layer hidden states at context-query positions are extracted as an N by D latent-context tensor for the downstream decoder.
ideas.conditions: Dense continuous representation. The paper does not specify an alignment projection between different backbone hidden dimensions.

ideas.title: Qwen2.5 encoder and decoder sizes
ideas.statement: The implemented C3 system uses Qwen2.5 1.5B as its context-compression encoder and Qwen2.5 3B as its decoder.
ideas.conditions: Model sizes and family used in this paper; no size-scaling ablation is reported.

ideas.title: Retrieval reduces visible context with potential global-information loss
ideas.statement: RAG keeps long context in an external store and retrieves relevant snippets for inference, with possible loss of global context and relations between snippets when retrieval is incomplete.
ideas.conditions: Background characterization by the C3 authors; applicability depends on the retrieval task.

ideas.title: Small discrepancies between plotted, tabulated and prose results
ideas.statement: The source is internally inconsistent: page 6 says 98.8% for 900-1000 tokens at over 30x, but Table 2 and Figure 1 show 98.7%; Table 2 prints 31.0x for 1000-1100 tokens with 32 latents, while Figure 1 shows 33.0x. Table 1 has DS-OCR 64-token precision 85.9% and 76.4% in the 900-1000 and 1100-1200 bins, whereas Figure 1 labels 85.8% and 76.3%.
ideas.conditions: Extraction retains the literal table results and flags the conflicting source locations; the original experiment outputs are not available in the PDF.

ideas.title: Reconstruction errors tend to accumulate toward the end
ideas.statement: The qualitative analysis reports that under excessive compression, early text can be preserved while errors concentrate in later portions, described as sequential information loss.
ideas.conditions: Case-based qualitative observation. The comparison to uniformly degraded optical text and human memory is not a quantitative position-dependent error or cognitive study.

ideas.title: Reported tolerance of varied training lengths and simple aggregation
ideas.statement: The authors report that straightforward aggregation of text samples of diverse lengths was sufficient and that extensive data engineering or complex curation was unnecessary.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative training observation, without a controlled curation or input-length robustness ablation.

ideas.title: Hard context compression
ideas.statement: Hard compression removes or rewrites surface text. The paper distinguishes token-level pruning and sentence-level extractive or abstractive compression.

ideas.title: Hardware, effective batch and optimization schedule
ideas.statement: C3 is trained for 40,000 steps on eight NVIDIA H800 GPUs with per-device batch 2 and 16 gradient-accumulation steps (global batch 256), AdamW peak learning rate 1e-5, cosine decay and 100 initial linear-warmup steps.
ideas.conditions: The report does not specify wall-clock training time or a measured inference latency/memory comparison.

ideas.title: One million OCR ground-truth text pages for training
ideas.statement: Training uses ground-truth text from one million internet-collected OCR pages, mainly English and Chinese and predominantly document related.
ideas.conditions: Exact dataset membership, train/test overlap audit and language proportions are not supplied in this report.

ideas.title: Direct-text results suggested as a reference for optical compression limits
ideas.statement: The authors suggest that C3 provides a potential upper bound or reference for achievable optical text-token-to-visual-token compression ratios.
ideas.conditions: A conjectural interpretation of empirical reconstruction results, not a proved theoretical upper bound; fixed model and finite data settings.

ideas.title: Explanation for the precision advantage over optical compression
ideas.statement: The authors attribute C3 superiority to avoiding the optical pathway's layout, resolution and image-blurring bottlenecks and using pretrained LLM semantic understanding directly.
ideas.conditions: This explanation is an interpretation of the comparison; text access and differing encoders/decoders are not controlled in an ablation.

ideas.title: Context eigenstates form a 2^n-state GHZ-derived basis
ideas.statement: The paper calls each CSCO a context and its unique joint basis of 2^n states context eigenstates. GHZ=(|0^n⟩+|1^n⟩)/√2 belongs to the even base context, while GHZ-i=(|0^n⟩+i|1^n⟩)/√2 belongs to the odd base context. One phase bit z and n−1 flip bits α enumerate the basis.
ideas.conditions: Even-n family as defined in Appendix B.

ideas.title: Unified formula for indexed context eigenstates
ideas.statement: Equation B11 is |φ_{z,α,C^s_β}⟩=Γβ (X^{α1}⊗…⊗X^{α(n−1)}⊗I)(Z^z⊗I^{⊗(n−1)})(S^s⊗I^{⊗(n−1)})|GHZ⟩. Here s and β select one of 2×3^n contexts, while z and α select one of 2^n eigenstates; training identifies states by these index tuples.
ideas.conditions: Even n; n≥4 for the stated distinct context count. Only GHZ preparation requires two-qubit gates.

ideas.title: GHZ circuit depth depends on connectivity
ideas.statement: The didactic preparation circuit uses n−1 two-qubit layers, depth O(n); higher connectivity permits lower-depth GHZ generation. All later context-state transformations are local one-qubit operations.
ideas.conditions: Two-qubit-gate-layer depth rather than total physical gate duration.

ideas.title: Two city-level correctness measures
ideas.statement: City-level correctness is evaluated through directly predicted city names and by reverse geocoding predicted coordinates, labeled ACC City and ACC Loglat in Table 2.
ideas.conditions: China-focused CCL-Bench.
validity_flags: The reverse-geocoding provider, normalization rules and city boundary conventions are not specified.

ideas.title: Reported 32B coder and instruct comparison
ideas.statement: The prose reports Qwen-32B PKP 0.142, Coder-32B 0.173 and Coder-32B-Instruct 0.027 and argues that size does not eliminate tuning artifacts.
validity_flags: No 32B Qwen rows or supporting special-token values are provided in Table 6.
Generation quality claims are inferred from cold-start mass.

ideas.title: R1 distillation reduces cold-start keyword mass relative to Qwen base
ideas.statement: Qwen2.5-1.5B PKP 0.143 is compared with R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B 0.0042, nearly 97% lower; 32B base 0.142 is compared with distilled 0.0019. Leading keywords shift from import/package/from toward basic void/int/is.
validity_flags: Comparison does not isolate distillation from changed objective or prompt-format requirements.
The 32B ratio implies about 98.7% reduction, exceeding the conclusion’s up-to-97% wording.

ideas.title: The 1.5B distilled model greatly increases structural-token mass
ideas.statement: R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B STP is 0.7246 compared with original Qwen2.5-1.5B about 0.125; the authors warn of possible syntactic noise.
validity_flags: Special-token increases are not uniform at every model size; 7B and 14B distilled STP are below corresponding base rows.
Cold-start structural mass is not a measured noise rate.

ideas.title: Model-collapse analogy for distillation distribution changes
ideas.statement: The paper relates shifted distilled-token distributions to Dohmatob et al. (2024), describing synthetic-data training as narrowing probability distributions and pruning vocabulary tails.
validity_flags: This is an analogy, not a model-collapse experiment or proof for these LLMs.
The cited title concerns regression; the passage’s vocabulary-tail interpretation is not validated here.

ideas.title: Temperature and sampling mediate observable outputs
ideas.statement: The paper notes that raw model logits can differ from observed output because post-processing and temperature alter sampling; low temperature concentrates choices and high temperature increases diversity, while implementations may differ.
validity_flags: No temperature sweep, scaling equation or cross-model implementation test is supplied.

ideas.title: Cold-start coding-quality prediction is asserted but not validated
ideas.statement: The conclusion calls initialization token probabilities reliable coding-ability predictors, but the reported evidence consists of vocabulary and cold-start distributions; no benchmark correlation, calibrated predictor, significance analysis or controlled generated-code evaluation is reported.
validity_flags: Author claim exceeds the validation presented.

ideas.title: Shared vocabularies should not be confused with shared probability distributions
ideas.statement: The conclusion claims code-specialized and general models lack distinct token distributions while also emphasizing differing token-level behavior with shared vocabularies. Tables demonstrate probability differences, so the supported shared property is vocabulary identity within families.

ideas.title: Complete keyword vocabulary-rank inventory
ideas.statement: Table 1 reports every listed present keyword’s language-list count, minimum rank, median rank, tokenizer-presence count, and individual Qwen2.5/DeepSeek-V3/Llama ranks. The complete four-page evidence retains the numerical inventory; absent entries are dashes, not zero ranks.
ideas.conditions: Reserved-word and framework-term lists compiled by the authors; rank is vocabulary position, not measured token probability.
validity_flags: Exact text evidence preserves extracted table rows; visual evidence restores _Generic and _Bool identifiers whose underscores the text parser omitted.

ideas.title: Common keywords have low Qwen and Llama ranks
ideas.statement: Examples in Qwen/DeepSeek/Llama order: in 258/261/258; import 474/1897/475; return 689/3916/693; def 750/3465/755; class 1040/3767/1058; try 1539/26976/1568. Table 1 assigns if, return, else and for to 11 language lists.
validity_flags: Lower vocabulary rank is not by itself a downstream efficiency result.

ideas.title: DeepSeek has lower rank for some common and Go-related tokens
ideas.statement: Despite the general higher-rank pattern, is has Qwen/DeepSeek/Llama ranks 285/278/285; go 3346/2710/3427; chan 5658/3991/5776. Thus DeepSeek’s rank is not uniformly worse at the token level.

ideas.title: Domain-specific terms can have much higher DeepSeek ranks
ideas.statement: Table 1 examples include extern 4301/76215/4399, inline 5057/46900/5167 and match 6347/50374/6481 in Qwen/DeepSeek/Llama order, showing large cross-tokenizer rank differences even when the terms exist in all three.
validity_flags: Presence is distinct from rank; no actual splitting of these present tokens is demonstrated.

ideas.title: Framework vocabulary terms differ in rank and availability
ideas.statement: Table 1 gives React ranks 14799/54635/15143, provider 19979/96058/20576 and hook 20873/80513/21543 in Qwen/DeepSeek/Llama order. The same continuation marks undef and readonly absent in DeepSeek but present in Qwen and Llama.
ideas.conditions: These are selected framework/code terms, not all formal reserved words.

ideas.title: Many specialized tail keywords are absent only from DeepSeek
ideas.statement: Table 1 marks constexpr, nullptr, useState, crate, defer, concept, decltype, explicit, implements and callable absent in DeepSeek-V3 but present in Qwen2.5 and Llama; callable has ranks 95192 and 96292 in those two vocabularies.
validity_flags: Absence as a whole vocabulary item does not mean the model cannot represent or generate the string via subtokens.

ideas.title: C keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 59-term C list, whole-keyword presence is 71.2% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 59.3% in DeepSeek-R1 and 71.2% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.title: Prior optical allocation lacks query relevance
ideas.statement: The authors characterize prior optical strategies as globally uniform or based on positional proximity and position RAGOCR as adapting resolution to semantic relevance between a passage and a query.
validity_flags: Novelty characterization by the authors, not independently verified across all prior literature.

ideas.title: Research questions for question-based retrieval compression
ideas.statement: The study asks whether generated questions improve retrieval over traditional chunking, how syntactic reranking and paper-cards affect accuracy and efficiency, and whether question generation supports scalable fine-tuning-free RAG.

ideas.title: C# keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 77-term C# list, whole-keyword presence is 97.4% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 84.4% in DeepSeek-R1 and 97.4% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.title: LaMP development labels serve as the reported test set
ideas.statement: Because official LaMP test labels were unavailable, the authors evaluate on its official development set. ROUGE metrics use greedy decoding.
ideas.conditions: This affects benchmark comparability; the user-based split still holds users out from training.

ideas.title: Use gemma-2b-it with rank-64 LoRA
ideas.statement: Implementation uses Hugging Face gemma-2b-it and PEFT, with LoRA rank 64, alpha 16 and dropout 0.1.
ideas.conditions: Appendix specifies the instruction-tuned Gemma variant; this is Gemma-2b, not Gemma 2.

ideas.title: Train LoRA and compression embeddings with different learning rates
ideas.statement: Training uses AdamW with weight decay 0.001, maximum gradient norm 0.3, cosine scheduling and 3% warmup. Maximum learning rates are 3e-2 for prompt tuning, 1e-4 for ComMer LoRA, and 1e-2 for ComMer compression embeddings. Authors report a homogeneous learning rate is suboptimal.
ideas.conditions: No numerical ablation of homogeneous learning rates is provided.

ideas.title: RL optimization of RAG components
ideas.statement: The cited RL approaches optimize search (Search-r1 interleaves reasoning and retrieval), generation (RAG-RL uses GRPO and rule rewards for relevant versus distractor passages), or reranking (REARANK optimizes reasoning-based listwise ranking). RAGOCR instead applies RL to optical context compression.
validity_flags: The claim that prior RL leaves compression untouched is the paper’s literature characterization.

ideas.title: Task-specific training batches epochs and validation stopping
ideas.statement: LaMP uses batch size 16 and up to 20 epochs; PerLTQA uses batch size 1 and one epoch of 80,000 examples. Training early-stops using perplexity on a reserved validation set of 1,024 examples.
ideas.conditions: Distinct from the default one-epoch reconstruction pretraining.

ideas.title: TypeScript keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 46-term TypeScript list, whole-keyword presence is 95.7% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 91.3% in DeepSeek-R1 and 95.7% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.title: Ruby keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 41-term Ruby list, whole-keyword presence is 87.8% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 78.0% in DeepSeek-R1 and 87.8% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.title: PHP keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 62-term PHP list, whole-keyword presence is 85.5% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 75.8% in DeepSeek-R1 and 85.5% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.title: Rust keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 51-term Rust list, whole-keyword presence is 96.1% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 86.3% in DeepSeek-R1 and 96.1% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.

ideas.title: Original TempWiki reports thresholded token-F1 hit rate
ideas.statement: Strip think traces/chat suffixes; use an Answer line or first non-empty line; normalize lowercase, remove articles a/an/the and ASCII punctuation, collapse whitespace, and tokenize into multisets. With shared-token count S, P=S/Npred, R=S/Ngold, F1=2PR/(P+R). Original TempWiki makes a binary hit at F1≥0.5 and averages across eight rollouts and prompts (SCORE_MEAN@8).
validity_flags: Main Figure 3 is labeled object F1, while the appendix defines the reported original metric as thresholded hit rate; use reported labels cautiously. Zero-token edge cases are unspecified.

ideas.title: JavaScript keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 46-term JavaScript list, whole-keyword presence is 95.7% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 91.3% in DeepSeek-R1 and 95.7% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.statement: For the 35-term Python list, whole-keyword presence is 97.1% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 94.3% in DeepSeek-R1 and 97.1% in Llama.

ideas.statement: For the 25-term Go list, whole-keyword presence is 96.0% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 92.0% in DeepSeek-R1 and 96.0% in Llama.

ideas.statement: For the 30-term React list, whole-keyword presence is 56.7% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 43.3% in DeepSeek-R1 and 56.7% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.

ideas.title: Question-generated retrieval representations
ideas.statement: The proposed method encodes document content as generated questions and queries spanning lexical and semantic information, coupled with syntactic reranking, to improve retrieval without model fine-tuning.
ideas.conditions: Retrieval-focused compression of scientific literature, not a demonstrated lossless document encoding.

ideas.title: C++ keyword vocabulary coverage
ideas.statement: For the 93-term C++ list, whole-keyword presence is 73.1% in Qwen2.5-Coder, 64.5% in DeepSeek-R1 and 73.1% in Llama.
ideas.conditions: Table 2; curated language/framework list, with shared words counted in each applicable list.
validity_flags: Whole-token presence is not direct language understanding or generated-code accuracy.

ideas.title: Unrepresented specialized and framework keywords
ideas.statement: The source supplies a complete absent-keyword inventory spanning C/C++ system and type constructs, PHP/Ruby terms and React hooks. Examples include _Complex, static_assert, thread_local, _Thread_local, _BitInt, _Atomic, _Static_assert, typeof_unqual, sbyte, stackalloc, useEffect/useMemo/useReducer, const_cast, noexcept, co_await, reinterpret_cast and char32_t.
ideas.conditions: Inventory is printed without per-tokenizer columns; the passage calls these absent keywords.
validity_flags: No particular tokenizer is assigned to each absence in this paragraph.
React terms include framework concepts, not language-reserved words.

ideas.title: R1-Qwen-1.5B cold-start statistics
ideas.statement: Table 4 reports R1-Qwen-1.5B: PKP=0.0042, STP=0.7246, KAP=1.53E-05, special-token average=3.59E-05, natural-language probability=0.00017. Top-keyword and special-token entries are reproduced in the exact evidence.
ideas.conditions: Model name abbreviated in Table 4; DeepSeek-R1 distilled checkpoint. Special-token strings can be escaped tokenizer-byte representations.
validity_flags: Prompt-free distribution measurement does not establish coding quality.

Reported KAP 2.78e-7 does not equal reported PKP 0.0017 divided by 276; retained as printed, not silently corrected.

ideas.title: Special-token average probability is a table-only metric
ideas.statement: Tables 4 and 6 report a Special tok Avg Prob column alongside cumulative STP; the body provides no explicit averaging-set definition for this additional statistic.
validity_flags: Do not assume the averaging denominator equals Table 3 symbol-containing vocabulary count.

ideas.title: Cosmetic Wikipedia edits and binary scoring confound fact-update conclusions
ideas.statement: Original TempWiki pools every changed relation, including reformatting, disambiguation, list reordering and annotation changes without genuine new facts. Binary thresholding obscures partial knowledge changes; the authors say these effects inflate apparent drift–stable divergence.

ideas.title: TempWiki-Easy filters genuine updates and reports continuous F1
ideas.statement: TempWiki-Easy retains the same snapshots and three-slice chain but allow-lists single-valued factual/verifiable relation types, uses an LLM judge to discard cosmetic/ambiguous edits, regenerates Q/A, and reports continuous word-level F1 rather than F1≥0.5 hits.
validity_flags: Exact relation allow-list, judge identity/prompt, sample sizes and filtering error rates are not provided; filtering and metric changes are bundled.

ideas.title: Cleaning TempWiki removes most stable-fact damage and preserves modest RL gains
ideas.statement: On TempWiki-Easy (Qwen3-8B non-thinking, seed 42), SFT/SDFT closely track zero-shot drift and stable baselines. SDPO reaches about .22 final-slice drift F1 versus .17 zero-shot, with mild stable movement; GRPO reaches about .22 final drift with stable F1 preserved. The strong original stable-fact collapse largely disappears.
validity_flags: Single seed; filtering and scoring are jointly changed, so individual confound contributions cannot be isolated. The source caption has missing numeric placeholders, which are not reconstructed.

ideas.title: R1-Qwen-1.5B formatting-token probabilities
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports cold-start probabilities for R1-Qwen-1.5B: tab 3.58E-07, newline 6.70E-02, two spaces 4.47E-06, four spaces 1.01E-06.
ideas.conditions: Individual formatting-token probabilities for the five distilled models; no prompt.
validity_flags: No sequence-level formatting benchmark is measured.

ideas.title: R1-Qwen-7B formatting-token probabilities
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports cold-start probabilities for R1-Qwen-7B: tab 4.29E-06, newline 5.62E-05, two spaces 5.90E-06, four spaces 4.53E-06.
ideas.conditions: Individual formatting-token probabilities for the five distilled models; no prompt.
validity_flags: No sequence-level formatting benchmark is measured.

ideas.title: R1-Qwen-14B formatting-token probabilities
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports cold-start probabilities for R1-Qwen-14B: tab 2.09E-06, newline 6.59E-05, two spaces 9.18E-06, four spaces 1.48E-05.
ideas.conditions: Individual formatting-token probabilities for the five distilled models; no prompt.
validity_flags: No sequence-level formatting benchmark is measured.

ideas.title: R1-Qwen-32B formatting-token probabilities
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports cold-start probabilities for R1-Qwen-32B: tab 2.03E-06, newline 0.04132080078, two spaces 0.0002186, four spaces 7.99E-05.
ideas.conditions: Individual formatting-token probabilities for the five distilled models; no prompt.
validity_flags: No sequence-level formatting benchmark is measured.

ideas.title: RAG conditional generation
ideas.statement: For query q and N retrieved documents D={d1,...,dN}, a generator produces a_hat=G(q,D), Equation (1). Conventional RAG concatenates their text tokens with q.

ideas.title: Removing a format rule helps GPT-5.2 but hurts Gemini
ideas.statement: Removing answer-format-completion from the 12-seed bank improves GPT-5.2 by 4–6 points across three n=50 probes, but causes a 4.2-point regression on Gemini’s full EgoSchema 500. Authors attribute this to the rule addressing Gemini premature abandonment absent in GPT-5.2.
ideas.conditions: Small GPT-5.2 probe samples versus full Gemini benchmark; per-model bank composition is required.

ideas.title: Guided memory beats raw concatenation in most static QA cells
ideas.statement: Guide exceeds Cat in six of eight Table 3 cells by a mean 1.24 points and maximum 3.80 on Gemini EgoSchema. The authors hypothesize that explicit abstraction helps one-pass MC tasks, whereas workspace agents may benefit from concrete procedural traces during tool/edit/check loops.

ideas.title: Guided evolution is the most consistent static QA variant
ideas.statement: Table 3 Guide averages +3.85 percentage points over Plain across eight model/dataset cells, peaking at +15.80 on Gemini EgoSchema. Gemini seed skills already improve by +6.10 on average; Guide adds +0.33 over Seed for Gemini and +1.31 for GPT-5.2. Guide alone raises GPT-5.2 above Plain on average (+1.27).

ideas.title: Guided memory prefix for reusable skill induction
ideas.statement: The Guide variant computes delta S_Guide = E(P_guide(R) ⊕ P0(S,D_fail)); the prefix labels examples as failure-related evidence and asks for reusable skills without scenario-specific details. Memory affects subsequent skill updates rather than every answer prompt.

ideas.title: Question-retrieved full skills with a compact cold catalogue
ideas.statement: A sentence-transformer ranks skills against each question. Top-k full bodies enter the system prompt, while all remaining skills appear as name/description pairs and may be fetched on demand; full-body injection is limited by k rather than bank size.

ideas.title: Hygiene is inactive in headline runs but useful in supplements
ideas.statement: At 500–1000 questions, F1 produces zero name-Jaccard rejections and F2 is disabled in headline runs. Supplementary V-MME short/TeleEgo report 11/5 F1 rejections, two F2 pruning events removing ten skills and 24–37% bank-size reduction within ±1 point accuracy.
ideas.conditions: Supplementary longer/diverse tasks; headline gains cannot be attributed to active pruning.

ideas.title: Memory concatenation at evolution time
ideas.statement: The Cat variant computes delta S_Cat = E(P0(S,D_fail) ⊕ R), where R is bounded memory retrieved against the current failure batch. It appends auxiliary context without changing the standard evolution instruction, reducing the frequency of memory injection versus per-question SkillMemCat.

ideas.title: R1-Llama-8B formatting-token probabilities
ideas.statement: Table 5 reports cold-start probabilities for R1-Llama-8B: tab 1.43E-06, newline 9.95E-05, two spaces 1.75E-05, four spaces 8.71E-05.
ideas.conditions: Individual formatting-token probabilities for the five distilled models; no prompt.
validity_flags: No sequence-level formatting benchmark is measured.

ideas.title: Full quantized Qwen2.5-Coder-7B probability sweep
ideas.conditions: Fourteen quantization configurations; model identified as Qwen2.5-Coder-7B in Section 2.7.1. Exact remaining columns and top keywords retained in evidence.
validity_flags: Not monotonic in quantization bit depth; configuration suffixes matter.
No execution accuracy, latency or memory measurements are included.

ideas.title: Q8_0 nearly preserves the unquantized coder distribution
ideas.statement: Table 6 compares Q8_0 PKP/STP 0.1070/0.3025 with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 0.1080/0.2985; both report NLP 0.0019 and import/package/from with **/#// as leading token groups.
ideas.conditions: Cold-start probability comparison, not a test of equivalence in generated code.

ideas.title: Qwen 1.5B variant comparison
ideas.statement: At 1.5B, base/instruct/coder/coder-instruct PKP values are 0.1434/0.0389/0.1215/0.0003, STP 0.1254/0.4482/0.3104/0.0262, and NLP 0.0043/0.0040/0.0005/5.47e-5. Coder-instruct top keywords change to or, if, int and top structural tokens to period, comma and slash.
ideas.conditions: Table 6 cold-start measurements; complete KAP and special-average columns retained in exact evidence.
validity_flags: Different fine-tuning objectives and empty-input conventions are not isolated.
Changes in probability mass do not alone demonstrate better or worse coding accuracy.

ideas.title: Qwen 7B variant comparison
ideas.statement: At 7B, base/instruct/coder/coder-instruct PKP values are 0.1131/0.1399/0.1080/0.2572, STP 0.1470/0.1644/0.2985/0.4495 and NLP 0.0049/0.0042/0.0019/0.0007. Both general and coder instruction tuning increase PKP and STP at this size.
ideas.conditions: Table 6 cold-start measurements; complete KAP and special-average columns retained in exact evidence.
validity_flags: Different fine-tuning objectives and empty-input conventions are not isolated.
Changes in probability mass do not alone demonstrate better or worse coding accuracy.

ideas.title: Qwen 14B variant comparison
ideas.statement: At 14B, base/instruct/coder/coder-instruct PKP values are 0.1232/0.0758/0.0857/0.0108, STP 0.1249/0.1062/0.2587/0.2361 and NLP 0.0068/0.0024/0.0019/0.0026. Both general and coder instruction tuning decrease PKP and STP at this size; coder-instruct leading structural tokens are slash, hyphen and colon.
ideas.conditions: Table 6 cold-start measurements; complete KAP and special-average columns retained in exact evidence.
validity_flags: Different fine-tuning objectives and empty-input conventions are not isolated.
Changes in probability mass do not alone demonstrate better or worse coding accuracy.

ideas.title: Cause of the small coder-instruct distribution anomaly
ideas.statement: The authors explicitly say it is unclear why Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct has radically lower PKP and different leading keywords than the remaining family. Determining the training or evaluation cause remains unresolved.

ideas.title: Organize generated questions and sources in a graph
ideas.statement: Generated questions are linked to papers but lack broader organization for scaling. The authors propose a structured graph of queries, questions, and sources for interpretable, robust retrieval over larger corpora.
ideas.conditions: Proposed extension; the current system does not implement or evaluate the graph.

ideas.title: Adapt lexical threshold to context and relevance
ideas.statement: The syntactic reranker’s fixed L is an acknowledged limitation. The authors propose allowing a dynamic range and automatically selecting L based on context and passage relevance.
ideas.conditions: Current evaluated values are fixed L=2 or L=3; adaptation is future work.

ideas.title: Appendix generates one method-plus-domain or method-plus-goal query
ideas.statement: The appendix gives two prompts: generate one query combining the principal technical approach/method with the application domain or specific technique; and produce CSV queries per item from existing questions/queries that combine the main approach/method with a broader goal or alternative perspective.
ideas.conditions: Prompt text is evidence of the paper’s query generation procedure; it is not an instruction to this extraction worker.
validity_flags: Appendix omits detailed question-generation, card-generation, embedding, and reranking prompt/configuration templates.

ideas.title: Tanh affine modal alignment
ideas.statement: The aligner maps visual features into the LLM embedding dimension using v_hat_i=tanh(v_tilde_i W_m+b_m), with trainable W_m in R^(d_v×d_lm) and b_m in R^d_lm.

ideas.title: Instruction tuning compresses prompt and response independently
ideas.statement: Instruction tuning covers short-query/long-response writing and long-query/short-output tasks. Query and response are independently split into K-token chunks encoded as beta visual tokens.

ideas.title: Align compressed-context reasoning with verifiable rewards
ideas.statement: Beyond pretraining and supervised instruction tuning, the authors propose reinforcement-learning alignment designed for modal-interleaved contexts to harmonize reasoning with verifiable rewards.

ideas.title: VIST2 model sizes and hardware
ideas.statement: Experiments retain the visual modules while varying Qwen3 backbone size across 0.6B, 4B, and 8B; the randomly initialized MLP connector has reported hidden dimension 19,456, and experiments use eight Nvidia H200 GPUs.

ideas.title: Multi-turn OCR reverses text and visual chunk order
ideas.statement: MT-OCR uses [v_hat_1,c_hat_1,...,v_hat_n,c_hat_n] to reconstruct text from optical features, updating the visual encoder and aligner with the LLM frozen. The printed loss is −sum_i sum_j log P_theta(u_j^i | {V_hat_k}_{k<i}, C_hat_<i, u_<j^i).
validity_flags: Printed OCR loss omits current image k=i even though the stated OCR task and input sequence use it; do not infer corrected indexing.

ideas.title: Augment NarrativeXL with generated reasoning
ideas.statement: NarrativeXL supplies long-document comprehension with an answer-option letter. Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 generates reasoning answers; only thought-analysis-option formatted responses longer than 2048 tokens enter training.
ideas.conditions: Generator identity is printed in the footnote URL on page 10.

ideas.title: Direct memory concatenation changes effect by model and baseline
ideas.statement: Appendix A.7 reports SkillMemCat at −2.0 points on Gemini EgoSchema and +3.20 on GPT-5.2, while memory-to-evolver fusion is positive for both; it recommends per-model injection tuning on non-source benchmarks.
ideas.conditions: Gemini −2.0 matches SkillMemCat versus Seed (65.20−67.20), whereas GPT +3.20 matches SkillMemCat versus Plain (67.20−64.00). The appendix does not explicitly name the different comparison baselines.

ideas.title: Correct examples condition failure-triggered skill evolution
ideas.statement: The dense episodic store keeps correctly answered examples and retrieves high-confidence matches. Once failures since the last evolution reach N_evo, the offline evolver uses the current skill bank, failure batch and retrieved memories to propose new skills.

ideas.title: Low-frequency evolution reduces memory context traffic
ideas.statement: The paper reports memory conditioning only once per roughly 21–59 questions and estimates about 40 times less memory traffic than per-question concatenation.
ideas.conditions: Based on retrieval counts, not a directly tabulated memory-token comparison; Algorithm 1 separately writes memory retrieval inside every question iteration.

ideas.title: Group-normalized GRPO advantage
ideas.statement: GRPO samples G responses with scalar rewards rk and computes Ak=(rk-mean({rj}))/[std({rj})+epsilon], Equation (2). It needs no separately trained value model and regularizes deviation from a reference policy with KL weight beta.

ideas.title: EgoPlan-Bench token, cost and latency profile
ideas.statement: Table 17 source profiles ordered accuracy %, input tokens/Q, output tokens/Q, dollars/run, dollars/Q, latency seconds/Q, KF/Q: Gemini Plain [24.62,1352,10.5,.40,.0004,8.55,1.13]; Gemini FullEvo [28.85,10728,1.5,2.97,.0032,8.99,1.13]; GPT Plain [28.42,1198,5.1,.34,.0004,5.43,1.13]; GPT FullEvo [28.85,10207,5.2,2.83,.0031,4.11,1.13].
ideas.conditions: Profiles copied as labelled rather than silently reconciled with Table 3. Gemini EgoSchema FullEvo 68.00 differs from Guide 68.40; GPT EgoPlan FullEvo 28.85 differs from Guide 29.39; NextQA GPT row explicitly uses hybrid-3 68.10. Evolution generally increases prompt tokens versus plain cascade.

ideas.title: EgoSchema token, cost and latency profile
ideas.statement: Table 17 source profiles ordered accuracy %, input tokens/Q, output tokens/Q, dollars/run, dollars/Q, latency seconds/Q, KF/Q: Gemini Plain [52.60,3430,15.1,.53,.0011,9.05,2.96]; Gemini FullEvo [68.00,9524,5.9,1.44,.0029,9.80,2.95]; GPT Plain [64.00,905,5.0,.14,.0003,4.39,2.95]; GPT FullEvo [68.00,6369,4.9,.96,.0019,5.43,2.95].
ideas.conditions: Profiles copied as labelled rather than silently reconciled with Table 3. Gemini EgoSchema FullEvo 68.00 differs from Guide 68.40; GPT EgoPlan FullEvo 28.85 differs from Guide 29.39; NextQA GPT row explicitly uses hybrid-3 68.10. Evolution generally increases prompt tokens versus plain cascade.

ideas.title: Prior quantization robustness comparison
ideas.statement: The paper relates its moderate-quantization observation to Fang et al. (2025), citing greater noise resilience of some quantized code models compared with full precision.
validity_flags: Cited finding used as an analogy; this paper does not perform the same noise-perturbation benchmark.

ideas.title: Prior concern about rare-token preservation under compression
ideas.statement: The background cites preliminary evidence that quantization can harm rare-token handling and warns that distillation can bias distributions if specialized tokens are not preserved.
validity_flags: Prior-work claim and motivation, not a causal result established by this paper.

ideas.title: Generalized special-token prompt compression
ideas.statement: 500xCompressor encodes approximately 500 input tokens into as few as one special token for original-text regeneration and downstream QA, while leaving the original decoder LLM frozen. The reported achieved token compression range is 6x–480x across input lengths and compressed-token settings.
ideas.conditions: A lossy learned soft representation; token count is not byte or KV-memory compression.
validity_flags: Generality is evaluated on selected datasets and a single base model; it is not a guarantee for arbitrary text.

ideas.title: OCR curriculum increases the number of images
ideas.statement: MT-OCR curriculum has easy single-image OCR, medium OCR over 2–4 images, and hard OCR over more than four images.

ideas.title: Whole-text reconstruction as nonselective compression
ideas.statement: The compression objective reconstructs the entire original text so every input token contributes to training, instead of explicitly selecting high-information text spans. The compressed prompt is intended to support both reconstruction and QA without adapting decoder weights.
validity_flags: An all-token training objective does not establish equal preservation of every input token.

ideas.title: HYDRA combines pruning and robust training
ideas.statement: HYDRA integrates the pruning objective with robust training, illustrating a relationship between network sparsity and adversarial robustness.

ideas.title: Bidirectional cloud-edge generative knowledge transfer
ideas.statement: Prior architecture [28] supplies pretrained cloud knowledge to edge models and aggregates personalized edge knowledge for the global model.

ideas.title: GRPO improves factual drift without inverse stable-fact trend
ideas.statement: The paper reports GRPO averaging +1.6 points over drift baseline and a +6.2-point s2 gain, the largest measured gain among weight-update methods, while its stable F1 generally improves.
validity_flags: Reported +6.2-point s2 gain is relative to that slice’s baseline, not a monotonic cross-slice improvement.
