ideas.statement: A difference h(P)-h(Q) is bounded by ||c||_1 ||k||_infty max_p sum_q |A_pq| times ||attn(P)-attn(Q)||_Hk; fixed parameter bounds and attention continuity give equicontinuity. The zero-intercept displayed bound is sup_P |h(P)|<=R^2 sqrt(n)[C_f s(n)(log n)^(-d/2)n^(R log n)+1].
ideas.conditions: For nonzero fixed Phi(0), add |Phi(0)|. The proof invokes an Arzela–Ascoli argument but cites Lemma 5 instead of 4, and does not explicitly show the limit stays in the parameterized class. Bounded closed finite-dimensional parameters offer the needed closure argument.

ideas.title: Theorem 3: compact encoder hypothesis class
ideas.statement: H_R,n is a compact subset of C(P(Omega)) with uniform norm; thus its covering numbers are finite and the continuous empirical risk attains a minimum.
ideas.conditions: Fixed n,R,k,f,query discretization and fixed output intercept under the bounded parameter construction.

ideas.title: Continuity proof from universal-kernel weak topology
ideas.statement: Approximate g/f uniformly by k sections; multiplying by f proves universality of ktilde. Universal kernels on compact Omega metrize the same weak topology, and the ktilde mean embedding is an isometry, so attention is continuous for any universal input metric kprime.
ideas.conditions: Continuous f bounded away from zero; relies on Appendix Lemma 5.

ideas.title: Uniform covering number
ideas.statement: N(H_R,n,epsilon,||.||_infty) is the smallest number of uniform-norm balls of radius epsilon covering the encoder class. Compactness makes it finite and enables generalization analysis.
ideas.conditions: epsilon>0 and the fixed bounded hypothesis class.

ideas.title: Propagation of kernel interpolation error to the encoder
ideas.statement: Reproducing property gives <a_p,attn(P)>=integral a_p(x)f(x)dP. Sigmoid Lipschitz continuity bounds output perturbation by 2||c||_1 C_f max_p ||a_p-a_pprime||_infty; interpolation yields squared L2 discretization error <=16 C^2 C_f^2 n1 exp[-c_k n2^(1/d)/sqrt(d)].
ideas.conditions: Uses ||c||_1<=2rC and ||a_p||_Hk<=sqrt(n1)/r.

ideas.title: Discretization size and information retention
ideas.statement: For an empirical measure and query set equal to its support, sampled kernel attention recovers the empirical kernel-attention form. n2 controls discretization while n1 controls target-functional approximation; the paper interprets larger n2 as retaining more input-distribution information and relates it to longer contexts.
ideas.conditions: This does not prove finite-query losslessness or monotonic accuracy for arbitrary query replacements.

ideas.title: Theorem 1: continuous injective attention embedding
ideas.statement: For universal kernels k and kprime, attn induced by k and f is injective and continuous from (P(Omega),gamma_kprime) to H_k. Choosing kprime(x,y)=f(x)k(x,y)f(y) makes it an isometry onto G_k,f.
ideas.conditions: Compact Omega; f continuous and bounded away from zero. The lossless object is an entire RKHS function, not a finite token vector.

ideas.title: Discretized attention and ReLU encoder
ideas.statement: For distinct T={t_1,...,t_n2}, define [g]_T=(g(t_j))_j and H_n1,n2(P)=c^T ReLU(A[attn(P)]_T+b)+b0. A has n1 rows and n2 columns, c,b have length n1.
ideas.conditions: Definition 3 uses fixed universal-kernel attention, a query discretization and a shallow scalar-output FNN.

ideas.title: Lemma 3: encoder metric entropy
ideas.statement: The paper states log N(H_R,n,epsilon,||.||_infty)<=R1 n(log n)^d log(Rtilde/epsilon)+R2 n(log n)^(d+2), with R1=6C_k,d, R2=2(8R+3d), Rtilde=6R^2(1+2C_k,d)max{1,2C_f(C_k,d+1)}.
ideas.conditions: n>=3; useful small positive covering radii. Proof ends with doubled R1=12C_k,d and R2=4(8R+3d), and Rtilde=3RC4 with C4=2C3R(1+2C_k,d), C3=max{2,4C_f(C_k,d+1)}, also differing from stated Rtilde.

ideas.title: Parameter gridding bounds hypothesis covering numbers
ideas.statement: An epsilon perturbation of each c,A,b coordinate changes output by at most C4(log n)^d n^(2R log n) epsilon. Grid 2n output weights, 2n s(n) matrix entries and 2n biases at that resolution; taking logs yields O(n(log n)^d log(1/epsilon)+n(log n)^(d+2)) entropy.
ideas.conditions: Fixed attention and queries; large but bounded weights determine the sensitivity. Constants are not consistent between lemma statement and proof.

ideas.title: Squared-error empirical risk minimization
ideas.statement: Fit phi_Dhat,H in argmin_phi in H (1/m1) sum_i (phi(muhat_i)-y_i)^2.
ideas.conditions: Two-stage empirical distribution inputs; a specified hypothesis class H.

ideas.title: Lemma 2: five-term two-stage error decomposition
ideas.statement: For any comparator h in H_R,n, excess risk of clipped ERM is at most I1+I2+|I3|+|I4|+R. I1 is population-minus-first-stage excess loss of clipped ERM; I2 is first-stage-minus-population excess loss of h; I3=E_D(clipped ERM)-E_Dhat(clipped ERM); I4=E_Dhat(h)-E_D(h); R=E(h)-E(phi_rho).
ideas.conditions: Uses empirical optimality and the fact that clipping to the label interval cannot increase empirical squared loss.

ideas.title: Positive-offset ReLU components for learned features
ideas.statement: Remark 1 writes f(x)=sum_j c_j(ReLU(a_j.x+b_j)+epsilon_j), epsilon_j>0, and expands attention linearly over components. The authors use shallow-network universality to argue no loss of expressivity when relaxing nonvanishing f in applications.
ideas.conditions: Each positive-offset component is nonvanishing, but a signed sum can vanish; the remark does not prove injectivity for every resulting scalar f.

ideas.title: Oracle proof uses prior first-stage concentration inequalities
ideas.statement: The proof applies Yu et al. (2023) inequalities: P(I1>0.5 excess risk+epsilon)<=N(H,epsilon/(16M))exp[-3m1 epsilon/(2048M^2)] and P(I2>epsilon)<=exp[-m1 epsilon^2/{2(3M+||h||_infty)^2(R(H)+2epsilon/3)}].
ideas.conditions: I1 and I2 from Lemma 2; bounded squared-loss setting. This is an explicitly cited proof dependency.

ideas.title: Theorem 5: expected generalization bound
ideas.statement: For phi_rho=Phi_k,f and Phi(0)=0, choose N=floor(A7 sqrt(m1)[log(A3 sqrt(m1))]^d) free parameters and m2=ceil(A5 (A3 sqrt(m1))^[8R log(A3 sqrt(m1))]). The expected excess squared risk is <=A6 m1^(-1/2)[log(A3 sqrt(m1))]^(d+2). Constants depend only on C_f,C,M,d,alpha.
ideas.conditions: Gaussian kernel, cube domain, bounded labels, attention–Barron target, clipped exact ERM and sufficient second-stage samples. m2 grows as exp(O((log m1)^2)), a strong requirement.

ideas.title: Theorem 5 proof has inconsistent constant dependencies
ideas.statement: Theorem 5 says A3–A7 depend only on C_f,C,M,d,alpha, but the proof sets A5=[3m1/(4096Cstar^2 M^2)]A2, explicitly depending on m1. It also sets A4=2d[1+log(log A3)] without guaranteeing A3>1 and uses A7 as a sample-size threshold rather than explaining its parameter-count coefficient.
ideas.conditions: These are source-level proof issues; the extraction preserves the claimed rate but does not certify that the displayed proof proves the stated sample prescription.

ideas.title: Gram-inverse control and ReLU parameter rescaling
ideas.statement: Interpolation coefficients are bounded using sqrt(n2)||K_T^-1||_2 sqrt(n1). Replacing each clipped-ramp sigmoid by two ReLUs gives 2n units, and positive homogeneity rescales biases to <=1 while increasing output norm to <=8rC sqrt(n). A Gaussian Gram-inverse bound ||K_T^-1||_2<=C1(log n)^(-d)n^(C2 log n) yields H_R,n parameter constraints.
ideas.conditions: C1=(alpha sqrt(pi))^(-d) C_k,d^-1; C2=d pi^2 alpha^2 C_k,d^(2/d). Gram bound attributed to Example 1 of Zhou (2003).

ideas.title: Bounded parameter hypothesis class
ideas.statement: H_R,n fixes b0=Phi(0) and bounds ||c||_1<=R sqrt(n), |A_pq|<=R(log n)^(-d/2) n^(R log n), ||b||_infty<=R. R depends on r,C,d,k and query count is s(n).
ideas.conditions: The theorem calls the type (2n,s(n)) but the set display writes H_n,s(n); subsequent proofs count 2n units.

ideas.title: Integral probability metric and RKHS mean discrepancy
ideas.statement: gamma_F(P,Q)=sup_g in F |integral g d(P-Q)|. For the RKHS unit ball it equals the RKHS norm of mean embeddings k_P(P)-k_P(Q); a Mercer kernel alone need not separate distributions. W1 arises from the unit Lipschitz-seminorm class.
ideas.conditions: Mercer means symmetric, continuous, positive semidefinite on compact Omega; the source unbounded class C(Omega) example need not yield a finite metric.

ideas.title: Empirical kernel attention
ideas.statement: k-Attn(x_i)=(1/n) sum_j k(x_i,x_j) f(x_j)=integral k(x_i,x) f(x) d muhat_n(x).
ideas.conditions: Scalar feature f and empirical distribution muhat_n; the paper identifies this with attention but its displayed softmax kernel is already normalized.

ideas.title: Gaussian nodal interpolation on a uniform query mesh
ideas.statement: For a uniform mesh T in [-1,1]^d, interpolate a_p by a_p^n2(x)=sum_q a_p(t_q)u_q(x), with nodal vector u=K_T^(-1)(k(.,t_q))_q. The cited Gaussian interpolation bound is |a_p(x)-a_p^n2(x)|<=||a_p||_Hk exp[-c_k n2^(1/d)/(2 sqrt(d))].
ideas.conditions: n2=|T|; positive definite Gaussian Gram matrix; bound explicitly attributed to Zhou et al. (2024).

ideas.title: Kernel ridge distribution regression predecessors
ideas.statement: Earlier kernel mean embedding plus kernel ridge regression uses regularized ERM and target spaces characterized by kernel integral operators, deriving generalization bounds under regularity assumptions.
ideas.conditions: Szabo et al. (2016), Fang et al. (2020), Yu et al. (2021); described comparison, not a benchmark.

ideas.title: Task-specific query compression and prompt tuning
ideas.statement: The authors propose understanding learned query sets as a smaller task-specific discretization replacing a universal high-resolution mesh. Optimize corresponding task losses to obtain queries for lower-dimensional representations; they connect this interpretation to prompt tuning and Q-former cross-modal alignment.
ideas.conditions: Conceptual connection to Liu et al. (2023) and Li et al. (2023); no theorem supplies a size/error guarantee for learned queries or discrete prompt compression.

ideas.title: Mixture-of-experts scaling needs further analysis
ideas.statement: The discussion describes gating a query to one FNN from an expanding pool as a way to scale capacity with limited active computation, and proposes studying MoE within distribution regression.
ideas.conditions: Cites Eigen et al. (2013), Shazeer et al. (2016), Jiang et al. (2024); no MoE generalization theorem is proved here.

ideas.title: Multifeature Barron ridge functionals
ideas.statement: Phi(x)=g(<a_1,x>,...,<a_dprime,x>) with unit RKHS directions is Barron when g has continuous partial derivatives of order floor(dprime/2)+2 as specified. This allows distribution features from a dense RKHS instead of only prescribed polynomial features.
ideas.conditions: A smooth finite-dimensional ridge family is an example within the larger Barron class.

ideas.title: Sentence and token sampling analogy
ideas.statement: The authors interpret first-stage samples as sentence-level semantic distributions and second-stage samples as word-level tokens expressing that meaning.
ideas.conditions: This is an iid distribution-based abstraction of language, not a demonstrated stochastic model of ordered text.

ideas.title: Interpretation of normalization in attention
ideas.statement: Row normalization can introduce asymmetric dependencies even from a symmetric kernel and makes each row of weights sum to one; the authors suggest directional language structure and balanced, stable contributions as benefits.
ideas.conditions: Discussion-level interpretation, not a separate performance or stability theorem.

ideas.title: Normalized kernel attention as a quotient
ideas.statement: Normalized attention at each query is attnbar_k(mu)= [integral k(x,.) f(x)dmu(x)]/[integral k(y,.)dmu(y)]. The denominator can be represented by attention with constant feature 1; numerator and denominator can then be combined through multiplication and reciprocal networks.
ideas.conditions: Gaussian or Laplace kernel on compact cube ensures a positive denominator bounded away from zero. This is not a proof that arbitrary learned dot-product softmax equals a fixed universal Gaussian kernel.

ideas.title: ReLU construction of constant normalization feature
ideas.statement: Set f1(y)=0.5[ReLU(y+1)-2ReLU(y-1)+ReLU(y-3)] and fprime(y)=f1(y)+f1(-y); then fprime=1 on [-1,1]. Average its coordinatewise values for the constant feature on [-1,1]^d. Approximate reciprocal and multiplication by FNNs following Yarotsky (2017).
ideas.conditions: The denominator range is compact and separated from zero; source refers to nonexistent subsection 4.4.

ideas.title: Theorem 4: two-stage oracle inequality
ideas.statement: Let a=||h-phi_rho||_rho^2 and B=||h||_infty. P(||pi_M phi_Dhat-phi_rho||_rho^2>2a+8epsilon) is at most N(H_R,n,epsilon/(16M),||.||_infty) exp(-3m1 epsilon/(2048M^2)) + exp(-m1 epsilon^2/[2(3M+B)^2(a+2epsilon/3)]) +4m1 s(n) exp(-m2 epsilon^2/[128 max(B^2,M^2) C_f^2 C5^2 n^(4R log n)(log n)^d]), where C5=2C_k,d R^2.
ideas.conditions: n>=3, epsilon>0, h in H_R,n, m2=min_i m2,i; bounded labels and Gaussian bounded-parameter framework.

ideas.title: Polynomial-feature neural distribution regression
ideas.statement: The authors contrast their kernel-based architecture with Shi et al. (2023) FNNs and Yu et al. (2023) CNNs using Wasserstein input metrics and polynomial features, which may lose input information.
ideas.conditions: Comparison is to the cited architectures, not a theorem that all FNNs or CNNs are less expressive.

ideas.title: Population regression and excess risk
ideas.statement: Labels lie in [-M,M], phi_rho(mu)=integral y d rho(y|mu), and E(phi)=integral (phi(mu)-y)^2 d rho. The conditional mean minimizes squared risk; excess risk is its squared L2(rho_U) distance.
ideas.conditions: Omega=[-1,1]^d, M>0, distribution inputs P(Omega).

ideas.title: Logarithmic query count and approximation constant discrepancy
ideas.statement: Combining errors gives 4C_f C/sqrt(n1)+4CC_f sqrt(n1) exp[-c_k n2^(1/d)/(2 sqrt(d))]. With n2=ceil(C_k,d(log n1)^d) and C_k,d=(2 sqrt(d)/c_k)^d, the proof derives <=8C_f C/sqrt(n1).
ideas.conditions: For Gaussian k, r=C_f. Theorem 2 instead states (4C_f+r)C/sqrt(n)=5C_f C/sqrt(n); the printed proof establishes the same order with a different constant.

ideas.title: Generalization proof balances entropy and approximation
ideas.statement: Use a comparator with ||h||_infty<=2C_f C and squared approximation error Cstar^2/n, substitute entropy and oracle bounds, and restrict epsilon>=2Cstar^2 n^-1(log n)^(d+2). Choose n=floor(A3 sqrt(m1)), A3=[3Cstar^2/(2048 A1 M^2)]^(1/2), to absorb the entropy term into concentration.
ideas.conditions: Phi(0)=0; sufficiently large m1 with n>=3. Cstar is used without explicit definition; it denotes an approximation constant. Section 5.5 incorrectly calls the sigmoidal approximation Theorem 1 (it is Theorem 2 proof).

ideas.title: Approximation proof: clipped-ramp sigmoids and pushforward measure
ideas.statement: Split error into Barron approximation plus finite-query discretization. Choose phi(x)=ReLU(x+1/2)-ReLU(x-1/2), beta=sqrt(n1), so eta_beta<=1/beta. Push rho_U through continuous attention onto B_r and apply Lemma 1 for squared error <=(4rC)^2/n1.
ideas.conditions: General Phi requires the fixed intercept Phi(0) from Lemma 1; some proof displays omit it.

ideas.title: Ridge functionals express distribution statistics
ideas.statement: For ||a||_Hk=1 and univariate g with integral |t||g-hat(t)|dt finite, Phi(x)=g(<a,x>) is Barron and Phi(attn(P))=g(integral a(x)f(x)dP). The paper cites continuous second derivative as sufficient on a bounded interval.
ideas.conditions: Universal H_k is dense in C(Omega); functional smoothness and Fourier conditions remain required.

ideas.title: Kernel-section approximation of functional parameters
ideas.statement: Approximate each RKHS direction a_p by sum_q a_pq k(t_q,.); the reproducing identity replaces <a_p,g> by a linear combination of g(t_q), matching the finite encoder.
ideas.conditions: The paper explicitly attributes this idea to Zhou et al. (2024), Approximation of RKHS functionals by neural networks.

ideas.title: Width scaling balances approximation and estimation
ideas.statement: The proof chooses n proportional to sqrt(m1); increasing FNN width improves approximation but increases hypothesis complexity. The resulting model complexity should grow with first-stage sample size under this balance.
ideas.conditions: This is a sufficient theoretical choice for the analyzed class, not an empirically established optimal LLM scaling law.

ideas.title: Theoretical scope and practical interpretations
ideas.statement: The work analyzes a shallow kernel-attention Transformer encoder in two-stage distribution regression; the advertised insights for prompt tuning, adapters and scaling are interpretations within this framework rather than experimental validation.
ideas.conditions: Formal architecture, kernel, functional and sampling assumptions must hold.

ideas.title: Concentration of empirical kernel features
ideas.statement: For fixed query t, g_t(x)=k(x,t)f(x) is bounded by C_f. The proof bounds P(|E g_t-S_m2 g_t|>epsilon)<=2 exp[-m2 epsilon^2/(8C_f^2)], then unions over s(n) queries. Uniform network prediction error is <=C5 n^(2R log n)(log n)^(d/2) epsilon on this event.
ideas.conditions: Gaussian kernel bounded by one, iid second-stage samples, n>=3 and C5=2C_k,d R^2.

ideas.title: Second-stage loss tails close the oracle proof
ideas.statement: P(|I3|>epsilon)<=2m1s(n) exp[-m2 epsilon^2/(128M^2 C_f^2 C5^2 n^(4R log n)(log n)^d)]; P(|I4|>epsilon)<=2m1s(n) exp[-m2 epsilon^2/(32(M^2+||h||_infty^2)C_f^2 C5^2 n^(4R log n)(log n)^d)]. Union with first-stage tails gives Theorem 4.
ideas.conditions: Clipped ERM controls I3 loss sensitivity by 4M; h is bounded in the hypothesis class. Printed absolute-value event bars surround the inequality in places; intended events are |I_j|>epsilon.

ideas.title: Tail integration yields the expected excess-risk rate
ideas.statement: Above tau0=18Cstar^2 n^-1(log n)^(d+2), the proof claims tail <=3 exp[-sqrt(m1) tau/(768(4M+2C_f C)^2)]. Integrating P(error>tau) yields A6 m1^-1/2[log(A3 sqrt(m1))]^(d+2), with A6=36Cstar^2/A3+2304(4M+2C_f C)^2. A finite-sample fallback uses the clipped-loss bound 4M^2.
ideas.conditions: The printed preceding tail has m1 rather than sqrt(m1); this is a weakening for m1>=1. Small-m1 handling requires valid positive logarithms and adjusted constants.

ideas.title: Clipped empirical-risk estimator
ideas.statement: Minimize empirical squared risk over H_R,n on empirical distributions, then clip predictions to [-M,M] using pi_M. The final estimator is pi_M phi_Dhat,R,n.
ideas.conditions: Labels and the regression function are bounded by M; compactness gives ERM existence, not an efficient optimization algorithm.

ideas.title: Two-stage distribution regression
ideas.statement: First-stage pairs (mu_i,y_i), i=1,...,m1, are iid from meta-distribution rho on P(Omega) x R. Each unobserved mu_i generates iid x_i,j; observations use empirical measures muhat_i=(1/m2,i) sum_j delta_x_i,j.
ideas.conditions: Omega is compact in R^d; input distributions cannot be observed directly.

ideas.title: Universal query mesh has dimensional cost
ideas.statement: A uniform query mesh lets kernel evaluations replace arbitrary RKHS functional parameters, but its (log n)^d query factor makes the construction impractical in high-dimensional cases.
ideas.conditions: Universal approximation-oriented mesh; empirical task-specific query sets may be much smaller.

ideas.title: Universal and integrally strictly positive definite kernels
ideas.statement: Universality means H_k is dense in C(Omega). Integral strict positive definiteness means integral integral k(x,y)dmu(x)dmu(y)>0 for every nonzero finite signed Borel measure mu; the paper cites their equivalence on compact Omega. Universal kernels make the kernel mean map injective and MMD a metric.
ideas.conditions: Mercer kernel on compact Omega; examples listed are Gaussian, Laplacian, inverse multiquadrics and Matern.

ideas.title: Scaled dot-product attention and positionwise FNN
ideas.statement: Background single-head attention weights values W_v x_j by softmax of <W_q x_i,W_k x_j>/sqrt(d_in), then applies a two-layer positionwise FNN.
ideas.conditions: The analyzed architecture is shallow and scalar-output; this motivational expression does not itself establish the later universal-kernel conditions.

ideas.title: Appendix Lemma 5: universal-kernel MMD metrizes weak convergence
ideas.statement: On a compact metric Omega, a universal kernel k makes gamma_k metrize weak convergence of probability measures (attributed to Sriperumbudur et al., 2010). Approximate arbitrary g in C(Omega) by gprime in H_k to bound |integral g d(Pn-P)|<=2epsilon+||gprime||_Hk gamma_k(Pn,P).
ideas.conditions: The reverse implication is stated as trivial from boundedness; uniformity over the unit RKHS ball requires more than boundedness alone, e.g. continuity/compactness of the kernel structure.

ideas.title: Injectivity proof via a feature-weighted kernel
ideas.statement: Define ktilde(x,y)=f(x)k(x,y)f(y) and signed measure P_f(E)=integral_E f dP. Nonvanishing bounded f preserves nonzero finite signed measures, so universality of k makes ktilde integrally strictly positive definite. The attention difference norm equals the ktilde MMD, yielding injectivity.
ideas.conditions: Same compact-domain/nonvanishing-feature assumptions as Theorem 1. Equation (9) drops squared norm exponents in its final lines; the intended squared-norm identity is clear from the preceding double integrals.

ideas.title: Deterministic document rendering
ideas.statement: Each document maps to an image pi=R(di). With font f, canvas width w, padding m, average character width c(f), and line height ell(f), the line capacity is M=floor((w-2m)/c(f)). Wrapping WM(di) gives ni lines sij of at most M characters; height hi=2m+ni*ell(f), and pi=Draw(w,hi,{sij},f), Equations (3)-(7).
ideas.conditions: The same deterministic rendering parameters apply before query-conditioned resizing.

ideas.title: Precompute query-independent passage images
ideas.statement: Rendering is deterministic and independent of the query, so passage images can be precomputed offline; the authors characterize its inference overhead as negligible.
validity_flags: No isolated numerical rendering-overhead measurement is supplied.

ideas.title: Structured compression-factor policy
ideas.statement: The compressor samples a structured response y~pi_theta(.|q,P) and parses factors ci>=1 for all N images, Equation (8). It uses Qwen3-VL-2B as its backbone.

ideas.title: Image scaling from compression factors
ideas.statement: Each image dimension is multiplied by 1/sqrt(ci), so image area and the intended visual-token count fall by a factor ci.
ideas.conditions: ci>=1; proportionality is the paper’s idealized token model.
validity_flags: Practical patching/resizing constraints can discretize actual token counts; no exact universal token-count identity is proven.

ideas.title: GRPO clipped compressor objective
ideas.statement: For G sampled compressor outputs, Ahat_k=(rk-mean r)/(std r+delta). Equation (10) minimizes L=-E[(1/G) sum_k (1/|yk|) sum_t (min(rho_kt*Ahat_k,clip(rho_kt,1-epsilon,1+epsilon)*Ahat_k)-beta*D_KL_kt)], with per-token rho=pi_theta/pi_theta_old conditioned on q, earlier response tokens and P; KL compares current and reference policies.
ideas.conditions: Compressor training; generator remains fixed. GRPO itself is cited background, adapted here to compression.
validity_flags: Source does not report all optimizer, epsilon, beta or delta hyperparameters.

ideas.title: Task, compression and format reward
ideas.statement: The overall reward is r=r_task+lambda*r_comp*I(inject)+alpha*r_format, Equation (11). The fixed generator answers from the resized images, and compression reward is injected only at sparse training intervals to stabilize early training.
validity_flags: Sparse injection schedule and reward weights are not numerically specified in the paper.

ideas.title: Binary downstream-correctness reward
ideas.statement: The compressor receives r_task=1 if the fixed generator prediction a_hat equals ground truth a_star, otherwise 0, Equation (12).
validity_flags: Correctness reward encourages preservation but does not guarantee preservation for every passage or unseen query.

ideas.title: Correctness-gated logarithmic compression reward
ideas.statement: Equation (13) sets r_comp=(1/N) sum_i log(ci) only when r_task=1; otherwise r_comp=0. This prevents rewards for aggressive compression that causes an incorrect answer, and logarithms reduce preference for extreme factors.
validity_flags: Reward design limits one incentive to degenerate compression but supplies no formal guarantee against all failure modes.

ideas.title: Format reward and malformed-output gate
ideas.statement: Equation (14) gives a valid compression-template response r_format=1, otherwise 0. Invalid responses receive zero overall reward and skip the generator call.
validity_flags: Paper does not enumerate the full valid-template grammar or quantify the claimed reliability improvement.

ideas.title: Inverse compression factor as reranking score
ideas.statement: A passage relevance score is si=1/ci; sorting by si makes the compressor a reranker without a new module or training objective. The policy has jointly observed all retrieved passages.
ideas.conditions: Higher si means less compression and nominally more relevance; ties and score calibration are not specified.

ideas.title: Five medical knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks
ideas.statement: Evaluation uses MedQA (12,723 four-option USMLE questions), MedMCQA (over 194k entrance-exam questions, 2,400 topics and 21 subjects), PubMedQA (yes/no/maybe abstract questions), BioASQ yes/no subset, and MMLU-Med medical subjects.
ideas.conditions: Dataset descriptions are background; actual train/test choices continue on physical page 6.

ideas.title: Heterogeneous MedOmniKB retrieval protocol
ideas.statement: MedOmniKB supplies five knowledge sources: textbooks, clinical guidelines, research articles, encyclopedia entries and structured knowledge graphs. Retrieval takes top-k=3 per source for up to 15 candidate documents mixing free text and graph-derived content.
ideas.conditions: Medical QA experiments; retrieval repeated for each train and test question.

ideas.title: Medical training splits and answer evaluation
ideas.statement: The paper retains single-answer multiple-choice questions, combines training splits of MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA and BioASQ, and evaluates selected-option accuracy on all five benchmarks including nine medicine-related MMLU subjects.
validity_flags: Actual retained train/test counts, aggregation weights, and conversion details for yes/no/maybe tasks are not enumerated.

ideas.title: RAGOCR model and training settings
ideas.statement: Training uses Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking with GRPO, group size G=4, AdamW learning rate 5e-6 and cosine schedule. Eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs are split four for policy training and four for the frozen reward generator. The default generation backbone is Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking.

ideas.title: Naive, full-resolution and static optical baselines
ideas.statement: Naive RAG concatenates retrieved text with the query. Visual RAG renders every passage and sends full-resolution images without further compression. Static OCR Compress applies the same factor to all images, equal to RAGOCR’s average factor.
ideas.conditions: Shared Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking generator.

ideas.title: Text and visual Qwen reranking baselines
ideas.statement: Qwen3-Reranker-4B reranks text and Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B reranks passage images; each retains top-k=5 documents for the shared generator. Table 1 accuracy in BioASQ/MedMCQA/MedQA/MMLU/PubMedQA order: text reranker 68.41/48.25/46.50/59.41/57.60 (aggregate 54.52); visual reranker 70.33/50.00/64.02/64.37/52.80 (aggregate 60.49).

ideas.title: Text-compression comparison backbones
ideas.statement: LongLLMLingua, Provence, EXIT and FaviComp compress retrieved text before the common Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking generator. OSCAR uses released jointly trained compressor/generator checkpoints with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 or Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501.
validity_flags: OSCAR differs in generator architecture, size and joint-training pipeline, confounding direct method-only comparisons.

ideas.title: Main optical compression accuracy and token savings
ideas.statement: Section 4.3 reports RAGOCR accuracy 61.47% with 2,284 RAG input tokens per case, versus naive RAG 44.63% and 17,914 tokens: 16.84 percentage points higher and approximately 87% fewer input tokens.
ideas.conditions: Five medical benchmarks; default 15 retrieved passages and shared Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking generator.
validity_flags: Table 1 on physical page 7 instead prints RAGOCR average 62.51%; discrepancy remains unresolved.
Token reduction counts RAG input, not measured end-to-end runtime or full compressor overhead.

ideas.title: Token and accuracy tradeoffs against text compression
ideas.statement: The prose reports LongLLMLingua 8,813 tokens and 53.70% accuracy, Provence 3,036 tokens and 58.53%, EXIT 53.57% while retaining the most tokens among compression methods, and FaviComp about 16% retained-size ratio with substantially reduced accuracy (Table 1: 53.49%). Table 1 BioASQ/MedMCQA/MedQA/MMLU/PubMedQA scores: LongLLMLingua 71.61/50.17/43.05/54.82/58.80; Provence 63.04/52.58/60.41/64.83/47.20; EXIT 77.37/51.42/39.43/54.27/56.00; FaviComp 64.71/46.75/52.32/55.00/51.80.
ideas.conditions: Shared generator; input token figures are the paper’s reported averages.
validity_flags: Prose conclusions about why particular methods underperform are hypotheses; no mechanism-isolation test is reported.

ideas.title: OSCAR backbone-capacity comparison
ideas.statement: The prose reports OSCAR-24B at 61.93% and OSCAR-7B at 45.17%, describing their input-size ratio as similar to FaviComp and OSCAR-24B as having the fewest input tokens. Table 1 BioASQ/MedMCQA/MedQA/MMLU/PubMedQA scores are 77.62/35.75/34.89/50.37/31.80 for OSCAR-7B and 80.31/51.00/60.22/67.71/51.20 for OSCAR-24B.
validity_flags: Different backbone capacity and training confound causal attribution to soft compression; exact OSCAR token counts are not supplied.
Whether OSCAR-24B exceeds RAGOCR depends on unresolved 61.47-versus-62.51 RAGOCR aggregate discrepancy.

ideas.title: Full-resolution rendering helps; uniform compression degrades
ideas.statement: Naive RAG, Visual RAG and Static OCR Compress achieve reported aggregate accuracies 44.63%, 57.16% and 55.02%, respectively. Rendering alone improves accuracy by 12.53 points, while uniform image compression reduces it by 2.14 points. In Table 1 column order BioASQ/MedMCQA/MedQA/MMLU/PubMedQA, Naive RAG scores 61.76/40.75/36.14/41.32/56.00; Visual RAG 64.45/46.00/60.33/64.19/49.20; Static OCR Compress 61.13/44.58/58.99/62.53/44.00.
ideas.conditions: Same generator, retrieved knowledge and rendering pipeline.
validity_flags: Accuracy differences alone do not establish a general information-theoretic density claim or universal necessity of adaptive compression.

ideas.title: RAGOCR per-benchmark accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 1 reports RAGOCR accuracy (%) BioASQ 71.36, MedMCQA 45.75, MedQA 69.21, MMLU 68.87 and PubMedQA 58.00; the printed aggregate is 62.51. RAGOCR has the highest MedQA and MMLU values in this table, but does not win every dataset.
ideas.conditions: Default Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking; OSCAR exceptions use Mistral variants.
validity_flags: Aggregate inconsistency: Sections 4.3, 4.5 and 4.6 use 61.47 instead of Table 1’s 62.51.
Aggregation weights and sample counts are not reported; no confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

ideas.title: SlideVQA multimodal training and evaluation
ideas.statement: SlideVQA instances contain 20 slides with interleaved text and visuals; evidence lies on one to three slides and answers are short free-form spans. A compressor is trained on SlideVQA training data with the same GRPO procedure. Comparison uses full-resolution Visual RAG, uniform Static OCR Compress and Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B retaining ten of twenty slides.
ideas.conditions: All methods use Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking.
validity_flags: This is in-domain SlideVQA compressor training, not demonstrated zero-shot transfer from medical data.

ideas.title: Adaptive compression improves SlideVQA
ideas.statement: Table 2 scores (EM/F1/ANLS, percent scale): Visual RAG 57.86/69.80/65.45; Static OCR Compress 52.60/63.53/60.13; visual reranker 59.59/71.43/67.48; RAGOCR 61.59/73.41/68.96. RAGOCR leads all three metrics, improving EM by 3.73 points over Visual RAG and 2.00 over the reranker.
ideas.conditions: SlideVQA-trained compressor and shared Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking.
validity_flags: Fewer visual tokens are asserted without numerical SlideVQA token counts; no statistical uncertainty is reported.

ideas.title: SlideVQA preservation case
ideas.statement: Figure 3 illustrates a question about circles versus squares in a photograph background on the “Meet our panelist” slide. It reports preserving image 4 nearly at original resolution while substantially shrinking the other slides; the illustrated RAGOCR answer identifies squares versus the contrasted circles answer.
validity_flags: Illustrative single case, not a distributional result or independent verification of fine-grained visual recognition.

ideas.title: Dedicated reranking followed by adaptive optical compression
ideas.statement: R&R first reranks retrieved passages with Qwen3-Reranker-4B, then renders the selected documents and applies RAGOCR. The paper reports weighted accuracy 63.60%, compared with text reranker 54.52% and standalone RAGOCR 61.47%. Table 3 R&R benchmark accuracies are BioASQ 73.7, MedMCQA 51.3, MedQA 67.6, MMLU 70.8 and PubMedQA 61.6.
ideas.conditions: Reranker-filtered subset and default generator; R&R improves aggregate but MedQA is below standalone RAGOCR.
validity_flags: Standalone RAGOCR aggregate conflicts with Table 1’s 62.51; reported weighted averages cannot be reconstructed without weights.
Complementary document-utility explanations are interpretations, not an isolated causal test.

ideas.title: RAGOCR compression factors as a standalone reranker
ideas.statement: The Filter experiment ranks by ascending compression factor and keeps the same count as Qwen3-Reranker-4B (five passages). Its reported weighted accuracy is 59.15% versus 54.52% for the text reranker. Table 3 Filter scores are BioASQ 68.2, MedMCQA 49.0, MedQA 61.8, MMLU 63.7 and PubMedQA 52.6.
validity_flags: The prose says comparable or superior on four of five benchmarks; printed values are strictly superior on three and lower on two. “Comparable” is not quantified.
Claimed listwise benefit is an explanatory interpretation; model modality and size also differ.

ideas.title: Joint visual observation yields listwise ranking signal
ideas.statement: Because RAGOCR observes all rendered passages together with the query, ranking by its factors is effectively listwise, whereas the compared Qwen reranker scores documents independently. The authors propose render-then-rank as a direction for VLM reasoning over text passages.
ideas.conditions: This description concerns joint scoring context, not explicit supervised relevance labels or calibrated scores.

ideas.title: Adaptive compression after compressor-based filtering
ideas.statement: Applying optical compression after Filter produces reported weighted accuracy 60.10%; Table 3 scores are BioASQ 64.8, MedMCQA 49.8, MedQA 65.6, MMLU 68.7 and PubMedQA 44.8. It improves MedQA and MMLU over Filter but falls below R&R’s 63.60% overall.
validity_flags: The proposed explanation that filtering loses passages a dedicated reranker would preserve is not verified by a passage-level error analysis.

ideas.title: Set thresholds from the current magnitude-projection residual
ideas.statement: For the non-atomic examples, the threshold is dynamically set to tau=2 sigma, where sigma=rms(|rho-P_m rho|).
ideas.conditions: Original experiment setting; the prose gives one tau rule without explicitly resolving the two thresholds tau1 and tau2 appearing in the gradient update.

ideas.title: Wider rendering canvases improve aggregate accuracy
ideas.statement: At font size f=12, canvas widths 400/800/1600 yield mean heights 1703/918/484 and reported weighted accuracies 59.85/61.47/62.74%. Table 4 per-benchmark values in BioASQ/MedMCQA/MedQA/MMLU/PubMedQA order are 58.31/51.50/66.77/68.23/56.40 for width 400; 71.36/45.75/69.21/68.87/58.00 for width 800; 68.93/53.25/65.04/70.80/62.40 for width 1600.
ideas.conditions: Fixed font size 12; varying maximum canvas width changes aspect ratio.
validity_flags: No shape-specific token counts or controlled vision-encoder mechanism test are given.
Width-800 aggregate 61.47 conflicts with Table 1’s 62.51 for the same printed per-benchmark values.

ideas.title: Horizontal text layout may better suit visual patches
ideas.statement: The authors hypothesize that wider canvases align better with vision-encoder patch processing by placing more characters per row, reducing row count and producing locally coherent visual representations.
validity_flags: Mechanistic interpretation from aspect-ratio ablation, not an established theoretical result.

ideas.title: Unifying retrieval, compression and ranking
ideas.statement: The conclusion proposes future exploration of a unified retrieve-compress-rank paradigm, motivated by compression ratios that also encode relevance and by successful visual/text multimodal experiments.
validity_flags: Proposed research direction rather than a fully implemented unified retrieval system.

ideas.title: Scope and reporting limits of the evidence
ideas.statement: Evidence consists of five medical QA tasks using MedOmniKB and a separately trained SlideVQA compressor. The paper reports point accuracies and token counts for selected methods, with no formal information-preservation theorem, error bars, latency study or complete training hyperparameter specification. The conclusions should be interpreted within those demonstrated settings.
validity_flags: Extractor synthesis from complete source audit, not a separate author-stated limitations section.
No test-example counts or weighted-average formula are supplied; Table 1/prose conflict remains.

ideas.title: Stability and atom-density criteria for comparing algorithms
ideas.statement: The authors test periodic unit cells with sparse atomic charges. They assess stability after distributed noise, salt-and-pepper noise and a single large added charge, plus convergence from arbitrary initial phases. Increasing atom count makes convergence slower and eventually causes algorithms to fail; the preferred method works at the highest atom-to-measurement ratio.
ideas.conditions: Original numerical testing of HIO, SF, DM, HPR, RAAR and variants; no full per-method performance table or perturbation amplitudes is given.

ideas.title: Alternate Fourier consistency and sparsification
ideas.statement: A simple phase-retrieval iteration is rho_(n+1)=P_m O rho_n for a threshold, soft-threshold or squaring operator O. The paper treats these O operators as projectors with an acknowledged abuse of notation.
ideas.conditions: Background algorithm family; convergence is heuristic in the magnitude-only nonconvex setting.

ideas.title: Error-reduction baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)=P_s P_m rho_n.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: Generalize atomicity to other and redundant dictionaries
ideas.statement: The paper proposes replacing point atoms with sparse dictionaries of curves, beams or protein-fold descriptors, and using redundant representations if they describe the object with fewer terms.
ideas.conditions: Background/synthesis of compressed-sensing ideas; the paper does not establish recovery guarantees for every redundant dictionary. Fourier-amplitude-and-phase results motivate, but do not prove, magnitude-only recovery.

ideas.title: Proposed scope beyond atomic resolution
ideas.statement: The authors conclude that phase retrieval need not require atomic resolution or the finite-signal-bandwidth assumption, and propose crystal diffraction at arbitrary resolution when a suitable compressible representation exists.
ideas.conditions: Original conclusion motivated by sparse-atom and gradient-phantom simulations, with no general theorem for arbitrary objects, bases, noise or sampling geometries.

ideas.title: Averaged successive-reflection baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)=0.5[R_s R_m+I]rho_n.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: Espresso improves observed atomic-retrieval success
ideas.statement: Figure 3 compares charge flipping, Espresso and positivity-enforced Espresso on a 64 by 64 periodic unit cell containing 160 atoms of values 1–3. With beta=0.5 and thresholds 0.5 for charge flipping and 0.4 for Espresso, the two Espresso curves reach roughly 90% success by 10,000 iterations versus roughly 70% for charge flipping. Positive Espresso improves faster early, while the variant without positivity approaches it late.
ideas.conditions: Original simulation; plotted rates are approximate visual readings, not exact tabulated values. The figure labels thresholds optimal but provides no trial count, error bars, seed specification or explicit success tolerance. The prose claim of outperforming all alternatives is broader than the three curves displayed.

ideas.title: Sampling geometry determines autocorrelation recovery in simulations
ideas.statement: The paper reports exact sparse-autocorrelation recovery for random Fourier sampling and limited-angle tomography. Regular Bragg sampling at every other two Fourier components in each dimension fails to recover the unaliased autocorrelation, while randomly reduced Bragg observations and radially averaged powder data recover an aliased autocorrelation.
ideas.conditions: Simulations illustrated in Figure 2. Powder example uses an oblique unit cell to reduce peak overlap, averaging approximately ten overlapping peaks per radial shell; no repeated-trial numerical error statistics are given.

ideas.title: Hybrid projection-reflection baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)=0.5[R_s(R_m+(beta-1)P_m)+I+(1-beta)P_m]rho_n.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: Sparse autocorrelation gives a quadratic sampling upper bound
ideas.statement: Theorem 2.2, attributed to Moravec, Romberg and Baraniuk, prints K > C n_a^2 log(4M/n_a^2) for random Fourier-magnitude measurements of an n_a-sparse object. The argument uses an autocorrelation with at most n_a^2 nonzero terms; the prose summarizes this as exact autocorrelation recovery, not a general uniqueness proof for the original object.
ideas.conditions: Random measurements and sparse autocorrelation. M is not defined locally. The theorem wording says the object can be recovered, whereas subsequent explanation and homometric examples warrant the narrower autocorrelation interpretation.

ideas.title: Sparse autocorrelation reconstruction with SPARCO and SPGL1
ideas.statement: The experiment simulates atomic objects and attempts to reconstruct autocorrelation from masked Fourier intensities using sparse optimization, Fourier transforms, masks, and radial averaging. The prose names SPARCO for constructing operators and SPGL1 for quickly reaching a root. Equation 4 literally prints min |rho|_1 subject to |F a|^2=I_k, while defining a as the object autocorrelation.
ideas.conditions: Numerical experiment; equation mixes rho in the objective with a in the constraint and squares the autocorrelation transform. The extraction preserves this notation without endorsing it as a consistent implementation specification. References 14–15 list SPGL1 and a Pareto-frontier paper, creating an additional prose/citation-label mismatch.

ideas.title: Generalized projection for unresolved intensities
ideas.statement: For powder diffraction, partial coherence or broadband illumination, an averaging operator A generalizes the Fourier projector to tilde(rho)(k) sqrt[I(k_A)/(A|tilde(rho)(k)|^2)], with k_A indexing the measured intensity receiving contribution from mode k.
ideas.conditions: Background attributed to reference 30. The measured data combine intensities; treatment of a vanishing averaged denominator is not specified.

ideas.title: Fourier-localized sparsifying bases may fail
ideas.statement: The paper tests the conjecture that compressive phase retrieval extends beyond real-space sparsity, but warns that not every basis works: preliminary curvelet tests suggest failure when basis elements are too localized in Fourier space.
ideas.conditions: Original preliminary observation referencing curvelet construction in reference 31; no formal criterion, numerical test details or general impossibility theorem is supplied.

ideas.title: Basis pursuit from incomplete complex Fourier measurements
ideas.statement: Equations 2–3 minimize the l1 norm sum_x |rho(x)| subject to matching the measured complex Fourier coefficients on Omega. Under the sparse-recovery conditions cited in the paper, this requires no prior knowledge of support, nonzero count, locations, or amplitudes.
ideas.conditions: Complex Fourier measurements include phase; this convex statement alone does not solve magnitude-only phase retrieval.

ideas.title: Espresso uses a residual mask and optional positivity mask
ideas.statement: Espresso defines S1=1[|P_m rho-rho|>tau1], S2=1[P_m rho>0], and rho_(n+1)=(S1 AND S2)(P_m rho_n)+(1-S1)rho_n-beta P_m rho_n. If positivity cannot be enforced, S2 is set identically to one.
ideas.conditions: Original heuristic designed to remain usable after relaxing positivity or changing the sparsifying representation. S1 and S2 are elementwise binary masks; beta and threshold require selection.

ideas.title: Charge flipping can cancel sparse wrong peaks to first order
ideas.statement: If the threshold isolates only the distributed (a*/2)f(x0) component, flipping it and reapplying the magnitude projector gives P_m[rho+(a/2)delta(x-x0)+(a*/2)f(x0)]=rho+O(a^2). The paper concludes that a few wrong peaks can then be corrected easily, but explicitly limits the result to local convergence.
ideas.conditions: Original first-order argument for a specific threshold-separation regime around the solution; it is not a convergence guarantee from arbitrary initial phases.

ideas.title: Replace sparsifying projection with a doubled reflection step
ideas.statement: The paper defines R=2O-I and forms rho_(n+1)=P_m R rho_n. It describes the charge-flipping strategy as doubling the real-space step and reports improved convergence range relative to simple alternating projections.
ideas.conditions: Background reflection strategy; subsequent Appendix A supplies only a local perturbation explanation, not a global proof. For hard thresholding R preserves above-threshold components and flips below-threshold components.

ideas.title: Use image compressibility for phase retrieval without support or atomic resolution
ideas.statement: The proposed approach replaces reliance on finite-support sampling or atomic-resolution data with an assumption that the image has a sparse or compressible representation. Intended applications include tomography, crystallography, powder diffraction, small-angle scattering, and random Fourier-magnitude measurements.
ideas.conditions: Original proposal; listed applications are intended scope rather than separate validated experiments.

ideas.title: Quadratic autocorrelation sparsity is a worst-case estimate
ideas.statement: The paper notes that n_a^2 autocorrelation sparsity is a worst case, and says a connected object can have autocorrelation support growing linearly with object support, to twice the object size.
ideas.conditions: Background attributed to reference 13. The precise geometric and dimensional meaning of twice the size is not specified, so the statement is retained as a qualitative source claim.

ideas.title: Atomic direct methods and their scaling constraints
ideas.statement: Crystallographic direct methods constrain a molecule to finitely many atoms. The paper states that successful ab initio retrieval requires atomic resolution and approximately five strong peaks per atom, with deteriorating scalability because strong reflections decrease as atom count increases.
ideas.conditions: Background characterization of direct methods; approximate five-peak criterion is a source claim rather than a universally proven boundary here.

ideas.title: Difference-map baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)={I+beta P_s[(1+gamma_s)P_m-gamma_s I]-beta P_m[(1+gamma_m)P_s-gamma_m I]}rho_n.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: Fourier-magnitude projection
ideas.statement: The magnitude projector is P_m=F^(-1) tilde(P_m) F, where tilde(P_m) tilde(rho)(k)=sqrt(I(k)) tilde(rho)(k)/|tilde(rho)(k)|. It replaces estimated amplitudes with measured amplitudes while retaining current Fourier phases and transforms back to real space.
ideas.conditions: Background projection assumes individually resolved Fourier measurements; treatment of a zero estimated amplitude is not specified.

ideas.title: Apply Espresso jointly to the two gradient components
ideas.statement: In gradient space, for j in {x,y}, partial_j rho_(n+1)=(S1 AND S2)(partial_j P_m rho_n)+(1-S1)(partial_j rho_n)-beta partial_j P_m rho_n. The printed masks are S1=1[sqrt(|partial_x P_m rho-rho|^2+|partial_y P_m rho-rho|^2)>tau1] and S2=1[sqrt(|partial_x P_m rho|^2+|partial_y P_m rho-rho|^2)>tau2]. The two gradient components may alternatively use their own supports.
ideas.conditions: Original method. The printed masks subtract un-differentiated rho from derivatives, and S2 is asymmetric between x and y. These potential source errors are preserved; no corrected implementation is inferred.

ideas.title: Recover the object from compressed gradients with a regularized pseudoinverse
ideas.statement: Equation 12 reconstructs rho=F^(-1)[(tilde(D_x)^dagger F(partial_x rho)+tilde(D_y)^dagger F(partial_y rho))/(tilde(D_x)^dagger tilde(D_x)+tilde(D_y)^dagger tilde(D_y)+epsilon)].
ideas.conditions: Original use of a regularized gradient pseudoinverse; epsilon is called a regularization term but no numerical value is provided, and handling of the gradient-undetermined constant component is not specified.

ideas.title: Represent a non-atomic object by sparse discrete gradients
ideas.statement: The non-atomic test sparsifies the gradient of a Shepp–Logan phantom. A same-size two-dimensional kernel D_x begins with -1,+1 and is otherwise zero; partial_x rho=D_x*rho=F^(-1)(tilde(D_x)tilde(rho)), and D_y is D_x transposed. The joint magnitude sqrt(|partial_x rho|^2+|partial_y rho|^2) is used for sparsification.
ideas.conditions: Original application of finite differences and gradient sparsity to phase retrieval; intended for images whose gradients, rather than pixel values, are sparse.

ideas.title: Hard-threshold sparsifying operator
ideas.statement: Unknown-support retrieval can replace the support projector with O_tau(x)=x when |x|>tau and zero otherwise.
ideas.conditions: Background sparsifier applied elementwise in the chosen representation; threshold is a method parameter.

ideas.title: Hybrid input-output baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)(r)=P_m rho_n(r) for r in S, and (I-beta P_m)rho_n(r) for r outside S.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: InternVL3.5 baseline routes visual resolution
ideas.statement: The paper describes InternVL3.5 as using Cascade Reinforcement Learning and a Visual Resolution Router to balance reasoning with inference efficiency.

ideas.title: Lensless diffraction imaging and the phase problem
ideas.statement: Diffraction imaging records scattering and numerically performs the inverse Fourier reconstruction normally performed by a lens; incomplete Fourier information and lost phases limit reconstruction despite eliminating optical aberrations.
ideas.conditions: Background explanation for coherent X-ray diffraction microscopy.

ideas.title: Magnitude reflection removes the localized first-order charge error
ideas.statement: Using R_m=2P_m-I in the single-charge perturbation model yields R_m rho_prime=rho-a* f(x0)+O(a^2), eliminating the remaining localized half-charge term while retaining a distributed error.
ideas.conditions: Original Appendix A local first-order rationale for doubling the projection step; depends on the same small-perturbation and nonzero-denominator assumptions as Equation A2.

ideas.title: Direct sparse-object retrieval is a nonconvex heuristic problem
ideas.statement: The proposed phase-retrieval algorithms exploit the additional fact that a recovered autocorrelation belongs to an even sparser object. The resulting magnitude-only problem is nonconvex, and the paper characterizes practical projection procedures as heuristics rather than globally convergent methods.
ideas.conditions: Original motivation with background limitation; local or observed convergence does not establish global recovery.

ideas.title: Nyquist-sampled magnitudes are usually but not universally unique
ideas.statement: The paper cites near-always uniqueness of Nyquist-sampled diffraction reconstruction, but gives homometric objects with identical Fourier magnitudes as exceptions: convolution of two non-centrosymmetric objects can generate distinct images with the same measured magnitudes.
ideas.conditions: Background attributed to references 1 and 4–7; uniqueness excludes homometric counterexamples and ordinary phase-retrieval ambiguities.

ideas.title: Identify better sparsifying bases and compressive algorithms
ideas.statement: Finding the optimal sparsifying basis and improving compressive algorithms are left open as avenues for low-resolution X-ray phasing.
ideas.conditions: Original future direction; current success is demonstrated only for sparse real-space atoms and the phantom gradient representation.

ideas.title: Richardson–Lucy treatment of partially overlapping intensities
ideas.statement: The paper suggests using Richardson–Lucy deconvolution on the intensities under the projector square root when measured contributions partially overlap.
ideas.conditions: Background suggestion citing references 16–18, not a separately quantified experiment in this paper.

ideas.title: Bragg sampling produces periodic phantom reconstructions
ideas.statement: The gradient-space Espresso example recovers repeated phantom structures under a Bragg sampling grid. The paper interprets the periodic crystal symmetry as being discovered from the diffraction sampling.
ideas.conditions: Original 128x128 phantom example. This is a periodic/aliased reconstruction consistent with Bragg measurements, not identification of a unique isolated phantom position.

ideas.title: Gradient-space phase retrieval reconstructs a phantom under incomplete masks
ideas.statement: Figure 4 shows gradient-based reconstruction of a Shepp–Logan phantom embedded in a 128 by 128 image using full Fourier sampling, a central beamstop mask and limited-angle tomography. Reconstructions retain recognizable phantom boundaries and internal structures, sometimes shifted across periodic image boundaries.
ideas.conditions: Original illustrative simulations; no quantitative image-quality scores, sampling fractions, iteration counts or repeat statistics are supplied. These images do not establish exact arbitrary-mask recovery.

ideas.title: Powder averaging retains dominant object outlines rather than full detail
ideas.statement: With radially averaged powder data and about twenty peaks overlapping per measured point, gradient-space Espresso recovers the object outline or dominant gradient terms. An oblique unit cell is used to reduce peak overlaps.
ideas.conditions: Original 128x128 Shepp–Logan simulation; the displayed powder reconstruction has repeated elliptical outlines with much less visible interior detail than the other masks. This is partial structural recovery, not a claim of exact full-image reconstruction.

ideas.title: Relaxed averaged alternating-reflection baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)=[0.5 beta(R_s R_m+I)+(1-beta)P_m]rho_n.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: Printed random Fourier sampling theorem
ideas.statement: Theorem 2.1 attributes to Candès, Romberg and Tao exact recovery by l1 minimization of an n_a-sparse length-N signal from uniformly random Fourier coefficients. It prints K < C n_a log N, C=22(delta+1), and success probability greater than 1-N^(-delta). The coefficient phases as well as amplitudes are observed.
ideas.conditions: The inequality is preserved exactly as printed. Its direction appears inconsistent with a sufficient minimum-measurement condition; this extraction does not repair or independently verify the cited theorem.

ideas.title: Solvent-flipping baseline
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists the iteration rho_(n+1)=R_s P_m rho_n.
ideas.conditions: Background comparison algorithm in support/Fourier-magnitude projection notation; R=2P-I and I is identity. The table gives symbolic beta/gamma parameters rather than a full tuning protocol.

ideas.title: Thresholding and flipping respond differently to distributed noise
ideas.statement: Appendix A argues that a small random perturbation with rms sigma below the smallest positive signal value can be separated by thresholding, while larger surviving noise leads to stagnation at a local minimum. For low perturbations, flipping below-threshold values merely changes their first-order signs and at best removes second-order O(a^2/||rho||) noise contributions.
ideas.conditions: Original local qualitative analysis. An rms bound alone is not a bound on each noise sample; the asserted clean threshold separation requires stronger separation conditions than explicitly stated.

ideas.title: Magnitude projection splits a misplaced charge into local and diffuse errors
ideas.statement: For rho_prime=rho+a delta(x-x0), Appendix A expands the magnitude projector to first order and obtains P_m rho_prime=rho+(a/2)delta(x-x0)-(a*/2)f(x0)+O(a^2), where f is the inverse Fourier transform of (tilde(rho)/tilde(rho)*) exp(-ikx0). The paper interprets the phase ratio as rapidly oscillating, dispersing half the perturbation through the unit cell.
ideas.conditions: Original local Taylor analysis about a known solution; assumes small perturbation and nonzero Fourier denominators. The diffuse nature of f is an assumption about the underlying phases. One intermediate expansion writes a where the next line writes a*, so complex-amplitude consistency is not fully explicit.

ideas.title: Soft thresholding for l1-promoted sparsity
ideas.statement: The soft-threshold operator is O_l1(x)=x-tau x/|x| for |x|>tau and zero otherwise. It promotes sparsity through l1 optimization; using a known l1 norm as a hard constraint is limited because that norm is rarely known.
ideas.conditions: Background operator attributed to reference 34; the discussion of an l1 constraint is attributed to Moravec et al.

ideas.title: Sparse and compressible representations
ideas.statement: A sparse signal has few nonzero coefficients in a suitable basis; a compressible signal can be accurately approximated by a few coefficients. The premise is that effective structure, rather than full signal length, determines required measurements; choosing a basis and defining an interesting signal are acknowledged to be partly circular.
ideas.conditions: Background examples include atoms, stars, wavelet coefficients and possible protein folds; suitability depends on the signal and representation.

ideas.title: Sayre squaring operator and direct-method tangent formula
ideas.statement: The squaring sparsifier is O_2(x)=x^2. Alternating P_m with O_2 is identified with the tangent formula of direct methods, where real-space squaring is performed through a Fourier-space autocorrelation.
ideas.conditions: Background operator attributed to reference 20; a sparsity-promoting heuristic rather than an ordinary metric projection.

ideas.title: Support constraint and sub-Nyquist restriction
ideas.statement: Support-based diffraction reconstruction imposes rho(r)=0 for r outside a known support S. The required sampling restricts direct use of these projection algorithms for sub-Nyquist geometries such as Bragg sampling of periodic crystals.
ideas.conditions: Assumes adequate sampling for the support constraint to be informative.

ideas.title: Support projection and automated support refinement
ideas.statement: The support projector keeps rho(r) inside S and zeros it outside. Shrinkwrap support refinement permits reconstruction without an externally imaged support by seeking a compact sparse object consistent with the measurements.
ideas.conditions: Background attributed to reference 19; automated support estimation still uses measurement consistency and compactness assumptions.

ideas.title: Uniform uncertainty permits sparse recovery and approximate noisy recovery
ideas.statement: The paper attributes to Candès and colleagues a uniform-uncertainty condition giving high-probability exact reconstruction for sparse signals and good approximation for compressible or noisy signals, including suitable Fourier measurements of real-space sparse objects.
ideas.conditions: Cited background from reference 12; requires suitable measurement selection and the stated uncertainty condition, not arbitrary Fourier masks.

ideas.title: Conversion between fragility measures
ideas.statement: Fragility obeys m=A+(ln 10)A²/D, where A=log10[tau_alpha(Tg)]−log10(tau_0); calculations use tau_0=10^−14 s and tau_alpha(Tg)=100 s.

ideas.title: GCC improves KV-cache and FLOP ratios versus Glyph
ideas.statement: Figure 4 normalizes the text backbone to 1.0 and plots Glyph/VIST2 (legend says VISTA) ratios: KV-cache reduction 3.2×/4.5×, prefilling 4.8×/4.0×, decoding throughput 4.4×/5.2×, FLOPs 2.5×/3.8×. Prose compares both at roughly fourfold compression and attributes VIST2’s lower prefill benefit to fixed compression and lack of enhanced encoder/adaptive compression.
validity_flags: Figure legend says VISTA rather than VIST2. Prose describes equivalent throughput despite plotted 4.4× versus 5.2×. Abstract says average 3× first-token speedup, 77% memory and 74% FLOP reductions, while figure gives 4× prefilling and 4.5× KV-cache ratio (~77.8%); workload, averaging and end-to-end accounting are underspecified. The page-2 over-75%-each claim disagrees with abstract FLOPs 74%.

ideas.title: Preservation of fundamental abilities is approximate
ideas.statement: The authors interpret math and CMMLU results as retaining reasoning and bilingual ability, but VIST2’s displayed general-task scores are below the corresponding pure-text Qwen3 backbones, so no-sacrifice language is qualitative rather than exact equality.
validity_flags: The interpretation attributes retained abilities to CoT-aware compression and bilingual curation without controlled causal ablations for those factors.

ideas.title: Math and Chinese knowledge scores remain near text backbones
validity_flags: The displayed Qwen3-VL MATH values are unusually higher than both text and VIST2 rows, but source provides no explanation; do not silently repair. No statistical uncertainty provided.

ideas.title: GLM4.5V baseline targets reasoning and document understanding
ideas.statement: GLM4.5V is described as a large-scale multimodal baseline for multidisciplinary reasoning and high-resolution document understanding.

ideas.title: Global context compression includes generated responses
ideas.statement: VIST2 defines global context compression as saving context tokens during both prefilling and autoregressive inference, repeatedly turning completed input and output text chunks into visual representations. Partial compression compresses human queries for prefill while responses remain uncompressed.

ideas.title: Glyph as a partial optical compression predecessor
ideas.statement: Glyph is cited as rendering millions of tokens into images and achieving 4× lossless compression through a visual encoder.
validity_flags: This is the citing paper’s description of Glyph, not independent verification of losslessness.

ideas.title: Hierarchical encoding compresses ordered chunks
ideas.statement: Hierarchical encoding partitions long text into ordered chunks and compresses each into dense representations; the authors motivate optical compression as an instance using text-rendered images.
validity_flags: The prose claim that preserving complete context prevents information loss is a motivation, not a proof of lossless encoding.

ideas.title: Long-context baseline results are drawn from prior reports
ideas.statement: Appendix A.3 says LongBench Table 4 baseline results are reported by Li et al. 2025a (AdmTree) and LooGLE Table 5 baseline results by Li et al. 2024b; these comparisons use publicly available evaluation results.
validity_flags: Imported baseline results may not share VIST2’s training, evaluation prompts, inference setup or hardware; equivalence is not established.

ideas.title: LongBench gains concentrate in document QA
ideas.statement: Table 4 gives VIST2-0.6B/4B/8B scores (single QA,multi QA,summarization,few-shot,code)=(36.8,39.5,25.2,54.1,58.4)/(41.5,44.2,28.1,60.5,64.9)/(45.2,49.8,30.4,65.2,66.5). VIST2-8B leads the listed single/multiple-document QA scores. AdmTree-7B yields (41.6,45.9,30.2,69.9,66.8); Qwen3-8B-FT has few-shot 71.4 and naive Qwen3-8B has summarization 59.4.
validity_flags: Narrative summarization score 69.5 conflicts with 30.4 in Table 4. Narrative lead across all subtasks conflicts with higher listed summarization/few-shot/code baselines. No uncertainty intervals or repeated-run statistics.

ideas.title: Example compresses 3784 prompt tokens to 1024 visual tokens
ideas.statement: Appendix C reports that its long-query example reduces 3784 original prompt tokens to 1024 visual tokens, illustrating prefill KV-cache savings alongside response compression.
ideas.conditions: One illustrative sample; effective ratio about 3.70× rather than a measured aggregate benchmark.
validity_flags: Example demonstrates mechanics, not controlled accuracy or memory measurement.

ideas.title: Long document example visually separates query and response chunks
ideas.statement: Figure 7 shows four compressed Chinese query blocks on gray backgrounds, with the final question in red, then a compressed assistant block and raw text continuation. The source document discusses AI history; the question asks whether Transformer generality and reduced CNN/RNN inductive biases become liabilities with scarce data or strong prior knowledge. The response illustrates continuation of an analysis after visual compression.
validity_flags: Qualitative illustration with unverified generated technical/medical claims in its example text; these are not treated as independent scientific findings of VIST2.

ideas.title: LooGLE includes heterogeneous long-context systems
ideas.statement: LooGLE compares GPT4 with 8k/32k, GPT3.5-turbo-16k, LlamaIndex, ChatGLM2-6B-32k, LongLLaMA-3B-Instruct-256k, RWKV-4-14B-raven-8k, LLaMA2-7B-32k-Instruct, and Claude3-opus-200k for QA.

ideas.title: LooGLE long dependency QA retains compressed-context quality
ideas.statement: For long dependency QA at 8k×4 context, VIST2 0.6B/4B/8B yield ROUGE-L 33.45/37.10/38.12 and GPT4_score 48.30/54.12/56.45. VIST2-8B metric vector is (9.42,1.78,40.12,14.22,38.12,11.45,85.34,56.45). GPT4-32k gives ROUGE-L 24.04 and GPT4_score 54.09, while Claude3-opus-200k gives 36.56 and 20.71.
validity_flags: No uncertainty intervals or repeated runs; model comparisons have heterogeneous contexts.

ideas.title: LooGLE paper summarization improves with scale
ideas.statement: For arXiv summarization at context 8k×4, VIST2 0.6B/4B/8B have ROUGE-L 26.15/28.52/29.75 and GPT4_score 81.20/86.15/88.42. The 8B metric vector (BLEU1,BLEU4,ROUGE1,ROUGE4,ROUGE-L,Meteor,BERT_score,GPT4_score) is (29.15,2.15,33.24,11.45,29.75,22.88,85.12,88.42), exceeding the listed GPT4-8k GPT4_score 85.42 and GPT3.5-turbo-16k 86.84.
ideas.conditions: Listed comparators span different model families and windows; no common training budget or uncertainty supplied.
validity_flags: GPT4_score evaluation procedure/version and statistical uncertainty not specified sufficiently for independent reproduction.

ideas.title: MiMo-VL baseline emphasizes multimodal reinforcement learning
ideas.statement: MiMo-VL is described as using reinforcement learning for general multimodal and agentic tasks.

ideas.title: MinerU2.5 decouples layout and local recognition
ideas.statement: MinerU2.5 is described as a two-stage framework separating global layout analysis from local content recognition for formulas and tables.
validity_flags: Baseline cites Wang2024 MinerU paper although model is labeled MinerU2.5; citation/version mapping not independently resolved.

ideas.title: Higher compression increases OCR training loss
ideas.statement: Figure 3 shows stage-2 loss curves at 0.6B, 4B and 8B for ratios 1,2,4,8,10,16. Loss decreases sharply early; lower ratios generally finish lower, while high-ratio curves flatten and then rise. Larger models tend to reach lower losses.
validity_flags: Plots are descriptive single curves with no uncertainty bands; training-budget axis conflicts with the stated at-most-1024^3 tokens on page 4.

ideas.title: OCR compression sweep with fixed 256 visual tokens
ideas.statement: WuDao text is split into L-token chunks rendered into images with 256 patches/tokens; L={256,512,1024,2048,2560,4096} gives ratios {1,2,4,8,10,16}. Training is reported as at most 1024^3 tokens; OCR evaluation uses a disjoint 1M-token portion and ROUGE-L.
validity_flags: Prose refers to OCR scores as Table 3, while they are Table 2; Figure 3 horizontal axes reach 10 billion tokens, conflicting with at-most-1024^3 (~1.074B) text budget.

ideas.title: OCR retention depends on model and compression ratio
ideas.statement: At ratios 2/4/8/10/16, ROUGE-L for VIST2-0.6B is .972/.983/.938/.915/.890, for 4B .961/.942/.970/.928/.905, and for 8B .981/.950/.975/.925/.912. DeepSeek-OCR gives .996/.941/.986/.947/.927 and Qwen3-VL-SFT .988/.946/.987/.930/.908; untuned Qwen3-VL is much lower (.521/.368/.318/.370/.302). Other OCR baselines are PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU2.5, and DotsOCR.
ideas.conditions: WuDao held-out 1M tokens; columns omit r=1, though training sweep includes it.
validity_flags: Scores are nonmonotonic and no uncertainty estimates are supplied.

ideas.title: OLM ablation claim conflicts with plotted labels
ideas.statement: Appendix D claims intermediate OLM pretraining improves VIST2-4B SFT stability and smooths loss convergence. Figure 5, however, labels the blue high oscillating curve with OLM (about 7–10 after the initial rise) and the smoothly falling magenta curve w/o OLM (about 5 toward 1.3). Thus the plotted labels contradict the prose interpretation.
validity_flags: Internal contradiction between prose and curve labels; caption task also conflicts with appendix and plot title. Cannot determine from source whether labels, caption or interpretation is wrong. No independent evidence of claimed OLM benefit.

ideas.title: Continue long documents from optical prefix
ideas.statement: OLM data comprises documents exceeding 8k tokens from Arxiv, Gutenberg and WuDao. Evaluation supplies the first 1k tokens and generates at most 4k output tokens, using what the authors call perplexity calculated by GPT-4.
validity_flags: GPT-4 perplexity access/calculation is unspecified; Table 3 labels third corpus Wikipedia rather than WuDao.

ideas.title: OLM predicts each chunk from earlier optical context
ideas.statement: OLM loss is −sum_i sum_(j=1)^|C_hat_i| log P_theta(u_j^i | {V_hat_k}_{k<i},u_<j^i): previous chunks contribute visual context, while earlier tokens within the current chunk remain text.
validity_flags: Prose references Eq. 2 as OLM objective although Eq. 2 earlier describes PCC.

ideas.title: Optical language modeling from compressed previous chunks
ideas.statement: VIST2 interleaves text chunks and their visual encoding, predicting the next text token using compressed visual tokens for earlier chunks, while retaining autoregressive text within the current chunk.
ideas.conditions: Within-chunk text conditioning and exact objective are specified on page 3.

ideas.title: Qwen3 and SigLIP2 sandwich architecture
ideas.statement: VIST2 combines a pretrained visual encoder and pretrained LLM through a trainable modal aligner; the implementation uses Qwen3 and SigLIP2.
validity_flags: Introduction calls connector a linear projection; page 3 specifies tanh affine projection and calls it a multilayer perceptron.

ideas.title: OLM continuation scores approach text-only backbones
ideas.statement: Table 3 (Arxiv/Gutenberg/Wikipedia) reports VIST2 versus Qwen3 as 4.98/4.25/4.02 versus 4.85/4.20/3.95 at 0.6B, 3.25/2.98/2.65 versus 3.22/2.95/2.70 at 4B, and 2.22/1.90/1.62 versus 2.15/1.88/1.65 at 8B. Qwen3-VL scores are 3.48/3.12/2.82 at 4B and 2.32/2.05/1.78 at 8B.
validity_flags: The OLM protocol on page 6 calls training corpora Arxiv/Gutenberg/WuDao, whereas this table labels the third evaluation column Wikipedia. The claim of 0.2–0.5 average advantage over VLM is not supported by these displayed differences (~.1–.23). GPT-4 perplexity procedure is underspecified.

ideas.title: Optical compression as the motivating representation
ideas.statement: The authors credit Li et al. 2025b’s optical-compression/token-efficiency idea as opening a more promising hierarchical encoding route, illustrated through prior OCR models and Glyph.

ideas.title: Ovis2.5 baseline structurally aligns vision and language
ideas.statement: Ovis2.5 is characterized as using structural alignment for high-resolution images and visual reasoning.

ideas.title: PaddleOCR-VL combines dynamic-resolution vision with ERNIE
ideas.statement: PaddleOCR-VL is described as a 0.9B OCR model integrating a NaViT-style visual encoder and ERNIE-4.5-0.3B, for parsing in 109 languages.

ideas.title: Input-only compression leaves long-generation context growth
ideas.statement: The authors argue PCC can enlarge the context window up to tenfold for long-text understanding, but its compression applies only to prefilling; long generation and multistep reasoning still require storing/generated-text context.
validity_flags: The up-to-10× claim is contextual motivation with no local quantitative derivation.

ideas.title: Partial compression renders only source chunks
ideas.statement: PCC partitions source X into n contiguous k-token chunks, renders each as a grayscale optical image V_i in R^(H×W×3), and conditions generation on its visual tokens plus uncompressed earlier response tokens.
validity_flags: Eq. 2 prints a sum of conditional probabilities and inconsistent L/chunk/visual-token indexing, rather than a normalized joint probability factorization.

ideas.title: Qwen3-VL baseline uses enhanced interleaved MROPE
ideas.statement: The paper describes Qwen3-VL as using enhanced interleaved MROPE for spatiotemporal modeling and native interleaved contexts up to 256K tokens.

ideas.title: Use long reasoning responses from DeepSeek distillation
ideas.statement: The instruction set filters AM-DeepSeek-R1-0528-Distilled for responses longer than 4096 tokens to add long-response training examples.

ideas.title: Choose fourfold compression for subsequent experiments
ideas.statement: The authors select r=4 after noting convergence below r=10 and unstable model performance at ratios greater than four, to make the OLM stage tractable.

ideas.title: Compress a residual segment only when it saves tokens
ideas.statement: A tail segment of length m is converted to beta visual tokens only if m>beta; otherwise it remains raw text to preserve fine information.

ideas.title: Context-state parity is even, odd or unbiased
ideas.statement: Parity is P(|ψ⟩,O)=bit(⟨ψ|O|ψ⟩). In the defined context-eigenstate family, full-weight Pauli expectations take +1,−1,0, corresponding to parity 0 (even), 1 (odd), or 0.5 (unbiased); observables outside the eigenstate context have zero expectation.
ideas.conditions: Context eigenstates and full-weight Pauli observables in the even-n construction; general arbitrary states can have intermediate expectations.

ideas.title: Reduce arbitrary Pauli parity to canonical Z parity
ideas.statement: Equation C2 indexes full-weight parity observables as Oβ′=Γβ′ Z^{⊗n} Γβ′†. Therefore P(|φ⟩,Oβ′)=P(Γβ′†|φ⟩,Z^{⊗n}), which allows analytic evaluation from index relationships.

ideas.title: Matching generator parity is XOR of flip bits
ideas.statement: If β=β′, rotation cancellation makes the measured observable the context generator, and Equation C5 gives P=⊕_{i=1}^{n−1} α_i, independent of z and s.
ideas.conditions: Context eigenstates with even n and the paper’s index convention.

ideas.title: Partially matching rotation indices imply unbiased parity
ideas.statement: If β and β′ share at least one ternary digit and differ in another, Oβ′ is outside the state’s context because a context observable either shares every generator factor or none. Equation C6 consequently gives P=0.5.
ideas.conditions: At least one equal and one unequal same-position ternary digit.

ideas.title: Closed-form parity when all rotation digits differ
ideas.statement: When β_i≠β′_i for every position, define zero-padded α=(α1,…,α(n−1),0) and J=2⃗−(β⊖₃β′). Equation C7 gives P=z⊕[(sum(J)+s)/2]⊕J·α. Integer middle term selects parity 0/1; the half-integer case is interpreted by the authors as unbiased parity 0.5.
ideas.conditions: All β digits differ from β′; half-integer case uses the intended unbiased convention rather than ordinary binary XOR.

ideas.title: Cache even and odd parity fingerprints
ideas.statement: For all z,α and all fully different-index patterns J, the authors precompute even/odd parity fingerprints, reporting 2×2^n×2^n bits of storage, to evaluate any context-eigenstate parity efficiently. This cache is used in the eight-qubit implementation.
ideas.conditions: Cache scales exponentially in n; count is as reported, with unbiased-case handling supplied by the parity convention.

ideas.title: Measure a single parity by basis rotation and bit counting
