ideas.statement: To measure Oβ′=Γβ′ Z^{⊗n} Γβ′†, apply Γβ′†, measure every qubit canonically, and count output ones; even/odd count produces observable outcome +1/−1. Retaining only this parity collapses n qubits for a single output bit.

ideas.title: Future improvements in agent architectures and tool design
ideas.statement: The conclusion proposes optimizing agent architectures and expanding tool designs toward intelligent maps and location-based services.

ideas.title: Calibration domain changes safety and utility
ideas.statement: Figure 12 compares HOD→MM-SafetyBench with MM-SafetyBench→MM-SafetyBench calibration/test transfer. At 20% sparsity, in-domain calibration gives roughly 98% DSR versus HOD’s 88%, both at ~83–84% utility accuracy. At 50%, in-domain DSR reaches ~100% but the displayed accuracy falls nearly to zero, while HOD retains ~94% DSR and ~77% accuracy. The authors interpret heterogeneous HOD calibration as more generalizable than narrow in-domain cues.

ideas.title: Stable Diffusion v1.5 evaluation with centralized and uncoded-latent baselines
ideas.statement: Simulations use pretrained stable-diffusion-v1-5. Baselines are centralized image generation followed by image transmission and MEG raw latent transmission without compression encoder/decoder, isolating codec gain.

ideas.title: FLARE plus notes accuracy with GPT-4o-mini
ideas.statement: FLARE->FLARE+NotesWriting F1/GPT-4 percentages: Fanout 35.1/14.2->42.3/22.2; FRAMES 26.3/23.7->27.7/29.8; Hotpot 34.8/39.0->34.5/45.8; MultiHop 28.9/65.7->30.2/66.6.
ideas.conditions: Theta=0.8; point estimates under adapted baseline.
validity_flags: Not all metrics improve: GPT Hotpot F1 and Llama MultiHop F1/judge score decrease, qualifying broad improvement claims.

ideas.title: Compression-meta-prompt paraphrases show stable means
ideas.statement: Compression main-task and additional-guideline paraphrases yield BBH averages94.01 and94.17 versus94.13 original; reported per-task95% interval quantities range0.32-1.64 points.

ideas.title: Code rate and codec tuning jointly affect PSNR
ideas.statement: Figure 8 generally shows higher PSNR for longer codes (larger fc), but fc=0.8 outperforms neighboring 0.7 and 0.9 because the authors conducted extra experiments and more carefully tuned the decoder hyperparameters at 0.8.
validity_flags: Unequal hyperparameter tuning across rates confounds a pure code-length comparison.

ideas.title: Illustrated multimodal jailbreak formats
ideas.statement: Appendix A depicts FigStep as a harmful typographic heading with blank numbered list completion, MM-SafetyBench as SD-only, typography-only and combined images, and JailbreakV as integrating these source examples with nature/noise/SD/blank images and LLM-generated logic/template/persuasion attacks.

ideas.title: Detailed refusal safety prompt
ideas.statement: The authors’ safety prompt covers sensitive, graphic, harmful or inappropriate input, explicitly including injuries, violence, alcohol, weapons and other distressing material; it requests the fixed refusal “Sorry, I cannot help you.” and prohibits description, interpretation or further details.
ideas.conditions: Exact paper template retained in evidence; broad content-triggered refusal framing.

ideas.title: FLARE plus notes accuracy with Llama-3.1-70B
ideas.statement: FLARE->FLARE+NotesWriting F1/GPT-4 percentages: Fanout 23.0/11.4->35.8/24.2; FRAMES 16.4/18.6->20.0/25.3; Hotpot 24.7/31.2->34.0/47.0; MultiHop 36.1/67.0->30.5/66.4.
ideas.conditions: Theta=0.8; point estimates under adapted baseline.
validity_flags: Not all metrics improve: GPT Hotpot F1 and Llama MultiHop F1/judge score decrease, qualifying broad improvement claims.

ideas.title: NextQA token, cost and latency profile
ideas.statement: Table 17 source profiles ordered accuracy %, input tokens/Q, output tokens/Q, dollars/run, dollars/Q, latency seconds/Q, KF/Q: Gemini Plain [72.70,1750,4.0,.53,.0005,5.70,1.51]; Gemini FullEvo [74.50,8207,1.3,2.47,.0025,5.84,1.51]; GPT Plain [73.20,576,5.1,.18,.0002,2.95,1.51]; GPT hybrid-3 [68.10,2244,4.8,.68,.0007,9.24,1.51].
ideas.conditions: Profiles copied as labelled rather than silently reconciled with Table 3. Gemini EgoSchema FullEvo 68.00 differs from Guide 68.40; GPT EgoPlan FullEvo 28.85 differs from Guide 29.39; NextQA GPT row explicitly uses hybrid-3 68.10. Evolution generally increases prompt tokens versus plain cascade.

ideas.title: Video-MME long token, cost and latency profile
ideas.statement: Table 17 source profiles ordered accuracy %, input tokens/Q, output tokens/Q, dollars/run, dollars/Q, latency seconds/Q, KF/Q: Gemini Plain [60.33,6111,10.8,1.67,.0019,14.56,5.43]; Gemini FullEvo [64.22,13420,2.3,3.63,.0040,13.66,5.41]; GPT Plain [55.89,5461,4.9,6.18,.0069,9.82,5.40]; GPT FullEvo [55.89,6307,3.8,7.13,.0079,12.58,5.40].
ideas.conditions: Profiles copied as labelled rather than silently reconciled with Table 3. Gemini EgoSchema FullEvo 68.00 differs from Guide 68.40; GPT EgoPlan FullEvo 28.85 differs from Guide 29.39; NextQA GPT row explicitly uses hybrid-3 68.10. Evolution generally increases prompt tokens versus plain cascade.

ideas.title: Reasoning skills retain cross-model utility
ideas.statement: The remaining eleven reasoning-pattern seed skills are reported to improve GPT-5.2 EgoSchema by 2.60 points without the format rule.

ideas.title: Automatically scored failure evolution can amplify biases
ideas.statement: A self-evolving bank may amplify systematic answer-key biases such as MC option position or answer-length priors over many update rounds. The authors propose confidence-gated memory and hygiene plus periodic human audits of skill diffs.

ideas.title: Epistemic prompt propagates factive-complement commitments
ideas.statement: The final entailment prompt treats factive complements as true, propagates their truth commitments upward through embedded attitudes without asserting truth of the factive-containing clause, and leaves non-factive attitudes noncommittal otherwise. It combines these commitments with semantic/hyponymic, necessary commonsense and lexical entailments, requiring attitude-holder identity unless justified by coreference or hypernymy.
ideas.conditions: Reported final optimizer-generated task prompt; describes the experimental artifact rather than an independently validated general rule.

ideas.title: Movie prompt prioritizes era, impact and concrete artistic links
ideas.statement: The final recommendation prompt prioritizes era only when at least75% of input films share a cohesive timeframe; otherwise it emphasizes impact and explicit narrative/stylistic parallels over vague themes. It favors culturally influential or innovative films, evaluates viable era-aligned options before cross-era choices, and permits stronger impact/artistic identity to outweigh partial genre or weak thematic matches subject to those era rules.
ideas.conditions: Reported final optimizer-generated task prompt; describes the experimental artifact rather than an independently validated general rule.

ideas.title: Audio utility depends on query and alignment
ideas.statement: Audio contributes complementary temporal and semantic evidence, but usefulness depends on acoustic grounding of the query, temporal alignment, and fusion design.
ideas.conditions: Audio is not uniformly beneficial; especially relevant to sound-related or visually ambiguous queries.

ideas.title: LLMs coordinate edge AI models
ideas.statement: Prior Edge AI [26] uses a framework that leverages large language models to coordinate edge AI models for user service.

ideas.title: Wireless edge placement increases generative service accessibility
ideas.statement: The AIGC service architecture [27] places generative models at the wireless edge to improve service accessibility despite their resource-intensive nature.

ideas.title: GAN compresses and recovers channel-state feedback
ideas.statement: Prior work [21] proposes a generative adversarial network to compress and recover feedback CSI, reducing signaling overhead.

ideas.title: Potential memorization confounds compression evaluation
ideas.statement: The authors argue that evaluation on texts possibly overlapping LLaMA training data can confound retrieval from compressed states with pre-existing model memory, and that win rate does not quantitatively characterize information loss.
validity_flags: Potential leakage is a concern raised by the authors, not a verified overlap audit.

ideas.title: Qualitative dense caption combines appearance and relative position
ideas.statement: For object box (199,133,81,20,19,52), Figure 2 generates a caption identifying a black chair to the right of another chair; the indicated object is highlighted in the displayed scene.
ideas.conditions: Single illustrated caption, not a quantitative localization or factuality check.

ideas.title: Charades-STA and QVHighlights evaluation setting
ideas.statement: Charades-STA has 9,848 videos averaging 30.6 s, 12,408 training and 3,720 test annotations, 8.1 s average moments and 7.22-word queries. QVHighlights has 10,148 150 s videos, 7,218 training and 1,150 validation queries, 24.6 s average moments and 11.3-word queries.
ideas.conditions: Reported dataset descriptions; evaluation uses recall, mAP and mIoU; QVHighlights is the main long-video benchmark.

ideas.title: query_memory retrieves relevant content from identified raw memory
ideas.statement: query_memory requires summary_id: integer and query: string. Once manage_context has created a summary ID, the tool loads its raw saved JSON messages, passes them and the query to a querier LLM, and returns relevant extracted information as a tool result.
ideas.conditions: Access is through LLM-mediated retrieval from the chosen stored segment.

ideas.title: ICAE baseline preserves compressed embeddings
ideas.statement: ICAE is the comparator because it is a soft prompt method using a small set of compressed-token embeddings and can decode them with the original LLM without decoder finetuning.

ideas.title: Short compressed prefix reduces decoding attention work
ideas.statement: Replacing the original context prefix with fewer compressed tokens reduces the number of previous tokens attended by question and generated-answer tokens, which the authors use to explain faster QA decoding.
ideas.conditions: Decoder computation argument; source does not provide a full end-to-end latency benchmark including compression.
validity_flags: Speed benefit argued mechanistically, not measured as an end-to-end throughput result.

ideas.title: Five QA benchmarks target different capabilities
ideas.statement: Evaluation uses ArxivQA and SQuAD for information extraction, RelationExtraction (RE) for relation extraction, HotpotQA for multi-hop reasoning, and RACE for reading comprehension. ArxivQA is newly introduced; the other datasets are pre-existing.

ideas.title: Authors attribute occasional quality gains to redundancy removal
ideas.statement: The authors explain some compression methods outperforming full recomputation by attention-based removal of semantically redundant information.
ideas.conditions: A proposed explanation of benchmark scores, without a controlled causal analysis separating eviction from other factors.

ideas.title: Move prior memory concatenation into the lower-frequency evolver
ideas.statement: VisualClaw explicitly retains the memory-example concatenation idea attributed to Reflexion, MemGPT and MetaClaw, but routes it to the lower-frequency skill-evolution prompt rather than the current answer prompt.

ideas.title: Evolution improves an offline eight-frame baseline
ideas.statement: For Gemini 3 Flash, Uniform-8 Plain → Uniform-8 FullEvo Guide accuracies are EgoSchema 60.60→73.60 (+13.00), Video-MME long 61.44→66.78 (+5.34), EgoPlan-Bench 37.96→50.11 (+12.15), and NextQA 77.70→81.20 (+3.50).

ideas.title: Four static video QA datasets
ideas.statement: Evaluation uses 500 EgoSchema examples with roughly three-minute ego clips; 923 EgoPlan-Bench planning entries described as single observations; 900 Video-MME long questions with 30+ minute content; and 1,000 NextQA short-clip causal/temporal examples.

ideas.title: Seed and evolved V-MME skill activations have similar hit rates
ideas.statement: On Video-MME long, 12 seed skills record 219 activations at 73% accuracy and the top three evolved skills 314 activations at 71%; authors interpret this as the seed bank providing much of the long-video gain.
ideas.conditions: Per-skill selected activation statistics are not randomized causal estimates of skill benefit.

ideas.title: Projected one-hour wearable streaming savings
ideas.statement: The paper extrapolates a one-hour 1-fps wearable session from 3,600 frames and about 3.9M full-frame input tokens to 5–20 uploads using edge filtering, attributing this to roughly 98% rejection.
ideas.conditions: Deployment projection, not a reported one-hour live wearable trial. 98% rejection of 3,600 gives about 72 retained frames; 5–20 uploads needs unspecified frame batching/query rates, so frame and API-call counts should not be equated.

ideas.title: Anthropic Skill Creator is the detailed experimental baseline
ideas.statement: The paper compares W2S with Anthropic Skill Creator (ASC), described as an official skill-construction workflow that turns interaction evidence into a reusable SKILL.md through structured interview and drafting.
ideas.conditions: ASC implementation/version, model, prompts, interview settings, and resource budget are not specified in the paper.

ideas.title: AutoSkill maintains skills across sessions
ideas.statement: AutoSkill abstracts repeated user requirements and interaction patterns into explicit maintainable skills that can be updated and injected across sessions.

ideas.title: Reported averages are not the unweighted means of the displayed type rows
ideas.statement: The arithmetic means of Table 3’s eight displayed type scores are 0.550125 (W2S) and 0.49225 (ASC), whereas its Average row is 0.503 and 0.455. The paper gives no weighting rule or type counts, so this could reflect weighted aggregation but cannot be reconciled from the supplied table alone.
ideas.conditions: Extractor arithmetic check, not an author admission or proof that the reported averages are wrong.

ideas.title: Agent Workflow Memory induces and retrieves workflows
ideas.statement: Agent Workflow Memory induces reusable workflows from past web-agent trajectories and retrieves them to guide future actions.

ideas.title: WSA evidence is separated by role and observation provenance
ideas.statement: Equation 4 partitions evidence into E_W (units/order), E_S (node functions/decisions), and E_A (tools, resources, checks, state, output contracts). Each statement is marked directly observed, inferred from repeated behavior, or unobserved; the reconstruction stage does not assign numerical support scores.
ideas.conditions: The abstract mentions confidence annotations, but this method section specifies categorical provenance and no numerical support scoring.

ideas.title: Over-compression and over-generalization are distinct reconstruction failures
ideas.statement: Over-compression collapses distinct branches or validation cases into broad instructions. Over-generalization invents unsupported workflow steps, criteria, or attachments. Path-aware generation is intended to reduce the former while evidence discipline limits the latter.

ideas.title: Consistency feedback detects contradictions across components
ideas.statement: The consistency check detects contradictions such as workflow-required approval paired with an attachment section that makes the action unconditional.

ideas.title: Coverage feedback finds omitted WSA evidence
ideas.statement: The coverage check compares reconstructed WSA against trace evidence and flags missing path segments, branch outcomes, decision criteria, or attachments.

ideas.title: Eight WSA skill types enumerate component presence
ideas.statement: Table 1 defines T0 none: Prompt Fragment; T1 A: Attachment Wrapper; T2 S: Semantic Guideline; T3 S+A: Semantic Resource; T4 W: Bare Workflow; T5 W+A: Tool-Driven Workflow; T6 W+S: Semantically Guided Workflow; T7 W+S+A: Full Runtime Workflow.
ideas.conditions: Routing header is outside this three-component type classification. W requires at least two nodes and at least one directed edge.

ideas.title: Semantic cross-prompt KV reuse problem
ideas.statement: SemShareKV targets reuse of a precomputed KV cache for another semantically similar prompt, where lexical differences prevent exact-prefix or repeated-text cache matching.
ideas.conditions: Motivating use cases are multidocument summarization and conversational prompts; useful reuse depends on a suitable reference prompt.

ideas.title: ReAct, summary agents, memory agent and frontier comparisons
ideas.statement: ReAct has no management; ReSum and ACON summarize at a fixed threshold; ACE accumulates previous-rollout experience without dynamic within-trajectory context management; two stronger models provide reference comparisons.

ideas.title: Environmental module supplies macro geographic constraints
ideas.statement: The Environmental Module analyzes terrain, vegetation, and climate indicators to narrow large candidate regions, such as north versus south China or southeast hilly areas.

ideas.title: Evidence is obtained by executing actions against the world
ideas.statement: Equation (2) defines e_{t+1}=V(a_{t+1},W), where V verifies the selected probing action using external-world evidence W.

ideas.title: Non-neural scene embedding on CPU
ideas.statement: The second cascade stage computes a 128-dimensional cosine-comparable scene vector from HSV histogram, luminance, edge density and texture without a deep network or GPU.

ideas.title: Skill and memory agent background
ideas.statement: The source situates VisualClaw relative to Reflexion episodic verbal reflections, Voyager executable skills, ExpeL and Agent-KB natural-language experience rules, MemGPT/Generative Agents/Mem0/MemEvolve memories, and MetaClaw skill evolution coupled to RL; VisualClaw instead holds VLM weights frozen.

ideas.title: Executability feedback assesses actionable order and criteria
ideas.statement: The executability check asks whether downstream agents receive ordered steps, decision criteria at the right nodes, and sufficiently specific validation/output requirements.

ideas.title: Measure all commuting parities through one joint context-basis outcome
ideas.statement: A context-basis measurement resolves one of 2^n joint eigenstates using n canonical outcome bits, from which all parities in the commuting context can be derived. It inverts an alternative preparation circuit whose initial X gates select the eigenstate, avoiding repeated separate parity-only measurements.
ideas.conditions: The n-bit outcome determines mutually commuting parities, not independent access to all 3^n noncommuting observables at once.

ideas.title: Context measurement unitary is inverse rotation, fan-out CNOT, inverse phase and H
ideas.statement: Equation D1 defines M(s′,β′)=(H⊗I^{⊗(n−1)})(S^{s′†}⊗I^{⊗(n−1)})(∏_{i=2}^n CX(1,i))Γβ′†. Canonical measurement after M maps the selected context eigenbasis to computational-basis outputs.
ideas.conditions: Measured-context parameters s′,β′ may differ from state-preparation parameters.

ideas.title: Recover context-state indices from canonical outcomes
ideas.statement: From canonical outputs α′1,…,α′n, the context decoder uses α1=α′n, α_j=α′j⊕α′n for 2≤j≤n−1, and z=α′1⊕(s′α′n). These indices identify the collapsed context eigenstate and permit computing all its in-context parity outcomes using C5 and C7.
ideas.conditions: The inferred eigenstate refers to the selected pre-rotation measurement basis.

ideas.title: Prepare eight-qubit GHZ on Cairo in four CNOT layers
ideas.statement: Starting with H on Cairo qubit 1, Equation E1 uses CNOT layers: (1→2); (2→3,1→4); (3→5,4→7,1→0); (7→6). This generates the eight-qubit GHZ state in four entangling layers on Cairo, compared with three layers possible under sufficient connectivity.
ideas.conditions: Layer count refers to disjoint two-qubit gates; geometry and connectivity are specific to the chosen Cairo subgraph.

ideas.title: Choose connected Cairo qubits with low observed GHZ error
ideas.statement: The implementation selects Cairo qubits 0–7, with edges 0–1,1–2,2–3,3–5,1–4,4–7,7–6. The authors chose this subgraph for useful connectivity and lower GHZ-preparation errors than other qubits at the time.
ideas.conditions: Hardware calibration-dependent selection; error values and calibration date are not given.

ideas.title: Linear-chain fan-out uses a forward-and-reverse CNOT sequence
ideas.statement: Equation E2 decomposes common-control fan-out ∏_{i=2}^k CX(1,i) on a k-qubit line into 2k−3 CNOT layers: sweep from the far end toward control, apply CX(1,2) once, and sweep back. The common control is used in only one layer.
ideas.conditions: k linearly connected qubits; product read right to left.

ideas.title: Fine-tuned reasoning city accuracy and compliance
ideas.statement: Table 2 gives GeoReasoner-7B 18.33/17.67/78.33% and GLOBE-7B 26.33/23.33/60.30% for direct city accuracy, coordinate-derived city accuracy, and Location Compliance respectively.
ideas.conditions: CCL-Bench.

ideas.title: Model-inspired triggers cause observational selection bias
ideas.statement: HEP triggers reduce recorded data using familiar physics models, creating a streetlight effect that can exclude unanticipated events; relaxing filters is motivated as a route to broader new-physics searches.

ideas.title: Data growth motivates alternative storage
ideas.statement: The introduction reports approximately 1 TB/day for IceCube and 300 TB/day for the LHC and planned upgrades increasing production by an order of magnitude, motivating storage approaches that retain larger data fractions.
ideas.conditions: Historical rates and upgrade expectations cited by the authors, not newly measured here.

ideas.title: Faithful classical-to-quantum representations limit classification
ideas.statement: The authors identify the ability to find sufficiently faithful quantum representations of classical event data as a limitation of their electron-versus-muon classification and call for further investigation.

ideas.title: Full-weight Pauli parity observables
ideas.statement: For n qubits, measuring each spin along X, Y, or Z and multiplying the ±1 outcomes defines one of 3^n full-weight parity observables in {X,Y,Z}^{⊗n}. A parity eigenvalue λ maps to a bit by bit(λ)=(1−λ)/2.

ideas.title: Decode bits from mean ensemble parity
ideas.statement: Equation (1) maps an ensemble of n-qubit states to a 3^n-bit target by b_i=round(bit((1/M) Σ_j ⟨φ_j|O(i)|φ_j⟩)), with any chosen enumeration O of full-weight Pauli observables. It classically averages parity expectations before bit mapping and rounding.
ideas.conditions: An ensemble with parity means that reproduce the desired rounded values must be found; this is not arbitrary exact storage in one n-qubit state.

ideas.title: Atoms-per-bit comparison is an extrapolated illustration
ideas.statement: Figure 1 compares analog, digital and quantum atoms per accessible bit, using average character counts for analog formats and ISO fabrication estimates for digital media. The quantum contextual-encoding comparison extrapolates the protocol to a larger device; the bottom panel depicts binary conversion, state selection, storage, partial decoding and event classification.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative resource comparison rather than a measured end-to-end classical storage benchmark.

ideas.title: Quantum constraints frustrate direct arbitrary bit encoding
ideas.statement: Quantum constraints among spin-measurement eigenvalues can prevent a succinct representation of an arbitrary classical bitstring using one rounded parity observable per bit.

ideas.title: Encode each target bit in an XOR of parity pairs
ideas.statement: Following Ref. [14], each classical bit is the XOR of two majority-parity bits: equal parities encode 0 and unequal parities encode 1. With n-qubit full-weight observables there are (3^n−1)/2 pairs; a target of N bits has 2^N equivalent parity configurations, trading about half the nominal capacity for freedom to find feasible compact ensembles.
ideas.conditions: Uses an ensemble and majority parities; one unpaired observable is unused.

ideas.title: Base commuting parity contexts
ideas.statement: The protocol uses parity eigenstates of complete sets of commuting observables of size 2^(n−1)+1. The base even/odd contexts consist of Z^{⊗n} plus X/Y tensor products with respectively an even or odd number of X factors.
ideas.conditions: The supplemental derivation explicitly assumes even n; mutual commutation with Z^{⊗n} relies on that condition.

ideas.title: Generate rotated contexts with local Clifford gates
ideas.statement: The protocol generates 2×3^n contexts from the two base contexts using R(β)=⊗_j Γ_{β_j}, β_j∈{0,1,2}, Γ_0=I, Γ_1=HZS and Γ_2=SH. These gates cyclically permute Pauli axes while preserving eigenvalues.
ideas.conditions: Even-n context family, with n≥4 needed for the distinct-context count in Appendix B.

ideas.title: Reuse base-context eigenvalues to reduce enumeration
ideas.statement: Instead of storing approximately 12^n eigenvalues for all contexts, the implementation computes approximately 4^n base-context eigenvalues and reuses them under eigenvalue-preserving rotations and consistent observable ordering; analytic parity formulas further reduce calculation.
ideas.conditions: This reduces an exponential enumeration but does not make the overall representation search polynomial.

ideas.title: Optimize pair representation by summed closest-context distances
ideas.statement: The parity representation is parameterized by (3^n−1)/2 free bits, one per pair; the second bit is fixed by the target XOR. A genetic algorithm minimizes the sum, over contexts, of the minimum Hamming distance between the desired subset of parity bits and physically allowed context eigenstates, retaining each best-matching eigenstate.
ideas.conditions: Heuristic optimization; Hamming-nearest-state procedure cites thesis [15], genetic algorithms cite [16].

ideas.title: Optimize a subset of candidate context states
ideas.statement: A second genetic optimization uses a 2×3^n membership bitstring to select candidate context eigenstates that reproduce the desired collective parities. Main text describes penalizing mismatch while encouraging fewer quantum resources.
ideas.conditions: Main text describes a resource tradeoff qualitatively; Appendix G Equation (G7) explicitly specifies only parity mismatch.

ideas.title: Prepare context eigenstates from parameterized GHZ circuits
ideas.statement: The circuit first creates GHZ with H and CNOT gates, then applies S^s and Z^z phase gates, n−1 controlled-by-classical-bit X^α gates, and per-qubit Γ_β rotations. The parameter s chooses the even/odd base context, β chooses its rotation, and z and α choose its eigenstate.
ideas.conditions: The full supplemental construction is |φ⟩=Rβ Xα Z₀^z S₀^s |GHZ⟩. Main-text final counting expressions contain inconsistent factors.

ideas.title: Muon tracks and cascade event morphologies
ideas.statement: Muon charged-current neutrino interactions can produce long linear light tracks; electron charged-current and all-flavor neutral-current interactions produce roughly spherical cascades whose several-to-ten-metre extent appears point-like relative to interstring spacing. Optical modules detect light from charged secondary particles.

ideas.title: Classify tracks versus cascades using polar-angle CDFs
ideas.statement: Half of the events are used to design cuts on Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests of triggered-module polar-angle distributions; the same cuts are applied to decoded events. Figure 3 compares unencoded training distributions with encoded and retrieved distributions.
ideas.conditions: Simple polar-angle classification demonstration, not a learned quantum classifier; exact KS thresholds are not specified in the paper.

ideas.title: Class-conditional classification results before and after encoding
ideas.statement: Figure 3D reports simulated-training true-muon predictions of 69.05% muon/30.95% electron and true-electron predictions of 41.50% muon/58.50% electron. For quantum-readout test events, the corresponding rows are 76.70%/23.30% and 54.50%/45.50%. Encoding worsens electron recall while muon recall increases.
ideas.conditions: Different training and test subsets, rather than a matched per-event accuracy comparison; class totals and statistical uncertainty are not supplied.

ideas.title: Encoding distorts event polar-angle distributions despite accurate readout
ideas.statement: Figure 3 shows nearly matching encoded and retrieved polar-angle CDFs, while their shapes differ from simulated-data CDFs. The authors attribute classification degradation primarily to imperfect classical-to-quantum representations rather than hardware readout.

ideas.title: Selected Prometheus neutrino-event dataset
ideas.statement: The demonstration simulates muon- and electron-neutrino charged-current events using Prometheus, with energy 100 GeV to 5×10^5 GeV drawn from a power law with spectral index 1. It selects events with at least 20 detected photons and at most 20 hit optical modules; the latter restriction fits the eight-qubit protocol.
ideas.conditions: Approximately one thousand selected events; supplemental methods give geometry and injection details.

ideas.title: Serialize optical-module summaries into 3280 bits
ideas.statement: For each hit optical module, the target stores total detected photon count, mean photon arrival time, and spherical-coordinate position relative to the event charge-weighted center. Binary values are concatenated into (3^8−1)/2=3280 bits per event, zero-padding events with fewer than twenty hit modules.
ideas.conditions: The stored information is a per-module summary; binary field widths, quantization and detailed photon-level histories are not specified here.

ideas.title: Eight-qubit demonstration increases total two-level resources
ideas.statement: Median encoding uses 680^(+18)_(-25) eight-qubit states for 3280 classical bits, totaling 5440^(+144)_(-200) two-level systems. The authors explicitly report that net compression was not achieved; citing [14], compression is not expected until at least 14 qubits.
ideas.conditions: Median figures for this selected event sample. Paper does not define the reported uncertainty interval convention.

ideas.title: MultiFieldQA-En selector-swap result
ideas.statement: Under the same SEER answerer, MultiFieldQA-En scores 53.30 with BM25-selected pages and 53.94 with learned visual selection (+0.64 points).
ideas.conditions: Matched completed tasks and page budget; official task scorer.

ideas.title: Optimized quantum representations reproduce about 84 percent of target bits
ideas.statement: The optimized encoded states reproduce target event bitstrings with reported accuracy 84.32%^(+0.69%)_(-1.08%). This measures representation accuracy before hardware readout.
ideas.conditions: Approximately one thousand selected 3280-bit events represented in eight-qubit state ensembles; interval convention unspecified.

ideas.title: Cairo readout recovers prepared-state parity with near-perfect fidelity
ideas.statement: On IBM-Q Cairo, the low-depth GHZ preparation and measurement circuits recover theoretical prepared-state values with reported fidelity 100.00%^(+0.00%)_(-1.04%), distinct from 84.32% accuracy relative to original event bits.
ideas.conditions: Prepared-state parity readout metric, not whole-event lossless recovery.

ideas.title: Unencoded angular-cut classification achieves reported 63.8 percent success
ideas.statement: The angular CDF cuts achieve 63.8% predictive success on the unencoded training events. Applying the same cuts to decoded test events is described as substantially worse, with systematic representation errors proposed as the explanation.
ideas.conditions: Figure 3 provides the per-class confusion rates; decoded aggregate success is not stated.

ideas.title: Larger quantum systems may enable compression and trigger-less analysis
ideas.statement: The authors propose that larger quantum resources and this protocol could enable trigger-less HEP analysis, and claim greater-than-classical compression for more than fourteen qubits; IBM-Q, Sycamore and Rydberg platforms are prospective backends.
ideas.conditions: Prospective scaling claim, not demonstrated in the eight-qubit experiment; practical faithful representation remains unresolved.

ideas.title: End-to-end ternary edge FPGA acceleration
ideas.statement: TeLLMe combines table-lookup matrix multiplication, URAM weight management, mixed-precision streaming fusion, reversed fused prefill attention, and separate decoding attention to execute ternary LLM prefill and generation on AMD Kria KV260.
ideas.conditions: 1.58-bit ternary weights and INT8 activations for linear layers; FP16 operations remain elsewhere.
validity_flags: The claimed first-of-kind status is an author claim, not independently established.

ideas.title: Low-bit quantization as the motivating compression
ideas.statement: The paper situates TeLLMe within model-weight quantization, citing BitNet and BitNet-1.58 as training Transformers with binary or ternary weights. Its compression concerns model weights rather than removal or shortening of prompt tokens.
validity_flags: The paragraph also attributes ternary quantization to DeepSeek [10], but reference [10] is the DeepSeek-R1 reinforcement-learning paper; this attribution is not independently substantiated.

ideas.title: Decoding-only acceleration leaves prefill latency
ideas.statement: The authors identify neglected prefill latency as an edge deployment bottleneck because it directly determines time to first token and user responsiveness; decoding acceleration alone does not solve end-to-end latency.

ideas.title: CPU lookup acceleration has prefill parallelism limits
ideas.statement: T-MAC [15] is described as using table lookup for low-bit weights and high-bit activations on CPUs, with prefill throughput close to decoding throughput due to limited edge CPU compute parallelism.

ideas.title: Prior KV260 accelerator covers decoding with FP16 activations
ideas.statement: Li et al. [11] are described as deploying a 4-bit-weight LLaMA2-7B model on AMD KV260 with unquantized FP16 activations and decoding-only hardware acceleration.

ideas.title: LLaMAF pipelines FPGA linear work with ARM nonlinear operators
ideas.statement: LLaMAF [16] is described as INT8 TinyLLaMA on ZCU102 at 1.5 tokens/s using pipelined matrix-vector units and asynchronous nonlinear operations on ARM A53, with communication overhead and no prefill acceleration.

ideas.title: SECDA supports block-floating-point matmul on PYNQ
ideas.statement: SECDA [18] is described as reducing TinyLLaMA latency 11× over dual-core ARM NEON execution with block-floating-point quantized matmul, but delivering only 0.58 tokens/s.
validity_flags: This is the related-work summary; Table 1 separately labels the compared SECDA precision W4A16.

ideas.title: Prior attention reordering for dense vision attention
ideas.statement: Edge-MoE [17] is described as a task-sparse MoE vision-transformer accelerator whose specialized reordering reuses dense attention data on edge FPGAs.

ideas.title: MEADOW weight packing and mixed-precision scope
ideas.statement: MEADOW [19] is described as using weight packing for linear operations in both prefill and decoding on ZCU102 around 10 W, while omitting end-to-end FP16 smoothing and dequantization around INT8 SmoothQuant. The related-work prose reports 0.64 ms prefill at 64 tokens and 2 tokens/s decoding for OPT 1.3B.
validity_flags: The page-2 0.64 ms prefill claim conflicts by orders of magnitude with the 100 tokens/s value in Table 1 if interpreted end-to-end.
Page 10 later calls MEADOW decoding-only although this paragraph and Table 1 describe prefill support.

ideas.title: LightMamba uses W4A4 quantization on high-end FPGAs
ideas.statement: LightMamba [21] is described as FPGA-friendly post-training W4A4 quantization of Mamba2-2.7B with 7.21 and 93 tokens/s on Versal VCK190 and U280 respectively.

ideas.title: FlightLLM maps LLaMA2-7B to high-end FPGAs
ideas.statement: FlightLLM [22] is described as deploying LLaMA2-7B on Alveo U280 and Versal VHK158 with 153 tokens/s and outperforming NVIDIA GPUs in single-batch inference.
validity_flags: Reported by this paper; not independently reproduced.

ideas.title: EdgeLLM uses HBM-equipped VCU128
ideas.statement: EdgeLLM [23] is described as deploying LLaMA2-7B on VCU128 with HBM and obtaining higher decode throughput than FlightLLM.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-OCR optical context compression
ideas.statement: The cited DeepSeek-OCR work reports 97% OCR precision when text/vision token compression remains below 10×.
validity_flags: Cited external result; OCR metric and domain are not established by SEER experiments.

ideas.title: TerEffic trades high soft-logic use for ternary throughput
ideas.statement: TerEffic [24] is described as a ternary non-Transformer 1.3B model on U280 at 1400 tokens/s, with selection-based rather than lookup-based ternary multiplication consuming over 700K LUTs.

ideas.title: High-end FPGA throughput is not directly comparable with edge FPGA
ideas.statement: The authors describe the cited high-end FPGA platforms as having over 500K LUTs, thousands of DSPs and BRAMs, HBM bandwidth up to 460 GB/s, power above 50 W and cost above $10,000 versus a stated $248 KV260, and caution against direct performance comparisons.
validity_flags: Hardware and cost summary is source-reported, not a current price claim or verified property of every cited design.

ideas.title: Lookup tables amortize repeated ternary operations
ideas.statement: A ternary multiply selects an activation, its negation, or zero; the authors argue DSP multiplier blocks are underused by this operation and highly parallel selection logic duplicates computation, motivating LUTRAM tables shared across grouped activations.

ideas.title: Earlier FPGA lookup work lacks LLM memory integration
ideas.statement: The paper contrasts SIMD CPU lookup tables with FPGA distributed RAM and cites LUTNet, AmigoLUT and LogicNets as smaller lookup networks, plus Table-lookup MAC [14] as a CNN-oriented engine lacking end-to-end mixed-precision LLM dataflow and memory integration.
validity_flags: Characterization of prior work is an author interpretation.

ideas.title: Prefill and decoding have distinct computational patterns
ideas.statement: Prefill processes prompt tokens in parallel and is compute-bound; autoregressive decoding processes one token at a time and is memory-bound. TeLLMe therefore uses separate attention units while sharing its ternary projection engine.
ideas.conditions: The qualitative characterization targets the evaluated edge FPGA workload; it is not a universal performance law.

ideas.title: TeLLMe module and interface organization
ideas.statement: The accelerator contains TLMM-FUSE, WBMU, reversed prefill attention, decode attention and RMS-MAX. Function-level dataflow pipelining and distinct MAXI bundles provide DDR streams; four temporary DDR addresses hold intermediates and dedicated weight and KV-cache addresses support the two stages.

ideas.title: Offline grouping encodes ternary weights as lookup indices
ideas.statement: For W in {-1,0,1}^{n×k}, the offline stage groups G weights and encodes each group using B_idx=ceil(log2(3^G)) bits for N_TB=3^G combinations. T indices form an index vector so the encoded weight matrix has n/(T G) rows of T-index vectors and k output columns.
ideas.conditions: Padding is used when projection dimensions are not aligned to T G.

ideas.title: Post-dequantization operator routing supports SwiGLU and residuals
ideas.statement: An arbiter selects floating-point element-wise multiply with SILU, residual addition, RoPE or bypass. SwiGLU applies SILU to the gate projection then multiplies by the up projection; residual addition precedes RMSNorm.

ideas.title: Online activation tables replace ternary dot products
ideas.statement: For each group of G INT8 activations, an adder/subtractor precompute tree fills a distributed-RAM table with all 3^G partial sums. Encoded weights select partial sums, which accumulate into INT32 outputs. Each table is replicated Q times for parallel lookup across T tables.
ideas.conditions: The stated table entry width is B_TB=8+ceil(log2 G), and total table capacity is B_TB × N_TB × Q × T bits.
validity_flags: For unrestricted signed INT8 inputs including -128, a ternary negation or sum can require an extra sign range; the stated width needs the activation-range convention to be fully justified.

ideas.title: Pipelined table setup and parallel lookup schedule
ideas.statement: The TLMM first builds T tables from T G activations, then processes Q weight-index vectors at once and accumulates Q T lookup results into a k-entry INT32 output buffer. It traverses output columns in Q-sized steps, input groups in T G-sized steps and prompt tokens in the outer loop. The authors claim initiation interval one for lookup and accumulation.
validity_flags: Figure 3 and its caption specify G=3, while adjacent scheduling prose says G=4.
The prose calls the traversed row length m although A was defined m×n; the intended input-feature dimension is n.

ideas.title: One engine supports attention and feed-forward projections
ideas.statement: WBMU decouples loading one encoded weight matrix into URAM from TLMM computation and translates weight addresses for d_model×d_model Q/K/V/O projections, d_model×d_ffn up/gate projections, and d_ffn×d_model down projections, with zero-padded indices for alignment.
ideas.conditions: Capacity assumes the currently processed weight matrix fits the selected on-chip buffer, not the entire model.

ideas.title: Full lookup storage removes sign-handling logic
ideas.statement: TeLLMe stores all 3^G activation partial sums. The compared partial-storage scheme keeps (3^G−1)/2 sign-symmetric nonzero combinations but needs parallel sign-detection and inversion logic, while a selection-only baseline passes, negates or zeroes each activation. Full storage trades more table memory and precomputation for less lookup conversion logic.

ideas.title: LUT cost is decomposed into precompute, storage and lookup
ideas.statement: The estimated resource terms are LUT_PRE=T N_TB LUT_tree; LUT_TB=T Q N_TB LUT_entry; and LUT_LPL=T Q LUT_lp. LUT_tree is average precompute-output cost, LUT_entry is per-entry table storage cost and LUT_lp is lookup/conversion/reduction cost. Distributed RAM makes sign-handling lookup logic dominant for the half-storage design.
ideas.conditions: Analytical FPGA LUT estimates; actual synthesized results appear in Table 4.

ideas.title: Fuse element-wise floating-point work around integer matmul
ideas.statement: TLMM-FUSE overlaps quantization, dequantization, residual addition, SwiGLU/SILU multiplication and RoPE with TLMM using FIFO-based function pipelines and vector-wise FP operations sized to match TLMM throughput under DSP/LUT limits.

ideas.title: Vector resizing bridges FP16 AXI streams and grouped INT8 compute
ideas.statement: Quantization packs 16 FP16 values into a 256-bit stream/AXI vector and resizes it to T G INT8 activations for TLMM. Dequantization vector-multiplies groups of 16 INT32 results into FP16 outputs.

ideas.title: RoPE sinusoids are precomputed in DDR
ideas.statement: The design assumes precomputed sinusoids in DDR to avoid generating them on the FPGA; rotations use frequency theta_t=10000^(−2t/d_h), token position m and 0≤t<d_h/2.

ideas.title: Per-head query/key weight permutation makes RoPE streamable
ideas.statement: The source transforms query and key weight ordering from half-head pairs to consecutive pairs: positions 2t and 2t+1 correspond to old positions t and d_h/2+t. This preserves the rotation while allowing both members of a pair in one packed vector, avoiding cross-vector FIFO dependency and head-wide gathering.
ideas.conditions: A per-head permutation of Q and K weight organization, interpreted as reindexing rather than sequential overlapping swaps.

ideas.title: URAM-aware table count and logic budget
ideas.statement: A URAM block has 72-bit width and depth 4096 (288 Kb); a T-index vector occupies T B_idx bits. The paper prints T=ceil(72 c_URAM/B_idx), with cascade factor c_URAM, and constrains T(N_TB LUT_tree+Q N_TB LUT_entry+Q LUT_lp)≤LUT_max.
ideas.conditions: T also must permit place and route; the resource equations are design constraints rather than a guarantee of feasible timing.
validity_flags: The printed ceiling can make T B_idx exceed the nominal cascaded URAM width. The instantiated T=28 and B_idx=5 fit 144 bits (two URAM widths), whereas ceil(144/5)=29; the rounding rule is internally questionable.

ideas.title: Dual-port URAM partitions enable Q reads
ideas.statement: The weight buffer is cyclically partitioned into Q/2 banks to use two read ports per bank. The printed capacity formula is U=ceil(((Y_URAM/Q) ceil(X_URAM/(G T)))/4096) c_URAM (Q/2), constrained by U≤N_URAM.
ideas.conditions: Even Q; physical depth mapping of independent logical banks is assumed.
validity_flags: The formula uses Y_URAM/Q although cyclic partition count is Q/2; the paper does not resolve this apparent factor-of-two capacity ambiguity.

ideas.title: Padding provides aligned projection-weight accesses
ideas.statement: WBMU pads weight dimensions to make d_ffn and d_model aligned multiples of T G and supports differing strides for up and down projections. It maps 2D software weight indices into 3D physical URAM coordinates, with X_URAM=d_ffn-prime and Y_URAM=d_model-prime.
validity_flags: The printed address map omits explicit integer rounding/group scaling for y despite the grouped array dimension; it is retained as written, not validated as executable indexing.

ideas.title: Three independent DDR ports stream packed indices and RMS weights
ideas.statement: WBMU uses HP0, HP1 and HP3, each with 256-bit AXI width, burst length 16 and 16 outstanding transactions on independent QoS channels, for an aggregate 768 bits per access cycle. For T=28 and B=5, the stated transfer packs five 140-bit weight-index vectors and one FP16 RMSNorm weight.
validity_flags: The text prints ceil((768−16)/(T B)) but its concrete count of five agrees with floor, not ceiling (ceil(752/140)=6).

ideas.title: RMS-MAX separates scaling statistics from quantization
ideas.statement: RMS-MAX accumulates normalization statistics in FP32, then uses FP16 division and RMS weight scaling. FIFO-connected vector-wise maxima are reduced to the final channel maximum in a dedicated quant/dequant buffer, allowing max finding to overlap output streaming while decoupling it from quantization.

ideas.title: Naive prefill attention multiplies DDR traffic
ideas.statement: For N tokens, naive attention requires quadratic multi-head computation and writes/reads an N×N×N_head intermediate softmax matrix. Scaling the number of processing elements also raises input bandwidth demand, so edge FPGA attention needs reuse and fusion tailored to limited DSP and on-chip memory resources.

ideas.title: Running maximum and rescaling avoid materializing attention scores
ideas.statement: For a fixed query and successive keys/values, the fused kernel maintains a maximum m, denominator l and unnormalized output o. With score s and m_new=max(m_old,s), l_new=exp(m_old−m_new) l_old+exp(s−m_new) and o_new=exp(m_old−m_new) o_old+exp(s−m_new) v; final output is o/l. This avoids the full score matrix and global-max synchronization.
ideas.conditions: Head-wise score is scaled by 1/sqrt(d_h); described as a block-size-one FlashAttention variant.
validity_flags: Prose calls this Flash Attention V2 [31], while bibliography [31] is FlashAttention (2022), not FlashAttention-2.
Equation 11 uses the same i subscript for query and key while surrounding scheduling uses separate i,j; the fixed-query interpretation is necessary for ordinary attention.

ideas.title: Reverse query groups reuse key/value inputs and omit masked work
ideas.statement: The RPA schedules queries from the end of the prompt in groups of N_pe, unicasts a query to each PE, and multicasts keys and values across PEs. Subsequent query groups process successively fewer keys/values to avoid causal-mask-invalid work. Each PE performs head-wise MAC, running-max rescaling/accumulation, then final division/output.
ideas.conditions: Causal self-attention; Figure 6 illustrates N_pe=4.
validity_flags: The prose says schedule begins at q_(N−1), then describes its first batch as q_N through q_(N−3); starting-index notation is inconsistent.

ideas.title: Fused attention trades bounded buffers for rescale arithmetic
ideas.statement: RPA needs N_pe query buffers plus one key and one value input buffer. Per-head intermediate scores, maxima and denominators each use N_h N_pe entries, and output numerators use d_model N_pe entries. Running-max updates add an exponential and two floating-point rescale operations.
ideas.conditions: These buffers describe the proposed streamed prefill attention unit, independent of full N×N score storage.

ideas.title: Reverse prompt embeddings and RoPE cache to preserve burst access
ideas.statement: The implementation indexes embeddings using reversed prompt token IDs and reverses the RoPE cache. This supplies RPA its reverse order without an additional reversed-address DDR access path incompatible with AXI incremental burst addressing.
ideas.conditions: Scheduling/data-layout transformation; all prompt tokens are still processed and this is not token compression.

ideas.title: Decode attention retains scores on chip with partially fused softmax
ideas.statement: The DA unit holds the one-token query on chip, streams K and V caches from DDR, separates QK^T from the V-weighted aggregation, and partially fuses online softmax with QK^T. Intermediate attention scores remain in an on-chip stream buffer so softmax needs no DDR reload.
ideas.conditions: Decode attention costs O(N d_model) per generated token versus O(N² d_model) for prefill; cache reads make decoding bandwidth-bound.

ideas.title: KV260 implementation and measurement setup
ideas.statement: TeLLMe uses C/C++ Vitis HLS 2024.1 and Vivado 2024.1 on AMD Kria KV260/XCK26, with a 250 MHz final bitstream. End-to-end latencies are measured through PYNQ Runtime while latency breakdowns come from cycle-accurate RTL simulations.
ideas.conditions: Evaluation is on one FPGA platform and model; breakdowns and total latencies have distinct measurement sources.
validity_flags: Paper does not provide run counts, latency dispersion, detailed prompts, or power-measurement instrumentation in the inspected experimental setup.

ideas.title: BitNet 0.73B and instantiated lookup parameters
ideas.statement: The evaluated BitNet 0.73B has 49M LM-head/embedding parameters and 680M decoder parameters. Hardware parameters are G=3, T=28, Q=16, U=48 and B_idx=5, producing 140-bit encoded weight vectors.
ideas.conditions: The 48 URAMs are the weight buffer allocation; total design use is 60 URAMs.

ideas.title: The LM head remains on the processing-system CPU
ideas.statement: Routing/placement limits prevent an additional FPGA LM-head module, so the LM head runs on the PS with ARM NEON SIMD and W8A8 quantization. Its reported 9 ms latency is included in end-to-end results.
validity_flags: The source calls accuracy loss negligible but Table 2 only supplies cross-model perplexities, not a same-model unquantized LM-head ablation.

ideas.title: Longer prompt and generation lengths reduce throughput
ideas.conditions: BitNet 0.73B on KV260 at 250 MHz; measured end-to-end with PS LM-head latency included.
validity_flags: The headline 25 tokens/s is rounded from the best 24.6-token/s plotted configuration.

ideas.title: Profiling confirms different stage bottlenecks
ideas.statement: At length 128, Figure 11 assigns decode latency to attention 31%, linear 9%, RMSNorm 1% and weight loading 59%; prefill is attention 18%, linear 70%, RMSNorm 9% and weight loading 3%.
ideas.conditions: Cycle-accurate RTL breakdown at the stated sequence length, distinct from PYNQ end-to-end latency.

ideas.title: Resource use is concentrated in fusion logic and weight URAM
ideas.conditions: Synthesized/place-and-routed KV260 design; dash means unreported/unused as in the table.

ideas.title: Comparative claims about prefill support are inconsistent
ideas.statement: The comparison section asserts that LLaMAF and MEADOW accelerate decoding only and require another device for prefill. For MEADOW this conflicts with the same paper’s related-work description of both stages and its reported 100 tokens/s prefill baseline; the comparison should not be treated as resolved evidence of absent prefill support.
validity_flags: Internal inconsistency: MEADOW prefill support is both present and absent in different passages.

ideas.title: Cross-platform throughput and energy comparisons
ideas.statement: Table 1 reports TeLLMe W1.58A8 BitNet 0.73B at 4.8 W and theoretical 17.1 GB/s DDR bandwidth: prefill/decode 143/25 tokens/s and 29.8/5.2 tokens/J. Baselines: Raspberry Pi 5 Qwen 0.6B W4A16, 7.8 W, 17.1 GB/s, 61.8/16.6 tokens/s, 7.92/2.12 tokens/J; Jetson Orin Nano TinyLLaMA 1.1B W4A16, 25 W, 68.3 GB/s, 324.9/67.6 tokens/s, 12.9/2.70 tokens/J; LLaMAF ZCU102 TinyLLaMA W8A8, 5.1 W, 19.2 GB/s, decode 1.5 tokens/s and 0.29 tokens/J; MEADOW ZCU102 OPT 1.3B W8A8, 10 W, 19.2 GB/s, 100/2 tokens/s, 10/0.20 tokens/J; SECDA PYNQ TinyLLaMA W4A16 has 2.1 GB/s and 0.6 decode tokens/s, other Table 1 performance values unreported.
ideas.conditions: Baseline values are collected from cited work/tutorials on different models and platforms, not a controlled identical-model experiment.
validity_flags: Model size, precision, compute capability and measurement provenance differ between rows; ratios cannot isolate the architecture alone.

ideas.title: Perplexity-normalized throughput per joule
ideas.statement: The paper adopts Intelligence/J = (tokens/s)/(perplexity × power), citing Tenet [35], and evaluates it using WikiText-2 perplexity.
ideas.conditions: This metric is a chosen quality/energy proxy, not a comprehensive measure of model intelligence.

ideas.title: WikiText-2 and quality-normalized efficiency
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports WikiText-2 PPL and prefill/decode Intelligence/J: Raspberry Pi Qwen 0.6B 24.00 and 0.330/0.089; Jetson TinyLLaMA 1.1B 12.42 and 1.046/0.218; SECDA TinyLLaMA 12.42 and —/0.040 at 1.2 W; LLaMAF TinyLLaMA 8.89 and —/0.041; MEADOW OPT 1.3B 15.41 and 0.649/0.013; TeLLMe BitNet 0.73B 12.79 and 2.330/0.407.
ideas.conditions: Cross-model quality proxy on WikiText-2; power/throughput conditions follow Table 1 except SECDA power is supplied in Table 2.
validity_flags: Cross-model perplexity comparisons may also depend on tokenizer/evaluation conventions, which the paper does not fully document.

ideas.title: Sequence length limits practical responsiveness
ideas.statement: The authors recommend moderate sequence lengths: plotted prompts below 256 tokens retain >16 tokens/s decode and <2.25 s prefill, whereas 512-token prompts take 5.89 s to prefill and longer generation reduces throughput.
ideas.conditions: Recommendation applies to the evaluated edge design and plotted lengths; it is not a prompt-compression method.

ideas.title: Reported FPGA decoding improvements
ideas.statement: Using the compared systems in Tables 1–2, the paper reports TeLLMe decoding throughput 41.7× SECDA, 16.7× LLaMAF and 12.5× MEADOW; decoding energy efficiency is 17.9× LLaMAF and 26× MEADOW, and decoding Intelligence/J is 31.3× MEADOW.
ideas.conditions: Ratios use rounded source table values and different models/precisions, not matched models.
validity_flags: SECDA power is described as comparable in the prose, while Table 2 lists 1.2 W versus TeLLMe 4.8 W.
The attribution of speedups solely to optimized hardware is not isolated from model/precision differences.

ideas.title: Resource budgets of the compared FPGA baselines
ideas.statement: Table 1 gives LLaMAF 164K LUTs, 171K FFs, 528 DSPs and 223 BRAMs; MEADOW 150K LUTs, 845 DSPs and 2034 BRAMs, with FFs unreported. SECDA hardware resources are unreported. TeLLMe is reported at 98K LUTs, 137K FFs, 610 DSPs, 98.5 BRAMs and 60 URAMs.
ideas.conditions: Raw counts as reported in Table 1; different FPGA/model configurations and memory block conventions may limit direct comparability.

ideas.title: Reported edge CPU/GPU efficiency ratios
ideas.statement: The authors report TeLLMe versus Jetson Orin Nano at 25 versus 67.6 decode tokens/s but 4.8 versus 25 W, giving about 1.9× decoding energy efficiency. Against Raspberry Pi 5, 25 versus 16.6 tokens/s and 4.8 versus 7.8 W give about 1.5× throughput, 38% less power and 2.45× energy efficiency. Decoding Intelligence/J is 0.407 versus 0.218 (Jetson) and 0.089 (Pi), or about 1.9× and 4.6×.
ideas.conditions: Cross-platform, cross-model comparisons, with source-reported power; no matched-model or matched-quality causal inference.
validity_flags: The broad opening statement that CPU and GPU platforms offer higher throughput does not hold for the listed Pi decode result; numerical rows are retained.

ideas.title: Improve BitNet quality through more data and architecture refinement
ideas.statement: The paper identifies further training samples and BitNet architectural refinements as future work because TeLLMe’s WikiText-2 perplexity 12.79 remains above LLaMAF’s 8.89, while being close to the listed TinyLLaMA W4A16 value 12.42.
ideas.conditions: Different evaluated models/precisions; lower perplexity is the desired direction, not a prediction of guaranteed improvement.

ideas.title: Full lookup storage uses fewer LUTs at fixed parallelism
ideas.statement: At G=3, T=28, Q=16 and matched parallelism/latency, the full-table TLMM consumes 23,082 LUTs versus 43,176 for direct ternary selection and 35,200 for partial lookup storage. Table 4 decomposes partial storage into 3,117 precompute + 6,440 table + 25,643 lookup-logic LUTs; full storage into 5,301 + 11,452 + 6,329. Half-storage saves table bits but its parallel sign-inversion logic dominates.
ideas.conditions: Synthesized TLMM core only, not all TLMM-FUSE resources; partial storage keeps 13 of 27 combinations.

ideas.title: Reversed fused attention cuts measured latency at modest DSP cost
ideas.statement: With N_pe=8 and a prefill length of 128, the reverse attention design reports 7.6 ms on-board latency and 115 DSPs, versus 14.3 ms and 105 DSPs for the naive schedule. The added DSP cost is attributed to extra exponentials.
ideas.conditions: Same PE count for both attention-unit designs; this is attention-unit latency, not full-model prefill time.
validity_flags: Single reported operating point; no statistical uncertainty or run count is supplied.

ideas.title: Answer judge checks semantic inclusion of ground truth
ideas.statement: Figure 6 asks GPT-4 to compare predicted and ground-truth answers, accept equivalent substance rather than requiring exact wording, and output an explanation plus TRUE/FALSE based on whether the ground-truth meaning and vital facts are present.
ideas.conditions: Correctness metric used alongside F1; prompt artifact only.
validity_flags: Semantic-inclusion judging can differ from full factual precision of an answer; no human agreement validation is reported.

ideas.title: IRCoT and FLARE prompt makes short reasoning sentences retrieval queries
ideas.statement: Figure 4 prompts short reasoning sentences inside <s> tags for use as later retrieval queries, continuation of partial reasoning chains, planning when current knowledge is absent, and final answers inside <answer> tags. Four demonstrations cover an album, Cambodia, Ferrari and a birth-date comparison.
ideas.conditions: Prompt artifact for adapted IRCoT/FLARE evaluation, not an instruction to the extraction worker.
validity_flags: Fourth demonstration supplies Raoul Walsh's birth date in reasoning although its displayed documents concern Jan de Bont and films, showing reliance on information not in those documents.

ideas.title: Chain-of-Note learns relevance and reliability assessment
ideas.statement: Chain-of-Note generates sequential notes during training to evaluate retrieved-document relevance and reliability; the authors describe it as noise-robust but lacking explicit inference-time planning or iterative refinement.

ideas.title: Notes may preserve conflicting facts and iteration caps can truncate reasoning
ideas.statement: Iterative note retrieval can introduce conflicting information and hallucinated facts; a maximum iteration limit imposed for efficiency may reduce performance. The authors report better recovery in selected notes traces but do not claim to eliminate hallucination.
ideas.conditions: Selected conflict/hallucination examples appear in Tables 18-20.
validity_flags: The numerical maximum iteration limit is not specified in the source prose reviewed.

ideas.title: Cost-effectiveness claim lacks direct latency measurement
ideas.statement: The paper argues NotesWriting is cost-effective because combined main-plus-notes output tokens are on average 2-3 times baseline but about 100 times smaller than input tokens, and output tokens are claimed to dominate cost and latency. Appendix A.4 reports overall evaluation runtimes, but no matched baseline-vs-notes latency or complete dollar-cost comparison.
ideas.conditions: Depends on serving/pricing assumptions, prompt caching, parallelism and note extraction calls.
validity_flags: Overall evaluation runtimes are reported, but no matched per-method latency or dollar-cost comparison establishes the cost/compute/latency conclusion.

ideas.title: Four evaluation datasets and sample scope
ideas.statement: Evaluation uses FanoutQA dev (310 questions), FRAMES (549 examples after excluding tabular reasoning, original tasks requiring 2-15 hops), HotpotQA (500 dev examples; described as requiring 2-3 Wikipedia articles), and 500 MultiHop-RAG test questions over about 600 news articles using top-five BM25 articles per iteration.
ideas.conditions: Appendix A.3 clarifies 500 MultiHop-RAG test examples and calls FRAMES examples multiple-constraint-tagged; main text describes excluding tabular reasoning.
validity_flags: FRAMES excludes tabular reasoning, restricting generalizability.

ideas.title: Accuracy, cumulative token use and search steps
ideas.statement: The study measures answer F1, GPT-4-as-judge correctness, and average main-model and notes-model input/output tokens summed across all iterations; average steps means the number of search queries used to answer a question.
ideas.conditions: Cumulative tokens are throughput accounting across calls and are not a single prompt length.
validity_flags: Judge correctness is model-based, not an independent human adjudication.

ideas.title: Reported full-dataset evaluation runtimes
ideas.statement: With parallelization, Llama evaluation runs take about 9-10 hours for MultiHop-RAG, HotpotQA and FRAMES, and 15 hours for FanoutQA. GPT-4o-mini takes about 7 hours for FRAMES/FanoutQA, 2 hours for HotpotQA and 27 minutes for MultiHop-RAG, including rate limits, Wikipedia calls and notes writing.
ideas.conditions: Reported evaluation wall times, not matched per-question algorithm latency; hardware described in model configuration.

ideas.title: Retrieval may surface toxic or harmful information
ideas.statement: The authors acknowledge possible toxic or harmful requested retrieval content and rely on content moderation policies to reduce impact; hallucinations also affect QA experience.
ideas.conditions: Stated societal risk, not an evaluated mitigation.

ideas.title: Fanout notes trace gathers one fact per entity
ideas.statement: Table 10 shows GPT-4o-mini first identifying four recent Supreme Court justices, then making four targeted law-school queries and aggregating their note observations into an answer. This illustrates sequential entity expansion followed by attribute extraction.
ideas.conditions: Selected FanoutQA trace; political/biographical contents are quoted dataset evidence, not a current factual answer.
validity_flags: Illustrative trace does not estimate population-level success or establish the facts independently.

ideas.title: Correct answers sometimes use fewer searches than gold source pages
ideas.statement: Among correctly answered questions, percentages with fewer searches than ground-truth Wikipedia pages are ReNAct/ReAct: GPT Fanout 22.83/36.84, FRAMES 23.18/29.89, Hotpot 30.56/46.02; Llama Fanout 49.44/35.71, FRAMES 28.22/30.94, Hotpot 31.33/32.82.
ideas.conditions: Gold page count is a proxy for required searches; one search can return multiple pages.
validity_flags: Fewer-than-gold searches cannot alone establish better reasoning or absence of parametric knowledge use.

ideas.title: FLARE retrieves according to generation confidence
ideas.statement: The paper describes FLARE as triggering retrieval for low-confidence generated tokens using the preceding sentence and skipping retrieval when confidence is high. Its printed Equation 4 instead selects s_(t-1) when conf(s_(t-1))>theta, leaving an internal sign/definition inconsistency.
validity_flags: Equation 4 has a greater-than confidence condition inconsistent with the adjacent low-confidence-trigger prose; do not silently repair.

ideas.title: FLARE token savings vary substantially by dataset
ideas.statement: Table 9 token totals in Fanout/FRAMES/Hotpot/MultiHop order: GPT main input baseline->notes 268K->65K,50K->43K,36K->33K,204K->205K; main output 384->409,314->358,218->258,319->312; notes input 968K/47K/45K/14K and output 2.2K/56/49/49. Llama main input 195K->154K,86K->67K,83K->65K,301K->67K; main output 453->555,640->592,573->563,558->710; notes input 1.3M/47K/45K/15K and output 7.5K/66/77/38.
ideas.conditions: Average cumulative token use; retrieval confidence theta=0.8.
validity_flags: Main-input reduction is not uniform: GPT MultiHop input increases slightly; prose claim of at least 4x/1.5x reduction does not hold per dataset.
On Llama Fanout, 7.5K note outputs far exceed the 453 baseline main outputs, qualifying the global 2-3x output-overhead summary.

ideas.title: Plug-in notes preserve IRCoT and FLARE query policies
ideas.statement: NotesWriting changes generation input rather than each base framework's query policy: IRCoT still retrieves from the last sentence; FLARE still retrieves conditionally. Both generate from [O_t,x,s_<t], with empty O_t when FLARE skips retrieval.
ideas.conditions: Demonstrated for ReAct, IRCoT and FLARE; unrestricted framework generality is a design claim.
validity_flags: Section 3.3 calls Eq. 5 a generation step, but Eq. 5 defines ReAct query formulation.

ideas.title: Raw full-page iterative context overflows in most hard QA examples
ideas.statement: With top-five Wikipedia Markdown pages appended at every step, context limits are exceeded for GPT-4o-mini on 463/549 FRAMES questions (84.3%) and 244/310 FanoutQA (78.7%); Llama at 64K exceeds limits on 488/549 (88.8%) and 255/310 (82.2%), respectively.
ideas.conditions: Initial full-page baseline experiment; not the final chunked baselines used for accuracy comparisons.

ideas.title: Wikipedia text-matching search constrains retrieval
ideas.statement: Online searches use a Wikipedia API that only supports text-matching Wikipedia pages; the authors keep comparable knowledge tools across baselines to avoid paid search APIs.
ideas.conditions: Online Wikipedia-based evaluation; MultiHop-RAG separately uses news BM25.

ideas.title: Reported aggregate accuracy improvement
ideas.statement: Across three iterative RAG methods, two LLMs and four QA datasets, the paper reports an overall average 15.6 percentage-point performance improvement with NotesWriting and minimal increase in output tokens.
ideas.conditions: Aggregate reported by authors; detailed denominators and model/dataset results are extracted separately.
validity_flags: Aggregate headline does not itself provide uncertainty intervals or a statistical significance analysis.
Abstract/introduction call 15.6 points an average improvement, whereas conclusion calls it up to 15.6; per-condition table changes are more precise.

ideas.title: Infogent baseline substitutes search and embedding services
ideas.statement: The appendix adapts official Infogent code to AzureOpenAI, replaces OpenAI embeddings with all-mpnet-base-v2, and substitutes Wikipedia API for Serper Google Search due to access/credit limitations and comparable knowledge tools.
ideas.conditions: Adapted baseline, Apache 2.0 licensed code as described.
validity_flags: Search and embedding substitutions may change performance relative to original Infogent.

ideas.title: Infogent separates navigation extraction and aggregation
ideas.statement: Infogent uses an Aggregator whose textual feedback guides retrieval from a Navigator-Extractor that extracts readable relevant web content; the paper identifies context management as a remaining issue.

ideas.title: NotesWriting exceeds adapted Infogent on hard QA
ideas.statement: With GPT-4o-mini, Infogent/NotesWriting F1 and judge scores are FanoutQA 47.2/50.0 and 22.9/28.0, and FRAMES 28.0/46.8 and 29.9/52.3.
ideas.conditions: Table calls the comparator InfoAgent, while A.1 calls it Infogent; adapted search/embedding implementation.

ideas.title: IRCoT plus notes accuracy with GPT-4o-mini
ideas.statement: IRCoT->IRCoT+NotesWriting F1/GPT-4 percentages: Fanout 33.6/15.2->41.9/21.3; FRAMES 24.0/22.0->43.9/42.3; Hotpot 36.4/42.8->46.2/53.8; MultiHop 23.7/48.0->36.0/65.6.
ideas.conditions: Reimplemented chat-model IRCoT; no uncertainty intervals reported.

ideas.title: IRCoT plus notes accuracy with Llama-3.1-70B
ideas.statement: IRCoT->IRCoT+NotesWriting F1/GPT-4 percentages: Fanout 21.0/8.4->36.0/22.9; FRAMES 19.4/21.1->26.9/33.3; Hotpot 31.5/38.2->36.5/53.0; MultiHop 35.4/64.8->38.0/64.8.
ideas.conditions: Reimplemented chat-model IRCoT; no uncertainty intervals reported.

ideas.title: IRCoT and FLARE baselines use adapted chat prompts and recent dense retrieval
ideas.statement: IRCoT/FLARE few-shot prompts are adapted from completion-model use to chat models and explicit planning. Their older BM25 Wikipedia retrieval is replaced by the 20231101.en dump and dense ef-base-v2 embeddings; FLARE theta is 0.8.
ideas.conditions: Preserves ef-base-v2 spelling printed in source. Baselines use chunked setup, NotesWriting full pages.
validity_flags: Comparisons are to modified reimplementations; retrieval and prompt changes may affect baseline performance.

ideas.title: IRCoT uses the last reasoning sentence for retrieval
ideas.statement: IRCoT couples reasoning and information gathering by using the last generated chain-of-thought sentence s_(t-1) as the next retrieval query.

ideas.title: Adaptive similarity thresholds and hyperparameter tuning
ideas.statement: The matching threshold is empirical and several hyperparameters require careful tuning; adaptive selection is an open research direction.
ideas.conditions: No adaptive controller or robustness guarantee is supplied.

ideas.title: IRCoT notes shift input processing away from the main model
ideas.statement: Table 8 token totals in Fanout/FRAMES/Hotpot/MultiHop order: GPT main input baseline->notes 273K->68K,183K->37K,99K->26K,909K->189K; main output 385->444,312->280,205->193,322->412; notes input 902K/658K/433K/40K and output 1.8K/862/650/324. Llama main input 197K->154K,192K->116K,167K->100K,429K->99K; output 511->552,732->735,557->561,313->680; notes input 1.4M/1.2M/1.1M/338K and output 7.6K/3.9K/3.3K/2.9K.
ideas.conditions: Average cumulative input/output across calls; K=thousand, M=million.
validity_flags: Llama IRCoT main-input reduction is not uniformly at least 1.5x (Fanout 197K to 154K).

ideas.title: Accumulating retrieval creates context overload and distraction
ideas.statement: The paper motivates note compression by four problems of concatenating retrieved documents during iterative QA: finite context capacity, growing computation, irrelevant or redundant information that distracts reasoning/planning, and poor readability of long reasoning traces.
ideas.conditions: Iterative retrieval over multiple documents; motivation cites prior work rather than establishing a new theorem.

ideas.title: Iterative RAG query-retrieve-generate recurrence
ideas.statement: For question x and previous reasoning steps s_<t, generate q_t=Q(x,s_<t), retrieve D_qt=ret(q_t), and generate s_t=LM([D_qt,x,s_<t]); typically q_1=x and stop at a final answer or a maximum step count.
ideas.conditions: External document corpus D; generic formulation presented for iterative RAG.

ideas.title: Generalization to newer and smaller models remains open
ideas.statement: The authors identify evaluation on only two LLMs as a limitation and propose extending the work to newer, smaller open-source models.
ideas.conditions: GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-70B are the evaluated models.

ideas.title: Changing live Wikipedia can mismatch static benchmark answers
ideas.statement: The authors note that Wikipedia pages change frequently, so retrieved information can mismatch static benchmark ground truth and affect measured performance.
ideas.conditions: Dynamic online corpus evaluated against fixed QA labels.

ideas.title: The main model can substitute a company founding year for a birth year
ideas.statement: Table 20 attributes a hallucination to the main model: after notes identify Kodansha's founder and founding year and Evening's final year, it uses 1909 as the founder's birth year without retrieving that information, and returns age 113.
ideas.conditions: Selected FRAMES GPT-4o-mini trace, with conflicting magazine-name results also visible.
validity_flags: The displayed output also does not equal the simple year difference 2023-1909=114; dates and age basis are unsupported.

ideas.title: Matched reasoning and notes models at temperature 0.7
ideas.statement: Experiments use GPT-4o-mini with a 128K context and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct hosted by vLLM on eight A100-80GB GPUs with a configured 64K context. Temperature is 0.7, and the same LLM serves as main model and note writer.
ideas.conditions: Configured Llama context limit, not a claim about the model's maximum architecture limit.

ideas.title: Cross-model transfer and cache delivery
ideas.statement: DroidSpeak is described as selectively recomputing important KV layers for sharing across fine-tuned LLMs; LMCache is described as a knowledge delivery network for cache storage and transfer.
ideas.conditions: Background contextualization of reuse and system-level delivery.

ideas.title: Per-document notes are aggregated into the observation
ideas.statement: At iteration t, a dedicated note model extracts r_i=LM_notes(q_t,d_i) for each of the top-k documents; O_t is the union/aggregation of r_i over i=1..k. The main model receives compact O_t instead of raw documents.
ideas.conditions: Section 3.1 motivates a smaller note-taker, but experiments use the same model for main reasoning and note extraction. Appendix prompt also conditions on previously extracted content, omitted from Eq. 6.

ideas.title: Notes retain conflicting claims even when final query progresses
ideas.statement: Table 12 shows GPT-4o-mini rejecting an initially irrelevant football result, then receiving mutually conflicting claims about the first VAR-related World Cup goal, selecting one result and querying the player's club to finish with Atlético Madrid.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative FRAMES trace; extracted as evidence of conflict handling, not a sports fact.
validity_flags: Choosing one conflicting result is not independent verification; notes compression does not ensure fact consistency.

ideas.title: Notes trace resolves conflicting birthplace evidence with another query
ideas.statement: In Table 11, the Llama notes trace identifies a mayor, receives conflicting Oklahoma City/Oak Park birthplace observations, explicitly requests confirmation, then retrieves the census population and rounds it to 506,000.
ideas.conditions: Selected FRAMES trace, not an independently verified biographical or census claim.
validity_flags: Illustrates recovery on one example; does not quantify conflict detection reliability.

ideas.title: Illustrative notes-based two-hop reasoning
ideas.statement: Figure 1 illustrates a Colorado orogeny query: retrieve and note that its eastern sector reaches the High Plains, then retrieve and note the High Plains elevation range, then answer 1,800 to 7,000 ft. The notes LLM filters top Wikipedia pages before observations enter the reasoning context.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative workflow; not independent evidence of factual correctness or average performance.
validity_flags: Selected worked example, not controlled evaluation.

ideas.title: Notes prompt explicitly suppresses previously extracted and irrelevant content
ideas.statement: Figure 5 supplies a Markdown page, previous context and query, and requests only relevant information not already extracted, with no outside-source additions. Output begins YES# for usable new context and NO# for unknown answers, irrelevant text or duplicate content.
ideas.conditions: Prompted deduplication/relevance control; Eq.6 abstracts away previous context.
validity_flags: Prompt requirements do not guarantee factuality or exhaustive relevant-information retention.

ideas.title: Repeated searches can leave internally inconsistent quantitative notes
ideas.statement: Table 18 explicitly presents conflicting notes about the ninth-largest European country and a retry that selects Poland before answering Warsaw. The displayed ordered list is internally inconsistent: France's listed area exceeds Ukraine's despite a lower rank, and Poland's exceeds Finland's despite a lower rank.
ideas.conditions: Selected FRAMES failure/recovery illustration; no independent geographic claims inferred.
validity_flags: Author caption calls the retry corrective, but the displayed numeric ordering remains inconsistent; apparent recovery is not full evidence validation.

ideas.title: Implementation does not support FlashAttention
ideas.statement: The current SemShareKV prototype demonstrates the method using standard attention and does not support FlashAttention; integration is future work.
ideas.conditions: Reported efficiency is not an optimized FlashAttention serving-stack comparison.

ideas.title: Notes comparison explores the second entity and verifies a shared film
ideas.statement: For the same HotpotQA question as Tables 14-16, Table 17 NotesWriting identifies Lucy Fry, retrieves separate film notes for both actors, then explicitly checks Xavier Samuel in Mr. Church and returns that title after four searches.
ideas.conditions: Selected GPT-4o-mini comparison; main trace initially receives an incomplete list for Xavier Samuel but explores the other actor.
validity_flags: Paired example illustrates a possible benefit, not causal evidence that compression alone produces the better trajectory.

ideas.title: Repeated query reformulation can recover missing attributes
ideas.statement: Table 13 shows a GPT-4o-mini notes trace repeatedly receiving no relevant information, switching to a first-ladies list, then reformulating family queries until a mother's maiden name is found and combined into Jane Ballou.
