ideas.title: Source-text availability and OCR substitution
ideas.statement: The design focuses on deciding when exact text is needed; digital documents often retain source text, while an OCR component could replace lookup for scans without retraining the selector.
validity_flags: OCR replacement is proposed modularity, not evaluated as an equivalent noiseless lookup.

ideas.title: One retrieved page recovers most task-macro gain
ideas.statement: The category-macro k=0→all increase is 43.00→51.11 (+8.11), while the separate unweighted task-macro analysis gives +4.88. Retrieving one page recovers +3.00, or 61.5%, of the task-macro gap. Single-document QA gains +13.73 at k=1 and another +1.25 using all selections.
ideas.conditions: Do not combine task-macro intermediate-budget results with category-macro headline Avg.

ideas.title: Task-wise selected-count bucket heterogeneity
ideas.statement: Figure 4 reports SEER full bucket mean minus task-level Glyph score, in count-bucket order [0,1,2,3,4+], with null meaning empty: {"multifieldqa_zh": [null, 21.4, 3.0, 3.4, null], "passage_retrieval_zh": [9.0, 5.9, null, null, null], "multifieldqa_en": [null, 13.0, 10.5, 6.5, null], "dureader": [-2.4, 2.6, 8.1, -6.4, null], "qasper": [12.9, 8.3, 11.2, 3.4, null], "passage_retrieval_en": [-2.5, -2.8, 9.5, 9.5, null], "hotpotqa": [-6.9, -2.2, -3.0, 11.0, null], "narrativeqa": [5.0, 0.3, 4.3, 4.9, -21.8], "trec": [null, -6.5, -1.7, 0.3, null], "multi_news": [null, 6.3, 2.9, 0.1, 8.5], "vcsum": [1.0, 3.0, 3.4, 1.3, null], "qmsum": [2.0, 1.3, 1.5, 0.8, 3.5], "samsum": [-1.6, 0.8, -7.7, -1.1, null], "gov_report": [4.5, null, 11.7, 1.1, null]}.
ideas.conditions: 14 tasks with sufficient bucket coverage; task order uses SEER(all)−SEER(k0) endpoint gain.
validity_flags: Bucket means are observational; sparse buckets such as NarrativeQA4+ are noisy and not task-level effects.

ideas.title: Retrieval gains differ across tasks
ideas.statement: Figure 3 full-minus-k0 task endpoint gains are +30.42 MultiFieldQA-Zh, +8.37 Qasper, +0.79 QMSum and −3.17 GovReport. Bucket means compare different selected-count sample groups, not randomized budget interventions.
validity_flags: Sparse buckets are noisy; bucket differences are not causal retrieval effects.

ideas.title: Recursive-reader comparison configuration
ideas.statement: The comparison runs authors’ RLM framework and post-trained mit-oasys/rlm-qwen3-8b-v0.1 via a LongBench adapter. Full untruncated documents reside in a local REPL context variable; the root QA template points to it. Greedy decoding uses temperature0, top_p1, max_tokens2048, max_depth1, max_iterations8; native per-call window40960. Deterministic wrapper removal improves scoring.
ideas.conditions: Seven QA tasks only; vLLM OpenAI-compatible endpoint; RLM source Zhang et al. 2025.

ideas.title: Combine recursive text reading with visual compression
ideas.statement: Authors hypothesize that independent recursive calls can fragment cross-passage reasoning in single-window LongBench QA, whereas RLM is aimed at much larger corpora. Text recursion and visual compression operate along different axes and might be combined.
validity_flags: Mechanistic explanation and combinability are proposed, not experimentally isolated.

ideas.title: RLM underperforms in single-window LongBench QA comparison
ideas.conditions: Same official scorer, restricted QA-7 setup and RLM decoding protocol.
validity_flags: Does not assess RLM’s reported hundred-thousand/million-token regime; cross-family training differs.

ideas.title: No batch-one LongBench latency advantage
ideas.statement: GLM/Glyph/SEER server prefill is .23/.21/.22s and client+server .23/.29/.29s; median E2E is 1.07/3.61/5.47s, median output 8/235/381 tokens, mean prompt 5811/1983/7678, and n>30s is 1/10/14. Decode throughput is ~76/75.5/76.3 tok/s after matching GLM output length; its raw 36 tok/s reflects very short answers.
ideas.conditions: Latency subset differs from full 4750-sample token accounting; same 9B backbone.

ideas.title: Controlled latency protocol
ideas.statement: Single H100 80GB, batch 1, ten samples per each of 21 tasks; completed n=210 GLM, 200 Glyph, 210 SEER. Cold max_tokens=1 probes measure TTFT; server time excludes client construction/transfer while client+server includes them. Medians and counts over 30s expose long-output tails.
validity_flags: Different completed-sample counts across models; 10 Glyph samples absent.

ideas.title: Page-budget-matched intrinsic baselines
ideas.statement: Random, first-page and BM25 selectors receive the per-example SEER page count with a one-page minimum, averaging 1.77 pages against SEER 1.62 on gold-nonempty examples. All-pages and oracle are separate unrestricted/reference strategies.
validity_flags: One-page minimum prevents matched baselines from abstaining, confounding all-sample F1 comparison.

ideas.title: Learned selection ceiling limits distributed evidence
ideas.statement: The nearly three-page ceiling is inherited from training rather than scaling with context length, making single-round selection recall-limited when evidence extends over more than three pages.
validity_flags: Learned distributional ceiling, not a hard software cap; rare selections exceed three.

ideas.title: Raw selection distribution saturates near three pages
ideas.statement: Raw selected-count buckets 0/1/2/3/4+ have shares 5.9/47.2/16.5/30.3/0.3%. For contexts 1–3, 4–6, 7–10 and 11+ pages, the respective within-row shares are [1.0,65.3,21.9,11.8,0.0], [7.9,34.5,10.1,46.8,0.7], [13.2,28.9,12.7,45.2,0.0], [15.8,15.8,17.8,50.0,0.7]%. The modal budget shifts from one to three, then saturates.
ideas.conditions: Figure uses raw predictions before canonicalization; rounding may keep shares from summing exactly to 100%.

ideas.title: Visual and lexical selectors favor different evidence regimes
ideas.statement: SEER/BM25 page F1: low lexical overlap n1548 .487/.474; high overlap n1459 .675/.746; abstractive/summarization n908 .659/.661; distributed >3 gold pages n299 .516/.514. Both finite-budget selectors are limited on distributed evidence.
validity_flags: Subset definition thresholds and uncertainty are not specified in this passage.

ideas.title: SEER Select-Retrieve-Reason
ideas.statement: SEER visually scans all rendered pages, selects query-relevant images, retrieves their source text, and reasons over both global visual context and precise retrieved text.

ideas.title: Full-parameter SFT and token weights
ideas.statement: Training uses full-parameter Glyph-9B, AdamW β=(0.9,0.95), decay .01, learning rate 3e-6, warmup .05, clip 1, total batch 2, per-GPU microbatch 1, 6000 steps (~1.2 epochs), right truncation at 16384, bfloat16, full-shard FSDP without CPU offload, checkpointing, SDPA, seed 42. Tool-call tokens weight 2, format tags 1.2, answer boundary 1; final step-6000 checkpoint is reported.

ideas.title: Sparse valid retrieval selections
ideas.statement: Across 4,750 examples and 31,182 rendered pages (6.6 pages/example), SEER selects a mean 1.59 valid pages and median 1, with fewer than 1% selecting more than three.
ideas.conditions: Valid counts are after deduplication and index-range canonicalization.

ideas.statement: Token IDs: endoftext/padding 151329, user 151336, assistant 151337, observation 151338, think/open 151350 and close 151351, tool_call/open 151352 and close 151353, begin_of_image 151339, end_of_image 151340 and image placeholder 151363.

ideas.title: Tool-integrated reasoning background
ideas.statement: SEER adopts the tool-integrated reasoning paradigm: CoT generates intermediate steps, IRCoT and ReAct interleave reasoning with external tools, and trainable tool invocation can improve selection beyond fixed templates.

ideas.title: Teacher filtering and unevaluated modalities
ideas.statement: Answer-conditioned teacher filtering underrepresents distributed evidence; SEER is specialized for QA over rendered documents and was not evaluated on natural images, charts or OCR benchmarks.

ideas.title: Main SFT configuration
ideas.statement: SEER trains on 2 H100 80GB GPUs using Verl for 6,000 optimizer steps, learning rate 3e-6, global batch size 2, maximum sequence length 16,384, FSDP and gradient checkpointing.

ideas.title: Training sources use training splits
ideas.statement: Trajectories are constructed from training splits of 2WikiMQA, HotpotQA, GovReport, LCC-Python, MuSiQue, Qasper and TriviaQA.

ideas.title: Complete training trajectory example
ideas.statement: The example has three image inputs and selects pages 1 and 3, receives laptop and monitor source prices 1299.99 and 449.99, then reasons to 1749.98. It illustrates the sequence user→assistant tool_call→observation→think→answer.

ideas.title: Only selection, reasoning and answer receive supervision
ideas.statement: User inputs, the assistant generation prompt and system observations have mask zero; tool calls, CoT and final answers have mask one before optional weighting. Dataset-level masking leaves about 20–30% of sample tokens supervised.

ideas.title: Uniform compression loses query-critical details
ideas.statement: Applying the same visual compression across a document trades token efficiency against fine-grained details, although many queries need precise information from only a small subset of the context.
ideas.conditions: Claim concerns existing visual-text compression methods discussed by the paper.

ideas.title: Vist slow-fast compression
ideas.statement: Vist uses a fast visual path for distant low-salience context and a slow LLM path for proximal tokens, fixing compression by position rather than by the current query.

ideas.title: Query-conditioned page selection
ideas.statement: The same autoregressive model f predicts S=f(I,q), a subset of page indices {1,...,m}; duplicates are removed and invalid indices discarded without correction.

ideas.title: Visual-text compression
ideas.statement: A long textual context is rendered into images and encoded by a VLM; the text-token to vision-token ratio measures compression, with prior work commonly reporting 3–4 times fewer tokens.

ideas.title: GPT as an adaptive arithmetic-coding entropy model
ideas.statement: GPT-AC uses P_i(t_i|t_1,...,t_{i-1}) from the pretrained GPT as the next-token entropy distribution for both arithmetic encoding and decoding. A starting EOS token t_0 supplies P_1.

ideas.title: Efficiency may widen access and reduce energy use
ideas.statement: The impact statement proposes that cheaper personalization can improve access for users with limited data and reduce energy consumption and carbon footprint.
ideas.conditions: Prospective societal benefits; the paper reports neither energy measurements nor accessibility outcomes.

ideas.title: Test improved compressors inside the multi-document framework
ideas.statement: The authors hypothesize that improved single-document hyperparameters, architectures or weight optimization will improve multi-document compression and propose investigating alternative compressor architectures.
ideas.conditions: Only one Gemma-2b-based compressor architecture is experimentally evaluated here.

ideas.title: Compression can preserve discriminatory user-data signals
ideas.statement: User-specific compression may preserve biases in user data and cause unfair output; the authors identify compressing only relevant non-discriminatory signals as future work.
ideas.conditions: The study does not solve or experimentally evaluate bias mitigation.

ideas.title: Test whether skill-versus-knowledge behavior generalizes
ideas.statement: The authors conjecture the contrast between useful style averaging and harmful knowledge-detail averaging extends to broader task families and leave further tasks for future research.
ideas.conditions: Evidence covers two skill tasks and one processed synthetic knowledge task.

ideas.title: Concatenate separately compressed documents
ideas.statement: One ablation replaces mean pooling with concatenation of individual document compressions, increasing generator token-processing cost but preserving new-document update computation relative to ComMer.
ideas.conditions: Assumes storage overhead is negligible; a fixed per-document length makes aggregate length grow with document count.

ideas.title: Compress concatenated documents jointly
ideas.statement: A second ablation concatenates all documents before compression, preserving final generator-token count but increasing compression/update computation because changing the set requires recompressing the combined text.
ideas.conditions: Compared with independent compression plus mean pooling; applies when concatenated compressions are precomputed.

ideas.title: End-to-end response cross-entropy trains only compression parameters
ideas.statement: Each training example independently compresses its documents, merges them, and passes the aggregate with x_i and y_i through the frozen response LLM. Cross-entropy over y_i tokens backpropagates only into trainable compression embeddings and LoRA weights.
ideas.conditions: Backbone LLM parameters remain unchanged.

ideas.title: Compress each document with learned suffix embeddings and LoRA
ideas.statement: Append trainable compression embeddings to each document; process it independently with a frozen LLM augmented by trainable LoRA weights; use last-layer states at the compression embeddings as its soft prompt.
ideas.conditions: Architecture follows Ge et al. 2024 and uses Hu et al. 2022 LoRA; only adapter and compression embeddings train, not the backbone.

ideas.title: ComMer generalizes to additional test-time documents
ideas.statement: In tweet paraphrasing with four compression embeddings, ComMer improves when tested on more documents than used in training and degrades when tested on fewer. Even a one-document-trained compressor benefits from averaging multiple test document compressions.
ideas.conditions: Other experiments match training and testing document counts; ROUGE-L differences in this ablation are too noisy to expose a trend.

ideas.title: Generator concatenates merged compression with instruction embeddings
ideas.statement: ComMer supplies concat(mean_i compress(doc_i), embed(x)) to its generator, where embed is the shared backbone embedding layer.
ideas.conditions: Mean is elementwise across matching compressed document representations; compression length is varied in experiments.

ideas.title: Incremental mean update avoids recompressing old documents
ideas.statement: When a document is added, ComMer compresses only the new document and incorporates it into the existing aggregate with normalization maintaining the mean. Old documents need not be processed again.
ideas.conditions: A stored aggregate and document count suffice for additions; no quantitative update-latency benchmark is provided.

ideas.title: Additional irrelevant memories degrade ComMer knowledge QA
ideas.statement: On processed PerLTQA, a single document is best because additional documents contribute irrelevant information. Prompt-tuning remains comparatively robust, while adding documents worsens both perplexity and ROUGE-L for ComMer.
ideas.conditions: This contrasts with useful multi-document style signals in LaMP; it is not a claim that more relevant evidence always harms QA.

ideas.title: Mean pooling can destroy detailed knowledge
ideas.statement: The authors hypothesize that averaging causes destructive interference between individual-document details that are essential to knowledge-intensive answers, producing a broad summary representation that fails to preserve detailed information.
ideas.conditions: Offered as a possible explanation of PerLTQA degradation, not directly measured latent interference.

ideas.title: LaMP tests style transfer to unseen users
ideas.statement: ComMer is evaluated on personalized tweet paraphrasing using historical tweets and personalized news headline generation using past article-headline pairs. The LaMP user-based split holds out users from training.
ideas.conditions: Only these two LaMP tasks are evaluated, not all seven tasks.

ideas.title: Test skill compression on larger document collections
ideas.statement: The authors leave testing personalized skill learning on larger per-user document collections to future work, anticipating that more examples may improve style extraction.
ideas.conditions: The evaluated datasets contain at most eight documents for most users; empirical scaling beyond that is not established.

ideas.title: Extend latent compression to merged multi-document representations
ideas.statement: ComMer extends latent representation compression methods to multiple documents by merging their representations for further compression.
ideas.conditions: Authors cite Mu et al. 2023, Chevalier et al. 2023 and Ge et al. 2024 as latent-compression predecessors.

ideas.title: Single-document transfer is interpreted as latent-space linearity
ideas.statement: The authors interpret improved test-time mean pooling for a compressor trained with one document as suggesting linear behavior in neural latent spaces, citing Elhage, Bricken and Park.
ideas.conditions: Interpretation from one transfer experiment; this does not establish general linearity of neural networks.

ideas.title: Mean pooling creates an order-independent fixed-size soft prompt
ideas.statement: ComMer aggregates independently compressed document representations with elementwise mean pooling. The merged soft prompt shape is independent of document count and invariant to document order, and it conditions a frozen response-generating LLM.
ideas.conditions: Compression length and hidden dimension must match across documents; order invariance applies across documents, not tokens inside each document.

ideas.title: Mean pooling is competitive with concatenation alternatives
ideas.statement: For tweet paraphrasing, vanilla mean-pooling ComMer outperforms concatenating separate compressions. Compressing concatenated source documents offers only marginal quality improvement while incurring higher compression and update cost.
ideas.conditions: Authors conclude mean pooling is most cost-effective for this tested setting; Figure 7 uses perplexity against prompt token count. Figure 7 is for eight documents and favors mean pooling on the perplexity-versus-token frontier; concatenating compressions can yield better absolute ROUGE-L at much larger token budgets.

ideas.title: ROUGE-L variability motivates accompanying perplexity
ideas.statement: The paper uses perplexity and ROUGE-L on both LaMP tasks and processed PerLTQA. Authors report substantial noise in ROUGE-based metrics and base conclusions on perplexity supported by more variable ROUGE-L trends.
ideas.conditions: No human assessment is reported; conclusions depend on these automatic metrics.

ideas.title: Pretrain by reconstructing a randomly indexed document
ideas.statement: Following Ge et al. 2024, ComMer extends autoencoding to multi-document input: prefix each document with its index, merge compressions, and ask “What does document n contain?” for a randomly selected n. FineWeb documents are truncated to 150 characters and grouped into one million examples; the default pretraining duration is one epoch.
ideas.conditions: Unless otherwise stated, models undergo this pretraining; the task is unsupervised reconstruction rather than a user-labeled personalization task.

ideas.title: Knowledge evaluation uses synthetic persona memory subsets
ideas.statement: The authors derive PerLTQA examples by randomly choosing a subset of a synthetic persona’s memories and an associated question-answer pair, with 27 personas for training and 5 for testing. The task requires preserving details, sometimes verbatim.
ideas.conditions: The paper reuses the PerLTQA name for its processed version, so results do not necessarily describe the unmodified dataset.

ideas.title: Document-count generalization uses within-model perplexity differences
ideas.statement: Define P_ij as perplexity when a model trained with j documents is evaluated using i documents. Heatmap cell (i,j) reports P_ij − P_jj, with negative differences indicating improvement relative to its matched-count test baseline.
ideas.conditions: Tweet paraphrasing; four compression embeddings.

ideas.title: Personalization spans skill learning and knowledge-base use
ideas.statement: Personalized skill learning infers user-specific behavior or style from examples, whereas knowledge-base personalization answers questions using user-specific semantic and episodic memories.
ideas.conditions: Taxonomy in related work; LaMP and PerLTQA illustrate the two settings.

ideas.title: Per-user fine-tuning has training and freshness costs
ideas.statement: Adapting model weights separately for each user requires individualized training and updates; offline updates can compromise freshness, and users with little data can receive poor models.
ideas.conditions: Motivating background attributed to prior personalization literature.

ideas.title: Fixed soft prompts support fast user adaptation
ideas.statement: Figure 1 characterizes ComMer as frugal with inference tokens, invariant to document position, and able to adapt quickly to new data without per-user training.
ideas.conditions: The figure’s “No training required” describes user adaptation after shared compressor training; it is not a claim that the compressor is untrained.

ideas.title: PPlug uses query-dependent weighted document embeddings
ideas.statement: The paper describes concurrent PPlug as a frozen-encoder method using a query-dependent weighted average of document embeddings; this prevents precomputing the aggregate, unlike ComMer mean pooling. Authors further attribute embedding interference to its frozen encoder and small embedding dimension.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative comparison, not a controlled PPlug benchmark in this paper; interference explanation is the authors’ interpretation.

ideas.title: Pretrained language understanding supports a useful compressor
ideas.statement: The design assumes language understanding is required for document compression and reuses a frozen pretrained LLM to reduce training costs, with LoRA adapting it for compression.
ideas.conditions: Architectural rationale rather than a proven necessary condition.

ideas.title: Compare generic in-domain sequential and absent pretraining
ideas.statement: For tweet paraphrasing, the authors compare no pretraining, FineWeb reconstruction pretraining, reconstruction of users’ training tweets, and FineWeb followed by tweet reconstruction. They report lower downstream perplexity with pretraining and little effect of pretraining dataset choice. Averaged across embedding counts, perplexity is 2.144 without pretraining, 2.127 with FineWeb, 2.124 with tweets and 2.123 with FineWeb+tweets; ROUGE-L is 0.442, 0.444, 0.448 and 0.447 respectively. At 4 embeddings, FineWeb perplexity (2.202) is worse than no pretraining (2.190); at 32 embeddings, no pretraining gives higher ROUGE-L (0.454) than all three pretrained settings.
ideas.conditions: Results quantified in Table 1; ROUGE-L is more variable and pretraining benefit is not uniform for every cell.

ideas.title: Personalization on real user data raises unresolved privacy issues
ideas.statement: Training ComMer on sensitive real user information raises privacy and security concerns. The authors propose robust anonymization/security or high-quality synthetic data and acknowledge data-protection compliance as an unresolved deployment requirement.
ideas.conditions: These challenges are explicitly outside the paper’s scope; no privacy guarantee is established.

ideas.title: Prompt-based personalization scales with context length
ideas.statement: Supplying user documents in a prompt is constrained by context windows, positional bias, and inference latency and compute that scale with prompt length.
ideas.conditions: Motivating background, not a new quantitative cost measurement.

ideas.title: Prompt-tuning prepends learned embeddings to uncompressed documents
ideas.statement: The Lester et al. prompt-tuning baseline supplies concat(soft_prompt, embed(concat(doc_1,...,doc_n,x))). Its trainable soft-prompt length corresponds to ComMer’s compression length, but it retains the document text in the generator input.
ideas.conditions: Reported comparison is against this shared task-trained prompt-tuning baseline, not per-user full fine-tuning.

ideas.title: Merge document representations rather than model weights
ideas.statement: ComMer merges document representations rather than existing model or PEFT weights, permitting adaptation to new inputs without requiring an inventory of trained models.
ideas.conditions: Conceptual distinction from model merging literature.

ideas.title: Retrieve LaMP examples with BM25 and filter long inputs
ideas.statement: LaMP tweet and headline experiments use BM25 to retrieve relevant documents following LaMP methodology; examples longer than 2900 characters are excluded, including PerLTQA examples.
ideas.conditions: This input filtering constrains evaluation and long-document generalization.

ideas.title: Independent compression enables future retrieval-based subset merging
ideas.statement: The authors propose using only relevant documents per query with independently precomputed compressions. A single precomputed joint compression of all concatenated documents cannot provide this subset selection in the same way.
ideas.conditions: Potential future retrieval integration, not a tested retrieval-based ComMer system.

ideas.title: ComMer amortizes personalization training across users
ideas.statement: ComMer learns to compress user documents into compact representations, merge them, and feed them to a frozen LLM, with training cost amortized across users instead of separate user models.
ideas.conditions: Claim concerns shared compressor training; document compression still has a forward-pass cost.

ideas.title: More documents improve compressed style learning
ideas.statement: Figure 4 shows ComMer perplexity decreasing as document count grows for both tweet paraphrasing and headline generation across 4–128 compression embeddings. The authors characterize the trend as a power law and suggest further improvement with more documents.
ideas.conditions: Observed count range is 1–8 for tweets and 1–4 for headlines; no fitted exponent or extrapolation validation is given.

ideas.title: Vary document counts and compression lengths on skill tasks
ideas.statement: The skill-learning experiments vary document counts over 0,1,2,4,8 for tweet paraphrasing and 0,1,2,4 for news headlines, and embedding counts over 4,8,16,32,64,128 for ComMer and prompt-tuning.
ideas.conditions: Prompt length proxies computational cost; results are for Gemma-2b and default one-epoch pretraining.

ideas.title: ComMer improves the small-token-budget skill-learning frontier
ideas.statement: On tweet paraphrasing and headline generation, ComMer can use fewer inference prompt tokens for better quality than prompt-tuning in the small-token regime. For tweet perplexity the authors identify a budget up to 128 tokens; cutoffs differ for headline generation and ROUGE-L. Prompt-tuning can achieve better absolute quality with larger prompts.
ideas.conditions: Gemma-2b, specified document/embedding grid; cost means generator prompt tokens, not measured end-to-end runtime. Figure 3 does not show confidence intervals.

ideas.title: Averaging suppresses document specifics to reveal style
ideas.statement: The authors propose that each document suggests possible user styles; combining documents narrows the shared style signal, and averaging suppresses document-specific features while retaining that signal.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative explanation for observed style-task improvements, not an established mechanistic result.

ideas.title: Training requires documents instruction and personalized target triples
ideas.statement: The training set contains N examples, each comprising a variable-size document set, an instruction x_i, and response y_i based on personalized information from that set.
ideas.conditions: N_i is the number of documents for example i. Render confirms formal notation; the body’s repeated i in one document-set subscript is a typographic inconsistency.

ideas.title: Token-processing and document-update costs are distinct
ideas.statement: Token-processing cost concerns tokens passed through the frozen response backbone; update cost concerns computation to update the document-set representation when a new document arrives. Mean pooling aims to reduce both.
ideas.conditions: The paper discusses costs structurally rather than reporting measured runtime or hardware throughput.

ideas.title: Five context-management comparison criteria
ideas.statement: The comparison defines compact as actively compressing working context; trainable as learning the management policy; lossless as preserving raw content for later retrieval; agent-initiated as model-triggered compression; and open-source data as publicly released management-policy training data.

ideas.title: Data and compute constraints of open-domain video generation
ideas.statement: The paper motivates text-to-video synthesis as constrained by higher computational cost and less high-quality paired data than image generation; it contrasts billion-scale image-text corpora with approximately 10M WebVid videos.
ideas.conditions: Motivational assessment in the 2022 source, not a measured scaling law. The introduction calls [41] LAION-5B although the bibliography entry is LAION-400M.

ideas.title: Time-variable story conditioning
ideas.statement: A story is a sequence of textual prompts that narrates events over time; generation should condition frames at time t on the prompt active at time t. A single short prompt is argued to be inadequate for long videos.
ideas.conditions: The source presents this as a desired capability and a design motivation, rather than a formal sufficiency theorem.

ideas.title: Phenaki video token generation pipeline
ideas.statement: Phenaki encodes video into discrete compressed tokens using a temporally causal tokenizer, uses a bidirectional masked transformer conditioned on precomputed text tokens to generate video tokens, and decodes those tokens into video.
ideas.conditions: Open-domain text and potentially changing text prompts; compression concerns video representations, not shortening the text prompt.

ideas.title: Evolved skill banks grow from 12 seeds
ideas.statement: Gemini FullEvo retains 12 seeds and adds 28/45/55/32 evolved skills on EgoSchema/Video-MME long/EgoPlan-Bench/NextQA, ending with 40/57/67/44 skills.

ideas.title: Progressive disclosure loads full skill content selectively
ideas.statement: Skill runtimes package discovery metadata, natural-language procedures, and optional auxiliary files. Agents first inspect lightweight descriptions and load full procedures only when needed, allowing selective skill invocation without putting all available experience into context.

ideas.title: Replay evaluates behavioral consistency with reference skills
ideas.statement: For each WSA type, the same replay scenarios are run with reconstructed and reference skills to assess preservation of task progression, decisions, tool-use constraints, validation requirements, and final responses. Higher scores indicate more consistent behavior; scenarios vary execution paths, decisions, and attachments.

ideas.title: Reported overall replay fidelity increases from 0.455 to 0.503
ideas.statement: The paper reports average replay fidelity of 0.503 for W2S versus 0.455 for ASC, an absolute increase of 0.048. The relative increase computed from these displayed averages is about 10.55%, compatible with the abstract’s 10.5%.
ideas.conditions: Reported averaging weights and the aggregation unit are unspecified. The absolute gap is 4.8 percentage points if these are fractions, not a 10.5-point gain. Abstract reports 70 skills and describes summarization-/prompting-based baselines, while Section 6 details only ASC.

ideas.title: Generated skill should recover the evidence-derived WSA on re-parsing
ideas.statement: The unnumbered target is Parse_WSA(skill_hat) = (Ŵ, Ŝ, Â) ≈ (Ŵ(D), Ŝ(D), Â(D)). Readability permits approximation, but component boundaries should remain intact; non-workflow skills use a single-node graph with no edges.
ideas.conditions: A schematic fidelity aim rather than a defined numerical loss or exact equality guarantee.

ideas.title: Runtime attachments delimit execution dependencies and commitments
ideas.statement: A records runtime resources, interfaces, constraints, state interactions, validation requirements, and output commitments. Attachments describe what execution depends on or constrains, distinct from workflow topology and node behavior.

ideas.title: Summary-oriented induction can omit execution-critical details
ideas.statement: Summarizing traces can overfit incidental details and omit preconditions or recovery procedures; triggering conditions, task decomposition, tool policies, constraints, failure handling, and validation criteria play distinct execution roles that cannot be ranked solely by textual salience.

ideas.title: SMART remains stable on one static long moment
ideas.statement: Figure 9 example 2 shows both visual-text MLLM and SMART matching ground truth 124–150 s for a man and woman in front of a circular sculpture.
ideas.conditions: A selected low-motion example does not establish that complementary audio caused stable predictions.

ideas.title: Concise CoT baseline
ideas.statement: CCoT reduces explicit reasoning redundancy to obtain shorter outputs while aiming to preserve final-answer fidelity.

ideas.title: A redundant pause can be coherent without meaningful compression
ideas.statement: The negative example restates the relationship Ben=2×Suzy then writes B=2S and substitutes S=1. GPT-4o-mini scores utilization 1, continuity 5, confidence .90, demonstrating that local coherence alone does not establish a nontrivial compression gap.
ideas.conditions: Selected judge output; wording shifts from Ben’s age to Ben’s iPhone, so the high continuity score is reported, not independently endorsed.

ideas.title: Uniform-sampled Arena evolution also concentrates benefits on harder cases
ideas.statement: Table 8 Uniform-8 with/without evolution gives Codex easy/medium/hard scores 84.29/60.42/31.90 versus 85.83/58.19/29.03, and Claude Code 76.60/52.41/26.97 versus 77.73/49.92/24.58. Across backends, evolution lowers easy accuracy but improves medium/hard accuracy.
ideas.conditions: Same empirically defined tiers as the cascade comparison; no uncertainty intervals.

ideas.title: Unmodified Gemini skills correct a GPT-5.2 activity label
ideas.statement: Figure 7 Case 4 uses a Gemini-evolved bank unmodified on GPT-5.2 with one retained frame from 180. Visual-detail-matching and option-elimination distinguish long narrow knitting from a sweater, correcting B making a sweater to E knitting a scarf.
ideas.conditions: Selected illustrative win, not evidence that all skills transfer safely.

ideas.title: Comparison with selected-frame video systems
ideas.statement: Table 1 classifies prior LLoVi, MovieChat, MA-LMM, VideoAgent, Frame-Voyager, SeViLA, VideoTree, TimeChat, VTimeLLM, Video-LLaMA and LLaVA-Video as offline and without edge CPU or evolution; VisionClaw is online and edge CPU but lacks native evolution, while VisualClaw combines all three.
ideas.conditions: Authors’ qualitative comparison of the listed systems, not a measured universal priority claim.

ideas.title: Seeded markdown skill cards as preference rules
ideas.statement: Each skill has a name, one-line description used for retrieval, numbered procedural body, and anti-pattern section. The seed bank is bootstrapped from a held-out probe of the same evolver, then grows during use; cards are treated as implicit preference rules.

ideas.title: Evolver-only memory retrieval is infrequent
ideas.statement: Gemini FullEvo memory ingests/retrievals/retrievals-per-question are EgoSchema 340/11/.022, Video-MME long 578/22/.024, EgoPlan-Bench 266/44/.048, and NextQA 745/17/.017. Retrieved memories condition skill evolution and are never injected into the VLM answer prompt in these runs.

ideas.title: Balance engine transition attributes
ideas.statement: Following PlayGen, Yan records engine xyz position, alive state, collision and related attributes alongside images/actions, then samples across attributes for balanced transition characteristics such as uniform positions.
ideas.conditions: Applied after filtering to reduce scenario overfitting; balancing algorithm details are limited.

ideas.title: Joint fidelity, generalization and editable interaction
ideas.statement: The motivating challenges are jointly achieving high-fidelity real-time visuals, generalizable prompt control, and dynamic customization during interaction.
ideas.conditions: Problem framing for modern games requiring 1080P/60FPS, complex physics and granular inputs; not a formal impossibility result.

ideas.title: Interactive generative video
ideas.statement: Interactive generative video dynamically responds to user inputs to provide real-time, personalized visual experiences.
ideas.conditions: Contrasted with conventional video generation in the introduction.

ideas.title: Yan interactive video framework
ideas.statement: Yan combines AAA-level simulation, multi-modal generation and multi-granularity editing, all driven by user input; prompts can change during interaction to alter subsequent generated content.
ideas.conditions: Framework and demonstration scope; a static montage does not independently establish sustained real-time performance.

ideas.title: Routing header controls skill applicability and discovery
ideas.statement: Skill-IR separates a routing header (front matter and discovery description indicating when the skill applies) from three runtime components describing workflow, node-local decisions, and operational attachments.

ideas.title: SUPO trains on summarized multi-turn trajectories
ideas.statement: SUPO invokes a summarizer at fixed rollout intervals and replaces turns in both policy prompts and credit-assignment trajectories, computing RL over summarized histories.

ideas.title: Cheaper streaming inference also lowers surveillance cost
ideas.statement: The authors note that cheap always-on visual inference can enable covert surveillance as well as legitimate wearables, and place proposed governance at downstream policy and platform access controls.
ideas.conditions: Broader-impact discussion, not a tested governance mechanism.

ideas.title: Authors select L=150 in the audio-length sweep
ideas.statement: Under Overall Concatenation on QVHighlights, the authors select audio compression length L=150 and describe it as the best overall balance. Figure 5 shows the two recall curves peaking at L=150, while the plotted mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.75 curves rise slightly from L=150 to L=175. Thus the caption’s all-metrics optimum claim conflicts with the displayed mAP points.
ideas.conditions: Figure 5 tests L=50,75,100,125,150,175,200. L=150 is the authors’ chosen setting, not the maximum of every plotted series. The relative mAP ordering was checked by magnifying the original page-8 render; exact values of those points are not reported or inferred. The finite sweep does not establish a universal optimum; authors attribute shorter sequences to lost context and longer sequences to redundancy.

ideas.title: Keyword Average Probability (KAP)
ideas.statement: KAP is the mean probability over programming keywords, proposed as a keyword-bias diagnostic.
validity_flags: An average alone cannot measure distribution uniformity.
No explicit equation or set cardinality is given in this metric definition.

ideas.title: Method equations specify stage interfaces rather than a closed-form estimator
ideas.statement: The authors explicitly say W2S notation describes interfaces between reconstruction/generation stages, not a closed-form estimator.

ideas.title: Search benchmark answers use simple-evals LLM grading
ideas.statement: BrowseComp-Plus and DeepSearchQA use the simple-evals grader template to extract final answer, compare with gold for equivalence (small numerical margin allowed), emit correct yes/no and extract confidence, defaulting to100 if absent.
ideas.conditions: The paper supplies template but does not identify judge model or calibrate grading error.

ideas.title: WSA profiles stratify reconstruction by required components
ideas.statement: The dataset explicitly covers eight WSA combinations. Profiles identify a dominant type and trace-observable components. Non-workflow cases test semantic/resource reconstruction without a multistep scaffold; workflow cases test persistent execution contracts.

ideas.title: EgoPlan-Bench component ablation
ideas.statement: Accuracy percentages in order Cascade Plain, Seed, +Evolve, +SkillMemCat, memory-to-evolver Cat., Guide; after semicolon offline Uniform-8 Plain: Gemini [24.62,30.80,29.93,28.31,30.04,28.85;37.96]; GPT-5.2 [28.42,28.74,28.31,28.09,28.85,29.39;43.06].
ideas.conditions: Fixed VLM backbones; cascade at up to eight frames but often fewer. No uncertainty intervals reported for these table rows.

ideas.title: EgoSchema component ablation
ideas.statement: Accuracy percentages in order Cascade Plain, Seed, +Evolve, +SkillMemCat, memory-to-evolver Cat., Guide; after semicolon offline Uniform-8 Plain: Gemini [52.60,67.20,68.00,65.20,64.60,68.40;60.60]; GPT-5.2 [64.00,66.60,66.20,67.20,65.60,68.00;70.60].
ideas.conditions: Fixed VLM backbones; cascade at up to eight frames but often fewer. No uncertainty intervals reported for these table rows.

ideas.title: Weighted semantic return score
ideas.statement: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B compares source and revisit-tail images. Score is 0.45*appearance + 0.25*presence + 0.20*view + 0.10*scene, each in [0,5], then rescaled to [0,100]; appearance and presence dominate.

ideas.title: Cross-judge robustness sanity check
ideas.statement: On a shared stratified subset with identical images/prompts, Qwen scores 19.6±13.9; Claude Opus 4.6 20.7±11.1 (mean absolute difference 3.1, Pearson rho .93); GPT-5.5 21.1±11.4 (2.7,.94); human 20.9±11.9 (1.3,.96). Authors report preserved relative profile ordering.
ideas.conditions: Sanity check on a stratified subset; subset size and meaning of ± not specified here.
validity_flags: Subset size and uncertainty definition not specified
Agreement does not establish geometric truth

ideas.title: Admissible distance and density condition
ideas.statement: Appendix A defines an admissible nonnegative distance D on Omega×Omega as computable, symmetric and satisfying sum_y 2^(-D(x,y))≤1 for each x. In the density proof, the sum excludes y=x.
validity_flags: The text calls the uncomputable E admissible despite defining admissibility as computable; upper-semicomputability and diagonal/constant conventions require care.

ideas.title: I2V anchor-only baseline metric bundle
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Spatial Memory baseline metric bundle
ideas.statement: Spatial Memory baseline reports [13.6, 0.411, 0.554, 10.04, 0.26, 0.617, 6.0].
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Weight-only compression metric bundle
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Activation steering needs calibration
ideas.statement: Training-free interventions that manipulate internal activations offer flexibility but need careful calibration to avoid disrupting benign outputs.

ideas.title: Adaptive defense prompting
ideas.statement: The paper describes auto-refinement defenses that dynamically generate defense prompts to preemptively neutralize attacks, attributed to Wang et al. (2025b), the AdaShield citation.

ideas.title: Higher sparsity degrades benign VLM utility
ideas.statement: On TextVQA, RealWorldQA and ScienceQA, 20% sparsity changes Qwen2-VL-7B and LLaVA-Mistral-7B accuracy little, while InstructBLIP declines somewhat. At 50%, Safety-Potential Pruning roughly yields [57,55,66]% for LLaVA, [26,33,32]% for InstructBLIP and [81,65,76]% for Qwen2, with baseline roughly [65,60,72], [33,38,56] and [85,70,85] respectively. Magnitude pruning collapses InstructBLIP TextVQA to single-digit accuracy and harms Qwen2 strongly; Wanda often preserves more utility than Safety-Potential Pruning.
ideas.conditions: Approximate plot-read values; dataset vector order TextVQA, RealWorldQA, ScienceQA.

ideas.title: Aggressive pruning increases calibration-sampling variability
ideas.statement: With calibration size fixed at 128, six independent Qwen2-VL-7B pruning runs show greater DSR variability at 50% than 20% sparsity. Figure 11(b) spans roughly 93.9–95.0% at 20% and 96.1–98.6% at 50%, with medians around 94.5 and 97.7. The authors hypothesize that a compact diverse set exposes safety structure, whereas too many examples can activate irrelevant structure and dilute the signal.

ideas.title: Calibration size has a nonmonotonic safety effect
ideas.statement: For Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct, calibration size varies from 2 to 512; reported DSR improves to a peak near 64 examples and then declines, so simply enlarging calibration does not guarantee better safety. Figure 11(a) additionally shows a second near-equal 50%-sparsity peak at 256, rather than a strictly gradual decline after 64.
ideas.conditions: Figure 11 compares 20% and 50% pruning; specific test dataset is not stated in Section 5.2.

ideas.title: Activation-energy safety sensitivity
ideas.statement: For weight matrix W in R^(C_out × C_in) and input activations X in R^(B × L × C_in), channel sensitivity is S_j = ||A^S_j||_2^2 − ||A^NS_j||_2^2. Positive sensitivity means higher activation energy with the safety prompt; near-zero or negative sensitivity is treated as weak or counteractive safety response.

ideas.title: CoCA constitutional contrastive decoding
ideas.statement: CoCA computes the output-logit difference with versus without a safety principle, scales that difference, and adds it to the logits to steer generation without training.

ideas.title: Finer audio alignment and broader retrieval settings
ideas.statement: The authors propose dense audio-text alignment, open-world or zero-shot retrieval, additional modalities and hierarchical temporal modeling as future extensions.
ideas.conditions: Proposals rather than evaluated SMART capabilities.

ideas.title: Complex reasoning is more pruning-sensitive than object grounding
ideas.statement: Qwen2-VL-7B has little complex-task degradation at 20% sparsity, with slight MMMU/MM-Vet gains in several methods. At 50%, Figure 7 shows substantial MMMU/MM-Vet accuracy loss and relatively stable POPE. Safety-Potential Pruning is approximately 47% MMMU, 43% MM-Vet and 87% POPE versus dense roughly 54%,60%,86%. The text ranks sensitivity MM-Vet > MMMU > POPE, while separately calling MMMU’s 50% drop largest, an internal inconsistency. A possible moderate-pruning regularization effect is conjectural.

ideas.title: Concise refusal prompt
ideas.statement: The concise comparison prompt retains the sensitive/graphic/harmful/inappropriate-content condition and the fixed apology refusal, removing the authors’ enumerated examples and prohibition on elaboration.

ideas.title: Defense Success Rate and automated safety judging
ideas.statement: LLaMA Guard 2 labels responses safe or unsafe. Defense Success Rate (DSR) is the percentage of malicious queries that produce safe responses; benign visual-question-answering utility is assessed through VLMEvalKit.
ideas.conditions: DSR is judge-dependent; evaluation separates safety from benign utility.

ideas.title: Safety prompt activation shifts increase with depth
ideas.statement: Activation-difference histograms show small or negative shifts in shallow layers and larger positive shifts in deeper layers for Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct on HOD and MM-SafetyBench and LLaVA-V1.6-Mistral-7B on HOD.

ideas.title: ECSO image-to-text safety restoration
ideas.statement: ECSO is described as a training-free defense that transforms malicious visual inputs into descriptive text so the model re-evaluates the request using semantic content alone.

ideas.title: Pruning changes safety-conditioned representation separation
ideas.statement: The study fixes 160 MM-SafetyBench examples, extracts final-layer representations from Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct under four conditions (dense or 50% sparse, with or without a safety prompt), and visualizes them with 2D t-SNE. The authors report clearer separation between prompt conditions after pruning.

ideas.title: ETA evaluate-then-align defense
ideas.statement: ETA is described as a training-free two-phase inference framework that evaluates generation safety and aligns unsafe behavior using prefix conditioning and best-of-N selection.

ideas.title: Three patterns of automated false-unsafe judgments
ideas.statement: Manual review identifies automated unsafe labels for harmless or non-executable procedural-looking responses, responses acknowledging harmful intent without actionable details, and verbatim repetition of typography from the image. Figure 14 illustrates placeholder company names, a generic description without executable instructions, and simple repetition of an activity label. These are the paper’s human judgments, not a validated universal safety taxonomy.

ideas.title: AGNews one-shot prompt and label IDs
ideas.statement: Table 7 asks GPT to classify among World, Sports, Business and Science/Technology, shows two example text/label placeholders and a testing-text label slot, and lists label-token IDs World=10603, Sports=18153, Business=24749, Science/Technology=26959.
validity_flags: Illustrative two-example template does not document how one example per all four classes was instantiated.

ideas.title: Lossless GPT-AC decoding
ideas.statement: Find the token interval containing encoded value x, renormalize x to (x-F_i(t_i))/P_i(t_i), recompute the GPT next-token distribution from the decoded prefix, and repeat until EOS. Shared x and model phi suffice in the paper’s idealized description.
ideas.conditions: Encoder and decoder must use the same tokenization, distributions, EOS convention, and finite-precision coder.
validity_flags: Printed next-distribution notation phi(t2) is inconsistent with the preceding prefix-conditioned definition; preserve intended autoregressive decoding.

ideas.title: GPT-AC interval refinement
ideas.statement: Start from I_0=[0,1). With cumulative mass F_i(t_i), update low_i=low_(i-1)+(high_(i-1)-low_(i-1))*F_i(t_i) and high_i=low_(i-1)+(high_(i-1)-low_(i-1))*(F_i(t_i)+P_i(t_i)). A number in the final interval represents the token sequence.
ideas.conditions: Ideal interval description; finite-precision handling is discussed in Appendix C.
validity_flags: Algorithm 1 iterates through n+1 but input lists tokens through n; terminal EOS handling is implied by decoding, not made explicit in the input line.

ideas.title: BookCorpus lossless-compression ratios
ideas.statement: On the first gigabyte of BookCorpus, Table 1 reports GPT-AC ratios 10.55 for Llama2-7B, 8.34 for GPT2-L, 7.89 for GPT2-M and 7.22 for GPT2-S, versus GZIP 2.77, 7z 3.80, DZIP 3.95 and TRACE 4.58; NNCP is unreported. Ratios rise with model size among the tested GPT-2 variants.
ideas.conditions: First gigabyte of BookCorpus; shared pretrained model and stated chunking.
validity_flags: No pretraining-data overlap analysis or total-system encoding cost is supplied.

ideas.title: AGNews classification accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 3 reports AGNews accuracy (%) of GPT-AC 47.8±3.3, GZIP 30.2±3.0, GPT-prompt 47.2±2.9, GPT 37.7±7.2, BERT 45.5±3.1, and SBERT 45.8±10.2. GPT-AC is highest among the listed baselines.
ideas.conditions: One labeled training example per class; mean±standard deviation across five random seeds.

ideas.title: Banking77 classification accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 3 reports Banking77 accuracy (%) of GPT-AC 34.0±1.3, GZIP 20.3±1.5, GPT-prompt unreported, GPT 21.7±1.7, BERT 24.5±3.9, and SBERT 53.1±1.9. SBERT is higher than GPT-AC.
ideas.conditions: One labeled training example per class; mean±standard deviation across five random seeds.

ideas.title: CaseHOLD classification accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 3 reports CaseHOLD accuracy (%) of GPT-AC 58.3, GZIP 52.4, GPT-prompt 20.3, GPT 19.9, BERT 35.0, and SBERT 50.6. GPT-AC is highest among the listed baselines.
ideas.conditions: Zero-shot deterministic multiple-choice result.

ideas.title: Minimum shared conversion program for partial matching
ideas.statement: Following Li [31], Definition 5 gives E_min(x,y)=min{|p|: U(x,p,r)=y, U(y,p,q)=x, |p|+|q|+|r|≤E(x,y)}: p is a common conversion program with directional auxiliary information q and r.
validity_flags: The printed formulation suppresses algorithmic coding constants.

ideas.title: Classification datasets and comparison protocol
ideas.statement: Zero-shot multiple-choice classification uses PIQA (2 options) and CaseHOLD (5). One-shot classification uses AGNews (4 classes), Medical abstracts (5), SST5 (5), and Banking77 (77). Baselines include GZIP, GPT-2 prompts, fine-tuned GPT-2 and BERT classification layers, and cosine similarity with SBERT all-MiniLM-L12-v2.
ideas.conditions: One-shot accuracies are means and standard deviations over five random seeds; zero-shot runs are deterministic and have no reported standard deviation.

ideas.title: Medical classification accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 3 reports Medical accuracy (%) of GPT-AC 27.9±3.2, GZIP 25.6±2.8, GPT-prompt 22.1±1.2, GPT 23.7±3.5, BERT 23.8±4.8, and SBERT 39.7±9.1. SBERT is higher than GPT-AC.
ideas.conditions: One labeled training example per class; mean±standard deviation across five random seeds.

ideas.title: PIQA classification accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 3 reports PIQA accuracy (%) of GPT-AC 61.5, GZIP 53.4, GPT-prompt 50.5, GPT 49.2, BERT 50.1, and SBERT 56.5. GPT-AC is highest among the listed baselines.
ideas.conditions: Zero-shot deterministic multiple-choice result.
validity_flags: PIQA Table 3 value 61.5 differs from the best Log-Prob M_mean result 62.0 in Table 5.

ideas.title: SST5 classification accuracy
ideas.statement: Table 3 reports SST5 accuracy (%) of GPT-AC 26.8±3.1, GZIP 21.2±2.7, GPT-prompt 29.8±1.6, GPT 22.7±2.8, BERT 21.1±3.3, and SBERT 26.2±2.3. GPT-prompt is higher than GPT-AC.
ideas.conditions: One labeled training example per class; mean±standard deviation across five random seeds.

ideas.title: Coding-variant performance depends on dataset
ideas.statement: The paper observes a tendency for M_mean with Log-Rank and M_min with Log-Prob but explicitly declines a broader conclusion. Table 5 includes counterexamples: AGNews favors Log-Prob M_mean and TREC-COVID favors Log-Rank M_min.

ideas.title: Prior computable compression-distance methods
ideas.statement: Earlier work replaces uncomputable information distances with ordinary compressor lengths for clustering and plagiarism detection; NPC-LV uses trained latent-variable generative models for parameter-free downstream few-shot image classification, and GZIP has been used for text classification.

ideas.title: GPT-based compression distance for few-shot text learning
ideas.statement: Use a pretrained autoregressive language model as a compressor prior to approximate Kolmogorov-complexity information distances; apply the resulting numerical text distances directly to similarity, classification and ranking without task fine-tuning or prompt engineering.
ideas.conditions: Pretrained model provides output token probabilities; extensive unlabeled pretraining is allowed. GPT-AC approximates an uncomputable ideal rather than computing Kolmogorov complexity exactly.

ideas.title: Minimum conditional complexity alternative
ideas.statement: Theorem 2 states E_min(x,y)=min{K(x|y),K(y|x)}. The paper describes this alternative as symmetric, positive and universal but not triangle-inequality satisfying, and normalizes it into M_min.
validity_flags: Presented ideal theorem with omitted constant conventions; positive does not imply exact zero diagonal, and universality is not a demonstrated property of the GPT approximation.

ideas.title: Compression datasets and chunking
ideas.statement: Evaluate lossless compression on Enwik9 and the first gigabyte of BookCorpus. GPT-2 variants process independent 2,500-character chunks and Llama2-7B uses 10,000-character chunks; chunk independence enables parallel computation at a slight compression-ratio cost.
ideas.conditions: Compression ratio is original text length divided by compressed text length. Models serve as pretrained shared priors; model-storage/transmission cost is not included in a reported total-system comparison.
validity_flags: Model sizes, chunk lengths and pretraining vary across compressors; Table 1 is not a controlled equal-compute or equal-side-information comparison.

ideas.title: Compute coding length without actual compression
ideas.statement: Because information distance needs compressed length rather than a bitstream, compute GPT arithmetic-code length from cumulative token negative log probabilities and avoid arithmetic-coder execution overhead.
ideas.conditions: Language-model inference remains necessary; speed motivation has no quantitative runtime comparison in this paper.

ideas.title: Condition one text’s code length on another
ideas.statement: Approximate K(x) by C(x)=sum_i -log2 phi(x_<i)(x_i) and K(x|y) by C(x|y)=sum_i -log2 phi(y,x_<i)(x_i); compute the analogous values for y. Only x tokens contribute to C(x|y), while y supplies context.
ideas.conditions: Probabilities from one pretrained model; finite context and separator/tokenization choices affect the approximation.

ideas.title: Lower relative predicted-class distance is associated with higher accuracy
ideas.statement: Sort test examples by R_pred into ten groups each containing 10% of the data and plot group-average ratio against accuracy. Figure 2 generally associates lower ratios with higher one-shot classification accuracy on AGNews, Medical, SST5 and Banking77, with a weaker trend on SST5.
ideas.conditions: Descriptive binned analysis; no numerical correlation coefficient, calibrated risk guarantee or causal inference.

ideas.title: Apply one distance interface to NLP tasks
ideas.statement: Use sentence pairs for semantic similarity; compare label descriptions and options for zero-shot multiple choice; compare a class’s one labeled training sample with each test sample for one-shot classification; and compare documents to queries for reranking.
ideas.conditions: Classification selects the nearest class under the chosen metric; distance versus positive semantic-similarity score orientation is not fully specified in the text.
validity_flags: The paper calls M a distance yet reports positive Spearman correlation with increasing STS relatedness labels without explicitly documenting a sign transform.

ideas.title: Domain terminology can favor lexical retrieval
ideas.statement: The authors explain BM25’s strong reranking baseline by domain-specific out-of-distribution terms that can hinder a language model; GPT-AC is comparable in several domains, but lower than BM25 on TREC-NEWS and SciFact.
ideas.conditions: Author interpretation of the benchmark pattern; not an isolated causal experiment.

ideas.title: Downstream model evaluation scope
ideas.statement: Downstream experiments primarily use GPT-2 small (124M) and compare GPT-2 embedding/prompt baselines and BERT-base-uncased (110M). The authors state that probability-accessible models such as Llama can use the method, but Llama2-7B is tested here for compression rather than the downstream task suite.
ideas.conditions: Reported downstream findings are principally about GPT-2 small.

ideas.title: Why encode-time adaptation is unsuitable for short similarity inputs
ideas.statement: NNCP v3.1 updates a 199M-parameter transformer during encoding. The authors suggest GPT-AC could also improve compression via encode-time optimization, but argue that this benefits long messages, overfits the current message, and starts near ratio 1.0 under random initialization, limiting value for similarity measurement.
ideas.conditions: Reasoning about encode-time optimization is not accompanied by a GPT-AC adaptation experiment.
validity_flags: Proposed improvement and generalization concern are author arguments rather than measured GPT-AC results.

ideas.title: Enwik9 lossless-compression ratios
ideas.statement: On Enwik9, Table 1 reports GPT-AC ratios 15.56 for Llama2-7B, 8.05 for GPT2-L, 7.71 for GPT2-M and 6.53 for GPT2-S, versus GZIP 3.09, 7z 4.35, DZIP 4.47, TRACE 5.29 and NNCP 9.33. Llama2-7B is approximately 67% higher than the cited NNCP ratio.
ideas.conditions: Original/compressed text-length ratio, independent chunks; state-of-the-art language is the authors’ time-specific comparison.
validity_flags: Pretrained model cost and different chunk/model settings are not controlled in this ratio comparison.

ideas.title: Few-shot creation of new concepts as a proposed learning paradigm
ideas.statement: The authors contend that new concept creation will predominantly be few-shot even as large-data models improve, and that scarce labels leave both humans and machines searching for regularities that improve compression.
validity_flags: Author conceptual conjecture, not experimentally demonstrated equivalence of human and machine learning.

ideas.title: Prior approaches to few-shot learning
ideas.statement: Prior meta/transfer-learning methods constrain the hypothesis space with other-task/support-set knowledge, whereas data augmentation depends on dataset heuristics and often assumes nearby input points share a label. Pretraining supplies prior knowledge but may be expensive and weak out of distribution.

ideas.title: Formal class-core few-shot learning objective
ideas.statement: Following Jiang et al. [24], partition Omega into H disjoint classes C_h, allow n unlabeled samples inside or outside Omega and k labeled examples per class, and minimize sum_h sum_(i=1 to |C_h|) M(x_i,core_h) conditioned on the unlabeled samples and x_i∈C_h. The core is phi of k class examples; k=0 allows a description or comparison sample, and k=1 a single labeled example.

ideas.title: GPT/BERT one-shot fine-tuning search
ideas.statement: For GPT/BERT classification heads, the selected learning rate is 1e-5 after trying 1e-4, 5e-5, 5e-6 and 1e-6; batch sizes searched are 2,4,8 limited by class count, and epochs are 500,1000,1500,2000 until convergence. Maximum sequence lengths are GPT2 1024 and BERT 512.
validity_flags: The appendix does not fully specify validation split or hyperparameter-selection criteria, seeds, truncation details or optimal per-dataset configurations.

ideas.title: Finite-precision arithmetic interval handling
ideas.statement: Appendix C states that once floating-point precision would overflow, GPT-AC outputs several leading bits and shifts the current interval by those same bits.
ideas.conditions: Implementation-level description, with no precise numerical precision, underflow or rounding specification.

ideas.title: Larger priors and practical compression use
ideas.statement: The authors propose improved pretrained models and encode-time fine-tuning to increase compression ratios and suggest practical storage/transmission savings.
ideas.conditions: Future practical benefits are conditional on model availability and overhead; no deployment cost study is reported.
validity_flags: Extrapolation beyond tested model sizes and compression settings.

ideas.title: Combine compression distances with prompting or fine-tuning
ideas.statement: The authors leave combining compression-distance inference with further fine-tuning or prompting as future research.

ideas.title: Experimental hardware and aggregate compute
ideas.statement: Experiments use two 16 GB Tesla V100 GPUs with HuggingFace Transformers and PyTorch. Individual experiments take 20 minutes to 3 GPU hours depending on dataset size, and the full suite is reported within 300 GPU hours (about six days).
ideas.conditions: Aggregate training/evaluation budget; not a compressor speed benchmark.

ideas.title: Human-like few-shot classification setting
ideas.statement: For an object universe Omega and unlabeled subset U, learn a hypothesis phi(U); represent each class c using description or few-example information D_c and predict argmin_c M(x,D_c | phi(U)). GPT is the hypothesis learned from a large unlabeled corpus.
ideas.conditions: Extensive unlabeled pretraining is permitted, but very few class labels are provided.

ideas.title: Kolmogorov complexity and compression approximation
ideas.statement: Conditional Kolmogorov complexity K(x|y) is the length of the shortest program outputting x given y; it is uncomputable and is approximated in practice by compressed length.

ideas.title: Thermodynamic premise for information-distance learning
ideas.statement: Definition 7 states that irreversibly processing one bit costs 1 kT and reversible computation is free; the argument assumes a universal Turing machine and the Church–Turing thesis.
ideas.conditions: Paper’s idealized thermodynamic premise; k denotes Boltzmann constant and T temperature by the conventional interpretation.
validity_flags: The paper writes 1 kT per bit; the conventional bit-erasure Landauer bound includes ln 2. It concerns ideal logical erasure, not all physical computation cost.

ideas.title: Medical and SST5 prompt-template reporting inconsistency
ideas.statement: The rendered Table 7 Medical and SST5 templates repeat the AGNews instruction listing World, Sports, Business and Science/Technology. Medical’s listed mapping is Neoplasms=10603, Digestive system diseases=18153, Nervous system diseases=24749, Cardiovascular diseases=26959, Pathological conditions=0. SST5 maps very negative=10603, negative=18153, neutral=24749, positive=26959, very positive=0.
ideas.conditions: This is a defect in the published appendix; actual executed prompts cannot be determined from the PDF alone.
validity_flags: Possible copy/paste reporting error; could affect baseline interpretation if executed as printed, but execution error is not established.

ideas.title: Medical coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives Medical input token lengths len(x)=296, len(y)=268. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [25.4, 27.0, 27.9] and Log-Rank scores are [25.5, 26.3, 27.7], measured in accuracy %.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: AGNews coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives AGNews input token lengths len(x)=53, len(y)=53. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [41.3, 41.1, 47.8] and Log-Rank scores are [40.5, 39.9, 43.3], measured in accuracy %.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.
validity_flags: The prose tendency favoring Log-Rank for M_mean and Log-Prob for M_min is not universal.

ideas.title: ArguAna coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives ArguAna input token lengths len(x)=276, len(y)=247. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [0.277, 0.257, 0.301] and Log-Rank scores are [0.282, 0.262, 0.307], measured in NDCG@10.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: Metric axioms used in the appendix
ideas.statement: The paper defines a nonnegative metric by identity D(x,y)=0 iff x=y, symmetry D(x,y)=D(y,x), and triangle inequality D(x,y)≤D(x,z)+D(z,y).

ideas.title: Banking77 coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives Banking77 input token lengths len(x)=15, len(y)=14. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [30.6, 25.2, 33.9] and Log-Rank scores are [29.8, 24.7, 34.0], measured in accuracy %.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: BioASQ coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives BioASQ input token lengths len(x)=304, len(y)=14. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [0.306, 0.517, 0.364] and Log-Rank scores are [0.267, 0.507, 0.33], measured in NDCG@10.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: CaseHold coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives CaseHold input token lengths len(x)=29, len(y)=219. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [56.0, 27.2, 57.9] and Log-Rank scores are [55.2, 27.6, 58.3], measured in accuracy %.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: FiQA-2018 coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives FiQA-2018 input token lengths len(x)=247, len(y)=15. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [0.128, 0.239, 0.154] and Log-Rank scores are [0.118, 0.222, 0.143], measured in NDCG@10.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: Information-distance framing of metric-learning architectures
ideas.statement: The authors interpret Siamese networks via a contrastive-loss metric, prototypical networks via learned class-core representations D_c, and SBERT bi-encoders via cosine similarity within the same few-shot distance framework.
validity_flags: Conceptual unification, not a proof that these trained models compute universal information distance.

ideas.title: PIQA coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives PIQA input token lengths len(x)=24, len(y)=10. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [60.0, 56.4, 62.0] and Log-Rank scores are [59.5, 55.0, 61.5], measured in accuracy %.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: SciFact coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives SciFact input token lengths len(x)=345, len(y)=21. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [0.389, 0.648, 0.519] and Log-Rank scores are [0.351, 0.635, 0.478], measured in NDCG@10.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: Choose normalization based on matching structure
ideas.statement: The authors recommend M_mean for STS, one-shot classification and zero-shot multiple-choice tasks where both texts matter; use M_min for long-document/short-query reranking to emphasize query-relevant partial information. ArguAna uses similar-length query/document texts, favoring M_mean.
ideas.conditions: Empirical heuristic; the prose equates M_max/min with longer/shorter sequences, but the formulas select complexity values rather than raw token count.
validity_flags: Length-based explanation is an intuition and does not redefine the equations as token-length selection.

ideas.title: SST5 coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives SST5 input token lengths len(x)=23, len(y)=24. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [24.8, 26.2, 26.7] and Log-Rank scores are [24.3, 26.0, 26.8], measured in accuracy %.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: sts-b coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives sts-b input token lengths len(x)=13, len(y)=13. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [44.7, 47.6, 48.2] and Log-Rank scores are [50.4, 54.2, 55.0], measured in Spearman rho×100.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: TREC-COVID coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives TREC-COVID input token lengths len(x)=303, len(y)=17. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [0.459, 0.655, 0.467] and Log-Rank scores are [0.473, 0.694, 0.489], measured in NDCG@10.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.
validity_flags: The prose tendency favoring Log-Rank for M_mean and Log-Prob for M_min is not universal.

ideas.title: TREC-NEWS coding-variant and normalization ablation
ideas.statement: Table 5 gives TREC-NEWS input token lengths len(x)=808, len(y)=16. In (M_max,M_min,M_mean) order, Log-Prob scores are [0.173, 0.161, 0.167] and Log-Rank scores are [0.184, 0.161, 0.186], measured in NDCG@10.
ideas.conditions: Reported token-length summaries and six combinations; no uncertainty values in this ablation.

ideas.title: Model cards and dataset preprocessing sources
ideas.statement: Appendix D lists HuggingFace gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large, gpt2-xl, bert-base-uncased, and sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L12-v2. Datasets use HuggingFace preprocessing except Medical, which follows the sebischair/Medical-Abstracts-TC-Corpus repository.
ideas.conditions: gpt2-xl is listed but not a separate compression-result column; no pinned model or dataset revisions are stated.

ideas.title: Arithmetic code length equals token surprisal in the ideal model
ideas.statement: Each token multiplies interval width by P_i(t_i), giving final width product_i P_i(t_i). Its information length is C(T)=sum_i -log2 P_i(t_i), computable without producing the compressed stream.
ideas.conditions: Ideal information length; actual finite bitstreams require termination/rounding and finite-precision overhead.
validity_flags: Exact real-valued entropy length is not an exact integer bitstream-length identity.

ideas.title: Maximum normalized information distance
ideas.statement: Normalize the maximum conditional complexity by the maximum unconditional complexity: M_max(x,y)=max{K(x|y),K(y|x)}/max{K(x),K(y)}; use model-compression C values in practice.

ideas.title: Mean normalized compression distance
ideas.statement: The paper uses M_mean(x,y)=[C(x|y)+C(y|x)]/[C(x)+C(y)] and presents it as 2*CDM-1, with CDM=C(xy)/[C(x)+C(y)], adapted from compression-based dissimilarity.
validity_flags: For directional autoregressive coding, the CDM equality requires chain-rule and symmetric concatenation assumptions not guaranteed by C(xy)=C(yx). Claimed [0,1) range is not guaranteed for arbitrary model conditional lengths.

ideas.title: Minimum normalized information distance for partial matching
ideas.statement: For partial matching, where only portions of two objects correspond, use M_min(x,y)=min{K(x|y),K(y|x)}/min{K(x),K(y)} and substitute compression lengths in practice.

ideas.title: Downstream evaluation limited to older pretrained models
ideas.statement: The paper explicitly limits its downstream NLP evidence to older pretrained language-model versions because of compute and access constraints.

ideas.title: Partial matching can conflict with triangle inequality
ideas.statement: The appendix uses the man–centaur–horse example: man-to-horse dissimilarity may exceed the sum through a centaur when matching only shared parts. It relates question answering to such partial-information matching and motivates a minimum-based alternative.

ideas.title: Prediction distance ratio as a confidence-related statistic
ideas.statement: For one-shot prediction c*, define R_pred(x)=M(x,D_c*) / [(1/|C|) sum_c M(x,D_c)], where D_c is the one-shot example for class c. A smaller ratio means the chosen class has a smaller distance relative to the mean across classes.
ideas.conditions: M_mean with Log-Prob is used for Figure 2; this is not a calibrated probability.

ideas.title: Extend class-distance learning using an unlabeled-data prior
ideas.statement: Equation (10) replaces the distance with M(x_i,x_h | H(y_1,...,y_n)), summed over classes and members, where H is a pretrained model capturing unlabeled or external-data distributions.
validity_flags: Notation changes from core_h to x_h without a separate explicit definition of x_h.

ideas.title: Autoregressive pretraining as coding-length optimization
ideas.statement: The paper identifies autoregressive negative log likelihood L(T|p_model)=-log p_model(T)=sum_i -log2 P_i(t_i) with ideal coding length, and invokes Shannon–Fano–Elias coding to motivate an approximately negative-log-probability-plus-two-bit prefix code.
validity_flags: The printed entropy equality uses p_model: it is cross-entropy and equals source entropy only when model and source distributions agree; an integer prefix code also requires a rounding convention.

ideas.title: Prior compression-based in-context example selection
ideas.statement: Wu et al. [71] use compression length to select in-context examples from a large candidate set and apply the language model in generation mode. This paper distinguishes its direct zero/one-shot text-similarity adaptation from that demonstration-selection use.

ideas.title: Neural entropy models and prior text compressors
ideas.statement: Near-optimal entropy coding shifts the lossless-compression bottleneck to source-distribution estimation. Related work includes VAE BB-ANS, hierarchical Bit-Swap, flow-based image compression, recurrent-network arithmetic text coding, TRACE, and NNCP transformer adaptive coding.

ideas.title: Motivation from prompting and fine-tuning limitations
ideas.statement: The authors motivate compression-distance inference by reporting prompt-engineering demands, input-size and formatting constraints of in-context learning, and limited-data out-of-distribution limitations of fine-tuning.
validity_flags: Literature-based motivation, not a new universal impossibility result.

ideas.title: Banking77 prompting exceeds the practical GPT-2 context budget
ideas.statement: GPT-prompt was omitted for Banking77 because one example for each of 77 classes is difficult to fit and format within GPT-2’s prompt context.

ideas.title: Log-rank compression-length surrogate
ideas.statement: Rank all next-token vocabulary entries by GPT probability and replace each token with its rank, with more probable tokens assigned smaller indices; approximate sequence compression length by sum_i log2(rank_i).
ideas.conditions: Rank surrogate used for distance comparisons; the paper does not specify a complete rank-code bitstream construction or its overhead.
validity_flags: Sum log2(rank) is a surrogate; rank representation alone does not establish a uniquely decodable code of that exact length.
Reference [21] is cited as 2021, while the primary Stanford course page lists the matching report under Winter 2022; exact report release/version date is unresolved.

ideas.title: ArguAna reranking effectiveness
