ideas.statement: Equation 3 maps trace evidence D through WSAparse to estimated Θ=(W,S,A), then through skill generation to an estimated skill document. The method seeks component recovery before text rendering to avoid losing branches, decision criteria, tool constraints, or validation.
ideas.conditions: Stage-interface notation only; skill document is calligraphic S, distinct from semantic component S.

ideas.title: Iterative WSA-local revision re-parses and checks each candidate
ideas.statement: Equations 7–8 define skill_hat^(t+1)=Revise(skill_hat^t, Δ_W^t, Δ_S^t, Δ_A^t), with (Δ_W^t, Δ_S^t, Δ_A^t)=Check(Parse_WSA(skill_hat^t), E). Δ_W records node/link coverage errors, Δ_S node-function/criterion errors, and Δ_A missing/mis-scoped bindings. Iteration stops when no high-priority WSA error remains or a fixed refinement budget is exhausted.
ideas.conditions: The paper does not specify the refinement-budget value or operational high-priority threshold; no convergence guarantee is claimed.

ideas.title: WSA repairs target topology, node predicates, or operational bindings
ideas.statement: W-level repair splits collapsed nodes, restores links, or separates alternatives. S-level repair converts vague instructions into local predicates, adds accept/reject criteria, or relocates termination conditions to relevant nodes. A-level repair binds resources to usage nodes, marks approvals mandatory, or restores output schemas.
ideas.conditions: Repairs use the same WSA categories as evaluation; these are illustrative operations, not measured ablation results.

ideas.title: W2S exceeds ASC on seven of eight WSA types
ideas.conditions: Replay-based behavioral fidelity on WSASkill; no dispersion, confidence intervals, significance tests, or per-type sample counts are reported.

ideas.title: Workflow-to-Skill construction from heterogeneous traces
ideas.statement: W2S segments demonstrations, trajectories, tool-use traces, and logs into procedural units; induces path-local drafts; aligns and merges shared structure; reconciles branches; and compresses redundancy while preserving verification, approval, rollback, state management, evidence, and confidence annotations.

ideas.title: Workflow backbone is a directed node-link graph
ideas.statement: Equation 2 defines W = (N, E). Each node is an abstract execution unit; directed links encode ordering or dependency. A workflow backbone is present when there are at least two nodes connected by at least one directed link; a one-node skill has no structural backbone to reconstruct, though it can have semantics and attachments.
ideas.conditions: The taxonomy includes non-workflow skills with |N| ≤ 1; the paper does not demand a fully connected graph.

ideas.title: W-path enumeration collapses loops but preserves annotations
ideas.statement: For workflow-bearing reference skills, the method parses the graph and enumerates INPUT-to-OUTPUT routes, collapsing loops into loop units while retaining branch and loop annotations.

ideas.title: Reject candidates without validation improvement
ideas.statement: Choose P_(t+1)=argmax over current P_t and candidate P_t^c of f_B(P,D_val). The prose says candidates must strictly improve; Algorithm1 detects rejection through an unchanged prompt, while the argmax tie-breaking rule is not explicitly specified.
ideas.conditions: Monotonicity applies to accepted refinement updates on the fixed validation set, not compression or unseen test data.

ideas.title: Learnable or task-adaptive segmentation
ideas.statement: Future work is to replace heuristic blank-line segmentation with learnable or task-adaptive span boundaries for more robust compression in domains such as planning and long-horizon decision-making.

ideas.title: Sinkhorn alignment outperforms reported alternatives
ideas.statement: For GSM8K/AIME2025/GPQA, End_KL accuracy/length is 87.30/1204,21.33/10223,48.48/6910; pooled MSE gives 88.93/921,15.67/12785,43.43/8586; Sinkhorn gives 92.72/630,39.33/9568,54.55/4181. MSE length even exceeds Vanilla on AIME2025 and GPQA.
ideas.conditions: Same frozen-head projection space as described in §4.4.2; pooling order and exact baseline optimization are not fully specified.

ideas.title: Alignment algorithm safeguards
ideas.statement: Algorithm 1 returns zero alignment loss if no spans are dropped; otherwise it caps teacher-state rows, projects both sides, optionally normalizes each projected vector with norm plus δ, constructs squared distances, invokes Sinkhorn and averages over dropped spans.
ideas.conditions: normalize is an input but its chosen value, solver iterations L and δ are not specified.

ideas.title: Endpoint KL and pooled MSE alternatives
ideas.statement: End_KL matches the pause decoding distribution to the last teacher token; MSE averages the teacher span into one target and regresses the pause state to it. Both are described as using the same frozen-head projection space.
ideas.conditions: Alignment ablation; precise pooling-versus-projection order is not specified here.

ideas.title: Training improves alignment loss and lexical coverage
ideas.statement: Figure 4 shows Stage I OT loss falling rapidly then stabilizing near 0.61, while top-20 coverage rises to roughly 0.7–0.8, above a roughly 0.23 no-training baseline with externally inserted pauses.
ideas.conditions: Approximate visual reading; training examples, not a held-out semantic or causal test. Shading meaning is not specified.

ideas.title: Alternative pause schedules
ideas.statement: SPOT permits fixed token/character intervals, dynamic positions such as after equations, and prompt-dependent pause density. The authors claim similar accuracy–length tradeoffs at matched overall density; no supporting numerical comparison is supplied.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative appendix observation; default span schedule favors readability and tokenizer independence.

ideas.title: Visible truncation can reduce deliberation
ideas.statement: Autoregressive length–compute coupling means aggressive visible-trace truncation can constrain multi-step deduction and lower accuracy on harder instances.

ideas.title: Equation-of-state calibration weakly depends on bending energies
ideas.statement: Within the compact PS lattice model, cohesive energy and lattice cell parameter determine the EOS, while backbone and side-group bending energies exert only minor effects on specific volume, thermal expansion and isothermal compressibility; this motivates separate EOS and glass-property calibration.
ideas.conditions: The modeled PS molecular topology.

ideas.title: Compressibility suppression and beta relaxation
ideas.statement: Cited work reports lowered compressibility (density-fluctuation variance) accompanying suppression of beta relaxation by molecular additives, proposed as related to antiplasticization.
validity_flags: Literature association rather than causal demonstration in this paper

ideas.title: Baseline aggregate accuracy–length tradeoffs
ideas.statement: Table 1 average Δaccuracy points/relative Δlength are CCoT −0.4/−8.4%, DEER +0.0/−24.0%, ConciseHint +0.2/−22.6%, Step Entropy +0.2/−16.6%, L1-Max −8.2/−35.3%, COCONUT −29.3/−85.4%, CODI −25.2/−81.2%, LightThinker −4.3/−16.7%, Latent-SFT −17.7/−78.0%. Stronger fully latent compression is accompanied by substantial accuracy loss in these implementations.
ideas.conditions: Table 1; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, trained on GSM8K; means over ten sampled decoding seeds. Task order: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME2024, AIME2025, GPQA-Diamond.

ideas.title: Explicit and latent baseline suite
ideas.statement: Under the common 7B backbone, compare Vanilla; explicit methods CCoT, ConciseHint, Step Entropy, L1-Max and DEER; and latent methods COCONUT, CODI, LightThinker and Latent-SFT.

ideas.title: Evaluation sample sizes and answer constraints
ideas.statement: GSM8K has 7473 training/1319 test instances; MATH500 has 500 tests; AIME2024 and AIME2025 each 30 tests with integer answers 0–999; GPQA-Diamond has 198 science multiple-choice tests. Math uses boxed final answers and GPQA uses an A–D answer letter.
ideas.conditions: Small AIME test sets; ten decoding seeds do not increase distinct problem count.

ideas.title: Reasoning span segmentation
ideas.statement: Reasoning spans are a disjoint contiguous cover of the CoT; SPOT uses raw-text blank-line boundaries within <think>…</think>, accepting extra spaces/multiple blank lines. Paragraph versus sentence granularity is a domain-dependent design choice.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-style traces.

ideas.title: COCONUT continuous latent reasoning
ideas.statement: COCONUT replaces portions of explicit CoT with continuous non-text latent representations to reduce visible tokens.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: CODI reasoning distillation
ideas.statement: CODI distills teacher explicit reasoning into a student’s internalized representations, aiming to reproduce its reasoning effect without the full explicit trace.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: The compl keyword is a DeepSeek-only vocabulary exception
ideas.statement: Table 1 lists compl only in DeepSeek-V3 at rank 92843, with Qwen2.5 and Llama absent, contradicting a universal subset interpretation of DeepSeek’s smaller keyword coverage.

ideas.title: Reinforcement learning for discrete prompt editing
ideas.statement: PCRL [27] is described as treating prompt editing as a discrete decision process and learning efficient compression policies through reinforcement learning.

ideas.title: Combined summarization and utility-aware soft compression
ideas.statement: Reference [24] is described as integrating summarization, soft prompt compression and utility-aware mechanisms to reduce context processing while maintaining model utility.

ideas.title: Decentralized local-observation wireless control
ideas.statement: DICLID-MADRL [28] lets access points independently optimize user selection and power from local observations, aiming for global energy efficiency through decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning.

ideas.title: Block-coordinate and convex-approximation resource control
ideas.statement: Reference [29] jointly optimizes receive beamforming, power, HAPS location and computation resource distribution with block-coordinate descent and successive convex approximation.

ideas.title: Graph-neural joint power and spectrum allocation
ideas.statement: Reference [30] uses a graph neural network to jointly control power and spectrum in multiuser shared-channel interference settings.

ideas.title: Example fc=0.5 codec has 563,430,184 parameters
ideas.statement: Appendix A Table III gives encoder Flatten then Linear(16384→8192), 134,225,920 parameters. Decoder rows are labelled Relu(8192→16384), 134,234,112; Normalize(16384); Relu(16384→9000), 147,465,000; Normalize(9000); Relu(9000→16384), 147,472,384; LayerNorm(16384,eps=1e-6), 32,768. The total is 563,430,184 parameters.
ideas.conditions: Example compression rate fc=0.5.
validity_flags: Table calls parameterized width-changing decoder layers Relu; interpreted literally as table labels rather than asserting ReLU alone has weights.
Residual and unflatten layers described in the prose are not explicitly included as rows in this table.

ideas.title: Autoencoder combines reconstruction, adversarial and regularization objectives
ideas.statement: Equation (10) presents an encoder/decoder optimization against discriminator psi of Lrec(I,D(E(I)))-Ladv(D(E(I)))+log D_psi(I)+Lreg(I;E,D). Reconstruction minimizes image error, adversarial training follows [36], and regularization centers the latent. The objective is attributed to [35].
validity_flags: Equation (10) prints lim rather than an explicit minimization operator; preserve this source ambiguity.

ideas.title: Diffusion for multimodal image fusion
ideas.statement: The review attributes to [16] a DDPM-based denoising diffusion model for multimodality image fusion.

ideas.title: DDIM accelerates diffusion sampling
ideas.statement: DDIM [15] reduces diffusion-model sampling complexity by constructing non-Markovian diffusion processes.

ideas.title: DDPM as a foundational denoising generative model
ideas.statement: The literature review identifies denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) [14] as a foundational image diffusion model.

ideas.title: Generative models for wireless channel problems
ideas.statement: The related-work prose identifies channel modeling [20] as a generative-model communication application; the cited title specifically concerns channel estimation using a conditional GAN.

ideas.title: Generative models for signal detection
ideas.statement: The related-work discussion identifies signal detection [19] as an existing communication application of generative models.

ideas.title: Generate images from prompts at network nodes
ideas.statement: The generative network layer [23] places GAI at intermediate or edge nodes to generate images from prompts instead of transmitting images, aiming to improve communication efficiency.

ideas.title: Generative semantic communication improves image PSNR in prior simulation
ideas.statement: The review describes prior generative semantic communication [22] as improving image-transmission PSNR on CIFAR10 simulations.

ideas.title: Earlier molecular dynamics dilution trend
ideas.statement: Prior molecular-dynamics calculations report approximately linear Tg decrease with solvent volume fraction up to 25%, but do not explore diluent structure, interaction-energy effects or fragility changes.

ideas.title: Latent diffusion reduces diffusion complexity
ideas.statement: Repeated noise estimation/removal makes high-resolution diffusion expensive. LDM [17,18] performs diffusion in latent space to reduce complexity, explicitly inspiring this paper’s latent-space transmission.

ideas.title: NetGPT allocates suitable cloud and edge language models
ideas.statement: NetGPT [30] collaborates with LLMs at edge and cloud according to computing capability to provide personalized service.

ideas.title: Semantic-spatial GAN with iterative word-feature refinement
ideas.statement: Prior semantic-spatial aware GAN [12] iteratively refines features using fine-grained word embeddings for text-to-image synthesis.

ideas.title: Transformers in high-resolution GAN generation
ideas.statement: Prior work [13] constructs a GAN with transformers for high-resolution image generation.

ideas.title: Vector-quantized VAE for coherent image generation
ideas.statement: The literature review attributes higher-coherence and higher-fidelity image generation to a vector-quantized variational autoencoder [11].

ideas.title: Wireless perception guides resource-constrained generation
ideas.statement: Prior work [31] uses wireless sensing to guide GAI services in resource-limited mobile edge networks.

ideas.title: CLIP embeds prompts to a context tensor
ideas.statement: Equation (9) embeds prompt s as s_tilde=B_b(s), with tensor shape B×K×E, where B is batch size, K maximum text encoding length, and E embedding size. CLIP supplies this embedding.

ideas.title: Codec training channel is described inconsistently
ideas.statement: The prose says encoder/decoder training uses a perfect channel to minimize recovered-latent MSE, but Algorithm 2 says each epoch downloads the seed over a fading channel with normalized power before joint training. The actual training channel cannot be resolved from these descriptions alone.
validity_flags: Internal conflict between perfect-channel prose and fading-channel algorithm.

ideas.title: Conclusion calls communication reduction exponential without a scaling law
ideas.statement: The conclusion summarizes lower low-SNR distortion, FID improvement from power allocation, and a claimed exponential reduction of communication resources. The evidence is finite payload ratios and downsampling/compression formulas, without a demonstrated exponential scaling law.
validity_flags: Exponential reduction is wording in the source conclusion; no asymptotic law is established.

ideas.title: Dense normalized residual decoder reconstructs the latent tensor
ideas.statement: The compression decoder uses multiple dense layers, normalization layers, a residual layer, an unflatten layer, and ReLU activation. The paper describes three dense layers separated by normalization as empirically optimal.

ideas.title: ConciseHint guidance during decoding
ideas.statement: ConciseHint injects concise guidance during decoding to shorten fully textual reasoning while aiming to preserve correctness.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: Normalized frozen-head lexical coverage
ideas.statement: For paired teacher span S, remove special/trivial-formatting token IDs and define V(S) as its unique token set; coverage=|TopK(p(hpause),K)∩V(S)|/min(K,|V(S)|), K=20.
ideas.conditions: SpanDrop examples during Stage I; measures lexical overlap, not logical faithfulness.

ideas.title: DEER dynamic early exit
ideas.statement: DEER stops explicit generation adaptively once sufficient confidence is reached to save reasoning tokens.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: Dense pauses can induce repetition and malformed boundaries
ideas.statement: The dense-insertion GSM8K chalk example repeats intermediate calculations, restarts its reasoning and contains repeated <pause><think> boundaries. Such insertion can increase verbosity and weaken coherence despite a plausible final answer.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative failure mode; example concludes one day; source problem/ground truth are not supplied, so correctness is not independently established.

ideas.title: Endpoint alignment loses within-span semantics
ideas.statement: SPOT is motivated by endpoint-only latent supervision, whose one-to-one matching can under-represent semantics distributed across variable-length reasoning spans.

ideas.title: Common backbone and five-benchmark evaluation
ideas.statement: All methods use DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; SPOT trains on GSM8K and evaluates GSM8K, MATH500, AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and out-of-domain GPQA-Diamond. Decoding uses temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, maximum 16384 tokens, and averages ten random-seed runs.

ideas.title: Pass@1 and full-response token count
ideas.statement: Accuracy is mean pass@1 from one sampled completion per instance across ten seeds; output length #L counts all generated reasoning and final-answer tokens under the model tokenizer.

ideas.title: Method-specific prompts and common final-answer formats
ideas.statement: Evaluation concatenates method instruction, task format constraint, and instance. Vanilla asks for step-by-step reasoning; SPOT asks for efficient concise CoT and replacement of safely omitted steps with <pause>. Math requests a final boxed result; GPQA requests Answer: $LETTER. Released baselines may retain their default prompt/evaluation pipeline.
ideas.conditions: Prompt wording differs between methods; SPOT prompt explicitly asks pause emission despite external insertion and no pause-target CE.

ideas.title: Flatten and dense layers compress latent features
ideas.statement: The compression encoder flattens LDM latent features and applies dense layers. Output-layer width controls code length and compression rate fc; optimal structure and size may depend on the desired rate.

ideas.title: Frozen vocabulary-induced projection
ideas.statement: Project both student and teacher hidden states with p(h)=softmax(Wh+b) and φ(h)=p(h)ᵀE. W, b, and E are frozen throughout Stage I, yielding a fixed shared semantic space and direct decoding without an auxiliary probe.
ideas.conditions: Stage I alignment; gradients may still reach the student hidden state through the frozen mapping.

ideas.title: GPQA qualitative compression retains answer and response pattern
ideas.statement: In the selected heat-equation parallelization example, SPOT inserts three pauses and shortens explicit narration while retaining problem restatement, option screening and answer D, matching Vanilla’s selection. This illustrates format flexibility but does not independently validate every scientific statement in the generated trace.
ideas.conditions: Selected qualitative case; no per-case token counts; generated PDE claims are not accepted as independent research evidence.

ideas.title: Multiple spans per pause trade reliability for compression
ideas.statement: For MATH500/AIME2025/GPQA, G=1 accuracy/length is 93.80/2154,39.33/9568,54.55/4181; G=2 gives 90.62/1675,32.67/9478,48.49/3565; G=3 gives 89.84/1606,30.67/9230,47.65/3426. Increasing spans represented by one pause consistently reduces tokens and accuracy.
ideas.conditions: Each pause compresses G consecutive reasoning spans; maximum consecutive pause count fixed at one.

ideas.title: Reported average accuracy and length gains
ideas.statement: The abstract reports 2.3 percentage points higher average accuracy and 37.5% fewer generated tokens; detailed experimental conditions and table values appear later.
ideas.conditions: Five-benchmark macro-average versus Vanilla DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; Stage II; ten decoding seeds; accuracy changes in percentage points, length changes relative per-task percentages.

ideas.title: Externally controlled pause interval
ideas.statement: At inference, externally inject pause tokens every N explicit spans only inside the reasoning segment (<think>…</think> for DeepSeek-style outputs), preserving the native output format; N controls implicit-reasoning intensity.
ideas.conditions: Main evaluation: N=3 on four math benchmarks; N=1 on GPQA-Diamond.

ideas.title: Pause density controls length with accuracy cost
ideas.statement: The N=1…5 insertion sweep on MATH500, AIME2025 and GPQA-Diamond shows more frequent pause insertion generally shortens outputs; very dense insertion can harm accuracy, particularly on harder math.
ideas.conditions: External pause only inside <think>; Fig. 3 compares Vanilla and N=1…5.

ideas.title: Judge recognizes a missing train-time bridge
ideas.statement: A displayed boundary proceeds from second-train departure at minute 65 to using 125+20=145 for fourth-train arrival. GPT-4o-mini scores utilization/continuity 5/5 with confidence .9 and supplies the missing 65+60=125 bridge plus immediate third-train departure.
ideas.conditions: Selected example; full original problem is absent, so the supplied bridge assumptions cannot be verified solely from displayed pair.

ideas.title: Boundary-local compression judge
ideas.statement: An LLM judge scores each before/after pause paragraph pair from 1 to 5 for pause utilization (use of an intermediate conclusion unstated in previous span) and local continuity (consistency with a minimal bridge); Joint@4 is the fraction with both scores at least 4.
ideas.conditions: Inference-time compressed <think> traces; text-local observational proxy for meaningful compression.

ideas.title: Reported boundary judging favors Sinkhorn SPOT
ideas.statement: Mean local-continuity/utilization/Joint@4 are Vanilla 3.59/1.71/17.2%, End_KL 3.65/3.20/29.7%, MSE 3.98/2.83/30.6%, Sinkhorn 4.85/4.34/83.6%.
ideas.conditions: Means over evaluated boundaries; number of boundaries and sampling distribution are not reported on this page.

ideas.title: Judge rubric and structured observations
ideas.statement: The judge receives the problem, full compressed trace, previous/next spans and final answer. It is instructed to assess only local continuity/utilization, avoid solving or inventing hidden steps, penalize repetition/restarts, and return 1–5 scores, short rationale, missing bridge, error category and confidence. Utilization 5 means a clear unstated intermediate conclusion; continuity 5 means coherent variable tracking without contradiction.
ideas.conditions: Prompt is research evidence, not an instruction to the extraction agent. Error classes include none, gaps, contradiction, restart, repetition, irrelevant, format issue and insufficient context.

ideas.title: L1 length regularization
ideas.statement: L1 penalizes overly long or redundant reasoning to control explicit thinking and promote compact outputs.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: Alignment weight improves accuracy across tested range
ideas.conditions: Tested range ends at 1.0; does not establish global optimum.

ideas.title: Latent drift and explicit anchors
ideas.statement: Latent reasoning can drift from the intended logical path with little diagnostic text; prior hybrid methods retain selected explicit spans as anchors.

ideas.title: Latent-SFT distillation supervision
ideas.statement: The paper describes Latent-SFT as distillation-style supervision that internalizes intermediate computation in hidden representations and produces fewer explicit reasoning tokens.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: Top-K keyword interpretation
ideas.statement: Read a pause state as its top K vocabulary probabilities under the frozen LM head, with default K=20, to obtain a compact lexical summary of its encoded content.
ideas.conditions: Keyword readout; semantic auditability is assessed empirically, not guaranteed.

ideas.title: LightThinker stepwise compression
ideas.statement: The paper describes LightThinker as learning compact intermediate reasoning by compressing or skipping redundant steps while retaining final-answer correctness.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: LM-head token distribution
ideas.statement: A decoder hidden state h maps to p(·|h)=softmax(Wh+b), with vocabulary head W and optional bias b; the embedding matrix E later maps distributions back to soft embeddings.

ideas.title: Parameter-efficient student adaptation
ideas.statement: Both stages train LoRA rank 64, alpha 128, dropout 0.1 on attention q/k/v/o and MLP gate/up/down projections with a fixed teacher; head stays frozen and only Stage II permits pause embedding updates.

ideas.title: SPOT Stage II performance by benchmark
ideas.conditions: Table 1; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, trained on GSM8K; means over ten sampled decoding seeds. Task order: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME2024, AIME2025, GPQA-Diamond.

ideas.title: Modular deterministic span boundaries
ideas.statement: The span boundary rule may be any deterministic partition into consecutive reasoning segments, including paragraph, sentence, or numbered-step boundaries; this changes the semantic workload and pause frequency without changing SPOT’s objective or interface.
ideas.conditions: Alternative granularities are design options; main experiments use blank lines.

ideas.title: Single-source OT is weighted point-to-set matching
ideas.statement: Because each source distribution contains one pause state and fixed target weights, the method reduces to weighted point-to-set distance distributing unit mass according to the target marginal, rather than a learnable many-to-many transport plan.
ideas.conditions: Current SPOT single-pause-per-span design with fixed uniform target marginal.

ideas.title: Cost of verbose explicit reasoning
ideas.statement: The authors motivate reasoning compression by redundant explicit chain-of-thought steps that increase inference overhead without proportional accuracy gains.

ideas.title: Families of latent reasoning predecessors
ideas.statement: The related-work taxonomy distinguishes extra special/filler-token computation, continuous compression of rationales, dynamic compression or latent-token generation to limit context growth, and hybrids interleaving explicit anchors.

ideas.title: RFT trains pause embedding without pause emission supervision
ideas.statement: Stage II uses masked next-token cross-entropy on the selected target, with no pause prediction targets; it retains the frozen LM head and ordinary embeddings but permits the pause embedding and the Stage I student parameters to update.

ideas.title: Shortest correct rejection-sampling target
ideas.statement: For each query, generate a no-pause reference y(0), sample candidates under predefined insertion patterns, reject wrong final answers, then choose the correct candidate maximizing 1−|y(k)|/|y(0)| as the RFT target.
ideas.conditions: Candidate count, exact predefined insertion-pattern set, sampling settings for RFT, and fallback when no candidate is correct are not specified.

ideas.title: A pause bridges an omitted arithmetic aggregation
ideas.statement: The selected successful trace states Carol has 20 and Jennifer 44 signatures, inserts pause, then computes 100−64=36 without explicitly adding 20+44 before the boundary; readout is illustrated with “add” and “64”. The final solution restores the explicit addition.
ideas.conditions: Single qualitative illustration; the final answer itself repeats the calculation.

ideas.title: Epsilon-scaling solver as printed
ideas.statement: Algorithm 2 sets εmin=blur², starts ε=max(εmin,median(C)), initializes u,v to ones and uniform target b, iterates u=a/(Kv+δ), v=b/(Kᵀu+δ) with K=exp(−C/ε), reduces ε by scaling until the threshold, clamps Π=diag(u)Kdiag(v) at δ, and returns cost minus ε∑Π(logΠ−1).
ideas.conditions: Current application m=1, source a=[1], b=1/n; blur=.05, scaling=.9. Printed pseudocode does not solve again after ε reaches εmin; if initially ε=εmin the loop does not define K.

ideas.title: Transport coupling and printed entropy objective
ideas.statement: The paper defines U(a,b)={Π≥0:Π1=a, Πᵀ1=b} and OT=min⟨Π,C⟩. Its Eq. (4) prints OTε=min[⟨Π,C⟩−ε∑Πij(logΠij−1)], ε>0, and says it is computed using Sinkhorn iterations. The entropy sign must be read as printed; Appendix A.5 repeats the minus sign while using K=exp(−C/ε), so the printed objective and conventional entropy-smoothed kernel are formally inconsistent. The fixed single-source plan makes the entropy term constant with respect to the student state in the stated formulation.
ideas.conditions: Background definitions reproduced from SPOT §§2.2/A.5; sign consistency caveat is an extractor observation, not a corrected source formula.

ideas.title: Uniform one-to-span alignment loss
ideas.statement: For each dropped span, project pause state z and every teacher state through φ; use squared Euclidean costs C1,t=||φ(z)−φ(htea_t)||², source marginal [1], uniform target 1/|S|, and average OTε over dropped spans.

ideas.title: SpanDrop training data
ideas.statement: Independently select each teacher span with probability 0.3 and replace it by one <pause>, preserving retained span order. Add <pause> to the tokenizer and shared token embedding matrix; each training tuple contains the input, full teacher trace, and compressed trace.

ideas.title: Fried and generalized logarithmic relations
ideas.statement: Fried gives ln(Tg/Tg,p)=phi_s ln(Tg,s/Tg,p)/[(1−phi_s)(Tg,s/Tg,p)+phi_s]. A cited variant replaces Tg,s/Tg,p in the denominator with fitted k_1.

ideas.title: Span-level Pause-of-Thought
ideas.statement: SPOT compresses explicit chain-of-thought spans into latent <pause> tokens while preserving flexible response structure, using span-level Sinkhorn semantic alignment and a frozen pretrained language head.

ideas.title: Masked cross-entropy plus alignment
ideas.statement: Stage I minimizes LCE+λLalign, where LCE=−∑t 1[ỹt≠<pause>] log pθ(ỹt|x,ỹ<t). It freezes LM head and all token embeddings and trains remaining student parameters; pause is conditioning context, not a cross-entropy prediction target.

ideas.title: RFT raises accuracy but usually uses more tokens
ideas.statement: Stage I accuracy/token counts are 92.19/576,92.24/1626,52.67/8281,34.67/9471,51.01/4142. Stage II improves all five accuracies to 92.72,93.80,53.33,39.33,54.55 but length increases on four tasks; only AIME2024 shortens further (8281→7885).
ideas.conditions: Table 1; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, trained on GSM8K; means over ten sampled decoding seeds. Task order: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME2024, AIME2025, GPQA-Diamond.

ideas.title: Step Entropy pruning
ideas.statement: Step Entropy non-parametrically identifies and prunes low-utility reasoning segments using token/step uncertainty without changing backbone parameters.
ideas.conditions: Description attributed to SPOT Appendix A.4, not an independent reproduction of the cited method.

ideas.title: Full-span teacher supervision
ideas.statement: The fixed teacher processes the full trace and supplies all final-layer states in each omitted span; the student processes the compressed trace and aligns its single pause-position final-layer state to that variable-length teacher-state collection. Uniform subsampling caps long-span targets.

ideas.title: SPOT training implementation
ideas.statement: Stage I uses max length 4096, per-device batch 1, accumulation 8, AdamW for 5 epochs at 2e-5, warmup 0.05 and gradient norm 1; Sinkhorn blur 0.05/scaling 0.9; λ=1 and ≤256 uniformly sampled teacher states per span. RFT shares optimizer settings. Training uses bfloat16 PyTorch/Transformers DDP on two 48GB RTX 5880 Ada GPUs.

ideas.title: Two-stage alignment then rejection fine-tuning
ideas.statement: SPOT first aligns latent pause states to teacher spans under a frozen LM head, then rejection-samples correct, preferably short completions to stabilize response to varied external pause insertion patterns.

ideas.title: Vocabulary-space superposition prior work
ideas.statement: The authors credit Deng et al. [8] with representing latent thoughts as vocabulary-space superpositions to make hidden states directly decodable as token distributions.

ideas.title: Short codes and low SNR jointly increase FID
ideas.statement: Figure 9 shows highest FID where both SNR and fc are low. The authors report high FID for fc<0.4, medium values over approximately 0.4<fc<0.8, a transition near -20 dB, and generally low FID above -10 dB. FID distinguishes conditions more strongly than PSNR.
ideas.conditions: Specific simulation configuration; thresholds are qualitative.
validity_flags: Middle-rate interval is malformed in prose as <0.4fc<0.8; interpretation is approximate.

ideas.title: Encode latent features into a smaller noise-resistant seed
ideas.statement: Equation (2) defines x=C_omega(G_alpha(s),fc), with ES neural compression encoder C, weights omega, and feature compression rate fc. Direct latent downlink is feasible, but additional encoding targets further compression and noise resistance; encoders and decoders require training for each compression-rate setting.

ideas.title: Joint codec training minimizes recovered-latent MSE under symbol constraints
ideas.statement: P1 minimizes E[||z-z_hat||_2^2] over encoder omega and decoder psi, subject to 0<|x_Ig|<fd^-2 |x_Ic| with fd>1. The two devices’ codec modules train jointly but independently of the pretrained GAI model, using a saved latent dataset. Equation (27) repeats the same latent MSE loss.
validity_flags: Experimental fc values are fractions in (0,1), with payload proportional to fc in Table II; this conflicts with the inverse-fc payload equation in section III.D.

ideas.title: Non-Markov DDIM conditional diffusion
ideas.statement: The DDIM formulation uses q(zT|z0)=N(sqrt(alpha_T)z0,(1-alpha_T)I) and a conditional q(zt-1|zt,z0)=N(sqrt(alpha_t-1)z0+sqrt(1-alpha_t-1-sigma_t^2)*(zt-sqrt(alpha_t)z0)/sqrt(1-alpha_t),sigma_t^2 I).
validity_flags: Text defines alpha_T=1-beta_T without clarifying cumulative-product convention; later alpha/sigma parameterizations differ.

ideas.title: Run DDIM inference on the stronger edge server
ideas.statement: Iterative DDIM sampling is assigned to ES because of its compute and GPU-memory requirements. Equation (25) uses z_(t-1)=sqrt(alpha_(t-1))*(zt-sqrt(1-alpha_t)epsilon_theta^t(zt))/sqrt(alpha_t)+sqrt(1-alpha_(t-1)-sigma_t^2)*epsilon_theta^t(zt)+sigma_t epsilon_t.

ideas.title: Diffusion ELBO becomes weighted denoising error
ideas.statement: Equation (17) bounds -log p(z0) with terminal KL(q(zT|z0)||p(zT)) plus a sum of expected reverse-transition KL terms. Equation (21) rewrites the latter as a sum of expected squared clean-latent errors weighted by one half the difference alpha_(t-1)^2/sigma_(t-1)^2-alpha_t^2/sigma_t^2.
validity_flags: Equation (21) has unmatched brackets and incomplete p(z_(t-1)) conditioning in the printed left side; extraction records intended loss relation without endorsing a corrected derivation.

ideas.title: Gaussian forward diffusion with variance schedule
ideas.statement: The diffusion background starts with a data latent z0 and adds isotropic Gaussian noise using schedule beta_1,...,beta_T. Equation (13) specifies q(zt|zt-1)=N(zt;sqrt(1-beta_t)zt-1,beta_t I). Equation (12) prints q(z1:T|z0)=q(zT|z0) product_{t=2}^T q(zt|zt-1).
validity_flags: Printed factorization (12) is inconsistent with the usual forward Markov joint: initial factor uses zT instead of z1.

ideas.title: Predict clean latent from estimated diffusion noise
ideas.statement: A neural reverse model learns p_theta(zt-1|zt) from q(zt-1|zt,z0). Equation (15) estimates clean latent f_theta,t(zt)=(zt-sqrt(1-alpha_t)*epsilon_theta,t(zt))/sqrt(alpha_t); equation (16) uses a Gaussian reverse transition with learned mean f_theta and covariance Sigma_theta. Generation quality depends on noise-estimation accuracy.

ideas.title: Background: recursive AutoCompressor
ideas.statement: AutoCompressor is described as recursively compressing prompts to accommodate longer inputs, with a finetuned LLM and a more complex training process.

ideas.title: Parameterize denoising posterior through a predicted clean latent
ideas.statement: Equations (18)-(20) replace the unknown clean latent in the reverse conditional by a network estimate z_theta(zt,t). The posterior mean is alpha_(t|t-1)*sigma_(t-1)^2/sigma_t^2 *zt + alpha_(t-1)*sigma_(t|t-1)^2/sigma_t^2 *z_theta(zt,t). Equation (22) reparameterizes epsilon_theta=(zt-alpha_t z_theta)/sigma_t.
validity_flags: Equation (19) variance includes malformed sigma_(t+-1) notation/bracket; preserve as ambiguous rather than repairing it from external diffusion formulas.
Equations (15) and (22) use differing alpha conventions without explicit reconciliation.

ideas.title: Actor-critic training records full seed episodes
ideas.statement: Algorithm 3 initializes actor and critic, samples the old policy, checks remaining budget, transmits all seed symbols with zero intermediate rewards, decodes the final image and calculates terminal reward, records state/action/reward/next-state tuples, and samples tuples over training epochs to update networks.

ideas.title: Scale each seed segment by allocated transmission power
ideas.statement: Equation (29) prints y_t=h_t p_t x_t+n, calling p_t the power allocated to coherence block t. A DRL agent distributes one generation task’s limited budget among time slots to improve final FID.
validity_flags: p_t is called power but appears as an amplitude multiplier rather than sqrt(power); source convention remains unresolved.

ideas.title: Edge-inferencing placement of inferencing and generating models
ideas.statement: The system adopts edge inferencing [32]: a base-station ES performs the inferencing portion and the UE hosts the generating model that produces the final image.

ideas.title: Simulation evidence leaves data and reproducibility details unresolved
ideas.statement: The reported setup supplies model checkpoint, image dimensions, training settings, baseline definitions, plot curves and total model sizes, but does not specify the evaluated prompt/data sample count, repeated-run uncertainty, or hardware timing. Results establish the shown simulations rather than broad deployment guarantees.
validity_flags: Reporting limitation inferred from the whole supplied PDF. Appendix A does supply an example codec architecture for fc=0.5, separately extracted.

ideas.title: FID compares Inception feature distributions
ideas.statement: The paper uses 2048-dimensional pretrained Inception-v3 activation features and feature means/covariances to measure distance between generated and ideal images; smaller FID is better. Equation (8) combines a mean-distance term with Tr(Cg+C0-2 sqrt(Cg C0)).
validity_flags: FID equation (8) has anomalous mean-term notation and inconsistent I0/Ip labels; do not treat printed formula as unambiguous standard FID.

ideas.title: Background: entropy and perplexity based hard compression
ideas.statement: The related-work account attributes sentence/word selection by entropy or perplexity to SelectiveSentence and token deletion tolerant of disfluency to LLMLingua and LongLLMLingua.

ideas.title: Coded MEG lowers FID substantially at low SNR but has a high-SNR floor
ideas.statement: Figure 7 shows fc=0.5 MEG FID substantially below both baselines at low SNR; at -20 dB MEG AWGN is approximately 26 versus centralized 71 and raw features 130. At high SNR raw features approach zero FID while MEG has a residual floor (roughly 4–8). The paper describes a deterioration threshold near -20 dB.
ideas.conditions: Approximate chart readings, AWGN values unless specified.
validity_flags: Prose broadly claims raw features outperform centralized FID, but Figure 7 shows raw features worse at low SNR, only improving relative to centralized at higher SNR.
Threshold language is approximate and channel-dependent; MEG Rayleigh visibly degrades before -20 dB.

ideas.title: Flower-field example remains recognizable at lower SNR with coded seeds
ideas.statement: Figure 5 compares centralized generation, raw features, and MEG under AWGN/Rayleigh at SNRs 40,30,20,10,0,-10,-20,-30,-40 dB. The coded MEG rows preserve recognizable flower-field structure at 0 and -10 dB, where centralized output is noise and raw-feature decoding is severely corrupted; all methods degrade at sufficiently low SNR.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative single-example illustration; no claim of prompt-wide statistical generalization.

ideas.title: Network capacity affects generative service quality
ideas.statement: Transmission errors can degrade received generated content, while delays increase user waiting time; efficient ES–UE transmission is a distinct consideration from model training and inference cost.

ideas.title: Joint generative-model and codec training remains unexplored
ideas.statement: The pretrained GAI model and compression pair are trained separately. The paper does not fully explore jointly training the encoder with the generative model and proposes this as a possible image-quality improvement.

ideas.title: KL-regularized autoencoder maps pixels into downsampled latent space
ideas.statement: Following [17], E maps images of shape B×C×H×W to latents B×Z×H/fd×W/fd. A slight KL penalty toward a standard normal distribution discourages high variance and centers the latent features. The UE auto-decoder maps recovered latents to images.

ideas.title: Prompt-conditioned latent feature generation
ideas.statement: Equation (1) defines z=G_alpha(s,z0,fd), where s is the text prompt, z0 random noise, alpha inferencer parameters, and fd the pixel-to-latent downsampling factor. Latent features are underlying image characteristics not directly observable; generation moves to pixel space only on the UE.

ideas.title: Latent representation reduces transmitted symbol count
ideas.statement: Remark 1 asserts |z|<fd^-2 |I_g| for fd>1 and consequently |x|<|z|<<|I_g|, motivating communication savings from compressed latent transmission.
ideas.conditions: Claim assumes favorable latent channel count and actual compression.
validity_flags: Generic inequality suppresses latent-versus-pixel channel multiplicity; the dimension ratio is not solely fd^-2.

ideas.title: Hard and soft prompt compression
ideas.statement: The paper distinguishes hard prompt compression, which removes low-information sentences, words or tokens, from soft compression, which maps natural-language tokens into a smaller set of special tokens. SelectiveSentence and LLMLingua exemplify hard methods; GIST, AutoCompressor and ICAE exemplify soft methods.

ideas.title: Communicate latent features without intermediate human-perceivable output
ideas.statement: MEG exchanges encoded latent features between ES and UE, exploiting the freedom to operate in machine-perceivable space before final output to reduce transmission overhead.

ideas.title: LDM-based MEG trains only the added compression codec
ideas.statement: MEG builds on LDM [17] with five components: prompt embedder, denoising model, compression encoder, compression decoder, and autoencoder. Prompt embedder, denoiser, and autoencoder are pretrained; training focuses on the added compression encoder/decoder.

ideas.title: LDM noise prediction MSE
ideas.statement: Equation (23) equates squared clean-latent error to (sigma_t^2/alpha_t^2) times squared noise error. Equation (24) gives conditional LDM loss E[||epsilon-epsilon_theta(zt,s_hat,t)||_2^2], with Gaussian added noise and text conditioning. MEG uses a pretrained UNet for this denoising.
validity_flags: Condition notation in (24) is inconsistent with s_tilde embedding notation; expectation includes an unexplained p_tilde symbol.

ideas.title: Point-to-point downlink and lossless ignored prompt uplink
ideas.statement: MEG models point-to-point transmission with no interfering users. Prompt uplink bandwidth is deemed minimal, so uplink transmission is neglected and the prompt is assumed received without loss at the ES.
validity_flags: Idealized no-interference downlink and lossless prompt uplink; uplink cost excluded.

ideas.title: Coded-seed corruption appears as semantic rather than pixel noise
ideas.statement: For the flower-field example, the authors describe reduced pixel noise but chaotic flowers or superimposed images below about -20 dB; centralized transmission is almost invisible by 0 dB, whereas raw features preserve some flower structure. Prose claims fc=0.9 yields better quality than fc=0.5.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative prompt: colorful flowers on a field.
validity_flags: Figure 5 visually labels MEG rows by AWGN/Rayleigh, not by the fc=0.5/0.9 comparison described in this prose.

ideas.title: MEG as a modality-independent network architecture
ideas.statement: MEG enables AI-based content generation at the edge of cellular or other networks. Its definition is not restricted to a generated data modality or specific GAI algorithm.

ideas.title: Mobile edge generation splits generative inference across edge server and user equipment
ideas.statement: MEG deploys cooperating GAI components on an edge server (ES) and user equipment (UE); their exchange jointly completes user-prompted generation with less communication overhead. The framework can interoperate with different generative methods but needs model-specific deployment and encoding.

ideas.title: MEG generation execution sequence
ideas.statement: Algorithm 1 initializes pretrained embedder/autoencoder/UNet and trained compression modules, uploads and embeds the prompt, generates the latent at ES, compresses and downloads the seed, decodes it on UE, and runs the image auto-decoder.

ideas.title: Larger compression networks increase total model storage
ideas.statement: Longer encoded vectors increase encoder/decoder network size and complexity. The authors claim overall deployment feasibility for ES/UE based on models around 7.4–10.08 GB, but report total model size rather than separate UE memory, execution time, energy, or deployment measurements.
validity_flags: The prose calls the models sub-10GB although the table includes 10.08 GB.
Deployment feasibility is asserted without hardware-specific runtime evidence.

ideas.title: Extend seed-based MEG to multiple users or cells
ideas.statement: Suggested extensions include TDMA for sequential ES access and CDMA or NOMA for multi-user communication. Beyond communication, multi-user MEG must handle model accessibility, resource allocation, and personalized user demands; these extensions are not evaluated.

ideas.title: Learned codec introduces a reconstruction-error floor
ideas.statement: The authors attribute high-SNR MEG disadvantage to imperfect DNN encoding/decoding after finite training, discussing overfitting as limiting additional training. They suggest other coding methods may avoid this error but lose the neural codec’s low-SNR benefit.
validity_flags: Overfitting explanation is asserted rather than established by a reported ablation.

ideas.title: Seed transmission can combine alternative source and error-correction codes
ideas.statement: The paper notes JPEG-style source coding, Turbo codes, and LDPC as conventional image coding approaches and argues applicable encoding technologies can also be used for seed transmission; MEG is not tied to the proposed neural codec.

ideas.title: Measured payload counts and total model sizes across compression rates
ideas.statement: Table II reports centralized generation: 1,048,576 transmitted floating-point numbers and 7.17 GB model; raw-feature transmission: 16,384 and 7.17 GB. MEG fc={0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} uses {1,638;4,915;8,192;11,469;14,746} transmitted numbers with total model sizes {7.4;8.16;8.78;9.64;10.08} GB. These are symbol/float counts, not measured wire bytes.
validity_flags: Table II grows payload in proportion to fc, conflicting with inverse-fc formula in section III.D.
Centralized count 1,048,576 implies four values per 512×512 pixel; the pixel-channel convention is not explained.

ideas.title: Human-perceivable and machine-perceivable information
ideas.statement: Human-perceivable information can be captured and analyzed by human senses; machine-perceivable information is digital information processed by computers or AI models. An AI source permits generation and transmission to remain in machine space until presentation to the user.

ideas.title: Text regeneration metrics
ideas.statement: Text reconstruction is evaluated with ROUGE-L F-measure, based on longest common subsequence and precision/recall, and BLEU, based on n-gram precision against the original text.
validity_flags: Lexical similarity scores do not directly establish factual correctness or total retained information.

ideas.title: Qualitative fidelity/error/power reward
ideas.statement: Per-user episodic reward aims to maximize fidelity while penalizing bit-error probability and power usage.
validity_flags: No explicit reward equation, penalty coefficients, or formal mapping from energy/latency/fidelity constraints is supplied.

ideas.title: Evaluate against error-free generated reference images
ideas.statement: Image quality is measured against I0 generated with zero transmission errors and sufficient computing power, using PSNR and FID. The reference is an ideal generated image, not an external real-world ground-truth photograph.

ideas.title: Optimize generated-image FID under a total transmission budget
ideas.statement: P2 minimizes FID(I0,Ig) over slot powers p_t, with identical denoising-step counts for ideal and received images, sum_{t=0}^T p_t<=pmax, and 0<|x_Ig|<fd^-2|x_Ic| for fd>1. The denoising count is calligraphic T while T in the power sum is the transmission period.

ideas.title: Continuous power action is clipped to remaining budget
ideas.statement: The agent emits a_t in [0,1] and proposes p_t=a_t*pmax; if this exceeds remaining power, it spends all remaining power instead. Equations (32)-(33) enforce the cumulative budget operationally.
validity_flags: Equation (33) uses a sum through t containing p_t itself; operational description implies prior spent power.

ideas.title: ES controls power over one seed-transmission episode
ideas.statement: The ES DRL agent begins after the seed is generated; each fading-coherence block is a time slot and the entire transmission plus final generation is an episode. Final-image FID supplies the delayed reward for the long-term budget-constrained MDP.

ideas.title: Power-control state includes seed segment, channel, and budget
ideas.statement: Equation (31) defines state s_t={x_t,h_t,pmax-sum_{0}^{t}p_t}: the feature fragment to transmit, channel state information, and remaining power budget.
ideas.conditions: Assumes channel-state information is available at decision time.
validity_flags: Printed remaining-budget sum includes the current p_t before that action is selected, causing a time-index ambiguity.

ideas.title: Background: GIST generalization and limitations
ideas.statement: The paper credits GIST with generalizing learned compression beyond prompt-specific training, while describing a need to finetune the original LLM and typically short source prompts below thirty tokens.
validity_flags: Summary is the citing paper’s characterization of GIST, not independently verified here.

ideas.title: PPO uses clipped likelihood-ratio advantage updates
ideas.statement: The power agent uses stochastic policy pi_varpi(a_t|s_t), likelihood ratio u_t=pi_varpi/pi_varpi_old, surrogate E[u_t A_t], and clipped objective E[min(u_t A_t,clip(u_t,1-epsilon,1+epsilon)A_t)] to limit destabilizing policy changes; A_t is the advantage from [37].

ideas.title: PPO converges to lower FID than average or random power allocation
ideas.statement: Figure 10 compares PPO, average, and random power allocation at Pmax=1 and 2 mW over about 14,000 training steps. At 2 mW PPO settles near FID 20 after about 4,000 steps, versus average near 25 and random near 30. At 1 mW PPO settles near 40 after about 11,000 steps, versus average near 53 and random near 62. Prose reports a FID gain reaching 20 at 1 mW.
ideas.conditions: Approximate values read from training curves; no uncertainty bands or repeat-run counts shown.
validity_flags: Claimed 20-point gain at 1 mW aligns approximately with random baseline, while the average-power gap is about 13; prose comparator is unclear.

ideas.title: PPO combines clipped policy, value loss and entropy bonus
ideas.statement: Equations (37),(39),(40) use L=E[L_CLIP-c1 L_VF+c2 S[pi](s_t)], with value loss E[(V_varpi(s_t)-V_pi_old(s_t))^2], entropy encouraging exploration, and gradient ascent varpi←varpi+alpha grad_varpi L.
validity_flags: Source does not give numerical PPO clip, entropy/value coefficients, advantage estimator, or actor/critic architecture in the inspected agent-training section.

ideas.title: MSE and PSNR of generated images
ideas.statement: Equations (6)-(7) define MSE=sum_m,n (Ig-I0)^2/(M*N) and PSNR=10 log10(imax^2/MSE); M,N are image rows and columns, and imax is the highest possible pixel value (255 for unsigned 8-bit images).

ideas.title: Background: ICAE reconstruction compressor
ideas.statement: The paper describes ICAE as pretraining a compressor without adding decoder parameters, handling roughly 500-token inputs with an unchanged original LLM; it characterizes prior ICAE compression as at most about 15x. The experiments here deliberately train ICAE at more aggressive settings for comparison.
ideas.conditions: The stated prior-work ratio is distinct from this paper’s reimplemented ICAE sweep.

ideas.title: Neural seed compression trades high-SNR fidelity for low-SNR robustness
ideas.statement: Figure 6 compares AWGN and Rayleigh PSNR across -25 to 25 dB at fc=0.5. MEG has a small low-SNR advantage but saturates near 28.5 (AWGN) or 28.1 (Rayleigh), while uncoded latent/image transmission overtakes it as SNR rises. At 25 dB, raw-feature AWGN is approximately 33.1 and centralized AWGN 30.7 versus MEG AWGN 28.5.
ideas.conditions: Graph-read values approximate; no error bars shown.
validity_flags: Prose describes crossover after 10 dB, but specific crossover differs by baseline/channel; plotted centralized AWGN overtakes MEG closer to 20 dB.

ideas.title: Plasticization versus antiplasticization
ideas.statement: Both plasticizers and antiplasticizers depress the polymer glass transition temperature; plasticizers often increase flexibility in the glass, whereas antiplasticizers increase glass-state shear or bulk modulus.

ideas.title: Packing frustration controls glass formation
ideas.statement: Prior generalized entropy theory attributes strongly temperature-dependent structural relaxation to packing frustration from complex monomer shapes, chain connectivity and backbone or side-group stiffness; longer flexible side groups can cause internal plasticization.
validity_flags: Prior theory reported by authors; not independently verified

ideas.title: Prior lattice-theory dilution result
ideas.statement: DiMarzio and coworkers identify ideal glass transition with extrapolated zero configurational entropy and predict a nearly universal linear glass-transition depression with plasticizer mole fraction.

ideas.title: Miscible single-transition scope
ideas.statement: The multicomponent ETGF extension assumes a single calorimetric glass transition in miscible binary fluids; initial analysis focuses on moderate additive concentration about 10 mass percent and thermodynamics mainly above Tg.
validity_flags: Single-transition miscible-fluid model; does not establish behavior in separated or multiple-transition systems

ideas.title: Lattice cluster thermodynamics combined with Adam–Gibbs dynamics
ideas.statement: ETGF uses lattice cluster theory to include short-range correlations from chain connectivity, semiflexibility and monomer structure, and combines configurational entropy with Adam–Gibbs structural relaxation dynamics.

ideas.title: Entropy-controlled structural relaxation
ideas.statement: The adopted relation is tau_alpha = tau_0 exp{Delta_mu s_c*/[k_B T s_c(T)]}, where tau_0 is the high-temperature relaxation limit, Delta_mu the high-temperature activation energy and s_c* the peak configurational entropy density.

ideas.title: Low-temperature configurational entropy and VFT fragility
ideas.statement: For Tg < T < T_I, s_c(T)=s_0(1-T_0/T) gives tau_alpha=tau_0 exp{Delta_mu s_c*/[s_0 k_B(T-T_0)]} and D=[Delta_mu/(k_B T_0)](s_c*/s_0).

ideas.title: Activation-energy closure from crossover temperature
ideas.statement: The empirical closure Delta_mu/k_B approximately 6 T_I avoids an independently fitted composition dependence of activation energy; T_I is the inflection of T s_c(T), identified with experimental mode-coupling temperature T_mc.

ideas.title: Glass transition criterion
ideas.statement: This work defines Tg by computed structural relaxation time tau_alpha=100 s, noting prior Lindemann-based predictions are similar.

ideas.title: Compact united-atom polystyrene model
ideas.statement: Because cyclic monomer portions are not implemented, PS is approximated by a compact lattice topology with two backbone and six side-group united-atom carbon sites. Backbone and side-group bending energies differ; one effective van der Waals energy applies to all carbons.
validity_flags: Coarse-grained topology; ignores differing carbon-site energies

ideas.title: Calibration of high-molar-mass PS
ideas.statement: Specific-volume fitting over 350–450 K for PS with N=8000 gives epsilon=275 K and a_cell=2.72 Å as printed. Fitting Tg=375 K and fragility m=139 gives E_b=650 K and E_s=1300 K; side groups are twice as stiff as backbone.
validity_flags: Source calls a_cell a cell volume but prints Å, a dimensional inconsistency retained without correction
Calibrated to selected experimental Tg and fragility values

ideas.title: Scatter in experimental PS calibration targets
ideas.statement: Reported PS Tg spans 360–375 K; reported m values include 116,124,143,146, and VFT D values include 3.83,4.75,5.77,7.80, so calibration targets are not unique.

ideas.title: SF polymer and flexible oligomer test system
ideas.statement: Model SF polymer has stiff backbone and flexible side groups: N=8000, E_b=900 K, E_s=450 K. It is mixed with 10 mass percent fully flexible oligomer (E_b=E_s=0); both have 1-pentene monomers with two backbone and three side-group sites. Pure SF has Tg,p=321 K, K_p=1/D_p=0.30 and m_p=194.

ideas.title: Smaller flexible additives depress Tg and fragility more
ideas.statement: At fixed 10 mass percent additive, smaller fully flexible oligomers produce larger Tg depression and lower K (stronger glass formation), accompanied by decreased excess free volume at Tg; Tg depression saturates for large additive N. Compressibility and density change little with additive size.
ideas.conditions: SF model and diluent cohesive energies 100,200,300,400 K in Fig. 2; N from 2 to 1000.

ideas.title: Berthelot mixing rule for polymer–diluent attraction
ideas.statement: Polymer–solvent attraction is constrained to epsilon_ps=(epsilon_pp epsilon_ss)^(1/2); the SF host interaction is fixed at epsilon_pp=200 K while epsilon_ss varies.
validity_flags: Cross interactions constrained rather than independently varied

ideas.title: Stronger diluent attraction reduces Tg depression and fragility
ideas.statement: At fixed flexible-additive size, increased cohesive energy makes Tg depression smaller while lowering fragility K; Delta Tg varies approximately linearly with epsilon.
ideas.conditions: 10 mass percent flexible diluent in SF polymer, Berthelot rule.

ideas.title: Cohesion controls glass softening and densification
ideas.statement: Figures 4 and 5 show high-cohesion additives lower mixture compressibility and raise density, while weak-cohesion additives have the opposite effects; dependence on additive N is small compared with cohesion dependence.
ideas.conditions: SF host with 10 mass percent fully flexible additive, properties compared with pure SF at mixture Tg; cohesive energies 100–400 K.

ideas.title: Compressibility and density do not diagnose melt softness
ideas.statement: Plasticization terminology here refers strictly to the glass state. Unlike shear modulus in some cited systems, calculated density and compressibility do not invert relative values above and below Tg and cannot reliably characterize melt-state softness; a glass antiplasticizer can be a fluid-state plasticizer.

ideas.title: Cohesive-energy criterion for plasticizer class
ideas.statement: Under geometric mixing, epsilon_ss>epsilon_pp lowers compressibility (glass toughening/antiplasticization), whereas epsilon_ss<epsilon_pp raises it (glass softening/plasticization). Antiplasticizers modestly raise density at Tg; plasticizers tend to lower it. Density alone is insufficient to classify the additive.
ideas.conditions: Flexible additives within the modeled binary fluids; compressibility trends persist across temperatures.
validity_flags: Compressibility-based classification, not direct modulus calculation

ideas.title: Molecular design guidelines for additives
ideas.statement: Most effective modeled glass plasticizers are small, flexible, weakly attractive species; antiplasticizers are compact and strongly attractive to polymer. Very strong attraction can yield only small Tg depression or increase Tg. Size and flexibility mainly affect Tg; cohesive energy affects both Tg and softness.
validity_flags: Model-derived guideline; conditional extrapolation to very strong attraction

ideas.title: Independent thermodynamic guideline reported
ideas.statement: Dong and Fried are cited as obtaining similar statistical-thermodynamic conclusions: efficient plasticizers are small relative to polymer statistical segment size and weakly interact with the host.

ideas.title: Stiff additives suppress transition depression
ideas.statement: With 10 mass percent SF-polymer diluent and E_b/E_s=2, T_0 depends sigmoidally on additive E_b, plateauing at low and high rigidity; increasing rigidity diminishes transition depression and can produce a rise. The effect is larger for higher-molar-mass diluents containing more stiff bond pairs.
ideas.conditions: N=2 or 10, epsilon=100 or 400 K, E_b=0–2000 K. T_0 is zero-entropy extrapolation.
validity_flags: Extension from T_0 to Tg assumes the correlation established for flexible additives persists with stiffness

ideas.title: Combined size–cohesion scaling of Tg depression
ideas.statement: Delta Tg(N,epsilon)=−phi_s Tg,p ln[(a+b/N)/(1+k epsilon)]. SF-fit constants are a=3.11±0.04, b=4.30±0.09 and k=(0.53±0.01)×10^−2 (with epsilon in K). Thus (1+k epsilon) exp[−Delta Tg/(Tg,p phi_s)] is linear in 1/N and collapses the computed size/energy data.
ideas.conditions: Fully flexible oligomeric additives in a high-molar-mass SF host; low additive fraction, Fig.7 uses data from Fig.2.
validity_flags: Empirical collapse of model calculations, not general proof

ideas.title: Fragility correlates with excess free volume in mixtures
ideas.statement: Changes in K and excess free-volume fraction at respective glass transitions strongly correlate for SF mixtures, but different cohesive energies do not collapse to one curve. Dependences on diluent size and cohesion qualitatively resemble chain-size and cohesion effects in pure melts.
ideas.conditions: 10 mass percent fully flexible oligomer in SF host, varied N and epsilon.

ideas.title: Dilute plasticizer efficiency
ideas.statement: At low additive mass fraction phi_s, Tg=Tg,p−lambda_0 phi_s defines plasticizer efficiency lambda_0. The cited diffusion-based linear relation fails at high diluent content, typically above 40 mass percent, where Tg becomes nonlinear.

ideas.title: PS mixture results target general trends
ideas.statement: The PS N=8000 computations use 0–20 mass percent fully flexible oligomers with styrene subunit topology; limitations in representing PS and diluent monomers mean these calculations target qualitative trends rather than quantitative reproduction of experiments.

ideas.title: PS Tg efficiency trends and numerical comparison
ideas.statement: PS mixture Tg is nearly linear in additive mass fraction from 0 to 0.20. The most efficient Tg depressors are small and weakly attractive; strong polymer–diluent attraction toughens the glass while reducing Tg-depression efficiency. Computed lambda_0 ranges 81–446 K versus cited experimental 241–524 K.
ideas.conditions: PS N=8000, flexible additive N=2 or 5, epsilon=140 or 550 K; experimental comparison is across different plasticizers.
validity_flags: Qualitative comparison, not matched-chemical quantitative validation

ideas.title: Both plasticizers and antiplasticizers reduce PS fragility
ideas.statement: Both additive classes reduce fragility. For 0–20 mass percent diluent, m=m_p−eta_0 phi_s is approximately linear with computed slopes eta_0=134–202.
ideas.conditions: PS model with flexible N=2/5 additives and low/high cohesive energies.

ideas.title: PS mechanical-proxy response to additive fraction
ideas.statement: In Fig.11, weak-cohesion 140 K diluents increasingly raise compressibility ratio with mass fraction and slightly lower density ratio; strong-cohesion 550 K diluents lower compressibility and raise density. Size N=2 versus 5 has a much smaller mechanical-proxy effect than cohesion.
ideas.conditions: Ratios evaluated against undiluted PS at each mixture Tg; phi_s=0–0.2.

ideas.title: Semiflexible additive A for full-composition calculations
ideas.statement: PS-A mixtures use N=5 additive A with 1-pentene monomers, E_b=600 K, E_s=200 K and epsilon=200 K. Its Tg,s=200 K is lower than PS Tg,p=378 K; this provides a model plasticizer with measurable Tg for full composition analysis.

ideas.title: Approximately linear activation-energy mixing
ideas.statement: Crossover T_I and peak configurational entropy density s_c* are approximately linear in mixture composition; using Delta_mu/k_B≈6T_I predicts Delta_mu(phi_s)=(1−phi_s)Delta_mu_p+phi_s Delta_mu_s. For PS-A, the endpoints are 25.6 and 16.5 kJ/mol.

ideas.title: Near-linear entropy and inverse relaxation exponent
ideas.statement: For PS-A at fixed T, s_c≈alpha(phi_0,p−phi_p), and 1/Omega=(beta Delta_mu)^−1(s_c/s_c*) is approximately linear over the composition range, with slight deviations at high dilution.
ideas.conditions: Fig.12 examples T=270,290,310 K; phi_p is polymer mass fraction.

ideas.title: Angell relaxation law and zero mobility concentration
ideas.statement: The computed composition dependence at fixed T follows tau_alpha(phi_p)=tau_0 exp{beta Delta_mu(phi_p)s_c*(phi_p)/s_c(phi_p)}≈A exp{B/(phi_0,p−phi_p)}. A and B are concentration-independent; phi_0,p is the extrapolated concentration where relaxation time diverges.
ideas.conditions: PS-A mixture model; approximate near-linearity of inverse exponent.
validity_flags: Divergence is extrapolated, not an observed transition

ideas.title: Plasticizer efficiency decreases across full dilution range
ideas.statement: PS-A Tg varies nonlinearly over the full composition range; lambda(phi_s)=−dTg/dphi_s declines with added diluent, consistent with cited PS solvent observations. Over 0–20 mass percent A, slope is approximately constant and Delta Tg≈−lambda_0 phi_s.

ideas.title: Jenckel–Heusch composition relation
ideas.statement: The cited Jenckel–Heusch relation is Tg=(1−phi_s)Tg,p+phi_s Tg,s+b(Tg,p−Tg,s)phi_s(1−phi_s), where b describes solvent quality.

ideas.title: Fox relation and assumptions
ideas.statement: Fox mixing relation is 1/Tg=(1−phi_s)/Tg,p+phi_s/Tg,s. Its stated derivation assumes random mixing, equal heat-capacity jumps near transition and zero excess mixing volume across compositions.

ideas.title: Comparison of Tg mixing relations
ideas.statement: For computed PS-A mixtures, Fried describes Tg poorly, Fox is closer, and the generalized logarithmic relation fits excellently with k_1=0.93 instead of pure-component Tg,s/Tg,p≈0.53. Both parameter-free laws predict declining plasticizer efficiency with dilution.
validity_flags: Benchmark against ETGF computations rather than direct experimental data

ideas.title: VFT temperature follows logarithmic mixing
ideas.statement: ln(T_0/T_0,p)=phi_s ln(T_0,s/T_0,p)/[(1−phi_s)k_1+phi_s] describes calculated PS-A VFT temperatures with k_1=0.89.

ideas.title: Approximate geometric Tg mixing and efficiency
ideas.statement: Setting fitted k_1≈1 gives Tg=Tg,p^(1−phi_s) Tg,s^phi_s and lambda(phi_s)=Tg,p^(1−phi_s) Tg,s^phi_s ln(Tg,p/Tg,s).
ideas.conditions: Approximation to fitted logarithmic law for PS-A mixtures.

ideas.title: Pure-component Tg ratio predicts dilute transition depression
ideas.statement: For small phi_s, Delta Tg≈−phi_s Tg,p ln(Tg,p/Tg,s). It reproduces computed PS-A shifts over 0–30 mass percent A with relative errors at most 5.6%.

ideas.title: Rationalizing size and attraction scaling
ideas.statement: Combining 1/Tg=1/Tg_infinity+K/N and approximately linear Tg=A+k epsilon for fixed topology with the dilute logarithmic shift rationalizes Eq.(3) size/cohesion scaling. The same trend fits fully flexible additives although those have no definite Tg.
validity_flags: Heuristic transfer of a Tg-based relation to fully flexible additives lacking definite Tg

ideas.title: Temperature range and meaning of zero mobility concentration
ideas.statement: For PS-A at ambient pressure and T<T_0,p≈330 K, extrapolated zero mobility concentration phi_0,p decreases on cooling. For T>T_0,p, no mixture composition has an extrapolated relaxation divergence, so phi_0,p cannot strictly be interpreted as a physical zero mobility concentration.
validity_flags: Extrapolated divergence and temperature, not measured singularities

ideas.title: Zero mobility concentration decreases with pressure
ideas.statement: PS-A phi_0,p is approximately linear at low pressure and approaches saturation at high pressure. Over T=250–310 K the low-pressure slope is about −0.001 MPa^−1; temperature slope is about 0.004 K^−1 with weak pressure dependence.
ideas.conditions: Pressure calculations span 0–500 MPa.

ideas.title: Kauzmann pressure derivative from composition derivatives
ideas.statement: Using dT_K/dP=−(partial phi_0,p/partial P)/(partial phi_0,p/partial T) gives about 0.25 K/MPa, compared with direct pure-PS computation 0.30 K/MPa and cited experimental VFT derivative 0.32±0.05 K/MPa over 10–80 MPa.
ideas.conditions: Low-pressure limit; T_K is extrapolated zero-entropy temperature.
validity_flags: Comparison of theoretical Kauzmann and experimental Vogel temperatures

ideas.title: Reported activation energies of fragile polymers
ideas.statement: The source reports segmental high-temperature activation energies from 12.1 kJ/mol for polybutylene (m=85) to 17.2 kJ/mol for poly(methyl acrylate) (m=102), tending to higher values for strong polymers.
validity_flags: Reported literature examples, not new measurements

ideas.title: Joint temperature–pressure fit
ideas.statement: phi_0,p=[1+(phi_0−T_0/T)+h(phi_infinity−T_infinity/T)P]/(1+hP). Fitted parameters are phi_0=1, T_0=317.9 K, phi_infinity=1.335, T_infinity=239.6 K, h=0.003 MPa^−1. Low-pressure slope is approximately −kappa h with kappa=1+(phi_0−phi_infinity)+(T_infinity−T_0)/T.
ideas.conditions: PS-A, 250–310 K, 0–500 MPa; phi_0 and T_0 describe ambient-pressure behavior, infinity parameters high-pressure behavior.
validity_flags: Phenomenological fit; kappa here is a fit combination, not the earlier isothermal compressibility

ideas.title: Inverse host-chain-length scaling
ideas.statement: At fixed T<T_0,p, phi_0,p=phi_0,p_infinity+theta/N. Fits give (phi_infinity,theta)=(0.973,1.739) at 310 K, (0.902,1.608) at 290 K, and (0.824,1.572) at 270 K.
ideas.conditions: N is polymerization index of PS host, not diluent.

ideas.title: Approximate host-Tg scaling of plasticizer efficiency
ideas.statement: Authors approximate the efficiency change between host chain lengths by the ratio of host Tg values. At 20 mass percent A, N_l=20 PS has Tg,p=361.3 K and Delta Tg=−44.1 K, versus N_h=8000 with Tg,p=378.1 K and Delta Tg=−47.7 K; host-Tg scaling predicts −45.6 K for the short host.
validity_flags: Approximate proportionality ignores dependence of the logarithmic Tg ratio in Eq.(15)
Page 10 calls A a PS oligomer, whereas page 8 specifies 1-pentene topology; source inconsistency retained

ideas.title: Theory underestimates PS molecular-weight dependence
ideas.statement: ETGF underestimates the experimental slope of 1/Tg,p versus 1/N for PS by a factor of 3. Using experimental chain-length dependence would imply a somewhat larger relative efficiency change, Delta lambda/lambda≈0.1, from very large N down to N=20.

ideas.title: Mechanical crossover temperature is not resolved
ideas.statement: The computed density and compressibility remain qualitatively shifted in the same direction across temperature and cannot reveal the cited antiplasticization temperature T_a below which antiplasticization occurs and above which only plasticization appears.

ideas.title: Phase separation and two glass transitions
ideas.statement: Future ETGF mixture work should resolve whether phase-separated fluids have two glass transitions. Authors suggest applying tau_alpha~100 s to both phases, but say this criterion cannot treat two transitions within one phase.

ideas.title: No sharp entropy change at pure-component transitions
ideas.statement: Fully miscible PS-A calculations do not show sharp configurational-entropy variation near either pure-component Tg, even when those Tg values differ by over 170 K.

ideas.title: Independent cross interactions remain unexplored
ideas.statement: The work fixes Berthelot interactions to reduce parameters; future work should vary exchange energy epsilon=epsilon_pp+epsilon_ss−2epsilon_ps independently to determine its influence for fixed diluent architecture and host properties.

ideas.title: Ablation separates BoN and length filtering
ideas.statement: MathQA-Python ablations vary BoN N while disabling length filtering, vary MAD cutoff α while removing BoN, and compare with full N=3, α=1 SEER; other training and evaluation settings are held constant.
ideas.conditions: Only MathQA-Python ablations are reported.

ideas.title: Correct, nonempty, nonlooping, shortest Best-of-N selection
ideas.statement: SEER samples N candidate CoT responses per training question, discards incorrect final answers, retains nonempty nonlooping CoTs, and selects the shortest remaining CoT. This is intended to reduce loops and redundant expansions while preserving answer correctness.
ideas.conditions: Requires a correctness oracle such as unit tests or known labels; shortest is chosen only among valid correct candidates.

ideas.title: Best-of-N benefit saturates without filtering
ideas.statement: Without the length filter, N=1/3/5 yield MathQA-Python pass@1 73.49/74.45/74.40%, average CoT 1,191/1,177/1,163 tokens, and compression 18.20/19.16/20.12%. The accuracy gain largely saturates at N=3, while length changes only modestly.
ideas.conditions: Table 5; base 63.67% accuracy and 1,456 CoT tokens.

ideas.title: Fixed token budget and neutral code prompt
ideas.statement: The empirical comparison uses a 16K budget for all models and excludes instructions explicitly encouraging or constraining reasoning; its HumanEval prompt asks for a Python program returned in a code block. Table 1 specifies 16,384 maximum generated tokens.
ideas.conditions: Page 5 calls this maximum context length; Table 1 calls it maximum generated tokens.

ideas.title: C3oT learns mappings between long and short traces
ideas.statement: The paper describes C3oT [14] as jointly training on long and short CoTs to learn mappings, then using conditioned inference for short outputs.

ideas.title: CCoT prompt-based concise reasoning
ideas.statement: The related-work section describes CCoT [5] as using a concise-CoT template that encourages brevity through prompt wording.

ideas.title: Chain-of-Draft terse reasoning template
ideas.statement: The paper describes CoD [37] as using a Chain-of-Draft template that limits reasoning to within five words.

ideas.title: CODI continuous-space self-distillation
ideas.statement: The paper describes CODI [26] as distilling CoT into continuous space through joint learning of explicit and implicit reasoning traces.

ideas.title: Chain-of-Draft adaptation to software engineering
ideas.statement: The paper describes CoD [38] as adapting Chain-of-Draft to software-engineering tasks to reduce token usage.

ideas.title: Combining BoN and MAD filtering
ideas.statement: Full SEER with N=3 and α=1 reaches MathQA-Python pass@1 74.88%, 877 average CoT tokens and 39.77% compression, the highest accuracy in the Table 5 ablation while retaining substantial compression. The authors choose this configuration as their default.
ideas.conditions: Baseline in Table 5 is 63.67% accuracy and 1,456 CoT tokens; α=.5 without BoN compresses more but has lower accuracy.

ideas.title: Matched sampling budget and TokenSkip settings
ideas.statement: The main comparison uses DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B under a 16K token limit. Naive BoN and SEER both sample N=3 candidates. TokenSkip is tested at γ=0.5 and γ=0.8; smaller γ requests stronger compression.
ideas.conditions: Default SEER α=1; all task methods use the predefined task-specific train/test splits.

ideas.title: Relative CoT compression rate
ideas.statement: Compression rate is ρ=1−λ′/λ, where λ is original/reference CoT token count and λ′ is evaluated-model CoT token count; higher ρ means a larger relative token reduction. Negative values represent expansion.
ideas.conditions: Reported table rates compare average generated CoT lengths with each task baseline.

ideas.title: Conciseness-guided system prompt
ideas.statement: The prompt baseline appends a general system instruction requesting reasoning as concisely as possible and avoiding redundant or unnecessary steps.
ideas.conditions: Evaluated on HumanEval and MBPP-Sanitized; prompt is an experimental artifact, not a worker instruction.
