ideas.title: gpt-oss-20b response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, gpt-oss-20b shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 481→238 (-50.5%), accuracy +4.88 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 470→241 (-48.7%), accuracy -2.64 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Llama-8B response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, DeepSeek-Llama-8B shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 3,640→3,063 (-15.9%), accuracy +2.44 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 2,568→2,564 (-0.2%), accuracy -1.85 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-14B response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, DeepSeek-Qwen-14B shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 3,282→2,890 (-11.9%), accuracy +1.82 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 2,078→1,952 (-6.1%), accuracy -1.06 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: Qwen3-8B response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, Qwen3-8B shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 3,604→2,490 (-30.9%), accuracy +3.05 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 3,663→2,545 (-30.5%), accuracy +3.70 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-32B response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, DeepSeek-Qwen-32B shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 3,136→2,610 (-16.8%), accuracy +1.83 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 2,333→1,890 (-19.0%), accuracy +1.58 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-7B response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, DeepSeek-Qwen-7B shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 3,839→3,464 (-9.8%), accuracy +0.61 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 2,459→1,946 (-20.9%), accuracy -5.55 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: QwQ-32B response to conciseness prompting
ideas.statement: With conciseness-guided prompting, QwQ-32B shows original→concise average CoT token length and accuracy change: HumanEval 2,363→2,236 (-5.4%), accuracy 0.00 percentage points; MBPP-Sanitized 1,929→1,779 (-7.8%), accuracy +0.53 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Table 3; HumanEval 164 problems, MBPP-Sanitized 378.

ideas.title: CoT accuracy gains can be offset by verbosity
ideas.statement: The study reports an average 7.4 percentage-point pass@1 increase when enabling CoT, with generation cost reaching roughly ten times the CoT-disabled setting and a maximum observed truncation rate of 17.1%. The effect is not uniformly positive: DeepSeek-Qwen-32B on MBPP drops from 88.62% to 88.10% with 7.4% truncation.
ideas.conditions: Average over the four models and two benchmarks with CoT-disabled comparisons in Table 1.

ideas.title: CoT training gains may not transfer to coding
ideas.statement: The paper cites Liu et al. [19] as finding that some apparently effective CoT training paradigms do not transfer well to real-world coding tasks.

ideas.title: Chain-of-thought reasoning
ideas.statement: Chain-of-thought prompting asks an LLM to articulate intermediate reasoning steps and decompose a problem before producing its answer.

ideas.title: Three observed CoT pathologies
ideas.statement: Figure 1 illustrates overthinking (reconsidering unnecessary test-harness choices), looping (repeatedly questioning inclusion of zero), and semantically unproductive reasoning (dwelling on elementary syntax) across Deepseek-R1, GPT-OSS-120B, and QwQ-32B, including trivial HumanEval tasks.
ideas.conditions: Qualitative examples, not a prevalence estimate.

ideas.title: Measure compression by problem difficulty
ideas.statement: The paper does not stratify benchmark instances by complexity and leaves a finer-grained analysis of difficulty-dependent CoT compression for future work.

ideas.title: Suppressing explicit CoT for a comparison
ideas.statement: The study appends an empty <think> </think> segment to the input to suppress explicit intermediate reasoning in models supporting CoT disabling, following Qwen3 practice.
ideas.conditions: Table 1 excludes disabled-CoT variants for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B and gpt-oss-20b because the paper says these models do not support disabling CoT.

ideas.title: Software-engineering domain limits
ideas.statement: The evaluation focuses on software-engineering tasks, potentially limiting transfer to other reasoning domains; covering code generation, defect detection and code search offers diversity within this domain.

ideas.title: Compressed traces converge to a narrow length range
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compression yields approximately 150–230 tokens for most models, despite much larger and more variable raw CoT lengths; most reported retention ratios are under 10%, while gpt-oss-20b retains approximately 27–31%. The authors interpret this as substantial surface redundancy.
ideas.conditions: A diagnostic LLM-compression proxy, excluding truncations. QwQ-32B MBPP retention is 10.05%, so the under-10% statement is approximate.

ideas.title: Broader models, domains and latency-sensitive agents
ideas.statement: The authors propose extending SEER to additional domains and model families and integrating it into latency-sensitive agent pipelines.

ideas.title: GPT-4o compression as an effective-reasoning proxy
ideas.statement: The study uses GPT-4o to remove surface verbosity while retaining original logic, essential steps and planning instructions, runs compression three times per CoT, and averages results. It excludes truncated traces. Effective reasoning ratio is defined as retained compressed tokens divided by original CoT tokens.
ideas.conditions: Diagnostic analysis only; GPT-4o is not used by SEER training. Truncated instances omitted.

ideas.title: Initial code-generation study design
ideas.statement: The empirical study evaluates HumanEval and MBPP-Sanitized Python problems with signatures, natural-language docstrings and correctness unit tests. Models are DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 7B/14B/32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B, Qwen3-8B and gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: HumanEval and MBPP are held out from training
ideas.statement: HumanEval and MBPP-Sanitized are used exclusively for evaluation to assess transfer to unseen code-generation tasks; they are excluded from SEER and baseline training.

ideas.title: Explicit and implicit CoT compression
ideas.statement: The paper distinguishes explicit rewriting or pruning of CoT (e.g., TokenSkip with LLMLingua and C3oT with GPT-4) from implicit compression through repeated sampling/distillation of simpler traces (e.g., Naive BoN). It argues that explicit compression can lose information or cause thought leaps, whereas implicit compression often has a lower compression ratio.

ideas.title: SEER preserves explicit reasoning format
ideas.statement: SEER directly fine-tunes on the model’s filtered concise correct outputs using Best-of-N and a lightweight length filter, avoiding additional compression modules or latent reasoning representations and retaining visible intermediate reasoning steps.
ideas.conditions: Visible steps do not establish faithful explanation of internal computation.

ideas.title: Length filtering may discard needed long reasoning
ideas.statement: The authors acknowledge that filtering may exclude difficult cases naturally needing longer CoTs. SEER aims to teach concise reasoning to an already reasoning-capable model, not create reasoning ability from scratch. They say BoN operates on traces rather than problems to avoid removing problem instances.
ideas.conditions: The described algorithm retains one shortest correct trace per question before thresholding; the paper does not specify a fallback when all traces for a problem are removed.

ideas.title: gpt-oss-20b GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses gpt-oss-20b CoTs from an average 481 to 149 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 31.11%) and from 470 to 128 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 27.27%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Llama-8B GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses DeepSeek-Llama-8B CoTs from an average 3,594 to 212 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 5.91%) and from 2,538 to 164 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 6.50%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-14B GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses DeepSeek-Qwen-14B CoTs from an average 3,076 to 211 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 6.88%) and from 1,974 to 181 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 9.17%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: Qwen3-8B GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses Qwen3-8B CoTs from an average 3,456 to 228 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 6.62%) and from 3,527 to 155 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 4.41%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-32B GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses DeepSeek-Qwen-32B CoTs from an average 2,869 to 212 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 7.42%) and from 2,218 to 179 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 8.07%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-7B GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses DeepSeek-Qwen-7B CoTs from an average 3,677 to 210 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 5.71%) and from 2,334 to 177 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 7.62%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: LightThinker compact thought representations
ideas.statement: The paper describes LightThinker [41] as compressing verbose thoughts into compact internal representations and removing the original CoT from context.

ideas.title: QwQ-32B GPT-4o retention analysis
ideas.statement: GPT-4o compresses QwQ-32B CoTs from an average 2,311 to 216 tokens on HumanEval (reported retention 9.36%) and from 1,866 to 187 tokens on MBPP-Sanitized (reported retention 10.05%).
ideas.conditions: Table 2; nontruncated traces only; three compression runs per CoT averaged.

ideas.title: Heavy-tailed trace lengths motivate a robust cutoff
ideas.statement: The adaptive filter assumes that post-BoN CoT lengths can remain heavy-tailed; extreme traces from overthinking or loops can dominate training cost and learned behavior, motivating a distribution-aware robust cutoff.

ideas.title: CoT benefits versus decoding overhead
ideas.statement: Explicit intermediate reasoning may support decomposition and error correction but requires additional generated tokens, increasing latency and resource use, especially KV-cache demands; efficiency research aims to retain reasoning benefits while reducing this cost.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Llama-8B initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval pass@1=76.22%, CoT/total=3,640/4,021 tokens, 19/164 truncations (11.6%); MBPP-Sanitized pass@1=63.23%, CoT/total=2,568/2,910 tokens, 35/378 truncations (9.3%).
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-14B initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval: with CoT pass@1=87.20%, CoT/total=3,282/3,669 tokens, 18/164 truncations (11.0%); without CoT 82.32%, 456 tokens and zero truncations. MBPP-Sanitized: with CoT 86.51%, 2,078/2,453 tokens, 17/378 truncations (4.5%); without CoT 74.87%, 424 tokens and zero truncations.
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-32B initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval: with CoT pass@1=88.41%, CoT/total=3,136/3,539 tokens, 17/164 truncations (10.4%); without CoT 87.20%, 183 tokens and zero truncations. MBPP-Sanitized: with CoT 88.10%, 2,333/2,686 tokens, 28/378 truncations (7.4%); without CoT 88.62%, 199 tokens and zero truncations.
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: DeepSeek-Qwen-7B initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval: with CoT pass@1=78.04%, CoT/total=4,099/4,487 tokens, 28/164 truncations (17.1%); without CoT 65.24%, 412 total tokens and zero truncations. MBPP-Sanitized: with CoT 73.54%, 2,459/2,806 tokens, 33/378 truncations (8.7%); without CoT 50.79%, 173 tokens and zero truncations.
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: gpt-oss-20b initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval pass@1=92.68%, CoT/total=481/790 tokens, 1/164 truncations (0.6%); MBPP-Sanitized pass@1=94.44%, CoT/total=470/693 tokens, 3/378 truncations (0.8%).
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: Qwen3-8B initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval: with CoT pass@1=89.02%, CoT/total=3,604/3,701 tokens, 11/164 truncations (6.7%); without CoT 84.76%, 249 total tokens and zero truncations. MBPP-Sanitized: with CoT 84.13%, 3,663/3,712 tokens, 43/378 truncations (11.4%); without CoT 82.01%, 78 tokens and zero truncations.
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: QwQ-32B initial code-generation results
ideas.statement: HumanEval pass@1=93.90%, CoT/total=2,363/2,458 tokens, 2/164 truncations (1.2%); MBPP-Sanitized pass@1=93.65%, CoT/total=1,929/1,990 tokens, 6/378 truncations (1.6%).
ideas.conditions: Table 1; maximum generated tokens 16,384; HumanEval 164 questions and MBPP-Sanitized 378. No CoT-off comparison for DeepSeek-Llama-8B, QwQ-32B or gpt-oss-20b.

ideas.title: Longer failed traces on HumanEval/129
ideas.statement: For each of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 7B, 14B and 32B, the study generates 10,000 responses to HumanEval/129 with a 16,384-token limit. Failed versus passed median (mean) CoT lengths are 9,489 (9,786) versus 8,296 (8,503) for 7B; 7,562 (7,756) versus 6,797 (7,006) for 14B; and 7,792 (7,694) versus 7,124 (7,285) for 32B. Failed responses are longer on this selected problem.
ideas.conditions: HumanEval/129 chosen because its prompt is longest, as a proxy for difficulty; no official difficulty classification or length-control instruction.

ideas.title: Token length and truncation measurements
ideas.statement: Average generated-token length measures output verbosity; truncation number counts generations stopped because they exceed the maximum token budget, which can prevent a complete solution.

ideas.title: Reasoning loops and deterministic decoding
ideas.statement: Reasoning loops repeat identical or semantically redundant segments without advancing toward a solution. The paper cites prior work attributing them to misestimated action probabilities that favor easy repetitive continuations, with greedy or low-temperature decoding amplifying repetition; more randomness may mitigate but not remove the learning problem.

ideas.title: SEER loop mitigation on Defect-Detection
ideas.statement: On Defect-Detection (N=2,732), dataset-specific SEER reduces truncations from 235 (8.6%) to 7 (0.26%) and detected loops from 222 (8.1%) to 7 (0.26%), a reported loop-count reduction of 96.8%.
ideas.conditions: Table 6; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B base versus task-specific SEER, same evaluation budget; strict n=30,k=20 detector.

ideas.title: SEER loop mitigation on MathQA-Python
ideas.statement: On MathQA-Python (N=1,883), dataset-specific SEER reduces truncations from 110 (5.8%) to 30 (1.6%) and detected loops from 85 (4.5%) to 23 (1.2%), a reported loop-count reduction of 72.9%.
ideas.conditions: Table 6; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B base versus task-specific SEER, same evaluation budget; strict n=30,k=20 detector.

ideas.title: SEER loop mitigation on Code-Search
ideas.statement: On Code-Search (N=9,604), dataset-specific SEER reduces truncations from 18 (0.19%) to 1 (0.01%) and detected loops from 15 (0.16%) to 1 (0.01%), a reported loop-count reduction of 93.3%.
ideas.conditions: Table 6; DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B base versus task-specific SEER, same evaluation budget; strict n=30,k=20 detector.

ideas.title: Shorter traces may reduce opportunities for loops
ideas.statement: The authors explain SEER loop/truncation reductions by proposing that shorter reasoning offers fewer opportunities for repeated output; Table 6 demonstrates co-occurring reductions but does not isolate this mechanism from changes due to fine-tuning or candidate selection.

ideas.title: LoRA retains compression with smaller accuracy gains
ideas.statement: Table 7 reports base accuracy 63.67% and 1,456 CoT tokens; PEFT (LoRA) 67.71%, 949 tokens and 34.8% compression; full SFT 74.88%, 877 tokens and 39.8% compression. Thus parameter-efficient tuning improves over base but yields smaller accuracy gains than full SFT.
ideas.conditions: The table matches MathQA-Python base/full-SFT values; caption itself does not name the dataset. LoRA hyperparameters and resource measurements are not given here.

ideas.title: Stricter MAD filtering trades accuracy for compression
ideas.statement: Without BoN, α=2/1.5/1/0.5 yield MathQA-Python pass@1 74.40/74.19/73.50/72.76%, CoT lengths 1,071/918/878/836 tokens, and compression 26.44/36.95/39.70/42.58%. Stronger filtering removes more tokens but lowers measured accuracy.
ideas.conditions: Table 5; cutoff median+α·MAD; all other settings constant.

ideas.title: Median plus MAD adaptive CoT cutoff
ideas.statement: For valid selected traces with lengths λ_i, SEER computes λ̃=median({λ_i}), MAD=median(|λ_i−λ̃|), and λ_mad(α)=λ̃+α·MAD. The default α=1 defines λ_c=λ_mad(1); examples with λ_i>λ_c are discarded. The threshold adapts to the dataset length distribution rather than setting a per-query inference budget.
ideas.conditions: Computed on samples surviving output-validity filtering. Lower α imposes stronger filtering.

ideas.title: SEER average compression versus baselines
ideas.statement: Across MathQA-Python, Defect-Detection and Code-Search, Table 4 reports average compression of -4.2% for TokenSkip γ=0.5, 30.8% for TokenSkip γ=0.8, 20.9% for Self-Trained, 20.1% for Naive BoN N=3, 21.9% for Short CoT, and 41.6% for SEER. SEER exceeds the strongest reported baseline average by 10.8 percentage points.
ideas.conditions: Arithmetic average over the three benchmark-specific compression percentages; not a pooled token-weighted reduction.

ideas.title: Main Defect-Detection comparison
ideas.statement: Table 4 Defect-Detection results (pass@1 accuracy / average CoT tokens / relative reduction): Base: 44.7% / 1,836 / —; TokenSkip γ=0.5: 36.2% / 2,421 / -31.9%; TokenSkip γ=0.8: 47.2% / 1,004 / 45.3%; Self-Trained: 49.3% / 1,055 / 42.5%; Naive BoN N=3: 49.8% / 1,042 / 43.3%; Short CoT: 46.6% / 1,198 / 34.8%; SEER: 50.5% / 785 / 57.2%. SEER has highest measured accuracy and shortest trace among these settings.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, task-specific fine-tuning, 16K limit, N=3 for both BoN methods.

ideas.title: Main MathQA-Python comparison
ideas.statement: Table 4 MathQA-Python results (pass@1 accuracy / average CoT tokens / relative reduction): Base: 63.7% / 1,456 / —; TokenSkip γ=0.5: 1.6% / 1,196 / 17.9%; TokenSkip γ=0.8: 0.9% / 1,109 / 23.8%; Self-Trained: 74.6% / 1,177 / 19.2%; Naive BoN N=3: 73.6% / 1,191 / 18.2%; Short CoT: 55.6% / 1,236 / 15.1%; SEER: 74.9% / 877 / 39.8%. SEER has highest measured accuracy and shortest trace among these settings.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, task-specific fine-tuning, 16K limit, N=3 for both BoN methods.

ideas.title: Main Code-Search comparison
ideas.statement: Table 4 Code-Search results (pass@1 accuracy / average CoT tokens / relative reduction): Base: 72.4% / 472 / —; TokenSkip γ=0.5: 66.5% / 465 / 1.5%; TokenSkip γ=0.8: 76.4% / 362 / 23.3%; Self-Trained: 72.5% / 468 / 0.9%; Naive BoN N=3: 74.9% / 478 / -1.3%; Short CoT: 69.7% / 398 / 15.7%; SEER: 77.3% / 341 / 27.8%. SEER has highest measured accuracy and shortest trace among these settings.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, task-specific fine-tuning, 16K limit, N=3 for both BoN methods.

ideas.title: Naive BoN baseline
ideas.statement: Naive BoN processes pre-inference data using Best-of-N alone and then trains the model, omitting SEER adaptive CoT filtering.

ideas.title: Strict n-gram repetition detector
ideas.statement: Following Pipis et al. [25], an output is labeled looping if any n-gram occurs at least k times within the response; the study uses n=30 and k=20 across reasoning models. This detects severe degenerative repetition and may miss weaker or semantically repetitive loops.
ideas.conditions: Default n=30, k=20; intended for greedy or low-temperature decoding.

ideas.title: SEER optimization and sequence settings
ideas.statement: SEER training uses AdamW, gradient checkpointing, stated learning rate 1×10⁻⁵ with cosine decay and 10% warm-up, gradient clipping norm 1.0, and maximum tokenized sequence length 16,384. The framework is also compatible with LoRA and QLoRA.
ideas.conditions: Same primary full-parameter supervised fine-tuning run described on page 11.

ideas.title: Validity filtering precedes length filtering
ideas.statement: After Best-of-N selection, SEER first removes invalid, malformed or incomplete final outputs, such as unparseable code or code failing provided unit tests, before applying its length threshold.

ideas.title: Overthinking and a nonmonotonic length-accuracy relation
ideas.statement: The paper describes overthinking as reasoning beyond a useful length range: additional reasoning initially helps exploration but can later introduce redundant or erroneous content, noise, and deviation from a correct solution.

ideas.title: Pass@1 code-generation metric
ideas.statement: Pass@1 is the proportion of problems solved correctly on the first attempt, measuring single-attempt functional correctness. For programming evaluations all unit tests must pass; for binary classification it reduces to matching the ground-truth label in a single attempt.

ideas.title: Self-generated pre-inference training traces
ideas.statement: For each training question, the base model generates complete answers containing explicit step-by-step reasoning, with a 16K budget and simple task prompts (the same code prompt as the initial study). The rationale is to collect complete, diverse traces before filtering and reduce early truncation.
ideas.conditions: Training-data preparation cost is distinct from downstream inference cost.

ideas.title: Prompt-only CoT control is model dependent
ideas.statement: Conciseness instructions reduce CoT length in the tested models, but reductions and accuracy changes differ substantially by model and dataset; gpt-oss-20b reduces HumanEval CoT by over 50%, while several DeepSeek variants lose accuracy on MBPP. Thus prompting does not provide uniform compression/accuracy control.

ideas.title: Fixed prompts control but do not eliminate prompt sensitivity
ideas.statement: The authors use fixed prompts and consistent prompting strategies to reduce confounding and describe SEER as largely prompt-agnostic; the reported experiments do not establish uniform behavior under all prompt variations.

ideas.title: Structured CoT for code generation
ideas.statement: The paper identifies SCoT [18] as an early approach applying structured chain-of-thought prompting to code generation.

ideas.title: SEER self-enhancing compression
ideas.statement: SEER (Self-Enhancing Efficient Reasoning) generates its own CoT training data, refines them using Best-of-N sampling and a data-driven length filter, then fine-tunes the same model to internalize concise reasoning without an external compression tool.

ideas.title: Reported average SEER reduction
ideas.statement: The current PDF reports that SEER reduces CoT length by an average of 41.6% across three software-engineering tasks while preserving or improving task accuracy; it reports loop mitigation up to 96.8%.
ideas.conditions: Paper-level summary of the tested models and benchmarks; later tables provide task-specific metrics.

ideas.title: Direct self-training baseline
ideas.statement: Self-Training trains the model directly on its self-inference data, without the stated Best-of-N/adaptive filtering refinements.

ideas.title: Spatial awareness includes perception, reasoning, and generation
ideas.statement: 3D spatial awareness comprises perception of states such as locations and distances, plus reasoning and generation derived from perception, including embodied planning and spatial layout editing.

ideas.title: Full-parameter SEER training configuration
ideas.statement: The primary model is DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, fine-tuned with LLaMAFactory for three epochs and effective batch size eight. Hardware is four NVIDIA RTX A800 GPUs (80GB each), 128 Intel Xeon CPUs and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.
ideas.conditions: Full-parameter SFT is default; PEFT is explored separately.

ideas.title: Short-CoT prompting can lose task accuracy
ideas.statement: In the three-task study, Short CoT prompting averages 21.9% compression but reduces MathQA-Python pass@1 from 63.7% to 55.6%, an 8.1-point loss. The authors suggest the prompt may suppress necessary intermediate reasoning.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and the tested generic conciseness instruction.

ideas.title: SEER evaluation uses one fine-tuned base model
ideas.statement: Although the motivating study covers multiple models, the SEER training comparisons rely on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, so some improvements may depend on that architecture. The authors cite consistent settings and ablations as mitigation, but these do not establish generality across model families.
ideas.conditions: Distinguishes broad initial diagnostic study from one-model SEER intervention.

ideas.title: Complexity-aware token budgeting
ideas.statement: The paper describes Token-Budget [10] as a token-budget-aware reasoning framework that dynamically adjusts reasoning length according to estimated problem complexity.

ideas.title: Prompt-compression efficiency limits in related work
ideas.statement: The related-work section says Token Complexity [17] analyzes prompt-compression strategies and argues that many operate far from theoretical efficiency limits; this paper does not reproduce the underlying theorem or bounds.

ideas.title: TokenSkip adjustable token skipping
ideas.statement: TokenSkip fine-tunes a model to skip less important CoT tokens while retaining key tokens, enabling compressed reasoning with adjustable ratios.

ideas.title: Token-level compression can disrupt executable code
ideas.statement: The authors attribute TokenSkip MathQA-Python pass@1 near 1% at both tested ratios to compression that ignores code structure and produces unexecutable code. They also report output expansion and reduced accuracy for aggressive TokenSkip on Defect-Detection.
ideas.conditions: Observed baseline implementation/settings in this study; not a universal result for all TokenSkip configurations.

ideas.title: Grounded 3D-LLM noun phrase referent tokens
ideas.statement: Grounded 3D-LLM [12] is described as introducing noun phrase tokens that reference 3D scenes and enable processing of mixed 3D-textual data sequences.

ideas.title: Three task-specific training and test datasets
ideas.statement: SEER and all baselines use predefined train/test splits of MathQA-Python (generate executable Python for math problems), CodeXGLUE-Defect-Detection (binary defect/vulnerability prediction) and Code-Search-WebQuery (judge whether code satisfies a natural-language query), with in-domain evaluation on each test set.
ideas.conditions: Three software-engineering task formats; MathQA-Python is a code-generation benchmark involving mathematical questions.

ideas.title: Transfer after Defect-Detection fine-tuning
ideas.statement: SEER fine-tuned on Defect-Detection obtains HumanEval accuracy 82.9% with 3,090 average CoT tokens and MBPP accuracy 74.3% with 2,106 tokens. Figure 4 base values are 78.0%/4,100 on HumanEval and 73.5%/2,459 on MBPP, so both metrics improve in each evaluation.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; HumanEval and MBPP excluded from fine-tuning; maximum tokens 16,384.

ideas.title: Transfer after MathQA-Python fine-tuning
ideas.statement: SEER fine-tuned on MathQA-Python obtains HumanEval accuracy 86.0% with 2,396 average CoT tokens and MBPP accuracy 75.7% with 1,679 tokens. Figure 4 base values are 78.0%/4,100 on HumanEval and 73.5%/2,459 on MBPP, so both metrics improve in each evaluation.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; HumanEval and MBPP excluded from fine-tuning; maximum tokens 16,384.

ideas.title: Transfer after Code-Search fine-tuning
ideas.statement: SEER fine-tuned on Code-Search obtains HumanEval accuracy 87.8% with 2,403 average CoT tokens and MBPP accuracy 74.3% with 1,792 tokens. Figure 4 base values are 78.0%/4,100 on HumanEval and 73.5%/2,459 on MBPP, so both metrics improve in each evaluation.
ideas.conditions: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B; HumanEval and MBPP excluded from fine-tuning; maximum tokens 16,384.

ideas.title: Most truncations trigger the strict loop detector
ideas.statement: Across the tested models and code-generation datasets, 236 of 261 truncated responses (90.4%) meet the 30-gram/20-repetition loop criterion. Manual examination of remaining truncations found weaker loop-like patterns, suggesting undercounting by the strict detector.
ideas.conditions: Only truncated outputs; does not establish that every long output loops.

ideas.title: Uncertainty-triggered CoT for code generation
ideas.statement: The related-work section describes UnCert-CoT [46] as estimating uncertainty to decide when to invoke CoT and avoid unnecessary reasoning.

ideas.title: Decode received seed to latent feature and then image
ideas.statement: The UE compression decoder recovers a latent feature and the image decoder maps it to the generated image. Equations (4)-(5) print s_hat=C_psi^-1(x_hat,fc) and I_g=D_beta(C_psi^-1(s,fc),fd); the clearer later description is I_g=D(z_hat).
validity_flags: Source notation inconsistent: s elsewhere denotes text prompt, whereas decoder output should be latent feature; received y/x_hat conventions are not reconciled.

ideas.title: Centralized request-generate-download service
ideas.statement: The conventional service receives a user generation request, completes generation on a server, and downlinks the generated product. Repeated unsatisfactory generations increase network traffic, particularly for high-definition images and video.

ideas.title: A complete seed spans multiple fading coherence blocks
ideas.statement: The compression decoder requires the whole seed as one code block, but transmitting it may span multiple or dozens of channel-coherence blocks. Equation (28) models per-slot reception y_t=h_t x_t+n; unequal residual corruption across seed portions after equalization can harm decoding and image quality.

ideas.title: Chronological unseen-text evaluation
ideas.statement: The authors use January–April 2024 arXiv abstracts for evaluation and pre-July-2023 abstracts for training, arguing that this places test texts after LLaMA-3 knowledge cutoff and outside compressor training. Extractive QA uses context-span target answers to quantify information retention.
validity_flags: Temporal separation is based on stated training cutoff; it does not independently prove absence of prior overlapping content or eliminate all model knowledge.

ideas.title: LoRA encoder transfers per-layer compressed-token KV states
ideas.statement: 500xCompressor uses an autoencoder-like architecture comparable to ICAE: its encoder is the frozen base LLM plus trainable LoRA parameters and its decoder is the original frozen LLM. Given text T=(t1,…,tl) followed by compressed tokens C=(c1,…,ck), attention produces compressed-token keys and values H_C at every layer, which are passed to the decoder.

ideas.title: Teacher-forced reconstruction loss
ideas.statement: Pretraining minimizes L_P = −sum_{i=1}^{l} log P(t_i | H_C,[BOS],t_{1:i−1}; Θ_LLM,Θ_LoRA), with teacher forcing on the original text. H_C and BOS condition reconstruction, EOS marks stopping, and gradients train the encoder LoRA parameters while the base LLM remains frozen.
ideas.conditions: Pretraining stage; EOS is a stopping marker though not explicitly included in the displayed l-token sum.

ideas.title: A generation seed is an encoded latent feature
ideas.statement: The ES infers an encoded feature containing the information needed for final generation, downlinks this seed over a noisy wireless link, and the UE decodes it and generates the displayed image. The seed is not simply a random-number-generator seed.

ideas.title: Answer-token cross-entropy for instruction finetuning
ideas.statement: Instruction finetuning minimizes L_F = −sum_{j=1}^{n} log P(a_j | H_C,q_{1:m},a_{1:j−1}; Θ_LLM,Θ_LoRA), using question and answer tokens instead of the reconstructed original text. Only encoder LoRA is adapted; no new decoder parameters are added.
validity_flags: Frozen decoder parameters rule out new decoder-weight storage during this training, not every form of data leakage; the source overstates this as ensuring no leakage.

ideas.title: KV interface and standard BOS distinguish 500xCompressor from ICAE
ideas.statement: ICAE supplies compressed-token embeddings to its decoder, while 500xCompressor supplies compressed-token KV values across layers. 500xCompressor reuses BOS to trigger text reconstruction, whereas ICAE introduces a trainable token.
ideas.conditions: Authors claim greater information capacity and small GPU-memory impact; this v1 PDF does not quantify or benchmark the KV-versus-embedding GPU-memory tradeoff, including in Discussion.
validity_flags: Small GPU-memory impact is an author assertion, not a measured memory result; no memory-size formula or quantified KV-versus-embedding memory comparison is provided in this v1 PDF.

ideas.title: Frozen inference with reconstruction or question conditioning
ideas.statement: At prediction time both encoder and decoder are frozen. Reconstruction chooses t̂_i = argmax_ti P(t_i | H_C,[BOS],t_{1:i−1}; Θ_LLM), and QA chooses â_j = argmax_aj P(a_j | H_C,q_{1:m},a_{1:j−1}; Θ_LLM).

ideas.title: Chronological arXiv abstract corpus
ideas.statement: Arxiv Corpus consists of arXiv abstracts available before April 2024, with papers before July 2023 used for training and after January 2024 for development/test. Regeneration test groups are formed from abstracts with at least 96, 192, 288, 384, and 480 tokens.
ideas.conditions: Source wording uses before April and after January; Appendix Table 4 summarizes evaluation dates as Jan–Apr 2024.

ideas.title: Synthetic extractive ArxivQA construction
ideas.statement: LLaMA-3-70b-chat generates five extractive question-answer pairs per 96-token abstract, with count increasing proportionally to abstract length. Each record contains context, question, and a context-span answer. Train/development QA derives from Arxiv Corpus training abstracts; test QA derives from test abstracts.
validity_flags: Synthetic QA generator quality is asserted by the authors, without a reported human-validation guarantee.

ideas.title: Zero-shot and instructed full-context reference systems
ideas.statement: The study calls two uncompressed-input conditions gold standards: zero-shot full context gives the entire text without task instruction, while instructed full context includes instructions guiding extractive QA.
ideas.conditions: Gold here refers to comparison systems, not perfect answer accuracy; the source also evaluates generated answers against dataset targets.

ideas.title: Extractive QA metrics
ideas.statement: Extractive QA is evaluated with answer F1 (harmonic mean of precision and recall) and exact match (EM), which requires the predicted answer to match the target answer exactly.

ideas.title: Regeneration performance across compression settings
ideas.statement: With LLaMA-3-8b-chat, the authors compress 96, 192, 288, 384 and 480 input tokens into 1, 4 or 16 tokens (6x–480x token compression). Figure 3 averages results for each compressed-token count. Reported 500xCompressor advantages over ICAE are 12.18–18.96 in ROUGE-L F and 12.41–26.50 in BLEU when expressed on a 0–100 score scale.
validity_flags: Source labels score differences with percent signs; treated as score-point differences given 0–1 plot axes, not relative percent gains.
No uncertainty bars or statistical significance test are shown.

ideas.title: Information loss grows more sharply near one token
ideas.statement: Both 500xCompressor and ICAE show a larger per-token regeneration-score change between one and four compressed tokens than between four and sixteen; more aggressive compression loses lexical reconstruction quality.
ideas.conditions: Observed in the sampled compressed-token counts, not a proven universal scaling law.

ideas.title: ArxivQA performance advantage under compression
ideas.statement: For LLaMA-3-8b-chat answering ArxivQA from 96–480 token contexts compressed to 1,4,16 tokens, 500xCompressor improves over ICAE by reported F1 differences 2.06–9.23 and EM differences 0.56–7.20 on a 0–100 scale. ICAE degrades faster as token count falls.
ideas.conditions: Apparent unresolved source inconsistency: Figure 3’s rightmost ArxivQA EM panel places the one-token 500xCompressor and ICAE points at approximately 0.065 and 0.025 (roughly 6.5 and 2.5 on a 0–100 scale), whereas Table 2 prints 10.60 and 3.40 (0.1060 and 0.0340 on the plot scale) and a 7.20-point advantage, also reported in the prose. Four- and sixteen-token plotted EM values broadly agree with Table 2. These are approximate visual readings, not exact digitized values. The paper does not explain different averaging populations or otherwise reconcile the one-token values; neither source is silently corrected.
validity_flags: Source percent notation is treated as reported score-point differences rather than validated relative gains; the one-token plotted EM values do not reproduce the table/prose difference.

Apparent unresolved source inconsistency: Figure 3’s rightmost ArxivQA EM panel places the one-token 500xCompressor and ICAE points at approximately 0.065 and 0.025 (roughly 6.5 and 2.5 on a 0–100 scale), whereas Table 2 prints 10.60 and 3.40 (0.1060 and 0.0340 on the plot scale) and a 7.20-point advantage, also reported in the prose. Four- and sixteen-token plotted EM values broadly agree with Table 2. These are approximate visual readings, not exact digitized values. The paper does not explain different averaging populations or otherwise reconcile the one-token values; neither source is silently corrected.

ideas.title: Reconstruction errors need not predict QA errors
ideas.statement: In the Table 1 example, reconstruction and QA errors differ: 500xCompressor reconstructs “of a logarithmic de Rham-Witt” but omits it in a QA answer; it reconstructs “Kato modules” rather than “Kato complexes” yet returns “complexes” correctly in QA. Thus lexical reconstruction mistakes need not occur in the answer and vice versa.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative example only; does not quantify a general correlation.

ideas.title: Qualitative reconstruction and QA error categories
ideas.statement: Table 1 compares a 96-token technical abstract compressed to four tokens by each method. It annotates incorrect text (red), missing information (yellow italic), hallucinated text (blue), and paraphrases (green). 500xCompressor makes fewer illustrated errors than ICAE but still substitutes technical terms such as “cycle,” “modules,” and “complexes” in reconstruction, and produces incorrect or incomplete QA answers.
ideas.conditions: One illustrative technical abstract; 96→4 tokens (24x compression).
validity_flags: Single qualitative case, not population error rates.

ideas.title: Transfer to four QA task families
ideas.statement: Although trained on ArxivQA, 500xCompressor is evaluated on SQuAD, RE, HotpotQA and RACE. At the one-token setting it exceeds ICAE on all five benchmarks in F1 and EM, with the largest F1 gain being 18.62 points for RE. Advantages are mixed at four and sixteen tokens, so dominance is not uniform across all settings.
ideas.conditions: LLaMA-3-8b-chat; contexts up to about 500 tokens; values use Table 2 score units.

ideas.title: Some QA scores improve when reducing four tokens to one
ideas.statement: From four to one compressed token, 500xCompressor HotpotQA F1/EM rises from 36.86/19.69 to 37.47/21.13. RACE F1 rises from 21.49 to 21.75, but RACE EM declines from 7.86 to 7.56. Thus the prose statement that performance improves is metric-dependent.
ideas.conditions: Reported point estimates; no significance or run-to-run variation is supplied.

ideas.title: ArxivQA quantitative QA results
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports ArxivQA F1/EM on a 0–100 scale. With 16, 4 and 1 compressed tokens, respectively, 500xCompressor gives 40.77/14.00, 38.30/10.64, 29.73/10.60; ICAE gives 38.70/13.44, 33.31/7.54, 20.50/3.40. Full-context zero-shot is 28.41/0.04, and instructed full context is 55.90/13.74. Table 5 normalizes instructed full context to 100/100 per benchmark. For ArxivQA, normalized F1/EM at 16,4,1 compressed tokens is 72.93/101.00, 68.51/77.43, 53.18/77.14 for 500xCompressor and 69.23/97.81, 59.58/54.87, 36.67/24.74 for ICAE; zero-shot is 50.82/0.29.
ideas.conditions: Both methods are pretrained on Arxiv Corpus and finetuned on ArxivQA; downstream LLaMA-3-8b-chat decoder is frozen. Nominal 500→k labels summarize varied input lengths. Apparent unresolved source inconsistency: Figure 3’s rightmost ArxivQA EM panel places the one-token 500xCompressor and ICAE points at approximately 0.065 and 0.025 (roughly 6.5 and 2.5 on a 0–100 scale), whereas Table 2 prints 10.60 and 3.40 (0.1060 and 0.0340 on the plot scale) and a 7.20-point advantage, also reported in the prose. Four- and sixteen-token plotted EM values broadly agree with Table 2. These are approximate visual readings, not exact digitized values. The paper does not explain different averaging populations or otherwise reconcile the one-token values; neither source is silently corrected. The separate Table 5 sixteen-token normalized EM conflict (printed 101 versus approximately 101.89 from 14.00/13.74) is also retained.
validity_flags: Point estimates only; no uncertainty or repeated-run variation reported.

Table 5 prints 101 for 16-token ArxivQA normalized EM, but Table 2 ratio 14.00/13.74 implies approximately 101.89, and Table 5 delta 4.07 plus ICAE 97.81 implies 101.88. The printed cell is preserved.

Apparent unresolved source inconsistency: Figure 3’s rightmost ArxivQA EM panel places the one-token 500xCompressor and ICAE points at approximately 0.065 and 0.025 (roughly 6.5 and 2.5 on a 0–100 scale), whereas Table 2 prints 10.60 and 3.40 (0.1060 and 0.0340 on the plot scale) and a 7.20-point advantage, also reported in the prose. Four- and sixteen-token plotted EM values broadly agree with Table 2. These are approximate visual readings, not exact digitized values. The paper does not explain different averaging populations or otherwise reconcile the one-token values; neither source is silently corrected.

ideas.title: SQuAD quantitative QA results
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports SQuAD F1/EM on a 0–100 scale. With 16, 4 and 1 compressed tokens, respectively, 500xCompressor gives 50.01/28.59, 49.66/27.54, 42.86/22.75; ICAE gives 51.94/30.37, 47.48/26.49, 27.20/10.66. Full-context zero-shot is 29.95/1.02, and instructed full context is 70.65/36.79. Table 5 normalizes instructed full context to 100/100 per benchmark. For SQuAD, normalized F1/EM at 16,4,1 compressed tokens is 70.79/77.70, 70.29/74.87, 60.66/61.84 for 500xCompressor and 73.51/82.56, 67.21/71.99, 38.50/28.97 for ICAE; zero-shot is 42.39/2.77.
ideas.conditions: Both methods are pretrained on Arxiv Corpus and finetuned on ArxivQA; downstream LLaMA-3-8b-chat decoder is frozen. Nominal 500→k labels summarize varied input lengths.
validity_flags: Point estimates only; no uncertainty or repeated-run variation reported.

ideas.title: RE quantitative QA results
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports RE F1/EM on a 0–100 scale. With 16, 4 and 1 compressed tokens, respectively, 500xCompressor gives 68.73/50.44, 63.72/45.69, 63.09/45.31; ICAE gives 65.94/44.64, 67.28/50.91, 44.46/27.10. Full-context zero-shot is 25.75/1.39, and instructed full context is 71.36/53.15. Table 5 normalizes instructed full context to 100/100 per benchmark. For RE, normalized F1/EM at 16,4,1 compressed tokens is 96.31/94.89, 89.29/85.96, 88.40/85.25 for 500xCompressor and 92.40/83.98, 94.28/95.78, 62.30/50.98 for ICAE; zero-shot is 36.08/2.61.
ideas.conditions: Both methods are pretrained on Arxiv Corpus and finetuned on ArxivQA; downstream LLaMA-3-8b-chat decoder is frozen. Nominal 500→k labels summarize varied input lengths.
validity_flags: Point estimates only; no uncertainty or repeated-run variation reported.

ideas.title: HotpotQA quantitative QA results
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports HotpotQA F1/EM on a 0–100 scale. With 16, 4 and 1 compressed tokens, respectively, 500xCompressor gives 41.68/22.99, 36.86/19.69, 37.47/21.13; ICAE gives 42.11/24.57, 40.39/23.75, 22.44/9.38. Full-context zero-shot is 29.32/3.42, and instructed full context is 69.37/43.19. Table 5 normalizes instructed full context to 100/100 per benchmark. For HotpotQA, normalized F1/EM at 16,4,1 compressed tokens is 60.09/53.23, 53.13/45.58, 54.01/48.92 for 500xCompressor and 60.70/56.88, 58.23/55.00, 32.35/21.73 for ICAE; zero-shot is 42.27/7.92.
ideas.conditions: Both methods are pretrained on Arxiv Corpus and finetuned on ArxivQA; downstream LLaMA-3-8b-chat decoder is frozen. Nominal 500→k labels summarize varied input lengths.
validity_flags: Point estimates only; no uncertainty or repeated-run variation reported.

ideas.title: RACE quantitative QA results
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports RACE F1/EM on a 0–100 scale. With 16, 4 and 1 compressed tokens, respectively, 500xCompressor gives 35.42/10.97, 21.49/7.86, 21.75/7.56; ICAE gives 23.69/9.49, 20.06/6.82, 13.71/4.16. Full-context zero-shot is 15.31/0.59, and instructed full context is 39.52/13.94. The printed 35.42 for 500xCompressor at 16 tokens conflicts with the printed +1.73 difference over 23.69 and overall average 45.32, both consistent with 25.42; Appendix Table 5 likewise reports 64.34% of the 39.52 instructed baseline, approximately 25.43. Table 5 normalizes instructed full context to 100/100 per benchmark. For RACE, normalized F1/EM at 16,4,1 compressed tokens is 64.34/78.72, 54.38/56.38, 55.03/54.25 for 500xCompressor and 59.95/68.08, 50.75/48.93, 34.70/29.83 for ICAE; zero-shot is 38.74/4.25.
ideas.conditions: Both methods are pretrained on Arxiv Corpus and finetuned on ArxivQA; downstream LLaMA-3-8b-chat decoder is frozen. Nominal 500→k labels summarize varied input lengths.
validity_flags: Point estimates only; no uncertainty or repeated-run variation reported.
Internal source inconsistency: RACE 16-token F1 cell differs from its delta, average, and normalized value; no silent correction applied.

ideas.title: Average raw QA scores
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports average F1/EM as 45.32/25.40, 42.00/22.28 and 38.98/21.47 for 500xCompressor at 16,4,1 tokens; ICAE averages are 44.48/24.50, 41.70/23.10 and 25.66/10.94. Full-context zero-shot average is 25.75/1.29 and instructed average 61.36/32.16. At four tokens ICAE has the higher average EM despite lower average F1.
validity_flags: The 500xCompressor 16-token F1 average is incompatible with the printed RACE 35.42 cell; it is compatible with 25.42 instead.

ideas.title: Longer input contexts generally reduce reconstruction and QA scores
ideas.statement: Figure 4 varies context length 96,192,288,384,480 at fixed compressed-token counts 16,4,1, corresponding to ratios 6–30,24–120,96–480. Reconstruction ROUGE-L F generally decreases with length; 16-token 500xCompressor falls from nearly 1 at length 96 to about .50 at 480, where it converges with ICAE. Four- and one-token KV compression remain above ICAE over the plotted lengths. QA F1 mostly declines with length but has a slight 384→480 rise in the 16- and 1-token curves.
validity_flags: Visual approximate trend; no numerical table or uncertainty bars for the individual plotted points.

ideas.title: Analogy to prompt tuning and prefix tuning
ideas.statement: The authors compare ICAE embedding compression to Prompt Tuning and 500xCompressor per-layer KV compression to Prefix Tuning. Whereas those tuning methods encode task instructions in learned prefixes, these compressors aim to encode fine-grained input-context information as well.
ideas.conditions: Conceptual analogy with cited background methods; not an assertion that the compression models perform the same optimization.

ideas.title: Memory, modality and language interpretations of compressed prompts
ideas.statement: The discussion presents three interpretations: ICAE-like compressed tokens as memory slots (Ge et al.); compression as modality fusion with natural language (Cheng et al.); and compressed prompts as a new LLM language (Jiang et al.). The authors relate their own reconstruction, QA transfer and unseen-text handling to encoding, transmission and adaptation properties of language.
validity_flags: Conceptual framing rather than a formal proof that the representation constitutes a language.

ideas.title: Inference speed is not benchmarked
ideas.statement: The authors assert that 500xCompressor and ICAE should have similar computational savings at an equal number of compressed tokens, and explicitly do not analyze inference-speed improvements.
validity_flags: No measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or compression amortization analysis.

ideas.title: Background: prompt-specific KL compression
ideas.statement: The paper describes Wingate et al. (2022) as optimizing KL divergence between responses generated from original and compressed prompts, with new training required for every new prompt.

ideas.title: Background: paragraph, agent and retrieval compression
ideas.statement: The related-work overview cites sentinel-token paragraph compression (Ren et al.), agent compression (Jiang et al. 2024), and the RAG approaches xRAG (Cheng et al.) and COCOM (Rau et al.) as other applications of soft compressed representations.

ideas.title: Background: functional soft tokens need not retain detailed context
ideas.statement: The authors distinguish context-preserving compression from special prompts used for functions: Todd et al. function vectors support tasks such as antonyms or translation, while Shen et al. use special tokens for domain-specific performance.

ideas.title: Broader training and additional downstream applications
ideas.statement: The authors propose scaling training-corpus size and diversity beyond the relatively small arXiv and QA training data and investigating in-context learning, reasoning, personalized LLMs, RAG and role-playing.
ideas.conditions: Future work; these applications and scaling benefits are proposed rather than validated by the reported experiments.

ideas.title: Reported additional parameter fraction
ideas.statement: The PDF abstract reports approximately 0.25% additional parameters for 500xCompressor.
ideas.conditions: This v1 PDF says 0.25%; the imported arXiv metadata abstract says approximately 0.3%. The PDF does not break down the parameter count or report a corresponding memory benchmark.
validity_flags: PDF/metadata rounding discrepancy; no detailed parameter-count derivation in source.

ideas.title: Reported release of code, data, models and demo
ideas.statement: The authors state that code, datasets, models and a demo are released at https://github.com/ZongqianLi/500xCompressor.
ideas.conditions: Availability claim in paper; repository contents are not independently audited in this extraction.

ideas.title: Shared training hyperparameters and token-count schedules
ideas.statement: Table 3 gives settings for both 500xCompressor and ICAE. For 16,4,1 compressed tokens, pretraining runs 42,000,66,600,103,800 steps, respectively, with learning rate 1e−4; finetuning runs 20,000,15,000,10,000 steps, respectively, with learning rate 5e−5. All six configurations use 300 warm-up steps, batch size 4 and AdamW.
validity_flags: Training compute is not held fixed across compressed-token counts; LoRA rank and detailed parameter/memory accounting are not reported here.

ideas.title: Lower reconstruction evaluation losses for KV compression
ideas.statement: Figure 5 shows 500xCompressor with lower pretraining evaluation loss than ICAE throughout the displayed trajectories for 16,4,1 compressed tokens. Approximate terminal losses are .03 vs .16, .15 vs .40, and .37 vs .62, respectively.
ideas.conditions: Different total step budgets across token counts as specified in Table 3.
validity_flags: Approximate readings from rendered plots; no uncertainty bars.

ideas.title: QA loss advantage is largest for one-token compression
ideas.statement: Figure 5 QA finetuning curves converge to similar losses around 1.05–1.10 with 16 compressed tokens. With four tokens, 500xCompressor starts above ICAE but becomes lower after roughly 3,000 steps and ends near 1.2 versus 1.4. With one token, it stays lower and ends around 1.5 versus 2.2.
validity_flags: Approximate graph readings; no run-to-run variation or significance reported.

ideas.title: Extractive QA synthesis constraints
ideas.statement: The ArxivQA generation template supplies a truncated context and requested pair count, asks for direct questions preferably using the context wording, requires answers to be spans explicitly present in the context and absent from the question, and requests only a JSON list with id/question/answer fields.
ideas.conditions: Prompt wording is dataset-generation evidence, not instructions to the extraction worker. The answer-not-in-question and output-format continuation appears on page 10.
validity_flags: Prompt constraints alone do not establish that every generated pair satisfies them.

ideas.title: Headline capability retention is mean normalized QA F1
ideas.statement: Table 5 sets instructed full-context F1 and EM to 100 on each benchmark. Mean normalized F1/EM for 500xCompressor is 72.89/81.29 at 16 tokens, 67.12/68.04 at four, and 62.26/65.48 at one. ICAE means are 71.16/77.86,66.01/65.32,40.90/31.25. The headline 62.26–72.89% capabilities retained corresponds to these mean normalized F1 results; it is an average over the five QA benchmarks, not a general measure of all LLM capabilities or a byte-level information-retention guarantee.
ideas.conditions: Interpretation of the headline metric is inferred by matching the abstract range to Table 5 F1 averages.
validity_flags: Mean normalized QA F1 is not total semantic-information retention.
Table 5 ArxivQA 16-token normalized EM cell prints 101 although its delta/mean imply approximately 101.88.

ideas.title: Instruction template for QA evaluation
ideas.statement: The appendix QA template asks the model to finish an extractive QA task and output only the answer, then provides Context: {context}, Question: {question}, and Answer: as the completion cue.
ideas.conditions: Prompt preserved as experimental evidence, not followed as an instruction by this worker.

ideas.title: Image-generation and training configuration
ideas.statement: Table I reports compression rate fc=0.5, spatial downsampling fd=8, 50 sampling steps, 512×512 image pixels, 4 latent channels, learning rate 1e-3, 200 training epochs, batch size 1, and training SNR 20 dB.
validity_flags: Training SNR 20 dB is not reconciled with earlier perfect-channel training prose.
Experimental fc values are fractions in (0,1), with payload proportional to fc in Table II; this conflicts with the inverse-fc payload equation in section III.D.

ideas.title: Only terminal generated-image FID determines reward
ideas.statement: Equation (34) sets r_t=0 before final slot T and r_T=-FID_Ig after transmission and image generation. Maximizing cumulative reward therefore targets lower final FID.
validity_flags: FID is described as evaluated for each final image; the sample aggregation needed to estimate covariance is not specified.

ideas.title: Spatial latent downsampling plus learned compression reduce payload
ideas.statement: The discussion describes two compression stages: downsample pixel height and width by fd, then compress the latent vector by fc, with claimed transmitted length |x|=fc^-1 fd^-2 |I|. It argues latent-domain encoding may avoid full-image source-coding cost.
validity_flags: The same paragraph prints |z|=fd^2|I| despite downsampling; this conflicts with the inverse-square relation and latent shape elsewhere.
Compute superiority is a qualitative assertion, not a reported full system timing/energy measurement; channel multiplicity omitted from size equation.

ideas.title: Point-to-point seed transmission channel
ideas.statement: Equation (3) models the received seed as y=h x+n, where h is the fading channel and n is additive noise. The noise is additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN).

ideas.title: Nearest object centroid is the referent ground truth
ideas.statement: A visual referent’s ground-truth location is defined as the centroid of the nearest object; this assignment supplies supervision for center loss and pairwise spatial constraints.
ideas.conditions: Uses object-centroid supervision rather than treating the sampled point’s original coordinate as the target.

ideas.title: Author comparison of management systems
ideas.statement: In Table 1, ACM has all five properties. ACE has only open data; Mem1 has trainability and open data; ReSum and SUPO have compactness and trainability; ACON has compactness and open data; AgentFold has compactness, trainability and agent initiation. None of those six is classified as lossless.
ideas.conditions: Author-defined taxonomy; Appendix A gives the classification rationale.

ideas.title: Heuristic context compression operates outside agent decisions
ideas.statement: The paper groups externally invoked compressors and manually designed discard rules as heuristic compression, including fixed-timing ReSum, ACON history summaries, COMPASS Meta-Thinker contexts, DeepSeek full-history summarization/fixed-ratio truncation, and MemAgent chunkwise retained memory.

ideas.title: Teacher–student on-policy framework with dual timing constraints
ideas.statement: ACM adapts a teacher–student on-policy framework: the teacher inserts management into student rollouts without context-management tools and removes unnecessary management from rollouts with context-management tools, then the student resumes at the edited point and is trained on teacher soft supervision. Ordinary search/document tools remain available in the rollouts without context-management tools.
ideas.conditions: The authors explicitly cite Hinton et al. (2015) and Lu and Lab (2025) for the adopted framework.

ideas.title: AgentFold motivates agent-controlled folding but differs in released pipeline
ideas.statement: The authors identify AgentFold as closely related agent-driven context reduction, and position ACM as adding an openly released, efficient post-training data-generation pipeline without heavy reinforcement learning.

ideas.title: Memory-augmented context evolution and ACM scope
ideas.statement: Prior memory approaches update external state through reflection, distillation or optimization. MIPRO optimizes instructions and demonstrations, Dynamic Cheatsheet learns reusable notes, GEPA uses reflective Pareto search, ACE evolves context artifacts, and Mem1 updates compact memory. ACM is described as purely per-question compression and retrieval during reasoning.

ideas.title: Agent and environment interaction distribution
ideas.statement: For system prompt s, reasoning-plus-tool action a_t and response o_t, H_t={s,(a_1,o_1),…,(a_{t−1},o_{t−1})}; a_t~π_θ(·|H_t) and o_t~π_γ(·|H_t;a_t). Interaction ends on finish or exhaustion of the context window.
ideas.conditions: π_γ denotes the model/environment response via tool results.

ideas.title: Center loss penalizes referent coordinate error
ideas.statement: The center loss is L_center=(1/M)∑_(i=1)^M ||q_vr^(i)−q_gt^(i)||_2, averaging Euclidean coordinate error over M visual referents. The target for each referent is its nearest object centroid.
ideas.conditions: q_vr and q_gt are predicted and ground-truth coordinates; uses an unsquared L2 norm.

ideas.title: Autonomous compression and retrieval across memory segments
ideas.statement: Figure 1 contrasts ReAct hitting the window limit, a summary agent compressing at an illustrated 90% threshold and losing original messages, and ACM compressing earlier at agent-selected turns, offloading raw segments, then querying a past segment.
ideas.conditions: 90% is a diagram example; evaluated baseline threshold is specified separately in Appendix A.

ideas.title: Externally triggered summary replaces history
ideas.statement: A summary agent uses an external threshold monitor to call a_sum, obtains o_sum~π_γ(·|H_t;a_sum), discards previous messages and resumes with H′={s,o_sum}.
ideas.conditions: Generic summary-agent formulation; original raw messages are not available for retrieval.

ideas.title: manage_context summarizes and offloads raw turns
ideas.statement: manage_context takes no arguments (empty-object schema) and summarizes messages since the previous compression boundary or task start, excluding the calling message and preserving system prompt and original question. A summarizer LLM returns explored paths, reasoning and conclusions with a [summary_id: N] prefix; original messages remain in summary_{N}.json on disk, linked to the unique identifier.
ideas.conditions: Appendix B clarifies the ambiguous main-text phrase about the previous summary boundary. No additional recent-turn retention rule is specified.

ideas.title: Lossless means raw-message preservation and revisitation
ideas.statement: ACM calls its compression lossless because every removed message remains in external storage for later revisitation while working context stays short.
ideas.conditions: A storage/recoverability property, not a proof of perfect summaries or query answers.

ideas.title: Agent selects compression timing before peak pressure
ideas.statement: ACM exposes context management as an action callable during reasoning, allowing timing to follow current reasoning state and progress instead of a fixed schedule and potentially reducing peak tokens.

ideas.title: Generate student trajectories with and without management tools
ideas.statement: Phase 1 creates H+ rollouts with ACM tools and H− rollouts without them, exposing both untrained management behavior and ordinary exploration.

ideas.title: Inject management at redundant or unproductive exploration points
ideas.statement: With trajectory H−, prompt P+ and reference answer A*, the teacher identifies redundant topics, loops or sufficient accumulated context and replaces an action with a management call plus a justification.
ideas.conditions: Reference answer available to teacher; separate filters seek to avoid answer leakage.

ideas.title: Replace premature management with search, reading or an answer
ideas.statement: With H+ and P−, the teacher replaces unnecessary context calls when evidence already supports an answer or warrants further examination, using a search, document open or answer action with rationale; the student then resumes from the edited action.

ideas.title: BrowseComp-Plus accuracy, tool calls and peak context
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports (Pass@1 accuracy, average tool calls/episode, average peak tokens/episode): Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: 0.653, 15.6, 51K; Gemini3-Flash: 0.733, 22.9, 72K; ReAct Qwen3.5-9B: 0.570, 19.5, 63K; ReSum Qwen3.5-9B: 0.608, 24.7, 68K; ACON Qwen3.5-9B: 0.614, 28.2, 65K; ACE Qwen3.5-9B: 0.589, 19.8, 71K; ACM Base Qwen3.5-9B: 0.635, 30.8, 59K; ACM-Post-Trained Qwen3.5-9B: 0.727, 46.2, 54K.
ideas.conditions: Qwen3.5-9B for all framework comparisons; two frontier model references. Benchmark evaluation configuration in §5.1 and Appendix A.

ideas.title: DeepSearchQA accuracy, tool calls and peak context
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports (Pass@1 accuracy, average tool calls/episode, average peak tokens/episode): Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: 0.710, 28.3, 47K; Gemini3-Flash: 0.619, 54.3, 121K; ReAct Qwen3.5-9B: 0.367, 47.4, 46K; ReSum Qwen3.5-9B: 0.371, 48.6, 79K; ACON Qwen3.5-9B: 0.380, 51.3, 54K; ACE Qwen3.5-9B: 0.352, 48.2, 70K; ACM Base Qwen3.5-9B: 0.405, 88.7, 42K; ACM-Post-Trained Qwen3.5-9B: 0.425, 58.8, 41K.
ideas.conditions: Qwen3.5-9B for all framework comparisons; two frontier model references. Benchmark evaluation configuration in §5.1 and Appendix A.

ideas.title: SWE-Bench Verified accuracy, tool calls and peak context
ideas.statement: Table 2 reports (Pass@1 accuracy, average tool calls/episode, average peak tokens/episode): Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: 0.682, 58.9, 38K; Gemini3-Flash: 0.732, 66.7, 80K; ReAct Qwen3.5-9B: 0.489, 74.7, 59K; ReSum Qwen3.5-9B: 0.475, 75.2, 61K; ACON Qwen3.5-9B: 0.480, 76.1, 57K; ACE Qwen3.5-9B: 0.494, 75.6, 65K; ACM Base Qwen3.5-9B: 0.508, 77.6, 46K; ACM-Post-Trained Qwen3.5-9B: 0.530, 79.3, 50K.
ideas.conditions: Qwen3.5-9B for all framework comparisons; two frontier model references. Benchmark evaluation configuration in §5.1 and Appendix A.

ideas.title: Top-20 teacher cross-entropy on student assistant tokens
ideas.statement: L_ACM(θ)=−E_{τ~πθ}[Σ_{t∈T_a(τ)}Σ_{v∈V}p_T(v|s;h_<t) log πθ(v|s;h_<t)]. V is the teacher top-K candidate set with K=20; p_T is restricted and renormalized over V. Loss covers all student-generated assistant tokens, with system, user and tool-output tokens masked.
ideas.conditions: Teacher and student from same model family; h_<t is preceding interleaved actions and observations.

ideas.title: Retain problems not solved in every student trial
ideas.statement: Rejection sampling retains trajectories where the student fails to complete all trials successfully, focusing teacher supervision on challenging problems.
ideas.conditions: Source wording does not precisely specify whether all trajectories of qualifying problems or only failed individual trajectories are retained.

ideas.title: Filter teacher rationales for reference-answer leakage
ideas.statement: Content filters require teacher rationales to cite observable redundant queries, cyclic exploration or sufficient evidence instead of revealing the target answer, to teach timing patterns rather than answer-dependent cues.
ideas.conditions: The teacher itself sees A*; paper does not quantify leakage-filter performance.

ideas.title: Mix original student rollouts with teacher-annotated data
ideas.statement: To stabilize training, ACM resamples trajectories from original student rollouts, analogous to self-distillation, and mixes them with teacher-edited data.
ideas.conditions: Mix ratio unspecified in the paper.

ideas.title: Three long-horizon benchmarks with out-of-domain search evaluation
ideas.statement: BrowseComp-Plus uses 680 training and 150 evaluation examples; DeepSearchQA is exclusively out-of-domain evaluation using live web search; SWE-Gym supplies training for SWE-Bench Verified.
ideas.conditions: Simple tasks are argued to rarely need context management because they finish before substantial pressure.

ideas.title: Student, helper models and teacher training configuration
ideas.statement: Qwen3.5-9B supplies student rollouts, summarization and querying; Qwen3.5-397B-A17B is teacher. The authors run on-policy distillation for three epochs and release four rollout trials and teacher annotations from each epoch.
ideas.conditions: Chosen student scale intended to generate long coherent trajectories; Appendix D compares a smaller thinking model.

ideas.title: BrowseComp-Plus teacher-distillation ablation
ideas.statement: For Qwen3.5-9B under ACM, Table 3 gives (Pass@1, average tool calls, average peak tokens): Base ACM: 0.635, 30.8, 59K; GPT5.5 Distill: 0.623, 26.4, 62K; ACM training: 0.727, 46.2, 54K; Both: 0.734, 37.6, 59K.
ideas.conditions: Compare GPT-5.5 successful-trajectory distillation, ACM synthesized management data, and both.

ideas.title: DeepSearchQA teacher-distillation ablation
ideas.statement: For Qwen3.5-9B under ACM, Table 3 gives (Pass@1, average tool calls, average peak tokens): Base ACM: 0.405, 88.7, 42K; GPT5.5 Distill: 0.381, 49.6, 53K; ACM training: 0.425, 58.8, 41K; Both: 0.413, 62.5, 50K.
ideas.conditions: Compare GPT-5.5 successful-trajectory distillation, ACM synthesized management data, and both.

ideas.title: SWE-Bench Verified teacher-distillation ablation
ideas.statement: For Qwen3.5-9B under ACM, Table 3 gives (Pass@1, average tool calls, average peak tokens): Base ACM: 0.508, 77.6, 46K; GPT5.5 Distill: 0.542, 58.3, 45K; ACM training: 0.530, 79.3, 50K; Both: 0.564, 88.1, 57K.
ideas.conditions: Compare GPT-5.5 successful-trajectory distillation, ACM synthesized management data, and both.

ideas.title: Post-training improves accuracy over ReAct across three tasks
ideas.statement: The paper reports approximately 27%, 16% and 8% relative improvements for BrowseComp-Plus, DeepSearchQA and SWE-Bench Verified. Table 2 gives 0.570→0.727, 0.367→0.425 and 0.489→0.530 respectively.
ideas.conditions: Relative percentages, not percentage-point gains; benchmark-specific configurations.

ideas.title: ACM produces proactive sawtooth context trajectories
ideas.statement: Figure 3 shows individual ACM trajectories dropping at management calls before the 128K cap and a slower population-average context increase than ReAct, supporting longer interaction horizons.
ideas.conditions: BrowseComp-Plus trajectories; qualitative visual interpretation, approximate curve readings.

ideas.title: Post-training increases management, retrieval and search calls
ideas.statement: Figure 4 reports average search/get_document/manage_context/query_memory calls: GPT-5.5 ACM 18.9/4.2/0.1/0.0; base Qwen3.5-9B ACM 24.9/4.1/2.1/0.6; post-trained Qwen3.5-9B ACM 28.7/6.5/6.8/1.3.
ideas.conditions: BrowseComp-Plus; GPT-5.5 n=1×150, each Qwen condition n=4×150. Error bars shown, but their definition is not stated in caption.

ideas.title: Strong teachers may rarely demonstrate context management
ideas.statement: Because GPT-5.5 rarely calls management or retrieval on this benchmark, the authors argue that teacher-only distillation may offer too few management behaviors and favor curated student trajectories.
ideas.conditions: Inferred from these tasks/tool frequencies, not a universal inability of strong models.

ideas.title: Tool use correlates with accuracy and reduced peak context is argued to lower KV load
ideas.statement: The authors observe positive association between tool calls and Pass@1 for smaller agents, and infer that reduced context pressure lowers reasoning burden and server KV-cache overhead.
ideas.conditions: Not a controlled tool-budget or measured memory/latency study; total compute including helper LLMs is not quantified.

ideas.title: Pass@4 proxies capability and Pass^4 proxies consistency
ideas.statement: The paper evaluates K=4 repeated trials, interpreting Pass@4 as the capability boundary and Pass^4 as consistent success across independent trials, alongside average Pass@1.
ideas.conditions: Operational interpretation of repeated-sampling metrics; exact estimator formulas are not specified.

ideas.title: Four-trial performance improves over three ACM epochs
ideas.statement: Figure 5 reports (Pass@4, average Pass@1, Pass^4) percentages: ReAct 73.5/57.0/34.1; ACM Base 78.8/63.5/44.0; post-training epoch 1 80.0/67.7/50.7; epoch 2 82.0/69.8/56.0; epoch 3 82.0/72.7/59.3.
ideas.conditions: Qwen3.5-9B on BrowseComp-Plus; authors emphasize consistency gains larger than capability-boundary gains.

ideas.title: A successful multi-hop case traverses 222K raw tokens with a 98K plotted working peak
ideas.statement: On BCP qid 347, ACM-Post-Trained returns California Pizza Kitchen with reported 95% confidence after 83 turns, 63 searches, 9 document fetches, 7 management calls and 5 memory queries. The figure reports peak actual/raw contexts of 98K/222K, about 124K avoided; uncompressed history would pass 128K at turn 47; the base model succeeds 0/4.
ideas.conditions: Selected successful example, not average behavior; model confidence is self-report.

ideas.title: Case trace uses memory probes and incremental verification
ideas.statement: The qid347 trace compresses at turns 10 and 18, queries memory for a lead near turn49, compresses 78 messages at turn58 (raw158K versus actual2.3K), finds the dissertation at turn67 and confirms a coauthored paper near turn79 before answering at turn82.
ideas.conditions: The printed trace self-reports 114,364 input tokens at t58 versus figure peak actual98K, and mentions an81,920 limit at t18 versus configured131,072 elsewhere; preserve as model statements rather than measured counts.

ideas.title: Teacher distillation helps coding while ACM training improves all three tasks
ideas.statement: GPT-5.5 distillation alone falls below base ACM on both search tasks but raises coding accuracy; combining it with ACM training is best on BrowseComp-Plus and SWE-Bench Verified, while ACM training alone is best on DeepSearchQA.
ideas.conditions: The prose says DeepResearchQA at one point, but Table 3 and benchmark setup identify DeepSearchQA.

ideas.title: ACM presupposes sustained reasoning and tool use
ideas.statement: If the base policy fails or hallucinates within a few turns, trajectories are too short for compression to help; ACM requires a model capable of sustained long-horizon exploration.

ideas.title: Benchmark baselines are author reimplementations
ideas.statement: Because prior context-compression baselines were not evaluated on these three benchmarks, the authors reimplemented them and acknowledge possible minor differences despite attempting to follow original designs.

ideas.title: ReAct retains full history under a 128K cap
ideas.statement: The reimplemented ReAct baseline interleaves reasoning and tool calls, keeps entire history verbatim, has no compression/retrieval/external-memory primitive, and stops at final answer or the 128K context cap.

ideas.title: ReSum uses external fixed-threshold summarization
ideas.statement: The authors reimplement ReSum with original-paper threshold and summarizer-prompt recipe on Qwen3.5-9B, holding search tools, decoding parameters and 128K cap fixed; a concise paragraph replaces history with no raw retrieval.
ideas.conditions: The numeric threshold is not printed here.

ideas.title: ACON uses structured summary slots
ideas.statement: ACON replaces a past-turn window with a structured slot summary of entities, hypotheses and open questions; slots enter working memory under a heuristic context threshold, with no raw-history fetch. Authors use released slot schema and summarizer prompt on the same Qwen3.5-9B backbone.

ideas.title: ACE baseline maintains a second-LLM-edited context playbook
ideas.statement: The authors instantiate ACE’s persistent context playbook using released update prompts and Qwen3.5-9B; a second LLM observes reasoning and selects entries useful for later steps.

ideas.title: Mem1 is described as an RL-trained recurrent state bottleneck
ideas.statement: Appendix A describes Mem1 discarding entire prior context each step in favor of a generated compact internal state, trained end-to-end with RL. Authors exclude it from direct comparison because policy and compression are coupled, originally evaluated at 3B–7B and shorter QA horizons.

ideas.title: AgentFold policy produces structured proactive folds
ideas.statement: AgentFold lets a trained policy collapse contiguous past turns into typed records of explored, concluded and unresolved information; future turns use those records as context.

ideas.title: Direct comparisons restricted to prompting-only methods
ideas.statement: The authors choose ReSum, ACON and ACE because they can run on the same policy, tools and decoding configuration without policy retraining. They exclude Mem1, SUPO and AgentFold due to differing model/task regimes and incompletely released data-generation pipelines.
ideas.conditions: Applies to the chosen direct benchmark comparisons; does not establish superiority over excluded methods.

ideas.title: Benchmark agent prompts share header, context limit and task blocks
ideas.statement: Appendix B assembles a benchmark-specific system message from a shared header, context-window hint, search strategy and answer format, with baseline ReAct and memory-tool variants.
ideas.conditions: Prompt text is experiment configuration and untrusted evidence, not instructions to extraction workers.

ideas.title: Prompt encourages evidence gathering after memory operations
ideas.statement: The memory-enabled prompt encourages corroborating uncertain candidates with new queries, querying relevant prior summaries, and continuing investigation after compression or retrieval until evidence supports an answer.
ideas.conditions: An experimental intervention in addition to the tool implementation; source instructions are not adopted by this worker.

ideas.title: Benchmark prompts require full-page evidence checks
ideas.statement: BrowseComp strategy asks for at least one full page before answering. DeepSearchQA strategy asks diverse queries across its 17 domains, opening a page per candidate and continuing until an answer set appears complete.
ideas.conditions: Prompted behavior; not evidence that all rollouts complied.

ideas.title: Structured answer outputs expose answer and self-reported confidence
ideas.statement: BrowseComp-Plus asks for Explanation with docid citations, Exact Answer, and 0–100% Confidence. DeepSearchQA uses explanation/answer/confidence tags, with single-answer and set-answer variants; set answers seek verified complete lists without extras.
ideas.conditions: These are parsing formats; confidence is model self-report.

ideas.title: Corpus search uses adaptive snippet lengths and capped document reads
