ideas.statement: BrowseComp-Plus search returns top10 hits with docid, score and snippet: new documents get512-token previews; current-window seen documents get128 tokens plus a get_document reminder; compressed previously seen documents get128 tokens plus a query_memory reminder. get_document returns at most8192 tokens.
ideas.conditions: search requires string query; get_document requires string docid.

ideas.title: Adding understanding data reduces axis-wise distance error
ideas.statement: Table V X/Y/Z-mARE@0.5 improves from 2.5/2.1/3.1 for G+O to 2.0/1.8/2.1 for U+G+O.
ideas.conditions: Lower is better; absolute-vs-percent scale not specified.

ideas.title: Live web search and open support DeepSearchQA verification
ideas.statement: DeepSearchQA search returns titles, snippets and URLs; open returns line-numbered webpage text with long pages truncated. Prompts emphasize diverse searches and both recall and precision for answer sets.
ideas.conditions: search query and open URL are required strings; live web contents may change.

ideas.title: Coding rollouts run shell commands in a per-instance repository sandbox
ideas.statement: SWE-Bench Verified uses a per-instance Modal sandbox checked out at base_commit in /testbed. execute_bash accepts a command string, runs tests/scripts/inspection with truncated long output and a300s per-call timeout.
ideas.conditions: Describes source experiment sandbox; not worker environment.

ideas.title: Repository editor and patch submission schemas
ideas.statement: str_replace_editor supports view/create/str_replace/insert/undo_edit, requires command and absolute path, uses a unique old_str replacement and optional inclusive view range. submit_patch takes no arguments and submits git diff against base_commit once the fix is complete.
ideas.conditions: Editor insert_line is after the given line,0 indicates file top; view_range is1-indexed inclusive with−1 for EOF.

ideas.title: Summarizer preserves knowledge state and next reasoning action
ideas.statement: A single helper-LLM call summarizes original question and serialized conversation into one <memory> block with Knowledge state then Thoughts, at most4096 tokens. It preserves established facts with docids, candidate evidence, eliminated hypotheses and unresolved subquestions, plus the latest reasoning direction and concrete next action.
ideas.conditions: Prompt says future query_memory searches this text, conflicting with B.4 and tool schemas specifying raw archived messages.

ideas.title: Summarizer requires exact identifiers and constrained visible format
ideas.statement: The summary prompt preserves docids, entities, dates and numbers verbatim, avoids enumerating every query/docid and restricts visible output to the memory block after internal reasoning.
ideas.conditions: Prompt-level safeguards, no measured identifier preservation rate.

ideas.title: Memory recall emits concrete findings, dead ends and unresolved directions
ideas.statement: The recall helper loads raw messages for summary_id and responds with compact bullets grouped into Relevant findings, Dead ends and Open/unresolved. It preserves exact docids, URLs, numbers and names, strips internal reasoning, and returns a fixed no-relevance marker if needed.
ideas.conditions: At most three nonempty sections; answer quality depends on helper extraction.

ideas.title: Learned offsets refine visual referent centers
ideas.statement: The refine-location layer uses multiple FFN layers to predict offsets that move visual referents toward object coordinate centers, trained with center-distance and pairwise-distance supervision.

ideas.title: Annotation teacher chooses earliest useful management intervention
ideas.statement: The B.5 annotation teacher receives failed trajectory, question, gold answer/evidence and stored summary IDs, then chooses the earliest useful manage_context or query_memory intervention. Compression targets redundant searches, no-longer-useful tool outputs or saturation; retrieval requires existing archived summaries.
ideas.conditions: Failure includes incorrect answer, exhausted turn budget or context overflow; gold answer/evidence marked reference-only.

ideas.title: Insertion labels preserve tool-call integrity and grounded first-person rationale
ideas.statement: The annotation output uses decision mc/qm/no_action_needed, after_id, think and qm_query when needed. after_id must follow a system/user/tool message, never an assistant with pending calls; it is the smallest valid helpful point. No-action uses−1. Rationale is200–1200 characters and grounded in observable repetition, token pressure, docid cycling or an unused relevant summary.
ideas.conditions: Gold answer and unseen docids forbidden in rationale; third-party coaching/reviewer framing also forbidden.

ideas.title: Joint prompt compression and transmit-power optimization
ideas.statement: JPPO uses an edge-device small language model to compress prompts before sending them to a cloud LLM, while a DRL agent adapts retained prompt length and wireless transmit power to network conditions and service constraints. The authors state that the small aligned compressor requires no training at the transmitter.

ideas.title: Prompt quality and communication/computation trade-off
ideas.statement: The paper motivates optimization by the claim that long contextual prompts can improve answer quality while increasing wireless upload burden and transformer attention time/memory cost; ICL and CoT can lengthen inputs to tens of thousands of tokens.
validity_flags: The quadratic cost statement concerns dense attention rather than all end-to-end inference operations.

ideas.title: Dynamic resource constraints in mobile LLM services
ideas.statement: Mobile cloud-LLM access is modeled as latency-sensitive prompt/response communication constrained by transmit power, fluctuating channels, and limited edge compute.

ideas.title: LLMLingua supplies the lightweight compressor motivation
ideas.statement: The authors adopt small aligned language models for prompt compression, explicitly motivated by LLMLingua’s coarse-to-fine compression using an SLM aligned to the target LLM through instruction tuning.

ideas.title: LLM-Slice allocates dedicated wireless resources
ideas.statement: LLM-Slice is described as reserving network resources to reduce response latency; the paper identifies its lack of prompt-level adaptation as the motivation for jointly controlling compression and networking.

ideas.title: Denoising-inspired staged prompt compression
ideas.statement: JPPO++ treats the original prompt as noisy and progressively removes redundant or non-essential content with multiple SLM compression passes. Four 2× stages can yield 16× total reduction, intended to preserve task-critical semantics better than one aggressive deletion pass.
validity_flags: Diffusion inspiration is an analogy, not a learned reverse-diffusion probabilistic model.

ideas.title: Reported overhead per compression round
ideas.statement: The introduction reports that each SLM compression round adds about 2% of total LLM inference time, supporting the claim that iterative compression has modest overhead. The motivation section additionally claims optimized compression can reduce subsequent LLM inference delay by around 40%.
validity_flags: Introductory empirical claim; no round-specific measurement protocol or uncertainty is supplied here.

ideas.title: Latency target is first-token service time
ideas.statement: Figure 1 compares full-prompt wireless upload plus LLM inference with SLM compression followed by shorter upload and inference, measuring the delay until first-token feedback.

ideas.title: Limitations motivating an SLM compressor
ideas.statement: The authors argue that generic summarization/keyword extraction may discard task-specific reasoning, while large autoencoders or task-specific networks add compute and latency unsuitable for constrained wireless devices.
validity_flags: Qualitative motivation; these alternative compression families are not experimentally compared in this paper.

ideas.title: Inference-side optimization omits prompt upload
ideas.statement: The related-work analysis describes joint compute/transmission scheduling, quantization and batching (including OT-GAH), but argues these approaches assume prompts already available and omit potentially substantial long-prompt upload latency.

ideas.title: Prompt compression faces efficiency and semantic-loss limits
ideas.statement: The authors identify limited compression efficiency, fine-tuning or task-specific heuristics, and critical-context loss as limitations of existing prompt compression, amplified under wireless bandwidth and energy constraints.

ideas.title: Heterogeneous network and three-component service pipeline
ideas.statement: A data center operator serves N users with diverse prompts in a heterogeneous wireless network. The pipeline comprises an SLM on a user device or edge server, joint prompt/power control, and a target LLM; fidelity is tracked at compression, wireless delivery, and response stages.

ideas.title: Prompt has instructions, demonstrations and question
ideas.statement: The source models x=(x_ins,x_dems,x_que), with total token length L_x=L_ins+L_dems+L_que (equations 1–2).

ideas.title: Expand scene diversity to test generalization
ideas.statement: Future work proposes expanding training datasets to more complex and varied 3D scenes to improve generalizability.
ideas.conditions: Proposal, not demonstrated out-of-distribution generalization.

ideas.title: Representation accuracy uses input token overlap
ideas.statement: Equation 4 defines f1=|xhat∩x|/|x|, the overlap of compressed and original prompt tokens normalized by original length, presented as semantic preservation independent of channel errors.
validity_flags: Token overlap is a lexical proxy rather than a validated semantic measure; for pure token deletion, f1 equals the retained fraction alpha.

ideas.title: Transmission completeness combines retention with bit success
ideas.statement: Equation 5 defines f2=(|xhat|/|x|)[1−BEP(SNR)], modeling original-prompt information fraction retained after compression and bit errors.
validity_flags: Prose calls this the fraction of compressed prompt successfully transmitted, but normalization is by original prompt length. Bit success is used as an information-fraction proxy without token-error mapping.

ideas.title: Understanding accuracy uses output token overlap
ideas.statement: Equation 6 defines f3=|yhat∩y|/|y|, comparing the LLM response to the transmitted compressed input against the reference response for the original input.
validity_flags: Output overlap does not directly establish factual correctness or semantic equivalence; set/multiset and tokenization details are not specified.

ideas.title: Application-weighted composite fidelity
ideas.statement: Equation 7 defines f=phi1*f1+phi2*f2+phi3*f3 with application/QoS-dependent weights for representation, transmission and downstream utility.
validity_flags: No explicit normalization or nonnegativity constraint on fidelity weights is stated in this definition.

ideas.title: Printed compression trajectory and its notation inconsistency
ideas.statement: The source defines target psi_k=1/k and progress t∈[0,1], with monotone sigma(0)=0 and sigma(1)=1, then prints alpha(t)=psi_k^(−sigma(t)) (equation 8). Equation 9 gives beta(i)=alpha(t_i)/alpha(t_(i−1))=psi_k^[−(sigma(t_i)−sigma(t_(i−1)))].
validity_flags: Confirmed source inconsistency: with psi_k=1/k<1, the printed negative exponents yield alpha(1)=k>1, conflicting with retained-fraction alpha≤1 and target 1/k. Nearby example also says psi=16. No silent correction applied.

ideas.title: Linear compression schedule
ideas.statement: The linear schedule sigma(t)=t applies equal log-compression increments under uniform progress steps; the authors characterize it as consistent and computationally simple.
validity_flags: Compression direction depends on resolving the psi/exponent inconsistency in equations 8–9.

ideas.title: Cosine compression schedule
ideas.statement: The cosine schedule sigma(t)=[1−cos(pi*t)]/2 tapers changes near the beginning and end, intended to make compression transitions smoother and preserve quality.
validity_flags: Suggested task benefit is heuristic, not a proof of optimality.

ideas.title: Quadratic compression schedule
ideas.statement: The quadratic schedule sigma(t)=t² puts most compression in later stages and initially preserves more content; the authors suggest it for tasks needing careful late refinement.

ideas.title: Uniform M-step compression boundary claims
ideas.statement: For t_i=i/M, the printed constant per-step ratio is psi_k^(−1/M). The source states alpha(0)=1, alpha(1)=1/psi_k and continuous differentiability for smooth schedules.
validity_flags: The stated endpoint 1/psi_k is reciprocal to the preceding definition psi_k=1/k; this is the same unresolved source-level compression-factor convention inconsistency as equations 8–9.

ideas.title: Per-request compute energy combines SLM and LLM GPU costs
ideas.statement: Equations 13–14 model E(k,P_T)=E_e(k)+E_t(k,P_T), with E_e=t_e^SLM(k)*n_gpu^SLM*P_gpu^SLM+t_e^LLM(k)*n_gpu^LLM*P_gpu^LLM. GPU execution time, GPU count and thermal design power approximate compute energy, citing LLMCarbon [31].
validity_flags: Thermal design power is a proxy for actual energy. Although later described as an edge-device budget, equation 14 includes cloud LLM compute energy.

ideas.title: Wireless energy is power multiplied by compressed-bit upload time
ideas.statement: Equation 15 gives E_t=t_t(k)*P_T=[s(k)/R]*P_T, where s(k) is compressed prompt size in bits and R is uplink rate.

ideas.title: Shannon rate with distance loss and fading
ideas.statement: Equation 16 uses R=W*log2(1+gamma)=W*log2(1+P_T*g*d^(−omega)/lambda²), where g is described as a unit-mean exponential Rayleigh fading coefficient, d is distance, omega path-loss exponent, and lambda² AWGN noise.
validity_flags: The unit-mean exponential variable corresponds to Rayleigh power gain, despite being called a fading coefficient. The paper does not supply all physical parameters for replication.

ideas.title: Total service delay adds compression, LLM processing and upload
ideas.statement: Equation 17 models T(k,P_T)=t_e^SLM(k)+t_e^LLM(k)+t_t(k,P_T).
validity_flags: The modeled latency omits response downlink, network queueing and retransmission delay. Figure 1 frames it as first-token latency whereas some result prose says response generation.

ideas.title: Average bit-error probability integrates conditional errors over fading
ideas.statement: Equation 18 gives BEP=integral_0^infinity [zeta(mu2,mu1*tau)/(2*zeta(mu2))]*varphi_tau_n(tau) d tau. Zeta(.,.) is upper incomplete gamma, varphi the fading/SNR PDF, and mu1,mu2 encode modulation/detection choice; cited to [32] and special-function reference [33].
validity_flags: Specific mu values/modulation, fading PDF instantiation and coding/retransmission policy are not specified.

ideas.title: Joint compression-power objective maximizes fidelity under budgets
ideas.statement: Equation 19 maximizes f(k,eta(P_T)) over compression factor k and transmit power P_T, subject to E(k,P_T)≤E_th, P_T≤P_th, T≤T_th and f>f_th. Higher power may lower BEP but consume budget that favors more compression, which can harm f1 and f3.
validity_flags: No analytical optimum or feasibility guarantee is proved; the later DRL reward is described qualitatively and does not explicitly implement every constraint.

ideas.title: Centralized controller state
ideas.statement: A centralized DDQN controls N users; prose specifies per-user state as current fidelity, SNR and BEP, but the displayed supposedly three-dimensional vector is [f_n(eta_n),gamma_n, ] with an empty third entry.
validity_flags: Source-visible missing third vector coordinate; prose supplies BEP as intended state feature. Fairness and dynamic bandwidth allocation are asserted without a fairness criterion, and bandwidth is absent from the stated action.

ideas.title: Discrete joint action per user
ideas.statement: Each user action selects a compression level 0–4 and a transmit-power level 0–9. The source writes the multiuser action space as A={A1,…,AN}.

ideas.title: Double DQN separates action selection and value evaluation
ideas.statement: The current Q-network selects argmax_a′ Q(s′,a′;theta), while the target network evaluates it: y=r+mu*Q_target(s′,argmax_a′Q(s′,a′;theta);theta−) (equation 22). The authors use this background mechanism to mitigate overestimation and stabilize joint control.

ideas.title: Printed ordinary-DQN update and squared TD loss
ideas.statement: Equation 20 prints Q(s_t,a_t)←Q(s_t,a_t)+xi*r_(t+1)+mu*max_a Q(s_(t+1),a)−Q(s_t,a_t). Equation 21 prints the squared residual [r_(t+1)+mu max_a′Q_target(s_(t+1),a′;theta_i*)−Q(s_t,a_t;theta_i)]².
validity_flags: Equation 20 lacks brackets multiplying the whole TD error by xi, causing current Q terms to cancel literally; preserved as printed. Equation 21 is the ordinary DQN target, distinguished from Double DQN equation 22.

ideas.title: Replay-based DDQN training with exploration decay
ideas.statement: Algorithm 1 initializes current/target networks and replay memory, uses epsilon-greedy actions, stores transitions, samples minibatches, sets y=r for terminal states or equation 22 otherwise, descends squared TD loss, decays epsilon=max(epsilon*epsilon_decay,epsilon_min), and periodically copies theta−←theta.
validity_flags: Algorithm input includes unexplained target privacy parameters (epsilon,delta), unused in the algorithm; epsilon is also exploration rate. Network architecture, replay size, target-update interval, discount and exploration constants are not numerically specified.

ideas.title: DDQN time and space complexity
ideas.statement: Under parameter count P, K episodes, T steps/episode, batch B, replay capacity M and transition/state dimension d, the paper derives O(P) action evaluation, O(BP) update time, O(KTBP) total training time, and O(P+Md) space.
ideas.conditions: Assumes dense-network work scales linearly with P and transition storage scales with d; excludes LLM/SLM environment execution costs.

ideas.title: GPT-Neo/GPT-J evaluation on long prompts
ideas.statement: Following the LLMLingua platform, experiments use GPT-Neo 125M for compression and GPT-J 6B for responses, with MeetingBank-transcript and LongBench prompts exceeding 500 tokens.
validity_flags: No exact sample count, data split, compressor implementation settings, hardware, or generation parameters are specified.

ideas.title: MEC simulation configuration
ideas.statement: Simulations use total bandwidth 20 MHz, 1–10 dBm transmit power per user in ten 1 dBm levels (roughly 0.00126–0.01 W), dynamically varying channel quality 0.1–1, random heterogeneous user demands, episodes capped at 100 steps, and initialized NumPy/PyTorch seeds.
validity_flags: Seed values, N, channel-quality definition and channel evolution process are not numerically specified.

ideas.title: Reported training hyperparameters
ideas.statement: Table 2 lists learning rate 10^−3, alpha1/alpha2/alpha3=(0.4,0.3,0.3), total test-run range [1,10], and 10,000 episodes per run.
validity_flags: Table uses alpha for weights whereas fidelity equation uses phi; precise completed run count and relation to Figure 5’s 100 episodes/iterations are unclear.

ideas.title: Jointly learn schedule and iteration count
ideas.statement: The current framework fixes the denoising schedule and iteration count within a run. Future work could optimize both as decision variables, adapting trajectory to input type and balancing compute against compression quality.

ideas.title: Four 2× rounds versus one 16× round
ideas.statement: For Figure 4’s comparison, prose reports iterative fidelity 0.27 versus single-round 0.18, rewards 26.40 versus 17.74, and power 8.18 versus 2.90 unspecified units. Iterative total time is 5.90 s (compression 2.92, LLM 2.48, upload 0.50); single-round total is printed as 11.25 s (compression 6.59, LLM 4.12, upload 0.55).
ideas.conditions: Illustrative one-shot versus four-pass 16× compression comparison; model pair GPT-Neo 125M/GPT-J 6B.
validity_flags: Reported one-shot component times sum to 11.26 s rather than printed 11.25 s (rounding possible). Power units are unspecified; this is not a power-matched comparison. Figure 4 fidelity labels require separate inspection against prose.

ideas.title: 16× compression latency reductions under tolerated fidelity loss
ideas.statement: For MeetingBank-transcript prompts longer than 500 tokens, prioritizing compression while tolerating up to a 30% fidelity drop permits 16× reduction. The source reports total service-time reductions relative to no compression of 42.3% for one-shot JPPO and 46.5% for iterative JPPO++.
validity_flags: Aggregate uncertainty, sample count, and precise definition/baseline of the tolerated 30% fidelity drop are not supplied.

ideas.title: Illustrated fidelity components for one-shot versus iterative compression
ideas.statement: Figure 4 labels a roughly 1,000-token council transcript and roughly 60-token compressed versions. One-shot versus iterative values are f1=0.15 vs 0.21, f2=0.35 vs 0.58 and f3=0.05 vs 0.06, with total fidelity 0.18 vs 0.27. The iterative text includes the 9–0 approval vote absent from the one-shot example.
validity_flags: With alpha≈60/1000=.06, equations 4–5 imply f1≤alpha and f2≤alpha; illustrated f1/f2 exceed that bound, so displayed metrics are inconsistent with the formal definitions. Displayed text is excerpted and approximate token counts are not independently verifiable. Fidelity .27 versus weighted components .276 may reflect truncation/rounding.

ideas.title: Moderate compression and power generally maximize reward
ideas.statement: Across tabulated one-shot reward surfaces the authors find a compromise between prompt retention and channel reliability: too much compression harms content, too little increases processing/transmission cost, too little power raises BEP, and too much can exhaust energy budgets. Peak settings generally use moderate compression and power.
validity_flags: This shows optima in the paper’s simulated reward model rather than a general proof that all systems require the same compromise; mapping of table compression rows 1–10 to DDQN action levels 0–4 is unspecified.

ideas.title: Claimed schedule reward gains require comparison with tables
ideas.statement: The prose claims especially quadratic and cosine schedules improve peak reward over the single-shot baseline and quadratic exceeds it by over 10%. Table inspection supports the quadratic gain but not the stated cosine peak improvement.
validity_flags: Table 5 cosine maximum 11.64 is below Table 3 baseline maximum 12.06, contradicting the blanket cosine peak improvement claim. Table 6 quadratic maximum 13.46 does exceed baseline by about 11.6%.

ideas.title: Cosine DDQN training curve has highest eventual reward
ideas.statement: Figure 5 and its prose report DDQN training on MeetingBank long prompts across 100 episodes/iterations. Cosine reaches approximately 11 reward, linear and baseline approximately 10.2, and quadratic approximately 9 with visible oscillation; curves mostly level around episodes 30–40.
ideas.conditions: Approximate values visually read from Figure 5, not exact raw data.
validity_flags: No variance bands or repeated-run statistics shown. Prose claims optimal learned policies without an optimality proof. Figure labels 100 episodes/iterations while Table 2 lists 10,000 per run. Training outcome differs from one-shot table ranking; conditions explaining this reversal are not given.

ideas.title: Single-round reward matrix peak
ideas.statement: Table 3’s 10×10 compression-by-power grid peaks at 12.06 for compression row 4 and power level 3. Its lowest listed reward is 9.45 (row 1,power 10); power 3 is row-wise best throughout the grid.
validity_flags: Prose calls Table 3 single-round 16× compression, while table varies compression rows 1–10; exact row-to-ratio mapping is not fully defined.

ideas.title: Linear iterative reward matrix peak
ideas.statement: Table 4’s 10×10 grid peaks at 12.53 for compression rows 3 and 4, power level 4, versus baseline peak 12.06 (approximately 3.9% higher, derived from printed values). Minimum listed value is 10.25 at row 1/power 1; power 4 is row-wise best.

ideas.title: Cosine iterative reward matrix peak
ideas.statement: Table 5’s 10×10 grid peaks at 11.64 for compression row 3 and power 3, about 3.5% below baseline peak 12.06. Its minimum is 8.90 at row 10/power 10; power 3 is row-wise best.
validity_flags: Contradicts prose claiming cosine improves peak one-shot reward over baseline; does not contradict separate higher converged cosine reward in Figure 5 because protocols differ.

ideas.title: Quadratic iterative reward matrix peak
ideas.statement: Table 6’s 10×10 grid peaks at 13.46 for compression row 5 and power 5, approximately 11.6% above baseline peak 12.06. Minimum is 4.44 at row 1/power 1; power 5 is best for rows 2–10, while row 1 peaks at power 4.

ideas.title: Five MeetingBank samples show latency reductions over one-shot compression
ideas.statement: For five randomly selected MeetingBank-transcript samples, the source reports iterative JPPO++ upload-time reductions of approximately 10–65% and service-time reductions of 39–52% relative to one-shot compression. Figure 6 approximately shows per-sample upload reductions [10,54,33,63,61]% and service reductions [47,51,39,43,42]%.
validity_flags: Only five displayed samples, with no confidence intervals, cannot establish the claimed general real-world robustness; real wireless deployment was not evaluated. Exact approximate bar readings differ slightly from prose ranges.

ideas.title: Multi-news scores favor uncompressed and then one-shot prompts
ideas.statement: Figure 7a reports (QA F1, ROUGE-L) on Multi-news as no compression (.23,.25), JPPO (.20,.17), and JPPO++ (.19,.16). Both compressed methods use 16× total compression; JPPO++ is four 2× passes. Thus iterative compression is slightly worse than one-shot on both displayed metrics.
validity_flags: Contradicts the nearby prose that JPPO++ consistently has higher F1 and ROUGE-L than JPPO. No sample counts, variance or significance tests supplied.

ideas.title: GovReport scores improve with iterative compression but remain below uncompressed
ideas.statement: Figure 7b reports (QA F1, ROUGE-L) on GovReport as no compression (.37,.33), JPPO (.26,.18), and JPPO++ (.31,.21). Four 2× passes improve over one 16× pass while remaining below uncompressed input; the source attributes larger gaps to long information-dense documents.
validity_flags: Attribution to contextual density/coherence is the authors’ interpretation rather than an isolated causal experiment. Metric protocol and statistical uncertainty unspecified.

ideas.title: Hierarchical edge inference and distributed prompt-power control
ideas.statement: Future work proposes studying real-time edge SLM compression with cloud/edge LLM hierarchies and replacing centralized control with collaboration among edge nodes to improve scalability and resilience.

ideas.title: Personalize optimization to user and network needs
ideas.statement: Future work proposes incorporating user-specific demands and heterogeneous network conditions for context-aware service, including autonomous systems and smart-home tasks with different latency/efficiency requirements.

ideas.title: Abstract reports a separate 17% service-time reduction
ideas.statement: The abstract reports JPPO++ reducing service time by 17% compared with no compression while maintaining output quality.
validity_flags: The detailed experiments do not identify the exact setting, sample count, fidelity criterion or calculation behind this 17% abstract figure; it is distinct from the 46.5% aggressive-compression result and the five-sample comparison to one-shot compression.

ideas.title: Variable-rate prompts for cross-modal compression
ideas.statement: The source describes VR-CMC [26] as representing data at multiple granularities using variable-rate prompts for cross-modal compression.

ideas.title: Over-compression correction prioritizes any feasible commitment globally
ideas.statement: The correction teacher scans all candidate management calls for earliest answer-feasible commitment first; only if none exists does it scan for earliest novel productive search, then earliest useful fetch of a previously seen snippet docid; otherwise it emits no_replacement_possible.
ideas.conditions: Priority is action type globally, then earliest management step within that type; avoids choosing an early search when a later commitment is feasible.

ideas.title: Correction labels bind replacement actions to observed evidence
ideas.statement: Correction JSON uses a candidate replace_id, first-person think, human-only rationale and action-dependent fields: commit explanation/exact_answer/confidence, search_query, or docid_to_get. The think field is 200–1500 characters; rationale is one sentence to the experimenter for human review only; cited/fetched docids must already be retrieved at that point; search queries are 2–12 words.
ideas.conditions: Commit answer allowed from evidence already in context; replacement search can use gold evidence to propose a direction, while narrative and cited docids remain constrained.

ideas.title: Replacement search queries may draw distinctive terms from gold evidence
ideas.statement: The correction prompt requires a single concrete search query, not substring-equal to prior queries case-insensitively, and encourages distinctive previously untried terms from gold evidence. Replacement document reads must select an already visible snippet docid not yet fetched.
ideas.conditions: Gold-guided query generation is explicitly allowed despite general no-answer-leakage framing.

ideas.title: Holistic compression and isolated objects can omit multilevel spatial information
ideas.statement: The authors argue that compressing holistic 3D scenes or segmenting independent objects insufficiently represents spatial information at individual-object, object-grouping, and architectural levels, limiting 3D MLLM spatial awareness.
ideas.conditions: Motivating critique of existing 3D MLLMs; not a general theorem about compression.

ideas.title: Instruction-aligned Q-former embeddings may underrepresent spatial concepts
ideas.statement: The paper critiques 3D-LLM [3] and LL3DA [11] for extracting instruction-related scene information with Q-former [1]; it argues that overly instruction-aligned embeddings fail to fully capture spatial concepts.
ideas.conditions: Characterization by this source; no isolated Q-former causal experiment is supplied.

ideas.title: Progressive spatial enrichment creates visual prompts
ideas.statement: Spatial 3D-LLM integrates a frozen 3D scene encoder and LLM with intra-referent clustering/abstraction, distance-based inter-referent message passing, and contextual referent-scene interactions. Expanding the perception field enriches scene embeddings with location information for end-to-end instruction tuning.
ideas.conditions: The common model serves several 3D vision-language tasks; task-specific prompts and datasets still differ.

ideas.title: Existing spatial instruction data emphasize coarse relationships
ideas.statement: The authors characterize prior spatial QA data [13,14] as centered on object-pair relationships and metric estimates and 3D instruction data [15,16] as supporting QA, grounding, and spatial relation estimation while leaving fine-grained measurement and object-scene commonsense underexplored.

ideas.title: Spatial demands of standard 3D vision-language tasks
ideas.statement: The source contrasts holistic scene answering in 3D-VQA [17,18], locating described objects in 3D visual grounding [19,20], and describing objects or regions with their spatial context in dense captioning [21].

ideas.title: 3D-LLM special location tokens
ideas.statement: 3D-LLM [3] is described as introducing special location tokens to represent 3D spatial information and permit coordinate output.

ideas.title: LL3DA click and box prompts
ideas.statement: LL3DA [11] is described as using clicks and boxes as visual prompts to interact with 3D embeddings and generate spatial queries.

ideas.title: SpatialRGPT region-level reasoning
ideas.statement: SpatialRGPT [13] is described as improving region-level spatial reasoning through regional representation and acquisition of spatial knowledge.

ideas.title: Chat-3D v2 indexes segmented objects
ideas.statement: Chat-3D v2 [6] is described as segmenting scenes into objects, assigning each an index, and using special tokens for object attributes and spatial relations.

ideas.title: MODLE introduces distance measurement and layout editing
ideas.statement: The paper introduces Measure Object Distance and Layout Editing (MODLE), a 3D instruction dataset advertised as 263K annotations for object-distance measurement, object movement, and object placement.
ideas.conditions: The abstract and appendix use MODEL; main text/Table I use MODLE. Table I rounded row totals sum to 261K, whereas the prose reports 263K.

ideas.title: Template-generated object-distance questions
ideas.statement: The distance task asks for the spatial separation of two described objects. The authors generate 173K text-location pairs from manually defined question templates filled with ScanRefer [20] descriptions and answers derived from the objects’ actual 3D bounding-box coordinates.
ideas.conditions: Synthetic indoor-scene annotations; distances are later illustrated as per-axis absolute center-coordinate differences.

ideas.title: Distinct tokens delimit location and distance output
ideas.statement: Interaction tokens <loc>...</loc> delimit coordinate information and <gap>...</gap> delimit distance values in the generated answer.

ideas.title: Distance dataset size and output structure
ideas.statement: Table I lists 0.7K 3D scans and 171K training/2K validation language annotations for multi-object distance measurement, with object captions as input and bounding boxes plus distances as output.
ideas.conditions: Counts are rounded as printed; no independent dataset audit.

ideas.title: Movement dataset size and output structure
ideas.statement: Table I lists 0.7K scans and 36K training/9K validation annotations for single-object movement, using object captions and outputting bounding-box coordinates.
ideas.conditions: Counts rounded as printed.

ideas.title: Placement dataset size and output structure
ideas.statement: Table I lists 0.69K scans and 34K training/9K validation annotations for single-object placement, with [BOX] as the output type.
ideas.conditions: Table lists object captions as instructions, while appendix placement examples specify object type and size and return center coordinates; preserve source conventions.

ideas.title: Movement instructions translate a described object
ideas.statement: Object movement relocates the object selected by a description according to an editing instruction. The 45K text-location pairs use ScanRefer descriptions and randomly generated movement instructions in a template.
ideas.conditions: Predicts a new object position in a 3D scene; described relocation rather than a physical execution test.

ideas.title: Placement learns by reconstructing a masked object position
ideas.statement: For object placement, the authors create 33K ScanNet [22] sub-scenes containing 3–8 objects. During training and evaluation, one object is randomly masked and the model predicts a plausible position for an object of the specified size using the remaining scene layout.
ideas.conditions: Indoor sub-scenes derived from ScanNet; reconstruction supervision has one ground-truth placement although other plausible positions may exist.

ideas.title: PointNet++ yields 1,024 spatial point tokens
ideas.statement: A frozen PointNet++ [23] hierarchical scene encoder converts the unordered point cloud into 1,024 tokens F_enc=[p_enc,f_enc] in R^(1024×(3+256)), each holding three coordinate values and 256 feature dimensions.
ideas.conditions: The architecture freezes the scene encoder; initialized with pretrained weights described on page 4.

ideas.title: Farthest-point sampling reduces 1,024 scene points to 256 seeds
ideas.statement: The intra-referent module follows VoteNet [24] in using farthest-point sampling to choose 256 seed points from the 1,024 encoded scene points, obtaining F_seed=[p_seed,f_seed] in R^(256×(3+256)).
ideas.conditions: This is geometric sampling for visual referent formation, not text-token pruning or lossless compression.

ideas.title: FFN-predicted offsets move seeds toward object centers
ideas.statement: The intra-referent FFN predicts a 3D offset Δp_vote from each seed feature and updates its location using p_vr = p_seed + FFN(f_seed) = p_seed + Δp_vote, aiming to align referents with object centers.

ideas.title: Local clustering and pooling construct visual referent features
ideas.statement: Neighbor points around each visual referent location are grouped into local regions; their encoded features are pooled to obtain f_vr = Pooling(Cluster[p_vr,f_enc]). The resulting 256 referents F_vr=[p_vr,f_vr] have 3+256 dimensions and represent local point relationships.
ideas.conditions: The text describes the aggregation source as F_seed, while the equation and following explanation use f_enc; pooling type and cluster radius are unspecified.

ideas.title: Distance-based graph passing enriches referents with scene relationships
ideas.statement: The inter-referent module uses visual referent features as graph nodes and distances between referent locations to define edges. GCN message passing incorporates neighboring referents’ spatial context while retaining a 256×(3+256) referent representation.
ideas.conditions: The exact distance-to-edge rule and adjacency normalization are not specified in the paper.

ideas.title: Inter-referent GCN propagation
ideas.statement: The stated GCN layer update is H^(l+1)=σ(A H^(l) W^(l)), where H is the node embedding, A represents spatial adjacency, W is a learned layer weight matrix, and σ is the activation function.
ideas.conditions: Equation transcribed from the rendered page to resolve encoding loss; adjacency construction and activation type unspecified.

ideas.title: Contextual interaction alternates attention and location refinement
ideas.statement: Multiple contextual interaction blocks apply self-attention, cross-attention with global scene features f_enc, and a refine-location layer to the graph-refined referents F_vr-gcn, producing scene-aware features F_vr-enc that combine object features and positional information.
ideas.conditions: Block number, attention head count and detailed positional encoding are not given in the text.

ideas.title: Pairwise constraint matches inter-referent distances
ideas.statement: The pairwise spatial constraint loss is L_psc=(1/N)∑_(i,j) ||k_vr^(ij)−k_gt^(ij)||_2, comparing predicted and ground-truth distances for N visual referent pairs. Together with center loss it aims to preserve spatial relationships while improving locations.
ideas.conditions: k denotes a pair distance; the printed double-index upper limit is ambiguous given N is defined as pair count, so no unreported N×N summation is inferred.

ideas.title: Text coordinates are discretized to 0–255
ideas.statement: Following LL3DA [11], the model normalizes point-cloud coordinates to discrete unsigned integers in [0,255], distinguishing them from other text with <loc>...</loc> tokens.
ideas.conditions: Normalization parameters and treatment of out-of-range predictions are not detailed; reported example distances use these coordinate units.

ideas.title: An FFN projector aligns features and locations to the LLM
ideas.statement: A trainable multi-layer FFN projector maps F_visual=[f_vr,p_vr], concatenating referent features with location representation, into the LLM’s language space so spatial information can be processed alongside natural-language instructions.
ideas.conditions: Locations remain explicit in the visual prompt rather than being discarded after geometric sampling.

ideas.title: Instruction loss and two spatial losses are jointly optimized
ideas.statement: The objective is L_total=L_LLM+α1 L_psc+α2 L_center. L_LLM supervises instruction tuning on vision-language understanding and grounding tasks, while spatial losses supervise accurate coordinate perception and generation.
ideas.conditions: The paper does not supply α1 or α2 numerical values or isolated loss ablations.

ideas.title: Scene inputs are indoor ScanNet point clouds
ideas.statement: The experimental scene corpus is ScanNet [22], reported as 1,201 training scenes and 312 testing scenes.
ideas.conditions: The source labels the second partition testing; this extraction preserves that wording. Evidence is restricted to real indoor scenes.

ideas.title: Joint 3D understanding, grounding, and spatial task data
ideas.statement: Training/evaluation combines Scan2Cap [21], ScanQA [17], SQA3D [18] and embodiedQA from 3D-LLM [3] for understanding; ScanRefer [20] and Multi3DRefer [19] for single/multi-object grounding; and the proposed distance, movement and placement tasks.
ideas.conditions: Appendix page 7 separately states its Scene Description, Embodied Dialogue and Embodied Planning tasks come from LL3DA [11]; provenance wording differs.

ideas.title: Frozen pretrained encoder and Vicuna-7B LoRA tuning
ideas.statement: The scene encoder is initialized using pretrained Vote2Cap-DETR weights [25], and the language backbone uses pretrained Vicuna-7B with LoRA instruction tuning. Figure 1 marks the scene encoder as frozen and progressive spatial module and LLM as trained.
ideas.conditions: Reference [25] is titled Vote2Cap-DETR++ rather than the Vote2Cap-DETR name in the method; model checkpoint identity is not clarified.

ideas.title: Progressive module and LoRA train together on eight A100s
ideas.statement: The progressive spatial-awareness scheme and LoRA parameters are trained jointly across all task datasets using AdamW, learning rate between 10^-4 and 10^-7 and weight decay 0.1. The paper reports all experiments on eight A100 GPUs within one day.
ideas.conditions: Batch size, epochs, LoRA rank, seed and detailed learning-rate schedule are not stated.

ideas.title: All task evaluations share jointly trained model weights
ideas.statement: All tasks are trained concurrently and each evaluation uses the same model weights, rather than a separately fine-tuned checkpoint for every task.
ideas.conditions: Main comparison protocol; appendix Table V additionally varies task combinations.

ideas.title: Understanding comparison separates baseline training regimes
ideas.statement: Table II compares task-specific models, models with a unified pretrained backbone followed by task-specific fine-tuning, and generalist models. The understanding benchmarks are Scan2Cap, ScanQA and SQA3D.
ideas.conditions: Training regimes differ across baselines; this is not a strictly compute-matched architecture comparison.

ideas.title: Caption and answer metrics in Table II
ideas.statement: Table II uses CIDEr (C), BLEU-4 (B-4), METEOR (M), ROUGE (R), and top-1 exact match (EM@1). Scan2Cap n-gram scores are conditioned on IoU@0.5. Its dagger-marked 41.0 SQA3D result uses generated scene captions to prompt GPT-3.
ideas.conditions: Standard metrics attributed to references [26]–[29]; dagger protocol is a distinct baseline setting.

ideas.title: Scan2Cap improves CIDEr but not every language metric
ideas.statement: Spatial 3D-LLM reports Scan2Cap C/B-4/M/R=72.2/34.6/23.1/54.3 at IoU@0.5. CIDEr exceeds all reported baselines, including Grounded 3D-LLM 70.6; BLEU-4, METEOR and ROUGE are below the respective maxima 37.1, 27.1 and 55.6.
ideas.conditions: Reported comparisons across varied training regimes; no uncertainty intervals or repeat-run variability supplied.

ideas.title: ScanQA leads CIDEr, BLEU-4 and METEOR
ideas.statement: Spatial 3D-LLM reports ScanQA C/B-4/M/R=82.5/13.9/16.8/39.1. It leads reported CIDEr, BLEU-4 and METEOR values but its ROUGE 39.1 is below task-finetuned Chat-3D v2’s 40.1.
ideas.conditions: Same proposed-model weights across tasks; differing baseline training regimes.

ideas.title: SQA3D exact match is below stronger listed baselines
ideas.statement: Spatial 3D-LLM scores 46.2 EM@1 on SQA3D, compared with 48.5 for 3D-VisTA, 47.2 for ScanQA, and 41.0 for the Scan2Cap-caption-to-GPT-3 baseline.
ideas.conditions: Contrasts with the prose’s broad claim that Spatial 3D-LLM excels across all three tasks.

ideas.title: Grounding evaluation distinguishes boxes from object IDs
ideas.statement: ScanRefer uses Acc@0.25 and Acc@0.5; Multi3DRef uses F1@0.25 and F1@0.5. Table III labels models that generate bounding boxes [BOX] separately from models outputting existing object identifiers [ID].
ideas.conditions: Thresholds refer to grounding overlap criteria; output forms differ between systems.

ideas.title: ScanRefer grounding is competitive but below the top scores
ideas.statement: Spatial 3D-LLM directly outputs boxes and scores 44.3/37.2 Acc@0.25/0.5 on ScanRefer. It exceeds ScanRefer, LLM-Grounder, Chat-3D v2 and the row labeled ReGround3D 3D-LLM, but trails M3DRef-CLIP 51.9/44.7 and Grounded 3D-LLM 47.9/44.1.
ideas.conditions: Reference [32] attached to ReGround3D in the table is titled ScanReason in the bibliography; no correction inferred.

ideas.title: Multi-object grounding improves over listed baselines
ideas.statement: Spatial 3D-LLM obtains Multi3DRef F1@0.25/0.5=48.3/41.2, exceeding Grounded 3D-LLM’s 45.2/40.6 and M3DRef-CLIP’s 42.8/38.4 in Table III.
ideas.conditions: Only the three shown models have Multi3DRef numbers; the table does not provide ReGround3D Multi3DRef results.

ideas.title: Box-generation advantage and some baseline comparisons are not established by the table
ideas.statement: The prose claims a precise-box advantage over ReGround3D 3D-LLM and suggests outperforming it on Multi3DRef, but Table III also labels ReGround3D as [BOX] and provides no Multi3DRef score for that row. Those particular advantages cannot be established from the presented comparison.

ideas.title: Each progressive module improves captioning within the ablation
ideas.statement: Table IV Scan2Cap CIDEr/BLEU-4 rises from 52.1/32.5 with C1 (intra-referent) alone, to 67.1/33.3 with C1+C2 (inter-referent), to 72.2/34.6 with C1+C2+C3 (contextual interactions).
ideas.conditions: Nested component addition; no full factorial design, parameter-matched control, or uncertainty intervals.

ideas.title: Progressive components improve multi-object grounding
ideas.statement: Table IV Multi3DRef F1@0.25/0.5 improves from 30.4/15.9 for C1, to 43.4/37.0 for C1+C2, to 48.3/41.2 for all three components.
ideas.conditions: C1=intra-referent, C2=inter-referent, C3=contextual interactions; nested ablation.

ideas.title: Movement accuracy increases with spatial components
ideas.statement: Table IV movement Acc@0.5 is 31.7 with C1, 34.2 with C1+C2, and 40.3 with C1+C2+C3.
ideas.conditions: Proposed object movement task; overlap with one reference target; no external baseline reported.

ideas.title: Placement accuracy increases with spatial components
ideas.statement: Table IV placement Acc@0.5 is 46.8 with C1, 59.7 with C1+C2, and 66.4 with C1+C2+C3.
ideas.conditions: Masked-object reconstruction setting; no external baseline reported.

ideas.title: Progressive components reduce per-axis distance error
ideas.statement: Table IV X/Y/Z-mARE@0.5 declines from 7.5/8.7/7.2 with C1, to 2.6/2.1/4.5 with C1+C2, to 2.0/1.4/2.4 with all components.
ideas.conditions: Lower mean absolute relative error is better; the paper does not explicitly state whether displayed ARE numbers are percentages.

ideas.title: Improve real-time performance while retaining accuracy
ideas.statement: The authors plan to investigate faster inference without compromising accuracy for practical robotics and augmented-reality applications.
ideas.conditions: No real-time deployment, latency benchmark or embodied execution experiment is reported here.

ideas.title: Distance answers report per-axis absolute center gaps
ideas.statement: The appendix example in scene0011_00 identifies kitchen cabinets at (198,171,47,7,96,81) and a chair at (141,110,58,21,16,96), then reports x/y/z distances of 57/61/11. These equal absolute differences of the first three coordinates, illustrating axis-wise center separation rather than a single Euclidean scalar. Figure 2’s shelf and pillow centers (29,34,81) and (220,232,48) similarly yield (191,198,33).
ideas.conditions: Illustrated in discrete normalized coordinate units; this arithmetic interpretation is based on the explicit example.

ideas.title: Distance evaluation combines localization and per-axis relative error
ideas.statement: The main distance metric mARE@kIoU assesses mean absolute relative error for X, Y and Z distance predictions while considering localization accuracy of both objects, following the absolute relative error approach cited as [33].
ideas.conditions: The paper does not provide the ARE equation, explain zero-distance denominators, or specify the exact localization filtering/aggregation rule; Tables IV/V report k=0.5.

ideas.title: Movement output preserves size and changes the instructed coordinate
ideas.statement: In scene0011_00, moving the described cabinet forward by 110 units changes its box from (209,61,160,27,32,153) to (209,171,160,27,32,153). The example preserves size and adds 110 to the y coordinate. In Figure 2, a 29-unit rightward table movement changes (186,179,47,57,10,75) to (215,179,47,57,10,75), adding 29 to x.
ideas.conditions: Illustrates the example’s axis convention; does not establish a universal camera-relative forward direction.

ideas.title: Placement instruction gives object size and asks for a center
ideas.statement: The placement example asks to add a chair of w=27, h=22, l=96 to scene0011_00 and returns center coordinates (133,80,57). Figure 2 similarly places a monitor of w=10,h=18,l=49 at (139,106,98).
ideas.conditions: The size is supplied in the instruction; this example’s response is a center triplet rather than the [BOX] output described in Table I.

ideas.title: Layout edits are assessed by box overlap with ground truth
ideas.statement: Movement and placement evaluation use intersection-over-union between the predicted and ground-truth bounding boxes, following 3D visual grounding metrics, to assess predicted positions.
ideas.conditions: Tables IV/V use Acc@0.5. A single ground-truth box is a proxy for plausible placement, not a direct physical-validity or human-preference measurement.

ideas.title: Joint task training improves captioning in Table V
ideas.statement: With U=understanding, G=grounding and O=the proposed tasks, Table V Scan2Cap CIDEr/BLEU-4 is 66.9/33.0 for U-only, 68.2/34.2 for U+G, and 72.9/35.5 for U+G+O.
ideas.conditions: Different training-task combinations; no training-volume-matched control or statistical uncertainty is given.

ideas.title: Understanding and proposed tasks jointly improve grounding
ideas.statement: Table V Multi3DRef F1@0.25/0.5 is 45.3/40.3 for G-only, 47.2/40.1 for G+O, 48.3/42.7 for U+G, and 49.0/43.5 for U+G+O. Adding O to G alone improves F1@0.25 but slightly reduces F1@0.5; the full combination is highest.
ideas.conditions: U=understanding, G=grounding, O=proposed spatial tasks.

ideas.title: Adding understanding data improves movement and placement
ideas.statement: Table V movement/placement Acc@0.5 increases from 37.5/64.4 for G+O to 41.1/70.0 for U+G+O.
ideas.conditions: U=understanding, G=grounding, O=proposed tasks; only task combinations including O report these results.

ideas.title: Full-model results differ between the main and task-ablation tables
ideas.statement: The full model in Table IV has Scan2Cap 72.2/34.6, Multi3DRef 48.3/41.2, movement 40.3, placement 66.4 and distance 2.0/1.4/2.4; Table V U+G+O reports 72.9/35.5, 49.0/43.5, 41.1, 70.0 and 2.0/1.8/2.1 respectively. The paper does not explain this full-model result variation.
ideas.conditions: These are retained as distinct reported experimental settings; no averaging or reconciliation is inferred.

ideas.title: Appendix evaluates language outputs for three embodied tasks
ideas.statement: The appendix reports training and evaluation on Scene Description, Embodied Dialogue, and Embodied Planning from LL3DA [11], with results in Table VI and qualitative examples in Figure 2.
ideas.conditions: Text-output evaluation, not evidence of successful physical execution; main text attributes embodiedQA data to 3D-LLM [3].

ideas.title: Embodied QA compares zero-shot language models and LL3DA
ideas.statement: Table VI reports BLEU-1 through BLEU-4, CIDEr, METEOR and ROUGE-L (higher is better) for scene description, embodied dialogue and embodied planning. Each task includes zero-shot OPT-1.3B/2.7B/6.7B [34] and LLAMA-7B [35] rows, plus LL3DA [11] and the proposed model.
ideas.conditions: The table contrasts zero-shot and trained systems; the grouping label Ours above LL3DA is printed literally. Reference [35] is Llama 2 but the table labels the model LLAMA-7B.

ideas.title: Scene-description CIDEr and METEOR rise with mixed n-gram changes
ideas.statement: For scene description, the proposed model scores BLEU-1/2/3/4=42.67/25.03/15.29/9.37, CIDEr=5.50, METEOR=17.52, ROUGE-L=23.88. LL3DA scores 43.02/26.70/15.97/8.97, 0.96,14.65,24.84 respectively. The proposed model improves BLEU-4, CIDEr and METEOR but is lower on BLEU-1/2/3 and ROUGE-L.
ideas.conditions: All four zero-shot baseline vectors are retained in the exact table evidence; numbers preserved on the printed metric scale.

ideas.title: Embodied dialogue improves across all seven reported metrics
ideas.statement: For embodied dialogue, the proposed model scores BLEU-1/2/3/4=52.80/43.42/37.68/33.56, CIDEr=290.37, METEOR=27.46, ROUGE-L=51.54. LL3DA scores 41.38/32.59/27.47/23.95,190.01,23.50,40.61. The proposed model exceeds every baseline shown in every listed metric.
ideas.conditions: Reported automatic language-quality metrics; not a human evaluation of dialogue appropriateness.

ideas.title: Embodied planning improves longer n-grams, CIDEr and METEOR
ideas.statement: For embodied planning, the proposed model scores BLEU-1/2/3/4=37.35/26.42/19.56/14.65, CIDEr=195.92, METEOR=18.95, ROUGE-L=36.93. LL3DA scores 40.72/27.18/18.64/12.95,128.80,17.05,39.25. The proposed model improves BLEU-3/4, CIDEr and METEOR but trails on BLEU-1/2 and ROUGE-L.
ideas.conditions: Evaluation of generated planning text; no action success or embodied environment execution metric supplied.

ideas.title: Qualitative QA identifies a counter and counts chairs
ideas.statement: Figure 2’s QA panel shows an indoor reconstructed scene with answers Kitchen counter to a question about the counter below two windows and 2 chairs to a question about chairs at the table end.
ideas.conditions: Selected illustrative responses; no ground-truth overlay, case selection procedure or error-rate estimate is supplied.

ideas.title: Qualitative situated QA uses a described viewpoint
ideas.statement: Figure 2’s SQA3D example places the questioner at the bookshelf with two chairs behind them and asks the color of a backpack on the couch to the right; the displayed answer is black.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative viewpoint-conditioned language response; no independent correctness guarantee.

ideas.title: Qualitative grounding returns a box for a described table
ideas.statement: Figure 2 grounds the described brown square table next to the printer at (216,106,46,27,31,74), with the target shown by a colored bounding box in the scene.
ideas.conditions: Selected example; image does not provide a numerical overlap score.

ideas.title: Qualitative planning supplies a textual next step
ideas.statement: The Figure 2 embodied-planning prompt says the user wants to organize office supplies and has gone to the kitchen cabinets; the displayed next-step response is to arrange chairs around the tables.
ideas.conditions: The source presents this as qualitative output; task relevance and physical execution of this step are not independently established.

ideas.title: Qualitative dialogue adds a scene observation
ideas.statement: Figure 2 displays a dialogue in which a user describes a couch and two coffee tables, and the model adds that there is a chair near the couch and comments that it seems comfortable.
ideas.conditions: Illustrative conversational continuation; factuality and appropriateness are not independently scored.

ideas.title: Qualitative scene description mixes object relations with subjective prose
ideas.statement: Figure 2’s scene-description response names a couch, adjacent end table, central armchair, opposite-wall TV and nearby radiator, alongside subjective language about comfort, security and privacy.
ideas.conditions: An illustrative generation; the figure does not independently validate every named object or subjective assertion.

ideas.title: Does management fine-tuning broaden information-seeking directions?
ideas.statement: Appendix C asks whether training with memory tools encourages more diversified search than base ACM or ReAct, operationalized through semantic pivots between consecutive queries.
ideas.conditions: Investigated through a proxy metric in the same appendix, not an unresolved claim of mechanism.

ideas.title: Semantic query pivots are detected by embedding cosine thresholds
ideas.statement: Consecutive queries are embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-8B. A pivot is declared when cosine similarity s_t<τ; τ∈{0.3,0.4,0.5,0.6}, where a lower threshold demands a larger semantic shift.
ideas.conditions: Semantic-distance proxy for exploration, not direct verification of useful or novel hypotheses.

ideas.title: Running pivot fraction normalizes pivot count by transitions
ideas.statement: Equation1 defines f_t=(1/t)Σ_{i=1}^t1[s_i<τ], bounded in[0,1], the fraction of query transitions classified as pivots through t.
ideas.conditions: Authors assert convergence to a long-run average as t→∞ irrespective of query count; no stationarity/convergence assumptions or theorem are given.

ideas.title: Pivot curves align by relative token progress
ideas.statement: Appendix C normalizes each trajectory token position to[0,1] by its total token budget, intending all trajectories to contribute to each progress bin and avoid survivorship effects from shorter ReAct runs.
ideas.conditions: The text says total token budget while the plot labels0=start and1=end; binning/interpolation and whether budget means realized length are not specified.

ideas.title: Authors report higher average pivot rates after training
ideas.statement: Appendix C reports ACM-Post-Trained with the highest average pivot fraction at all four thresholds, base ACM close to ReAct, and large between-trajectory variance. Atτ=.6 it describes trained≈.50–.55 versus base/ReAct≈.45–.50.
ideas.conditions: Figure7 shows±1 standard-deviation bands, not confidence intervals; no significance test. Literal every-position ordering is stronger than the plotted low-threshold curves.

ideas.title: A smaller thinking model stops after two turns with low search accuracy
ideas.statement: Table4 under ReAct reports Qwen3-4B-thinking mean/max turns2.0/2, searches1.2 and accuracy3.4%; Qwen3.5-9B19.4/46, searches16.2 and accuracy57.3%. Authors attribute the difference to early rollout collapse before context management can help.
ideas.conditions: Comparison changes model generation and scale; the appendix9B57.3% is distinct from main-table57.0% and no reconciliation is given.

ideas.title: Spatial inject-none result
ideas.conditions: Shared spatial storage; vary only read-out. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Short rollouts offer little opportunity for compression or retrieval learning
ideas.statement: The authors argue that a model terminating at turn2 with under20% of token budget cannot provide useful management evaluation or RL signal, and select Qwen3.5-9B as the smallest tested family model able to sustain sufficient exploration.
ideas.conditions: Evidence compares one4B thinking model with9B; it does not establish a universal minimum model size.

ideas.title: Pivot plots show mean shifts with wide overlapping trajectory dispersion
ideas.statement: Figure7 plots all four thresholds with orange trained, green base ACM and blue ReAct means and±1SD bands. Approximate endpoints are around.04 versus.03 atτ=.3; .15 versus.15/.13 atτ=.4; .34 versus.32/.30 atτ=.5; .54 versus.53/.50 atτ=.6 for trained/ReAct/base, respectively.
ideas.conditions: Approximate readings from plotted curves, not source tabulated values; exact original plot data not available in the PDF.

ideas.title: A failed 4B case uses one search despite ample remaining context
ideas.statement: On qid124, Table5 reports20599 thinking characters then one broad search returning10 documents without the combined clues, followed by7104 thinking characters and a final answer. Total is1 tool call,2 turns,50s and≈23K/131K tokens≈18%. The answer The Game of Life is wrong against Magic Mommy Stories.
ideas.conditions: Representative selected example; thinking character counts and context-token counts are different quantities.

ideas.title: Failure trace invents a search restriction despite available token budget
ideas.statement: Figure8 reproduces qid124 turn2: the model recognizes23033/131072 tokens and says further searches are possible, then claims it cannot do real searches and guesses The Game of Life with70% confidence. Authors interpret this as failure to maintain a long-horizon plan rather than context exhaustion.
ideas.conditions: Model-generated trace quoted by authors; attribution of internal failure mechanism is interpretive.

ideas.title: Public ACM code, data and model resources
ideas.statement: The authors report releasing code, data and model checkpoints at https://github.com/lixiaochuan2020/agentic-context-management; the release is presented as a reproducibility contribution relative to methods without public data-generation pipelines.
ideas.conditions: Availability is an author claim in the paper; the repository was not independently fetched in this extraction.

ideas.title: Action world model and memory failure
ideas.statement: An action world model generates sequential video chunks from a first frame, text and camera actions while maintaining geometry, object identity and camera obedience across revisits; a plausible replacement scene or object on return is a memory failure.

ideas.title: Matched memory design matrix
ideas.statement: Echo-Memory holds the video diffusion backbone, optimizer, camera-action representation, sampler and evaluation fixed while varying capacity, compression, read-out and recurrence through Context, Compression, Spatial and State-Space families.

ideas.title: Memory comparisons confound capacity and access
ideas.statement: Larger raw context can improve performance by supplying more evidence; hidden compression costs and familiar in-domain textures can obscure loss of identity. Stored evidence must also be accessible through generator read-out.

ideas.title: Explicit retrieval, compression and implicit memory
ideas.statement: Prior long-horizon video interfaces append historical frames/features selected by overlap, geometry, identity or time; compress history by weighting, pooling, packing or summaries; or carry history through recurrent/state-space computation.

ideas.title: Target-only rectified flow regression
ideas.statement: The pretrained video DiT predicts v_theta(z_t;t,c_text,c_ctx,c_act), where z_t is a noised VAE latent and c_act is T by 12. Training minimizes E_{t,x,c}||v_theta-v*||_2^2, v*=z_1-z_0, on target frames only.
ideas.conditions: Shared pretrained backbone [52,53]; context tokens do not receive this target loss.

ideas.title: Per-frame VAE context
ideas.statement: One VAE latent token group per video frame aligns context and target temporal semantics and makes temporal compression an operation on a fixed latent stack.

ideas.title: Relative RT camera action encoding
ideas.statement: Each action uses 12 camera RT entries: nine rotation and three translation entries relative to the first frame of its segment. Absolute encodings are outside scope.

ideas.title: Anchor plus retrieved historical context
ideas.statement: For target segment s:e, C_{s:e}={(x_fk,p_fk)}_{k=0}^{K-1}, with f_0=s and remaining indices in {0,...,s-1}. The anchor is current segment start and K-1 observations come from historical retrieval R.

ideas.title: Cold-start context dropout
ideas.statement: With probability 0.1, drop all retrieved frames and retain the anchor to train for cold-start generation.

ideas.title: Memory profiles and isolated ablations
ideas.statement: Profiles specify storage, context length, compression, read-out and recurrence. Mutual-exclusion constraints prevent simultaneous state-space instantiations, and default rows match training/inference profiles with fixed timestep shift, relative RT and target-frame supervision.

ideas.title: Shared data and fixed field-of-view retrieval
ideas.statement: Training uses Context-as-Memory long camera trajectories with poses, prompts and videos; samples are 81 frames at 352 by 640. A fixed field-of-view retriever and the same first-frame relative camera convention operate in training and evaluation.

ideas.title: Single-stage training hyperparameters
ideas.statement: All rows use per-frame-VAE Video DiT, AdamW, 8 A100-80G GPUs and 5,000 optimization steps. K is 1,5 or 20 (default 5), with learning rate 5e-5 except 1e-4 at K=1; target-only supervision, relative RT and 10% overlap drop are enabled.
validity_flags: K=1 learning-rate exception to otherwise shared recipe

ideas.title: Fixed in-training replay diagnostic
ideas.statement: Fixed held-out replay cases sampled at matched training intervals use the evaluation generation path, retriever, relative actions and memory profile to inspect chunk boundaries, identity drift and action alignment beyond scalar denoising loss.

ideas.title: Three distinct evaluation branches
ideas.statement: Replay measures PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS under dataset camera trajectories; in-domain return uses a GT-backed 180-degree loop with image/VLM checks; open-domain return uses edited held-out first frames and a 45-degree leave-return probe.

ideas.title: Legacy hybrid State-Space metric bundle
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Block-wise State-Space metric bundle
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Raw Context K=5 metric bundle
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Raw Context K=20 metric bundle
ideas.conditions: Shared 5k-step, single-dataset protocol; metrics order is Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM (higher except LPIPS). Eight cases per row disclosed later.
validity_flags: Small evaluation sample; single training budget and dataset

ideas.title: Replay fidelity does not predict semantic return
ideas.statement: Spatial wins representative Replay PSNR, raw K=20 wins Replay SSIM/LPIPS, and block-wise State-Space wins open-domain VLM. Figure 7 reports correlation r=-0.03 between its normalized replay bundle and open-domain VLM, exposing differing capabilities.
ideas.conditions: Representative seven-row matrix; do not generalize correlation to all designs.

ideas.title: Spatial text KV concatenation result
ideas.statement: Spatial text KV concatenation yields [13.44, 0.412, 0.572, 9.35, 0.272, 0.614, 10.25].
ideas.conditions: Shared spatial storage; vary only read-out. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Spatial separate cross-attention result
ideas.statement: Spatial separate cross-attention yields [13.52, 0.409, 0.557, 8.49, 0.232, 0.664, 17.12].
ideas.conditions: Shared spatial storage; vary only read-out. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Spatial storage benefits can survive withheld read-out
ideas.statement: Inject-none withholds stored tokens yet has the best spatial-family replay bundle (14.66/.417/.541), while dedicated cross-attention gives highest family open-domain VLM 17.12, still far below raw Context and block-wise recurrence. Authors infer replay benefits can reflect regularization and both retention bandwidth and access are bottlenecks.
ideas.conditions: Mechanistic explanation is an interpretation of ablation, not a direct causal measurement.

ideas.title: Matched qualitative return reveals lost identity
ideas.statement: In the representative rainbow-bear street case, the Spatial revisit panel omits the bear, K=1 replaces it and changes scene, while Context-5 and block-wise recurrence retain conspicuous rainbow-bear appearance; compression and legacy examples show intermediate distortion.
ideas.conditions: One illustrative case, not an aggregate measurement.

ideas.title: Length compression r=2 result
ideas.conditions: Compression ablation, shared protocol. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Length compression r=4 result
ideas.conditions: Compression ablation, shared protocol. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Hybrid length r=2 plus weighting result
ideas.statement: Hybrid length r=2 plus weighting yields [9.1, 0.181, 0.734, 7.87, 0.277, 0.695, 8.75].
ideas.conditions: Compression ablation, shared protocol. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Hybrid length r=4 plus weighting result
ideas.statement: Hybrid length r=4 plus weighting yields [9.63, 0.215, 0.73, 8.81, 0.156, 0.625, 9.0].
ideas.conditions: Compression ablation, shared protocol. Values ordered Replay PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; in-domain PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; open-domain VLM.

ideas.title: Compression operator interaction is nonmonotonic
ideas.statement: Length r=4 achieves open-domain VLM 43.25 versus 22.38 for weight-only and 9.00 for hybrid r=4. Authors interpret shorter clean slots as more readable and pooling-before-weighting as potentially deleting return-critical views; token count alone cannot establish retained memory quality.
validity_flags: Evidence-deletion and attention-diffusion mechanisms are interpretations

ideas.title: Structured recurrence trades replay for return
ideas.statement: Block-wise recurrence nearly doubles open-domain VLM over legacy hybrid (69.00 versus 34.75), despite lower Replay PSNR (9.59 versus 12.69); authors propose depth-integrated non-bypassable state preserves history while competing with local reconstruction.
validity_flags: Non-bypassability/capacity explanation inferred rather than directly measured

ideas.title: Raw-context return gain is large and sublinear
ideas.statement: Increasing raw K from 1 to 5 raises open-domain VLM 12.25 to 50.75 (+38.50); K=20 adds 7.88 to 58.63. Replay PSNR rises 10.03 to 11.92 to 12.54. Authors use K=20 as a strong capacity calibration for compact memory.
ideas.conditions: Three tested K values, no established asymptotic law; raw context cost rises with K.

ideas.title: Normalized training cost versus replay quality
ideas.statement: Figure 9 plots normalized GPU-hour per step against normalized Replay PSNR, excluding the Comp-W outlier. Spatial occupies strong replay efficiency, Context-20 adds cost and block-wise state has low replay quality despite best semantic return; this plot does not rank semantic efficiency.
validity_flags: No absolute step costs printed in figure

ideas.title: Figure 9 in-domain PSNR plot differs from tables
ideas.statement: The plotted in-domain PSNR values for K=1 and K=5 are below 10 (roughly 9.4 and 9.7), whereas Tables 3/6 give 10.32 and 10.72; K=20 plotted near 11.3 versus table 11.07. Use printed tables for exact values and retain discrepancy unresolved.

ideas.title: Memory design has multiple objectives
ideas.statement: Local replay fidelity, step-time cost and revisit generalization select different designs; no row dominates all axes. Spatial suits replay efficiency, long raw context supplies robust uncompressed evidence, and block recurrence supplies strongest tested semantic return.

ideas.title: Separate retention, access and capacity in future studies
ideas.statement: Future tests should include raw-context scaling, fixed-storage varying read-out, fixed-read-out varying storage, object-level retention measures and recurrent integration depth; evaluate compression by retained high-value views/objects rather than only token reduction.

ideas.title: Return-aware supervision for future memory designs
ideas.statement: Proposed directions include spatial object-retention losses, source/return contrastive alignment, VLM-guided compression selection and explicit object/view prediction from recurrent states; these were not evaluated in this study.
ideas.conditions: Future proposals, not current implementation or established improvements.

ideas.title: Single-dataset, finite-budget and proxy-selection limits
ideas.statement: Memory rankings may change with noisy poses, camera statistics, compute or multistage curricula; open-domain VLM scoring needs broader human calibration and no cheap revisit-quality training signal is available. Reported rows are representative implementations, not definitive family optima.

ideas.title: Stronger generators still require return checks
ideas.statement: More capable generators can hallucinate visually plausible replacement objects, making failures hard to notice without return-specific semantic checks; authors recommend retaining three-branch evaluation as backbones improve.

ideas.title: Off-the-shelf Wan Video DiT substrate
ideas.statement: Echo-Memory uses off-the-shelf Video DiT [53] as the shared substrate. Per-frame action signals attach to corresponding latent-frame tokens and propagate via self-attention; memory choices are local edits to that substrate.

ideas.title: Camera injection-site possibilities
ideas.statement: Appendix A lists post-attention, pre-norm, pre-QKV and gated pre-QKV as action injection sites and calls site a design variable. No corresponding isolated injection-site result table is supplied; main analysis controls camera representation while varying memory.
validity_flags: Referenced section 3.2 contains memory design overview, not injection-site ablation

ideas.title: Implicit long-horizon memory in prior video work
ideas.statement: Prior state-space video models propagate causal hidden state through selected DiT blocks; recurrent gates, test-time fast weights, flow-equivariant states and plug-and-play memory tokens are alternative lighter/modular interfaces.

ideas.title: Mid-frame overlap retrieval convention
ideas.statement: Historical K-1 context frames are retrieved using precomputed field-of-view overlap labels keyed to target midpoint. Training reference r_train=(s+e)/2 aligns with in-domain evaluation r_eval=N_frames/2 for videos starting at 0; this retrieval reference is distinct from first-target-frame RT coordinates.

ideas.title: Pilot rationale for single-stage training
ideas.statement: At the tested pilot scale, authors could not find a multistage schedule consistently outperforming single-stage training, so use identical-length single-stage runs for interpretability.
ideas.conditions: Unquantified pilot observation, not evidence that multistage training generally fails.

ideas.title: Judge bibliography references do not uniquely identify reported judge
ideas.statement: Appendix A attaches [54,59] to examples including Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, but bibliography titles are Qwen2-VL and Qwen3-Omni respectively. Retain the reported judge name; these references do not directly document its exact implementation.

ideas.title: Batch, shifts, spike threshold and suffix placement
ideas.statement: Table 7 specifies per-device batch/gradient accumulation 1/1, timestep shift 15, spike-rejection threshold 15.0, flow-noise shift 1.0 and suffix context placement, with the same 5k-step eight-GPU training.
ideas.conditions: Paper does not specify a mathematical spike-rejection procedure beyond its threshold.

ideas.title: Construct camera trajectory before generation
ideas.statement: Replay converts dataset camera trajectory to relative 12D RT; return construction synthesizes symmetric yaw loops (180/360 degrees and short 45-degree open-domain probe). Actions are constructed before target frames are seen, preventing post-hoc alignment.

ideas.title: Frame/chunk diagnostics and retention ratios
ideas.statement: Store replay metrics at frame and chunk granularities: frame PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS locate drift onset; chunk means and retention ratios summarize degradation with distance from the anchor.
ideas.conditions: The excerpt names retention ratios but gives no formula or numerical ratio table.

ideas.title: Train-inference consistency invariants
ideas.statement: Evaluation requires matching context handling, context noise and K between training/inference; fixed target-only supervision and flow-noise shift; loaded camera-action parameters; mutually exclusive state instantiations and compression weighting/length unless explicitly hybrid.

ideas.title: Eight-case revisit snapshot
ideas.statement: Unless stated otherwise, each revisit row reports eight cases, with 180-degree in-domain loops and 45-degree open-domain probes; Replay means cover three GT-trajectory chunks. The 160-image source pool is not the evaluation sample count.
validity_flags: Eight cases per row; per-case variation not tabulated

ideas.title: Raw K=20 in-domain VLM prose result
ideas.statement: Appendix C.1 states raw Context K=20 has in-domain VLM 29.40 and calls it second-best; this metric is not included in printed headline tables. Later page 28 calls K=20 dominant on this column, so exact rank is unresolved.

ideas.title: In-domain reconstruction may conceal brittle memory
ideas.statement: Legacy state-space has highest in-domain PSNR and block-wise lowest in-domain LPIPS; authors interpret familiar textures and pixel-aligned views as allowing local reconstruction to succeed without robust state under shift.

ideas.title: Three spatial read-out paths
ideas.statement: Withheld read-out leaves stored tokens unreachable; text-KV concatenation appends spatial tokens to the existing text cross-attention slots; dedicated cross-attention gives spatial tokens their own queries and a zero-initialized gate trainable by the optimizer.

ideas.title: Spatial-grid identity bandwidth assumption
